70000001.name: Ur
70000001.description: The capital city of the Sumerian people, known as the political and economic centre of Ancient Mesopotamia. Famous for the great Ziggurats said to have been built by King Ur Nammu.

70000002.name: The Vergina Ruins
70000002.description: The remains of the ancient Macedonian capital Aigai. It is where the tombs of the Macedonian kings are believed to be located.

70000003.name: The Ruins at Olympia
70000003.description: There are many remains of ancient Greek temples and stadia. Because the Olympic Games were held here, there are various building for different athletic events.

70000004.name: Cappadocia
70000004.description: Strange rocks, beaten over the ages by the winds and rain, tower over these parts. Gouged into them are the dwellings once made by fleeing refugees.

70000005.name: Site of Carthage
70000005.description: The remains of a city state built by the ancient Phoenicians. It is said to have been laid to waste in the third Punic war. It was rebuilt by Caesar but fell into ruins at the end of the seventh century.

70000006.name: Karnak Megalithic Group
70000006.description: A group of prehistoric megaliths. Over 4000 stones stand lined in rows for an unknown purpose. The remains of stone structures abound, making it seem like a giant graveyard.

70000007.name: Pyramids of Giza
70000007.description: Three great pyramids in a row, built in precisely set huge stones. The largest is King Khufu's, followed by King Khafre's, and then King Menkaure's. I wonder if we could do the same with our current technology.

quests.name: Investigation of the Pyramids of Giza
Investigation of the Pyramids of Giza
Investigation of the Pyramids of Giza
Investigation of the Pyramids of Giza

70000008.name: Knossos Palace
70000008.description: The remains of the ancient Cretan civilization. The ruins of the castle of King Minos of Greek mythology. Behind this castle is said to lie the labyrinth of the Minotaur.

70000009.name: The Zimbabwe Ruins
70000009.description: A group of stone structures in the south of Africa. This was the capital of the Kingdom of Mutapa, meaning Stone house in the Shona language. African cultures who built in stone were rare.

70000010.name: Archaeological Area of Troy
70000010.description: The remains of Troy, written about in Homer's Iliad. Also know as Ilium, it is said to have been sacked when the Greek army entered the city in a wooden horse.

70000011.name: Paphos
70000011.description: There are ancient Roman remains on top of a hill in Cyprus. Several ruined buildings and mosaic walls can be found. Cyprus is a complex mixture of several cultures.

quests.name: Town dedicated to Goddess of Beauty
Town dedicated to Goddess of Beauty
Town dedicated to Goddess of Beauty
Town dedicated to Goddess of Beauty

70000012.name: Byblos
70000012.description: The remains of an ancient fortress and settlement. Because of the many changes in ruling powers, the traces of several cultures are intricately interwoven.

70000013.name: The Ruins of Persepolis
70000013.description: Ruins of the Persian Imperial Palace built by Darius I, king of the Achaemenian Empire. Several stone columns, many unique statues, and a magnificent relief remain on this vast site.

70000014.name: The Boyne Valley Ruins
70000014.description: Prehistoric remains in Ireland. Rows of tombstones with intricate stonework. The back of this sepulcher is illuminated by the morning sun on only a few days around the winter solstice.

70000015.name: The Ruins of Pompeii
70000015.description: An ancient Roman city wiped out in an instant by the eruption of mount Vesuvius. Buried in volcanic ash, it gives a morbid account of every-day life in the city of that time.

70000016.name: The Ruins of Leptis Magna
70000016.description: Remains of the city built by Septimus Severus, Emperor of Rome. The prosperity of the city can be seen in the lavish use of marble.

quests.name: Ruins of an ancient Roman city
Ruins of an ancient Roman city
Ruins of an ancient Roman city

70000017.name: Abu Simbel Temple
70000017.description: A temple built by Ramesses II, Pharaoh of ancient Egypt. Although there are many stone sculptures inside and outside, it is dominated by a statue of Ramesses II in the pose of the god Osiris. Next to it is a temple to a minor deity.

70000018.name: Karnak & Luxor Temples
70000018.description: A group of temples made in turn by generations of Pharaohs. There is a magnificent view of all the temples, idols, and rows of stone columns.

70000019.name: Konark Sun Temple
70000019.description: Temple of the sun god Surya. The whole temple is an image of Surya's chariot. It is said to have been built by Narashimha Dhruva I of the Ganga Dynasty to commemorate the defeat of the Islamic invaders.

quests.name: Temple dedicated to the sun god
Temple dedicated to the sun god

70000020.name: Stonehenge
70000020.description: Prehistoric remains in England. Believed to have been the site of religious rituals. The entrance faces where the sun would rise on the summer solstice and the stones are set in a perfect circle.

70000021.name: The Ruins at Delphi
70000021.description: This location was thought to be the centre of the world in ancient Greece. It housed the Temple of Apollo, whose prophecies were thought to be unfailing. Socrates also sought prophecies here.

70000022.name: Brihadisvara Temple
70000022.description: The temple of Shiva, Indian God of destruction, built by the Chola emperor Rajaraja I. It has a vast hall called Vimana.

70000023.name: Mohenjo-Daro
70000023.description: Remains of a city from the Indus civilization. It had extremely well laid out streets and fully functioning sewers. Called the hill of death for the human bones scattered all over the area.

70000024.name: The Jewel of Augustus
70000024.description: A giant cameo of Octavius Augustus, wearing a crown, sitting next to Venus. Augustus was Caesar's adopted son and Rome's first emperor.

70000025.name: Aurelian's Helmet
70000025.description: The helmet of Aurelianus, an emperor in the latter days of Rome. This wise ruler put down numerous rebellions and ruled strictly but fairly. He was assassinated during a campaign into Persia.

70000026.name: Agamemnon's Gold Mask
70000026.description: Burial accessories of King Agamemnon of Mycenae, who appears in tales of Greek mythology. These items prove the Iliad was not just some story, that Agamemnon and Achilles were real!

70000027.name: The Aksum Stele
70000027.description: A forest of giant stone columns, carved from single rocks. The tallest standing stone is 25m, some fallen stones are 33m. Judging by the chamber at the base, it seems to be a gravesite.

70000028.name: Agrippina Hair Dressing
70000028.description: Agrippina the Younger was the sister of ancient Roman emperor Caligula, wife of Claudius, and mother of Nero. She was said to be wearing these when she was assassinated by her son.

70000029.name: Abbas' Sword
70000029.description: A sword made by Abu al-'Abbas as-Saffah, who defeated the Umayya Caliphate and revived the Abassid Caliphate. The Abassids ruled for about five centuries until they were overthrown by the Mongolians.

70000030.name: The Apadana Reliefs
70000030.description: The Apadana was the name for the largest audience hall of Persepolis, the great palace of the Achaemenid Empire. The hall is carved with intricate reliefs showing Darius receiving tribute.

70000031.name: The Colossi at Abu Simbel
70000031.description: Four great statues of Ramises II standing at the entrance to the Abu Simbel temple. They are 20m tall with carvings of the Pharaoh's family at the feet.

70000032.name: Painted Pottery
70000032.description: Earthenware decorated with designs. Developed by many ancient civilizations, each with their own unique designs. A study of these designs is thought to be useful in clarifying the interactions between cultures.

70000033.name: Alexander the Great's Sword
70000033.description: The sword of Alexander the Great, the Macedonian King who ruled an empire from the Mediterranean to Persia. Using the best craftsmanship from East and West, it is a king of swords.

70000034.name: Alexander the Great's Armour
70000034.description: The armour of Alexander the Great, the Macedonian King who ruled an empire from the Mediterranean to Persia, exquisitely encrusted with jewels from Egypt and Persia.

quests.name: Land to which the king returned

70000035.name: Tomb of Alexander the Great
70000035.description: The Sarcophagus of Alexander theGreat who was struck down in the middle of building a great empire. Each side is covered with delicate reliefs depicting his conquests.

70000036.name: The Sceptre of Antoninus Pius
70000036.description: The Sceptre of Antoninus Pius, fourth of the Five Good Emperors. Beautifully made with marble, gold, coral, and pearls.

70000037.name: Canon of Medicine
70000037.description: The Canon of Medicine. Written by Islamic scientist, Ibn Sina; it is said to be the greatest work on Arabic medicine and is used widely from Persia to throughout Europe.

70000038.name: Ancient Millstones
70000038.description: A stone mortar made for milling grains and beans into powder form. In this form, they are easier to store and cook. They have been found at historical sites around the world.

70000039.name: Ancient Clothing
70000039.description: Ancient garments. They vary in materials, colours, and construction from place to place. It's possible to trace the transfer of cultures by comparing these styles.

maps.name: Ancient Clothing Map
maps.location: Africa North Coast South Mediterranean Sea

70000040.name: Iliad
70000040.description: Homer's epic poem. Written about the hero Achilles and the Trojan wars of Greek mythology. Iliad means the story of Ilios. Ilios is another name for Troy.

70000041.name: The Staff of Peter the Hermit
70000041.description: The staff of Peter the Hermit, the monk who lead the largest group in the People's Crusade at the end of the eleventh century. He lead a popular army of over twenty thousand people to defeat under the Turks.

70000042.name: The Indus Style Square Seal
70000042.description: A triangular seal of the Indus civilization. It is inscribed with geometric patterns, animals, and Indus symbols.

70000043.name: The Treasures of Vergina
70000043.description: Several burial accessories excavated from what is thought to be the grave of Philip II, father of Alexander the Great. Includes personal accessories and bronze armour.

70000044.name: Sword of the Sea People
70000044.description: Iron sword believed to have belonged to the Sea People, the mysterious culture that destroyed the Hittite Kingdom. Perhaps they stole iron smelting technology from the Hittites.

70000045.name: Sea People's Armour
70000045.description: Iron armour believed to have belonged to the Sea People, the unidentified ancient culture that destroyed the Hittite Kingdom and tormented the Egyptians. However, only the Hittites were thought to have known how to smelt iron.

70000046.name: Excalibur
70000046.description: The sword that appeared in the legends of King Arthur. King Arthur received it from the Lady of the Lake. Excalibur could cut through steel and it's scabbard is said to have healed it's bearer of all wounds.

70000047.name: Slate of Hieroglyphs
70000047.description: A stone slate inscribed with ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. Birds, beasts, and parts of the body are all displayed in characters. What could they mean?

70000048.name: Etienne's Staff
70000048.description: A staff belonging to twelve-year-old shepherd Stephen of Cloyes, who led the Children's Crusade. Many boys and girls became tragic sacrifices to history.

70000049.name: Epaminondas' Armour
70000049.description: Epaminondas was a politician and general from the Ancient Greek city-state of Thebes. Using new military tactics, he defeated Sparta's close-formation fighting.

70000050.name: The Statue of Ebih-Il
70000050.description: Stone statue from the Mesopotamian civilization. Made from alabaster, it gives a gentle impression. Mesopotamian statues are characterised by large eyes and flowing beards.

70000051.name: The Inscription of Ganjiname
70000051.description: Inscription. An inscription carved into the bare rock of a mountain. There are two: one belongs to Darius I, the other to his son Xerxes I.

70000052.name: The Erechtheion Statues of Girls
70000052.description: Standing near the Parthenon, the Erechtheion temple has the Caryatids, six draped female figures with an atmosphere of elegance, as supporting pillars.

70000053.name: The Cylindrical Seal
70000053.description: A round seal used in the area of ancient Mesopotamia. Used by rolling over a clay tablet.

70000054.name: The Discus
70000054.description: A sculpture said to have been made by the ancient Greek sculptor Myron. The original was said to be made of bronze, though this made of marble. Made during Roman times.

70000055.name: The Golden Coffin
70000055.description: A gold coffin. Thought to have belonged to an ancient royal, or noble family. It's exquisite ornamentation gives some indication of the power of the one buried.

70000056.name: The Golden Grave Burial Items
70000056.description: Golden grave burial items, buried along with the deceased. In many cases, items used while alive or exceptional items were interred to ease their life after death.

70000057.name: King Otto's Crown
70000057.description: Crown said to have been used by Otto I when he was crowned the first Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire. Gorgeously made with lavish use of gold and jewels.

70000058.name: Odysseia
70000058.description: Homer's epic poem. Tells the tale of Odysseus, whose Wooden Horse ended the Trojan War. Odysseus angered the gods, and as a result, underwent numerous hardships on his journey home.

70000059.name: Odoacer's Sword
70000059.description: Odoacer was the Germanic general who caused the end of the Western Roman Empire. The leader of a band of foederati of Western Rome, he drove out the Emperor and titled himself King of Italy.

70000060.name: Obelisk
70000060.description: A long thin stone column with an inscription created by the Egyptian civilization. It has a pointed tip and a distinctive appearance. They were also made in Ancient Rome.

70000061.name: Charlemagne's Crown
70000061.description: The jeweled crown used when Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor. With this, the Western Roman Empire was revived and a link forged between Imperial and Papal authority, creating a force capable of fighting the Byzantine Empire.

quests.name: Revival of the western Roman empire
Revival of the western Roman empire
Revival of the western Roman empire

70000062.name: Shell Money
70000062.description: Cowry and other shells. Commonly used as currency in many ancient civilizations. Shell remains can be found in several places.

70000063.name: The Marble Statue of Caesarion
70000063.description: Marble statue of Caesarion, son of Julius Caesar and Cleopatra VII. At one time the successor to Caesar, he was killed after Cleopatra's death.

70000064.name: The Gold Cup of Julius Caesar
70000064.description: A golden cup given to Julius Caesar by Cleopatra VII. Because of gold dust in the River Nile, Egypt was said to have been abundant in gold.

70000065.name: Caesar's Sword
70000065.description: Julius Caesar's sword. Said to have been worn while suppressing Gaul. Excavated from the remains of Pompeii, on the blade are written records of Celtic treasures.

70000066.name: Julius Caesar's Armour
70000066.description: Julius Caesar's armour. Are the scratches and dents from the suppression of Gaul or perhaps from crossing the Rubicon and occupying Rome?

70000067.name: Livestock Bones
70000067.description: Bones of cows, horses, and other domesticated animals. Goats and sheep were kept in many places around the world, but horses are not found in many civilizations.

70000068.name: The Paintings in Cappadocia
70000068.description: Murals which appear at various places inside Cappadocia. Drawn at diverse periods, they show many different styles.

quests.name: Something that should not be seen
Something that should not be seen

70000069.name: Marble Statue of Caracalla
70000069.description: Marble Statue of Emperor Caracalla, who was famous for building the Baths of Caracalla. A tyrant who killed all his political opponents, beginning with his younger brother, and waged war incessantly.

70000070.name: Glass Jewellery
70000070.description: Glass produced for ornamental use. Seen in many cultures, they are characterised by different colours and shapes. Glass is a material that has been used since ancient times.

70000071.name: Broken Glass
70000071.description: A fragment of an ancient glass vessel. Glass had varying colours and transparencies, depending on the technology of the cultures who created it.

70000072.name: Glassy Fragments
70000072.description: Pieces of broken pottery discovered at Mohenjo-daro that have been melted into something like glass. How could something like that happen?

70000073.name: Marble Statue of Caligula
70000073.description: Marble Statue of ancient Roman Emperor Caligula. Caligula was not his real name. He was the worst or second-worst tyrant in history.

70000074.name: Wooden Coffin
70000074.description: A wooden coffin, used for burials from ancient times. These coffins range from rectangular boxes to some made into intricate human forms.

70000075.name: A Slate in Greek
70000075.description: Stone tablet with Greek characters inscribed upon it. The inscription seems to have been written to last a long time.

70000076.name: The Epic of Gilgamesh
70000076.description: Ancient Mesopotamian epic poem. Said to be the oldest literature in the world. It tells of the adventures of king Gilgamesh and includes the original story of the flood.

70000077.name: Ancient Gold
70000077.description: Ancient money, made from gold and its alloys. Gold has been considered precious since ancient times.

70000078.name: Ancient Silver
70000078.description: Ancient money, made from silver. Normally second in value to gold, in ancient times it was more scarce than gold and valued more highly.

70000079.name: Ancient Gold Bowl
70000079.description: Vessels made from gold or plated with gold. Not for everyday use. Used only for festivals and special occasions.

70000080.name: Ancient Silver Bowl
70000080.description: Bowls made from silver. Not for everyday use. Used only for festivals and special occasions.

70000081.name: Gold Jewellery
70000081.description: Jewellery made from gold. Shape and usage differ depending on culture, which gives clues to the interaction and spread of ancient cultures.

70000082.name: Silver Jewellery
70000082.description: Jewellery made from silver. Not just for ornamentation, there are many charms and amulets and pieces with special purposes.

70000083.name: A Slate in Cuneiform
70000083.description: Stone tablets inscribed with Cuneiform. Cuneiform was used in the central part of ancient Mesopotamia. Probably inscribed on stone tablets to preserve writing for a long time.

70000084.name: A Clay Tablet in Cuneiform
70000084.description: Clay tablets inscribed with Cuneiform. Used in everyday life, large quantities have been excavated. Locations with many gathered in one place were likely libraries.

70000085.name: Statue of King Xerxes I
70000085.description: Xerxes I was king of the Achaemenian Empire. Son of Darius I, he carried out the construction of Persepolis.

70000086.name: The Sceptre of King Khufu
70000086.description: A magnificent sceptre, made with lavish amounts of gold and lapis lazuli. King Khufu was the pharaoh who built Egypt's largest pyramid at Giza.

quests.name: Master of the 7 wonders of the world
Master of the 7 wonders of the world
Master of the 7 wonders of the world
Master of the 7 wonders of the world

70000087.name: Ivory Statue of Khufu
70000087.description: A small ivory statue of King Khufu, builder of the first Pyramid of Giza. No other likenesses of King Khufu have been found.

70000088.name: Claimh Solais
70000088.description: Also known as the Sword of Light, one of the Four Treasures of Celtic myth. Belonging to Nuada, king of the mythical Tuatha De Danann, once drawn from its sheath, no one ever escaped from it.

70000089.name: Cleopatra's Perfume Bottle
70000089.description: Perfume bottle used by Cleopatra VII, said to be the most beautiful woman in the world. Various fragrant oils and extracts were used in ancient Egypt.

70000090.name: Cleopatra's Brooch
70000090.description: Gorgeous brooch used by Cleopatra VII. She particularly liked emeralds, and this brooch contains several large ones.

70000091.name: The Travels of Marco Polo
70000091.description: A book from the end of the thirteenth century recording the stories of Marco Polo, who worked for Kublai Khan. In it appears Jipangu, the country of gold.

quests.name: Investigation of 'The Travels of Marco Polo'

70000092.name: Gae Bulg
70000092.description: Magic lance, awarded to mythical Celtic hero, Cu Chulainn, by Scathach, Queen of the Kingdom of Shadows. After breaking a vow, Cu Chulainn is said to have been killed by this lance.

70000093.name: Celtic Jewellery
70000093.description: Accessories used by Celts. Celtic jewellery used much gold and sported unique writing and designs.

70000094.name: The Travel Bills of Xuanzang
70000094.description: Travel journal of Xuanzang Sancang, Buddhist monk who went from T'ang dynasty China to study in India. Xuanzang brought back 657 Sanskrit scrolls, which he translated.

70000095.name: The Scaly Pottery of Kot Dijian
70000095.description: Pottery painted with fish-scale designs, excavated from ruins throughout the lower Indus valley. Said to be the forerunner of the Indus Civilization.

70000096.name: Ancient Coffee
70000096.description: Coffee was originally produced in Ethiopia and drunk as medicine from ancient times. At the time, the beans were dried, boiled, and drunk.

70000097.name: Ancient Stone
70000097.description: Masonry used in stone structures from ancient civilizations. Some of them are very large and it is a mystery how they were transported and erected.

70000098.name: Ancient Wood
70000098.description: Lumber used in stone structures from ancient civilizations. Easy to work with, lumber was widely used, but because it decomposes it is difficult to make out the original shapes.

70000099.name: Emperor Commodus' Sword
70000099.description: Commodus was the last of the Five Good Emperors and son of Marcus Aurelius. He took part in spectacular gladiatorial contests at the Coliseum.

70000100.name: Painted Brick
70000100.description: Bricks in beautiful colours. Made in many different colours to be put together into patterns on doors and walls.

70000101.name: Anthology of Poetry by Sappho
70000101.description: Anthology of poetry by Sappho, an ancient Greek female poet. There were originally nine volumes, but in the middle ages, they were thought immoral due to the eulogies to beautiful virgins and many disappeared.

70000102.name: Victory of Samothrace
70000102.description: A beautiful winged statue put together with pieces of marble, discovered on the island of Samothrace. The arms and head have been lost, which enhances the beauty of the wings.

70000103.name: Saladin's Sword
70000103.description: Sword of Saladin, founder of the Ayyubid dynasty. Fought with Richard the Lionheart and the forces of the third Crusade. Known for his tolerance towards believers of other religions.

70000104.name: Travels in Asia and Africa
70000104.description: The greatest travel journals of the Islamic world, written by Ibn Battuta. They record his extensive travels in Africa, India, and China.

70000105.name: Ancient Rug
70000105.description: Rugs used in ancient civilizations. Woven with hemp and animal hair.

70000106.name: King Richard I's Armour
70000106.description: Armour of King Richard I, Plantagenet King of England and called Richard the Lionhearted. This was the armour he wore on the third crusade.

70000107.name: Zenobia's Short Sword
70000107.description: Zenobia was the Queen of Palmyra who rebelled against the Roman Empire. At one time she held a large territory, but was defeated by Emperor Aurelian and taken to Rome.

70000108.name: Ancient Human Bone
70000108.description: Human bones excavated from ancient ruins. The condition of these finds allow us certain insights into the conditions of the times.

70000109.name: Scipio's Helmet
70000109.description: The Helmet of Scipio, who fought Carthaginian general Hannibal. Scipio reclaimed the lands that Hannibal had taken, and utterly defeated Hannibal at the Battle of Zama.

quests.name: God of war vs. god of war

70000110.name: Gravestone of a Spartan Soldier
70000110.description: Gravestone put up to lament the Spartan troops annihilated by the Persian army at the Battle of Thermopylae. The Greek forces were only defeated after a local traitor showed the Persians a small path behind the Greek lines.

70000111.name: Saintly King's Armour
70000111.description: Armour of Louis IX, who was known as Saint Louis. Louis IX went on the 7th and 8th crusades, but contracted the bubonic plague in Tunis and died in battle.

quests.name: The king who became a saint

70000112.name: Bronze
70000112.description: Bronze vessels used by ancient civilizations. Bronze was easy to work with, and used by many ancient cultures.

70000113.name: Pieces of Bronze
70000113.description: Ancient pieces of a broken bronze vessel. Bronze was easy to work with, and used from ancient times.

70000114.name: Bronze Armour
70000114.description: Ancient armour made out of bronze. Easy to work with, bronze was used by many ancient cultures, but was soft and not suitable for war.

70000115.name: Introduction to World History
70000115.description: Ibn Khaldun's History of the World. Written in the second half of the 14th century, it investigates the principles governing the rise and fall of dynasties.

70000116.name: Sarcophagus
70000116.description: Stone coffin used to bury the dead. The coffins of important people had intricate reliefs carved into them.

70000117.name: Stone Tools
70000117.description: Prehistoric tools carved out of stone. Thought to have been tied to sticks and made into spears or used as knives.

70000118.name: Egyptian Murals
70000118.description: Murals often seen in ancient Egyptian temples and graveyards. Many of them are beautifully coloured, with sacred texts eulogizing gods or pharaohs.

70000119.name: Marble Statue of Seleucus I
70000119.description: Marble Statue of King Seleucus I, general of Alexander the Great and founder of the Seleucid dynasty of Syrian kings.

70000120.name: Prehistoric Wall Paintings
70000120.description: Prehistoric wall paintings found often in caves and burial mounds. Featuring animals and people, they shed some light on the way of life of that time.

70000121.name: Inlaid Bronze
70000121.description: Bronze vessels with elaborate inlays. Perhaps due to the precious metals, jewels and the high quality of workmanship needed, it is frequently used for royal burial accessories or the furnishings of affluent families.

70000122.name: The Cup of Socrates
70000122.description: Cup used by Socrates when he killed himself in prison by drinking hemlock. Socrates is considered the greatest Greek philosopher. Plato was his disciple.

quests.name: The philosopher and his bad wife

70000123.name: Solomon's Key
70000123.description: Book of magic believed to have been written by King Solomon, of ancient Judah. Said to contain the incantations for summoning the 72 demons.

70000124.name: Traces of a Prehistoric Bonfire
70000124.description: Remains of the use of fire by humans. Fire is the symbol of cultural development, and where you find it, you can guess that humans were active.

70000125.name: Darius I's Helmet
70000125.description: Helmet of Darius I, third Persian king of the Achaemenian Empire. He suppressed the uprisings of neighbouring warlords and built Persia into a great country. He was the king who began the construction of Persepolis.

quests.name: Golden age of the Achaemenid Empire

70000126.name: Darius III's Armour
70000126.description: The armour of Darius III, last Persian king of the Achaemenian Empire. After suffering repeated defeats by Alexander the Great, Darius retreats, but is killed by one of his satraps. His death signaled the fall of Persia.

70000127.name: King Chandragupta's Sword
70000127.description: The sword of Chandragupta II, third king of the Gupta Empire, also known as the Sun of Power. Through military power and strategic marriage, India was almost unified.

70000128.name: Golden Mask of Tutankhamun
70000128.description: A pure gold mask, excavated from the ancient Egyptian tomb of Tutankhamen. It is extravagantly decorated with lapis lazuli and other precious stones. On top of that are bunches of cornflowers.

70000129.name: Mosaic from House of Dionysus
70000129.description: A mosaic discovered inside a building in Pompeii known as the Villa dei Misteri.

quests.name: House of the god of drink
House of the god of drink
House of the god of drink

70000130.name: Iron Armour
70000130.description: Ancient iron armour. In the age of bronze, anyone who could have used hard iron would have been invincible. The only people to have iron smelting, the Hittites, became powerful.

70000131.name: Demetrius I's Armour
70000131.description: Demetrius I was the son of Antigonos I, who came to power after the death of Alexander the Great. He attempted to reunify the divided territories of Alexander's Empire, but was captured and died in captivity.

70000132.name: Knights Templar Armour
70000132.description: The Knights Templar were one of the three great orders of the crusading age. In spite of their great power, in the 14th century, they were suppressed and disbanded. This armour was kept at Edinburgh and is believed to have belonged to the order's leader Moray.

quests.name: Armour of the head of the Templar Knight

70000133.name: Teutonic Knights' Sword
70000133.description: The Teutonic Knights were one of the three great orders of the crusading age. Their crest was a black cross on a white background. They contributed to the conquest of Prussia. They held their own territory.

70000134.name: Ancient Pottery
70000134.description: Pottery baked with natural glaze. As technology developed, various different colours and patterns appeared.

70000135.name: Tughril Beg's Crown
70000135.description: Tughril Beg was the founder of the Turkish Seljuq Dynasty, and the first Sultan. This crown is said to have been given him upon his advancement from an Abbasid Caliph to a Sultan.

70000136.name: The Statue of Dwarapala
70000136.description: A single stone statue that stands in the entrance of the Brihadisvara Temple. Four metres high, and carved from a single rock, it acts as the temple's gatekeeper.

70000137.name: Pottery
70000137.description: Pottery baked from kneaded and shaped clay. It's not very strong, but serves its function and is simple to make, so can be seen widely among ancient civilizations.

70000138.name: Relief of the Emperor Trajan
70000138.description: Emperor Trajan was one of the Five Good Emperors. He brought the Roman Empire to it's greatest territorial size. This relief is said to have been made to commemorate his victory in battle.

quests.name: Relief of the ancient emperor of Rome
Relief of the ancient emperor of Rome
Relief of the ancient emperor of Rome
Relief of the ancient emperor of Rome

70000139.name: Ancient Cart
70000139.description: Made to carry large amounts of luggage at a single time. Used in cultures that had developed the wheel. Civilizations without wheels used rollers.

70000140.name: Ship of Neuf
70000140.description: According to East African legend, Neuf was the first person to build a ship. This type of ship is made from Arabia to East Africa and is still made the same way as in ancient times.

quests.name: An ancient yet highly advanced ship
An ancient yet highly advanced ship
An ancient yet highly advanced ship
An ancient yet highly advanced ship
An ancient yet highly advanced ship

70000141.name: Bronze Statue of Emperor Nerva
70000141.description: A statue of Emperor Nerva, one of the Five Good Emperors. Unrelated by blood to the previous Emperor, Nerva, himself adopted Trajan and makes him his heir. From that time, it became the practice for emperors to adopt talented characters as their heirs.

quests.name: Five wise emperors of ancient Rome

70000142.name: Bronze Statue of Emperor Nero
70000142.description: Nero was a Roman Emperor renowned for his atrocities. He buried every relative who got in his way, but he was very popular with the people for his enthusiasm in the pursuit of pleasure.

70000143.name: Ancient Farming Tool
70000143.description: Tools used for agriculture. There are many different kinds depending upon the culture.

70000144.name: Ancient Harness
70000144.description: Equipment for looking after horses. Until bits, stirrups, and saddles were invented, horses were only used for carrying cargo, ploughing, and pulling chariots.

70000145.name: The Treasure of Batu
70000145.description: Batu Khan was the son of Jochi, the oldest son of Genghis. He led European campaigns to revive the khanate of the Kipchaks. This seems to have been part of Batu's treasure.

70000146.name: Hatshepsut's Brooch
70000146.description: The brooch of Hatshepsut, wife of Thutmose II and the first female pharaoh of ancient Egypt. It is said that she dressed herself as a man while she was Pharaoh.

70000147.name: Marble Statue of Hadrian
70000147.description: Emperor Hadrian was the third of the Five Good Emperors. He built a system of defences and developed Rome.

quests.name: Marble statue of the five wise emperors
Marble statue of the five wise emperors
Marble statue of the five wise emperors
Marble statue of the five wise emperors
Marble statue of the five wise emperors

70000148.name: Papyrus Scrolls
70000148.description: Ancient Egyptian books. Made from beaten, stretched out stalks of papyrus, on it are recorded hieroglyphs, the sacred letters of ancient Egypt.

70000149.name: The Marble Statue of Hannibal
70000149.description: Hannibal was the Carthage general who successfully attacked the Republic of Rome. At one time, he invaded as far as the Italian peninsula but was beaten in the Battle of Zama by Scipio.

70000150.name: Hammurabi's Code of Laws
70000150.description: The body of law implemented by ancient Babylonian king, Hammurabi. It calls for An eye for an eye. This means to give fair punishments.

70000151.name: The Inscriptions of Bisutoun
70000151.description: Giant inscriptions found carved into the cliffs of the Behistun Mountains. They are said to commemorate the battle victories of Darius I of the Achaemenian Empire.

70000152.name: Historiai
70000152.description: A historical record written by the ancient Greek historian Herodotus. Focused largely on the Greco-Persian wars, it assumes a continuous division between Europe and Asia.

70000153.name: The Code of Hittite
70000153.description: The codes of the Hittites. Made up of 200 articles written in wedge-shaped letters.

70000154.name: King Pithana's Crown
70000154.description: King Pithana, along with his son Anitta, plays a primary role in the legends of the Hittites. It is said that he used the power of the gods to gain control of many cities.

70000155.name: Phalanx's Spear
70000155.description: A phalanx was an ancient Greek corps of close-ranked, hoplite infantry. They used long spears and wore armour, helmets and shin protectors, and charged their enemies.

70000156.name: Ancient Grave Burial Items
70000156.description: Various items that were buried with the dead. In ancient civilizations, everyday things, including weapons and ornaments, were buried with the deceased, so that they could be used in the after-life.

70000157.name: The Sceptre of Ptolemy I
70000157.description: Ptolemy I was the successor of Alexander the Great. After the great king died, he became Egyptian Pharaoh, built the Musaeum, and made great contributions to the development of science and learning.

70000158.name: Fragarach
70000158.description: Believed to be the magic sword of the mythical Celtic sun god Lugh. Once drawn from its scabbard, nobody can escape from its blade.

70000159.name: The Treasures of Hulagu
70000159.description: Kublai Khan's younger brother Hulagu invaded the Middle East and revived the Ilkhanate. This treasure was hidden under the instructions of Hulagu.

70000160.name: The Treasures of King Priam
70000160.description: The treasure of the last king of Troy from Greek mythology. A war was caused by Paris, son of King Priam, and Troy was destroyed by the Greeks.

quests.name: Treasure of the kings of Troy
Treasure of the kings of Troy
Treasure of the kings of Troy

70000161.name: Friedrich I's Armour
70000161.description: Friedrich I, called Barbarossa (Red Beard), Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire. He joined the 3rd Crusade, but falls off his horse while crossing a river near Cilicia, and drowns.

70000162.name: Brionac
70000162.description: One of the four treasures of Celtic Mythology. Carried by the sun god Lugh. A spear that shot light, it could bring down five enemies at once. From the sight of him wielding this spear, Lugh was known as Lugh of the Long Arm.

70000163.name: The Lapidary Jewellery
70000163.description: Accessories decorated with a variety of jewels. In ancient civilizations, jewels were believed to have special powers and so were used as talismans.

70000164.name: Bone Tools
70000164.description: Tools made in prehistoric times from bones and animal horns. Bones were not suited to blades, but were good for arrow heads, spears, and needles. They were also used as talismans and accessories.

70000165.name: Merlin's Wand
70000165.description: The wand of Merlin the wizard from Arthurian legend. Merlin raised Arthur and advised him after Arthur became king. He shared the secrets of his magic with the Lady of the Lake and was then captured.

70000166.name: The Laws of Manu
70000166.description: Laws of Hinduism. Comprised of twelve chapters that cover the fundamentals of Brahmanism and Hinduism. They record not only laws but also ceremonies and customs for living.

70000167.name: The Mahabharata
70000167.description: One of the oldest pieces of writing of ancient India. Comprised of a hundred thousand poems, it is an epic work. It tells the tale of the battles of the Bharata, with appearances by gods, the children of gods, and immortal wizards.

70000168.name: Statue of Marcus Aurelius
70000168.description: A bronze statue of Marcus Aurelius, one of the Five Good Emperors of ancient Rome. It is thought to be the oldest equestrian statue in the world. Not only does it have artistic value, but is also important in studying the ancient use of horses.

70000169.name: A Mummy
70000169.description: A body that has been embalmed and wrapped in order to preserve it. Ancient Egypt, in particular, believed in the resurrection of the dead, so these techniques are extremely advanced.

70000170.name: The Venus de Milo
70000170.description: A marble statue of a female excavated in the island of Milos. It is believed to have been displayed with other statues. The soft lines of the full limbs and flowing clothes are beautiful.

70000171.name: The Triad of Menkaure
70000171.description: King Menkaure was the lord of the smallest of the Pyramids of Giza. This stone statue shows Menkaure with a goddess on each side.

70000172.name: The Sceptre of Emperor Justinian
70000172.description: Justinian was an Emperor of the Byzantine Empire. He revived the empire, which had begun to decline. He achieved many things, including an encyclopedia of Roman law, and the building of Saint Sophia's Cathedral.

70000173.name: Parchment Archives
70000173.description: A book written on parchment made from sheep skin. It is stable and lasts for a long time. In the middle ages, books were all copied by hand, so they were incredibly valuable.

70000174.name: Shield of the Knights of St. John
70000174.description: The Knights of St. John, or Knights Hospitaller, were created at the time of the Crusades to look after the injured. The crest is an eight-pointed white cross. Today they continue their work around the Mediterranean.

quests.name: Knights from the time of the Crusades
Knights from the time of the Crusades
Knights from the time of the Crusades
Knights from the time of the Crusades

70000175.name: The Ramayana
70000175.description: An epic work of ancient India, comparable to the Mahabharata. It tells the story of Rama, an incarnation of Vishnu, and his battle with Ravana, a rakshasa who had kidnapped Rama's wife.

quests.name: The story of Rama and Sita

70000176.name: The Mystery Slate
70000176.description: A relatively new European style slate. I got the jade mask! Any bad feelings I had towards you are now cleared. You're a great adventurer! Schlattenwalder."

70000177.name: King Labarna's Sword
70000177.description: Labarna I revived the Hittite Kingdom and unified Anatolia. Through their iron smelting technology, the Hittites built a great nation, but during the time of Labarna, they were still using bronze.

70000178.name: Labrys
70000178.description: A religious symbol of the Cretan civilization that spread through the Aegean sea. A double headed axe with seals carved in various places. The palace of king Minos was known as the Labyrinth.

70000179.name: Ramses II's Headdress
70000179.description: Ramses II was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh who is thought to have built many buildings. Rameses II's tomb was desecrated by grave robbers, so it's unusual to find any of his possessions.

70000180.name: A Runic Stone
70000180.description: A stone inscribed with runes used in Northern Europe at that time. Many record achievements or commemorate deeds. Stones such as these were in common usage at that time.

70000181.name: The Code of Justinian
70000181.description: The laws made by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I. It consisted of the Institutiones, the Digesta, the Codex Constitutionum, and the Novellae. It forms the basis of jurisprudence.

70000182.name: The Rosetta Stone
70000182.description: A stone monument made from basalt, discovered on the banks of the Nile. It is inscribed with ancient Egyptian sacred and civil hieroglyphs and Greek letters. They contain announcements of the enactment of rituals.

70000183.name: Rollo's Helmet
70000183.description: A helmet said to have been used by Rollo, chief of the Vikings. He made frequent attacks on the French coast. To prevent these attacks, the Frankish king made Rollo the duke of Normandy.

70000184.name: Ancient Greek Vase
70000184.description: This is an urn thought to have been made in ancient Greek times. Several scenes from Greek mythology are painted on it.

70000185.name: Shield of Ancient Roman Militia
70000185.description: In ancient Rome, citizens joined the army. Citizens who joined paid for their own equipment and attended training. Equipment were made from bronze.

70000186.name: Gold/Lapis Lazuli Goat
70000186.description: Royal burial items made in ancient Mesopotamia. Gold, lapis lazuli, and shells were attached to a wooden statue. This shows the richness of the time.

70000187.name: The Statue of the Charioteer
70000187.description: A bronze statue of a charioteer found at the ruins of Delphi. This was probably presented to praise the efforts of a charioteer who won at the games. It is an outstanding statue with excellent proportions.

70000188.name: The Book of the Dead
70000188.description: A spell book for the dead, inserted with the body into the coffin in ancient Egyptian funerals. It was thought that if they carried this book, they would be found innocent when judged by Osiris in the afterlife.

70000189.name: The City of the Dead
70000189.description: Also called a Necropolis, it was a vast mass grave. The form and burial rituals were dependent on the culture, but this type of city of the dead can be seen in many different cultures.

70000190.name: Statue of a Celtic God
70000190.description: A statue of a god worshipped in the Celtic culture. Made of bronze, with a large head and small limbs it has a peculiar shape.

70000191.name: The Colonnade
70000191.description: The Hypostyle Hall of the Karnak temple has 134 standing stone pillars, with some all over 10 meters tall and some over 20 meters in height. They were commissioned by the ancient Egyptian pharaoh, Ramses II.

70000192.name: Zulu Jewellery
70000192.description: Accessories from inhabitants of southern Africa. They show intricate patterns made from coloured beads. The name Zulu means people of paradise. They are an extremely brave people.

70000193.name: Silver of Ancient India
70000193.description: Silver coins used in ancient India. Currency in ancient India was mostly silver. In addition to round and square shapes, there were also many-sided shapes, whose sides were shaved to manage the weight.

70000194.name: Ancient Lebanon Cedar
70000194.description: This lumber was used frequently from the Ancient middle east to Persia. It's of high quality and has many uses in the construction of buildings and ships. Because of deforestation, it is rarely seen today.

70000195.name: The Statue of Lamassu
70000195.description: Peculiar stone statues made by the ancient Mesopotamian civilization. Left beside gateways, they are thought to have acted as guards. Frequently in the form of oxen or lions.

70000196.name: The Criosphinx
70000196.description: Sphinxes with sheep's' heads that line the approach to Karnak temple. There are 40. The sheep was the sacred beast of the god Amun, who was worshipped here. Amun was the national god for the whole of Egypt.

70000197.name: Avesta
70000197.description: Zoroastrian scriptures. The originals were burnt by Alexander the Great, but they were later re-compiled and formed the religion of the Sassanid Empire. Zoroastrians, also called Mazdaism, believed in judgment after death and a final judgment.

70000198.name: The Statue of Agni
70000198.description: The god of fire from Indian mythology. With hair like flames, teeth of gold, and a seven-forked tongue, his form represents the origin of fire. He is believed to have the power of purification to remove evil.

70000199.name: The Atharvaveda
70000199.description: One of the holy texts of the Hindu religion. A collection of incantations, it was not originally treated as scripture. With roots in everyday life, the chants range from casting out demons to revitalising the growth of hair and more.

70000200.name: The Statue of Athena
70000200.description: A statue of the Greek goddess Athena, the goddess of industry, art, knowledge, and war. Known as Minerva in Roman theology. Athena was the guardian of the city state of Athens and the Parthenon was her temple.

70000201.name: The Statue of Anubis
70000201.description: The Egyptian god of the dead. He is depicted with the body, or the head of a jackal. Upon death, he measured a person's heart against the feather of Truth, and determined where they would go in the afterlife.

70000202.name: The Statue of Aphrodite
70000202.description: A statue of the Greek goddess of love and beauty. Known as Venus in Roman mythology. According to Greek mythology, the Trojan wars began as a result of a quarrel between Aphrodite, Athena, and Hera.

70000203.name: The Statue of Apollo
70000203.description: A statue of the Greek god Apollo. Apollo frequently made predictions from his oracle in Delphi. He was a beautiful god, who excelled at music, archery, and sports. He is often merged with Helios, god of the sun.

70000204.name: The Statue of Artemis
70000204.description: A statue of the Greek goddess Artemis, Apollo's twin sister. Known in Roman mythology as Diana. Artemis was the goddess of hunting and animals, childbirth, and abundant harvests. She is often merged with Selene, goddess of the moon.

70000205.name: The Statue of Ares
70000205.description: A statue of the Greek god of war Ares. Known in Roman mythology as Mars. He had several children with his lover Aphrodite, the goddess of beauty and love.

quests.name: Statue of the god of war
Statue of the god of war
Statue of the god of war

70000206.name: The Statue of Amma
70000206.description: A statue of the single god of the Dogon people who lived south of the Sahara. Amma created the stars, the sun, and the moon. Then he created the Earth and mixed in himself to make the spirits.

70000207.name: The Statue of Isis
70000207.description: A statue of the Egyptian goddess Isis, goddess of abundant harvests and motherhood. Also known as the Earth Mother. Married to her brother Osiris, she gave birth to the sky god Horus. When Osiris was killed by Set, she aided Horus in defeating Set.

70000208.name: Coronation Stone
70000208.description: Also known as the stone of destiny or the Lia Fail. It is said to have called out when touched by the true king. The mythical King Arthur drew his sword from a stone and became King. Some say that this is the stone it was drawn from.

70000209.name: The Statue of Indra
70000209.description: A statue of Indra, the most famous god in ancient Indian myth. A god of war, he used thunder and storms to defeat Vritra, the jet black evil dragon. For Hindus, Indra is ranked just below the three great gods.

70000210.name: Vajra
70000210.description: Weapon of the Hindu god Indra. It was made from the bones of the sage Dadhichi to slay the Asura Vritra, who was in the form of a great serpent.

quests.name: Weapon that pierced a demon god

70000211.name: The Statue of Vishnu
70000211.description: A statue of Vishnu, one of the three great gods of Indian theology. Though he is said to have 10 avatars, he is usually portrayed as a man with four arms. When the balance of the world is disrupted, it is said that he appears in the world in many different forms.

70000212.name: The Statue of Ushas
70000212.description: A statue of the ancient Indian goddess Ushas. She is the goddess of the dawn, with deep crimson clothes and a golden veil. She is said to be the most beautiful of all in the Rigveda and was the wife of the sun god Surya.

70000213.name: Statue of Unkulunkulu
70000213.description: A statue of Unkulunkulu, the sky god of the Zulu of southern Africa. In the Zulu language, his name means ancestor. When people became mortal, he allowed them to have children and gave them fire.

70000214.name: The Statue of Eshu
70000214.description: A statue of Eshu, a god of the Yoruba people of Africa. The god of lunar and solar eclipse, and many other things.

70000215.name: The Statue of Osiris
70000215.description: A statue of Osiris, the ancient Egyptian god of death and rebirth. Osiris was killed by his brother Set, who was then defeated by Osiris' wife Isis and his son Horus. Later Osiris became the king of the underworld.

70000216.name: The Statue of Oduduwa
70000216.description: A statue of Oduduwa, a god of the Yoruba people of Africa. Olorun, the highest god in the Indian pantheon, merged with the sea and gave birth to Oduduwa. Oduduwa is said to have created land and people.

70000217.name: Statue of Onyankopon
70000217.description: A statue of Onyankopon, a god of the Ashanti people of West Africa. The creator of all things. Originally he lived on the earth, but is said to have later lived in the heavens.

70000218.name: Hermes of Olympia
70000218.description: The Statue of Hermes from the Hera temple at Olympia. He is holding the baby Dionysus. Made by Praxiteles, the greatest sculptor of the time.

70000219.name: The Statue of Olorun
70000219.description: A statue of Olorun, the greatest god of the Yoruba people of Africa. Said to rule over 401 gods. In the beginning, the world was only sea, and Olorun merged with the sea to create Oduduwa and Obatala, whom he then made to create land and people.

70000220.name: The Statue of Kali
70000220.description: A statue of the Indian goddess Kali, a wife of Shiva, who is one of the three great gods. She is portrayed with black skin and a necklace of skulls. She is the goddess of slaughter and destruction.

70000221.name: The Statue of Ganesha
70000221.description: A statue of the Indian god Ganesha, the child of Shiva and Parvati, who had the head of an elephant. Since he is the master of luck, fortune, and learning, he is very popular as the god of trade.

quests.name: God with the head of a bull

70000222.name: The Theogony
70000222.description: Written by Hesiod, it describes the genealogies of the gods of Greek mythology. It describes the world being born from chaos, the birth of the gods, and the adventures of the heroes. For the first time, many of the Greek myths were brought together.

70000223.name: Gold Scarab
70000223.description: The scarab beetle is a type of dung beetle that rolls animal excrement into balls and lays eggs in them. In ancient Egypt, this practice called to mind the movement of the sun, causing them to treat the scarab as sacred. They were used for talismans.

70000224.name: The Statue of Krishna
70000224.description: A statue of Krishna, said to be the 8th incarnation of the Indian god Vishnu. He appears in the epic poem the Mahabharata and acts as an advisor to the 5 Pandava princes. He appears in many other myths, as well.

70000225.name: Goliath's Sword
70000225.description: Goliath appears in the Old Testament as a Philistine warrior. When the Philistines invaded Israel, a young shepherd called David hurled a stone at Goliath and knocked him down; he then took his sword and finished him off.

70000226.name: The Sama Veda
70000226.description: One of the holy texts of the Hindu religion. Like the Rigveda, it is a collection of eulogies to the gods, with melodies for Udgatar priests to sing at sacrifices.

70000227.name: Ancient Altar
70000227.description: An altar used for religious sacrifices. Depending on the culture and religion, there are many different kinds.

70000228.name: Festival Mask
70000228.description: A mask used for religious festivals. It's probably for the sake of dignity, but it has a strange expression. It is beautifully decorated with birds' feathers and coloured stones.

quests.name: Rumours of a mask from Ceuta

70000229.name: Sarasvati Statue
70000229.description: A statue of the Indian goddess Sarasvati, one of three great deities and the goddess of creation. She is the wife of Brahma and the most important female deity.

70000230.name: The Statue of Shiva
70000230.description: A statue of the Indian god Shiva, one of the three major deities and god of destruction, rebirth, and dancing. There are many myths surrounding Shiva and his many wives.

quests.name: Statue of the god of destruction
Statue of the god of destruction

70000231.name: The Statue of Surya
70000231.description: A statue of the Indian sun god Surya. His wife is Ushas, goddess of the dawn. It is said that because his whole body shines with light, when he appears in the morning, the eyes of Ushas are dazzled and she hides herself.

70000232.name: The Statue of Zeus
70000232.description: A statue of Zeus, the greatest Greek god. Known as Jupiter in Roman mythology. The god of the sky, he controls lightning. However, his amorous nature causes him to make advances towards one human woman after another. His temple at Olympia is well known.

quests.name: Statue of the greatest Greek God
Statue of the greatest Greek God
Statue of the greatest Greek God
Statue of the greatest Greek God
Statue of the greatest Greek God

70000233.name: The Statue of Zoco
70000233.description: A statue of Zoco, the creator deity from the mythology of the Nupe people of the Guinea coast of Western Africa. Many different tribes live in this area and have flourished since ancient times. Tribes have influenced each other's mythology, which is of great interest.

70000234.name: The Ark of the Covenant
70000234.description: Believed to be the Ark of the Covenant that appears in the Old Testament. At the bottom are four legs, and on the top surface two cherubs, as is written in the Bible. However the ten commandments, supposed to be inside, are nowhere to be seen and it is impossible to say whether or not it is the real thing.

70000235.name: The Solar Barge
70000235.description: A wooden ship found near King Khufu's pyramid at Giza. It is over forty metres long. It is thought to have been a ceremonial vessel to carry the spirits of the pharaohs to the sun god.

70000236.name: The Pillars of Dharma
70000236.description: In the ancient Indian Sanskrit language, Dharma means law. It includes the laws of the universe and truth, and is seen as the fundamental concept of Buddhism. This stone pillar was erected in the territory of King Ashoka, a devotee of Buddhism.

70000237.name: The Statue of Nyame
70000237.description: A statue of Nyame, the supreme god, worshipped in West Africa. Worshipped over a wide area, he has many other names, as well. Nyame first lived on the earth but ascended to the heavens to distance himself from people. There are many similar myths.

70000238.name: The Statue of Bastet
70000238.description: A statue of Bastet, an ancient Egyptian female deity with the form of a cat, or the head of a cat. Because of their ability to catch snakes, cats were highly valued. Eventually they were worshipped as gods. Bastet is the guardian of cats and also the goddess of love.

70000239.name: The Statue of Hades
70000239.description: A statue of Hades, the Greek god of the realm of the dead. Hades ruled the underworld and at the same time he was known as the god of fortune who looked over mining and precious stones.

70000240.name: The Statue of Hanuman
70000240.description: A statue of Hanuman, a monkey god that appears in Indian mythology. Widely worshipped for his role in the Ramayana of helping the main character Rama. Because he has white fur, white furred monkeys in India are protected as the messengers of Hanuman.

70000241.name: Athena in Parthenon
70000241.description: A part of the statue of Athena that once stood in the Parthenon Temple. Said to have been a wooden statue over ten metres tall covered in ivory for skin, lavishly dressed in clothes and accessories of gold. When the Ottomans invaded, it was thought to have been taken apart and sold.

70000242.name: Voodoo Altar
70000242.description: Voodoo is a new religion made from a combination of African religions and Christianity. This altar is used to call a spirit or Loa. Candles and needles are used in the rituals.

quests.name: Fusion of religions along the Atlantic
Fusion of religions along the Atlantic
Fusion of religions along the Atlantic
Fusion of religions along the Atlantic

70000243.name: Buddhist Sutras
70000243.description: Books containing the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama Buddha. Of these sacred scriptures, the Sutta Nipata is said to be the oldest and closest to his original words. Over time many sects have emerged and there are many versions existing.

70000244.name: Buddhist Relics
70000244.description: Said to be the ashes of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism. The holiest of holies in the Buddhist religion. The word is derived from the sanskrit word for body.

70000245.name: The Image of Buddha
70000245.description: A statue showing the many forms of the Buddha worshipped by Buddhists. The Buddha is a model of attaining enlightenment so the clothes are simple. There are thirty two Dharmachakras on the hands and feet.

70000246.name: The Statue of Brahma
70000246.description: A statue of Brahma, the greatest god in the Hindu religion. Brahma is the god of creation and one of the three major deities. However, Brahma does not seem to be as publicly worshipped as Shiva and Vishnu.

70000247.name: The Statue of Hestia
70000247.description: A Statue of Hestia, the Greek goddess of the hearth. She is the older sister of Zeus and widely worshipped in ancient Greece. Known as Vesta in Roman mythology.

70000248.name: The Statue of Hephaestus
70000248.description: A statue of the Greek god of fire and blacksmiths. Said to have an unsightly appearance, his wife was the most beautiful goddess of all, Aphrodite. His workshop is thought to have been underground on the Island of Sicily.

70000249.name: The Statue of Hera
70000249.description: A statue of the Greek goddess Hera. Hera was the wife of Zeus and the goddess of marriage. Known as Juno in Roman mythology. Known for her jealousy, there are many stories of her persecuting Zeus's many lovers and children.

quests.name: Statue of an ancient Greek god
Statue of an ancient Greek god
Statue of an ancient Greek god
Statue of an ancient Greek god
Statue of an ancient Greek god

70000250.name: The Statue of Hermes
70000250.description: A statue of the Greek god Hermes. Known as Mercurius or Mercury in Roman mythology. The guardian of merchants and shepherds on one hand, and on the other, the god of thieves.

70000251.name: The Statue of Bodhisattva
70000251.description: A Buddhist statue. Bodhisattva was originally used to refer to the pre-enlightenment Buddha. However, the interpretation changed and it now refers to those near enlightenment, who choose to not yet become a Buddha.

70000252.name: The Statue of Poseidon
70000252.description: A statue of the Greek god of the sea. Poseidon had many lovers and his children included many brutal monsters like Polyphemos. The notorious Medusa was also one of Poseidon's lovers and their child was Pegasus.

quests.name: Statue of the god of the sea
Statue of the god of the sea
Statue of the god of the sea
Statue of the god of the sea
Statue of the god of the sea

70000253.name: The Statue of Horus
70000253.description: A statue of the Egyptian god Horus. Horus was the son of Osiris and Isis and god of the sky. With the help of his mother, he avenged the murder of his father by his uncle Set. He is represented in the form of a falcon, or with the head of a falcon.

70000254.name: The Sanskrit Scroll
70000254.description: A scroll written in Sanskrit characters. The characters were originally used in general for the Sanskrit language, but over time, they began to be used more for religious writings.

70000255.name: The Clothes of the Virgin Mary
70000255.description: A scrap of clothing said to have once been worn by the virgin Mary. It is dyed red like in the painting. It's authenticity is unclear.

70000256.name: The Yajur Veda
70000256.description: One of the holy texts of the Hindu religion. It is a collection of sacred verses called Yajus. It is used by Adhvaryu priests who oversee religious rituals.

70000257.name: Yoruba Priest's Mask
70000257.description: A mask of the Yoruba people who prosper in the central region of Western Africa. This belongs to a high priest who acts as an oracle. The Yoruba excel in woodwork and bronze work and this mask demonstrates some exquisite craftwork.

70000258.name: Eye of Ra
70000258.description: A giant charm found in some Egyptian ruins. It points to the eyes of Ra, the god of the sun, but some say it refers to the goddess Sekhmet.

70000259.name: The Statue of Lakshmi
70000259.description: A statue of the Indian goddess Lakshmi, goddess of happiness and fortune and Queen to the god Vishnu.

70000260.name: The Rigveda
70000260.description: One of the holy texts of the Hindu religion. It is a collection of eulogies to the gods which the Hotr priests would chant at religious festivals to invite the gods.

70000261.name: The Spear of Longinus
70000261.description: The spear that was used to stab Jesus to make sure that he was dead after he was crucified on the hill of Golgotha. The name of the soldier who used it was Longinus. There's no way of proving whether this was the real thing.

70000262.name: The Statue of Ngewo
70000262.description: A statue of Ngewo, a god of the Mende people of Sierra Leone in Africa. Ngewo is god of the sky, and the Earth is his wife. Apparently he used to live near people, but later moved away from them.

quests.name: The god who returned to heaven

70000263.name: The Dead Sea Scrolls
70000263.description: A large deposit of copies of the religious manuscripts of the Old Testament. Thought to have belonged to a Judaic sect known as Qumran. A very early version of the Bible, its value to theologians is inestimable.

70000264.name: The Holy Cross
70000264.description: A part of the cross upon which Jesus was crucified. There are many legends concerning the holy cross, including one that says it was made from the tree of original sin which grew from Adam's grave.

70000265.name: The Arnolfini Wedding
70000265.description: Painted by Jan van Eyck. Thought to be a painting certifying the marriage of a banker and his wife. The painting includes many religious symbols and certainly conveys prayers for a happy married life. Starting with the convex mirror in the middle and the chandelier, the brushwork is almost impossibly detailed.

70000266.name: Ciborium of Mr. Alpais
70000266.description: A religious vessel made by craftsman G. Alpais of Limoges in the Limousin region of France. It was buried in the tomb of the Abbot of Montmajour Abbey but was so beautiful that it was taken to the church in Marseille.

quests.name: Grave burial items of the Abbot

70000267.name: Icon
70000267.description: An icon used for worship in the Orthodox Church. It depicts holy saints and important religious scenes.

70000268.name: The Birth of Venus
70000268.description: A fresco by Botticelli. It depicts the birth from the sea of Venus, known as Aphrodite in Greek mythology. To the left is Zephyros and Flora, and to the right one of the Horae, goddesses of the seasons.

70000269.name: The Woman with a Veil
70000269.description: A portrait of a woman by Raphael. Said to have been Raphael's lover wearing a noble's wedding dress. Raphael was very busy and frequently enlisted the aid of his pupils, but he is believed to have painted this one on his own.

quests.name: Portrait of woman in a veil
Portrait of woman in a veil
Portrait of woman in a veil
Portrait of woman in a veil

70000270.name: St. Etienne in Jerusalem
70000270.description: Painted by Vittore Carpaccio. Full title is La Predication de saint Etienne a Jerusalem. One of six works chronicling the life of Saint Etiene. The scene is Jerusalem with exotic vivid clothes and characterised by beautiful stone buildings.

70000271.name: Diane Chasseresse
70000271.description: Painting by an unknown artist. Depicts Diana from Roman mythology departing on a hunt with her dog. Noted for the soft, natural beauty of nudity. The model was said to have been a favored concubine of the King of France.

quests.name: Nude art with a mythical theme

70000272.name: The Virgin of the Rocks
70000272.description: A painting by Leonardo Da Vinci. Painted at the request of a church in Milan but a price could not be agreed upon, so the original was never handed over. In the painting are the Virgin, Saint John, and an angel.

70000273.name: The Virgin of the Rocks
70000273.description: A painting by Leonardo Da Vinci. A price could not be agreed upon with the church in Milan that commissioned the piece, so this copy was painted to meet the lower price. One of Leonardo's pupils aided with this painting.

70000274.name: Tapestry of the Old Testament
70000274.description: One of a series of tapestries based on the work Moses Saved from the Waters by Simon Vouet. Taken from the Old Testament, there are eight works in all. It is a gorgeous and extravagant Gobelin tapestry.

70000275.name: Decorated Goblet
70000275.description: A goblet decorated with allegoric procession. Made in a craft shop in Venice from lapis lazuli blue glass and enamel. Venice is rich in glass enameling technology. A piece like this could only be made in Venice.

70000276.name: Descent from the Cross
70000276.description: Part of an altarpiece by Rubens. The scene of the Virgin Mary and her friends taking Jesus down from the cross after his crucifixion. The exaggerated flesh and poses and the dramatic use of light set this apart from all previous paintings.

quests.name: Artist to the king and the king of artists

70000277.name: The Resurrection of Christ
70000277.description: A marble sculpture by Germain Pilon. It shows the crucified Christ after the resurrection. It was supposed to be combined with other sculptures, but it went unfinished.

70000278.name: The Raising of the Cross
70000278.description: An altar piece by Rubens. The scene of the elevation of the cross where Jesus is to be nailed. With the rippling muscles and floating white flesh of Christ's body, this expression departs from previous religious works.

70000279.name: The Crucifixion of Christ
70000279.description: El Greco's painting. The picture shows Jesus suspended from the cross and is composed with symmetry to the left and right with Christ's white body twisted so that he faces the sky. Because it ignored the religious symbolism of the time such as halos, it was not officially recognized at first.

quests.name: A different take on religious art
A different take on religious art

70000280.name: Fruit Basket
70000280.description: A painting of a basket of fruit by Caravaggio. The lack of a human figure in the painting was unusual. With the realism of the less-than-perfect fruit and wilting leaves, it has a charm previously unseen.

70000281.name: Description of Greece
70000281.description: A guide to ancient Greece written by Pausanias. He recorded in detail the places he actually walked through and saw. The study of ancient Greece could progress thanks to this work.

70000282.name: Deianeira Abducted by Nessus
70000282.description: One piece from a series on the Labours of Hercules by Guido Reni. The scene where Hercules' wife Dejanira was taken away by a Centaur called Nessus. It is a work with an exceptional sense of movement.

70000283.name: Golgotha (Mount Calvary)
70000283.description: An altar piece by Andrea Mantegna. A painting of Christ being nailed up on Golgotha with almost perfect perspective. Also valued for the fine detail in the clothes, weapons, and harnesses.

70000284.name: The Last Judgement
70000284.description: A ceiling painting by Giorgio Vasari. Christ's last supper is graphically depicted. Vasari is known not only as a painter, but as a writer as well.

70000285.name: The Last Judgement
70000285.description: A fresco by Michelangelo. It is a vast and impressive work of art. It depicts the last supper. In the centre is Jesus, those who follow him are to his left, ascending to heaven, and those pronounced sinful are to the right descending to hell.

70000286.name: The Last Supper
70000286.description: A work by Leonardo da Vinci. Because of the perspective used to draw the inside of the building, it appears to have great depth. Compared to the disciples, Jesus is painted simply, perhaps because he was serene, or perhaps because the work was unfinished.

70000287.name: Paradise Lost
70000287.description: Fresco by Masaccio. Full title is The Expulsion from the Garden of Eden. One of several works by different artists displayed on the walls of Brancacci Chapel. Through his lines of perspective, Masaccio brought to life his paintings in a way previously unseen.

70000288.name: The Annunciation
70000288.description: An altar piece by Simone Martini. Said to have been part of a large scale work comprised of multiple pictures. For religious paintings of its time, the people have rich facial expressions, making many believe this was the advent of a new age.

70000289.name: The Annunciation
70000289.description: A painting by Leonardo Da Vinci. Painted using perspective but there are places where it goes astray, such as Mary's right hand. This may have been deliberate. The flowers on the ground are drawn in great detail, and the angel's wings show anatomical research into birds' feathers.

70000290.name: The Annunciation
70000290.description: An altarpiece by Fra Angelico. Painted with vivid hues, this painting shows the artist's devout piety. Angelico was a nickname showing that this peaceful monk was like an angel.

70000291.name: Annunciation of the Virgin Mary
70000291.description: A coloured marble statue of Mary receiving the annunciation by Riemenschneider. With a charm different from that of other statues of Mary common in Italy, it's tidy beauty is memorable.

70000292.name: Victory
70000292.description: A marble sculpture by Michelangelo. One of the statues made for Julius II but was never finished. It shows the twisting body of a young man holding down that of an old man.

70000293.name: Tapestry of the History of Scipio
70000293.description: One of a series of tapestries woven based on a piece by Giulio Romano. It shows a scene from the ancient Roman Punic Wars, following Scipio's achievements.

70000294.name: The Virgin and Child with St Anne
70000294.description: A painting by Leonardo Da Vinci. Mary is sitting on St. Anne's knee reaching out to hold the baby Jesus. Anne is Mary's mother but here they are painted at the same age. This painting appears to be unfinished.

70000295.name: The Holy Family
70000295.description: A painting by Michelangelo. Compared to the works of other artists, the flesh and clothes seem three dimensional, possibly due to his expertise as a sculptor. The less than sacred appearance of Mary is thought to be the influence of the religious group Michelangelo was affiliated with at the time.

70000296.name: Martyrdom of St Denis
70000296.description: An altar piece by Henri Bellechose. It's full name is the Last Communion and Martyrdom of Saint Denis. At the time, it was the fashion to paint vivid colours in gold, and this follows that style.

70000297.name: St. Jerome and the Lion
70000297.description: A bronze statue by Bartolomeo Bellano. The scene of Saint Jerome taking a thorn from a lion's foot. Bronze sculptures were usually cast from molds, so copies could be made, However, this used a wax, but this one was made using a lost-wax method, so there is only one.

quests.name: Bronze statue of saint and beast

70000298.name: The Madonna and Child
70000298.description: A linden statue by an unknown artist of the Madonna and Child. Recorded to have once been in a church in Western Germany. The virgin is treading on a new moon, thought to refer to the Book of Revelation a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet.

70000299.name: Mary, Child with St. John
70000299.description: A painting by Raphael. It's real name is Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist, but is known as la Belle Jardiniere for the beautiful garden painted as the background. The soft brushwork makes this a masterpiece.

70000300.name: Madonna & Child with Angels
70000300.description: A painting of the Holy Mother, her child, and two angels, by Fra Filippo Lippi. Great importance was placed on the symbolism and form of religious art, but he painted works with realistic characters. The model for the Virgin is said to have been his own wife.

quests.name: Forerunner of the paintings of a beautiful women

70000301.name: Mary, Child, Young John
70000301.description: A painting by Raphael. It differs from Raphael's previous works on the Virgin, in that in this one she is bursting with life. There is a rumour that the model was his lover, Margherita.

70000302.name: The Coronation of the Virgin
70000302.description: An altarpiece by Fra Filippo Lippi. He created expressive pieces with unique colours the likes of which had never been seen before. He had a major influence on many renowned painters such as Botticelli and Da Vinci.

70000303.name: The Coronation of the Virgin
70000303.description: Part of an altarpiece by Fra Angelico. His name means angelic, and it was used to describe him after his death. He was a very pious monk, who created many wall paintings and altarpieces. The perspective style he used was considered at the forefront of the techniques of the day.

70000304.name: St. Mary of the Friars
70000304.description: A huge altarpiece by Tiziano. It appears Maria is being drawn towards heaven and is depicted here as full of life; this is quite different to images of the Holy Mother painted up to then. Tiziano's greatest achievements began with this painting.

70000305.name: St. John the Baptist
70000305.description: A painting of John the Baptist by Leonardo Da Vinci. It is thought that pointing towards heaven is an allusion to salvation through baptism. He has a mysterious and enigmatic smile.

70000306.name: The Ivory Ark
70000306.description: The sculptor is unknown, and the ivory tabernacle stands at around 30 cm in height. It is possible that it was made for worshipping at home. The right and left boards can be folded in. The Virgin and Child in the centre are embossed carvings, rather than full sculptures.

70000307.name: The Ivory Pipe
70000307.description: An ivory whistle made in Africa. A simple but unusual sculpture, that makes use of the original beautiful curves of the ivory. It is thought this was for practical use and not for decoration.

70000308.name: The Book of Genesis
70000308.description: A magnificent ceiling painting by Michelangelo. It completely covers the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. The main theme is taken from the Book of Genesis from the Old Testament, and famous stories such as the creation of Adam, the expulsion from the garden of Eden, and the great flood are drawn with dynamism and a wonderful touch.

70000309.name: The Statue of David
70000309.description: A marble statue by Michelangelo. A huge statue that stands at over 4m in height. This depicts David, just before he slayed Goliath. The joints, muscles, blood vessels, and so on are vividly realized and you get the impression that he could spring to life at any moment.

70000310.name: Fame Riding Pegasus
70000310.description: A huge marble statue that stands at over 3m in height. Depicting the figure of a goddess playing a trumpet sitting astride Pegasus. It was created to decorate the water place in the palace.

quests.name: Marble statue of Pegasus and goddess
Marble statue of Pegasus and goddess

70000311.name: Mercury Riding Pegasus
70000311.description: A huge marble statue and the pair to Fame Riding Pegasus. The Roman god Mercury sits astride Pegasus. Placed with it's pair, the two would make a glorious sight.

70000312.name: The View of Toledo
70000312.description: A landscape by El Greco. Landscape paintings of the time were not valued, but it is clear to all that this is a magnificent painting. This painting was not commissioned, but rather was done of the painter's own volition. It is dark, yet bright, and altogether mysterious.

70000313.name: Portrait of Nicholas Kratzer
70000313.description: A painting by the younger Hans Holbein. The characteristic trait of his paintings is their extreme realism. The subject of the painting is Nicholas, an astronomer to the English Royal palace, and so the tools of astronomy have been included in this portrait.

70000314.name: Allegory of the Trinity
70000314.description: A religious painting by France Floris. A mysterious composition bringing together unrealistic symbols. As with many artists of the Flandre province, the themes incline toward Protestant views.

70000315.name: The Tower of Babel
70000315.description: A painting by Pieter Brueghel (father). This painting depicts the construction of the Tower of Babel. Although not particularly large, the people involved in the construction and their tools are drawn with precision. The tower was in Babylon, but here a European town is used as a model.

quests.name: Painting of the Tower of Babel
