70000618.description: A town located between the Persian Gulf and the Arabian Sea. It has been an important port since ancient times, and has continued to prosper as a centre for trade. It has farm produce unique to the region as well as distributing ore and weaponry.

70000619.name: Machilipatnam
70000619.description: A town located on the east coast of India. It developed as a trade transit point. It distributes an abundant supply of tropical farm produce, as well as unique Indian fabric and textiles.

70000620.name: Massawa
70000620.description: A town in the northeast of Africa. It faces the Red Sea, and is also known as the Pearl of the Red Sea. The region has an ancient history, and there are many relics from early Christianity. It mainly distributes farm produce such as beans and cereals, as well as coffee local to the region.

70000621.name: Madeira
70000621.description: A town on an island southwest of the Iberian Peninsula. It was only discovered recently, and development has begun based around agriculture. Its low latitude and hot-humid climate are ideal for growing sugarcane. It's also a suitable climate for making wine.

70000622.name: Malaga
70000622.description: A town built by Phoenicians, and though the controlling power frequently changes, one that continues to develop. As with other towns in Iberia, its streets are a unity of Islamic and Europe cultures. It produces farm products, as well as saffron, cinnabar, and coral.

70000623.name: Marseille
70000623.description: A town built with the name Massilia during the times of ancient Greece. Merchants of Venice also came here and trade prospered. Since agriculture prospers in the surrounding area, it has a wealth of farm produce.

70000624.name: Mogadishu
70000624.description: A town on the northeast coast of Africa. It has been inhabited since ancient times, but its climate is harsh, making it unsuitable for farming. On the other hand, rearing livestock has been prosperous, and its main trade goods are animal products. It also produces mineral wealth.

70000625.name: Mozambique
70000625.description: A town located on the southeast coast of Africa. It is a good natural harbour and has prospered as a base for trade in east Africa. Farming has prospered and it is a distribution point for numerous produce; it also has an abundance of mining resources.

70000626.name: Mombasa
70000626.description: A town on the east coast of Africa. Since it is located at a central point between Africa, Arabia, and India, it has prospered as a port city since ancient times. Farming is widely cultivated and it distributes a lot of farm produce such as coffee.

70000627.name: Jaffa
70000627.description: A historic town that pre-dates Christianity. An intersection for many cultures, it has much historical significance. It produces crops that grow in dry climates, as well as products with high grade iron manufacturing technology.

70000628.name: Ragusa
70000628.description: A town located on the shore east of the Italian peninsula. Since being built, the town has prospered as a trade port, though the controlling power has changed a number of times. Various types of agriculture have prospered here, making it a distribution point for many farm products.

70000629.name: Las Palmas
70000629.description: A town on an island in the Canary Islands to the south of Madeira. Its warm climate makes it a comfortable place all year round, and it has beautiful scenery. The warm climate is suitable for farming sugarcane, and it seems that coral can be harvested from the surrounding sea.

70000630.name: Riga
70000630.description: A town built by Teutonic Knights in the early 13th century. It faces the Baltic Sea, and is an important trading base for the Russian region. Its important products include various types of minerals and feathers.

70000631.name: Lisbon
70000631.description: An old town built by Phoenicians. It underwent great development while controlled by Islamic forces, and has prospered as an important port. It is said to be the most beautiful town in Western Europe. It manufactures high quality ceramics.

70000632.name: Lubeck
70000632.description: A town known as the Queen of the Hanseatic since it was a major city for the Hanseatic League. Once a flourishing town, recently it has come under competition from cities such as Amsterdam, and it no longer commands its former influence. It does have an abundance of mining resources, and salt is its specialty.

70000633.name: Luanda
70000633.description: A town that only recently developed. Blessed with plenty of deep water and easy transportation, it has become an excellent trade port. An abundant supply of farm produce, lumber, and jewels can be found here.

70000634.name: London
70000634.description: A town built by the Romans and originally known as fortress Londinium. It has prospered since the 11th century, and is now the center of England. It trades a wealth of wool, as well as making remarkable strides in refining technology based on a background of mineral wealth from surrounding towns.

70000635.name: The Dying Gauls
70000635.description: A replica of the bronze statue thought to have been made for Attalus I of the Pergamon Kingdom. Although it is a replica, it is extremely well crafted. It perfectly captures the complex expressions of the Galatians, who frequently invaded the Pergamon Kingdom, upon facing death.

70000636.name: Cape Agulhas
70000636.description: The cape at the southernmost end of Africa. The Cape of Good Hope is dozens of kilometers northwest from here. Wouldn't that normally make this the Cape of Good Hope?

70000637.name: Ascension Island
70000637.description: A small island in the South Atlantic Ocean. A solitary point in the wide ocean, there is 2000km stretching between it and Africa. Because it is so hard to reach with any degree of accuracy, it appears impossible to build a town here.

70000638.name: The Azores Islands
70000638.description: Islands found 1300km to the west of the southwest coast of the Iberian Peninsula. They long remained undiscovered since sailing from the continent was a tricky affair with prior sailing techniques. Its warm weather makes it suitable for year-round farming.

quests.name: In the middle of the Atlantic
In the middle of the Atlantic
In the middle of the Atlantic
In the middle of the Atlantic

70000639.name: Boy Lighting a Candle
70000639.description: By El Greco. A famous picture depicting the peaceful, calm expression of a boy lighting a candle and capturing the moment the flame takes. This was painted before El Greco went to Spain, and so we don't see his characteristic use of subject enlargement.

70000640.name: The Arabian Peninsula
70000640.description: A large peninsula running between the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea. Its natural environment is extremely harsh with most of the land covered by desert. However, many cultures, including Islamic ones, have prospered greatly there.

70000641.name: The Andaman Island
70000641.description: Islands aligned in almost a straight line on the east of the Bay of Bengal. The indigenous people are around 140cm tall, and appear to be primarily hunter gatherers. Details are few though as they avoid contact with outsiders.

70000642.name: The Island of Malta
70000642.description: An island to the south of the Italian peninsula and Sicily. Due to its location between Italy and North Africa, the controlling power has often changed. The island has been inhabited since prehistoric times.

70000643.name: Cape Roca
70000643.description: A cape to the north of Lisbon and the westernmost point of the Iberian Peninsula. After leaving Lisbon, and rounding this cape, you come to Porto.

70000644.name: Cape Verde
70000644.description: The westernmost point of Africa and the landmark for explorations of continental Africa. Vert means Green in Portuguese.

70000645.name: The Cayman Islands
70000645.description: Islands located to the south of Cuba in the Caribbean Sea. It was also called Tortuga island (which means turtle) when first discovered. The islands are quite lovely with many being made up of coral reefs.

70000646.name: The Island of Tenerife
70000646.description: The largest island in the Canary Isles. It's about 100km in length and 50km wide with good, fertile land. However, there is also a volcano named Teide that stands at 3700m in height; a thorough investigation will be needed before starting any settlements.

70000647.name: Cyprus
70000647.description: A huge island in the eastern Mediterranean sea. It is known as Kypros in Greek and Kibris in Turkish. Civilization has prospered here since prehistoric times, and due to its geographic location it has been ruled by various powers.

70000648.name: The Cape of Good Hope
70000648.description: A cape in southern Africa. Due to the extremely rough climate around it, Dias abandoned his attempts at sailing around it. Dias gave it the name the Cape of Storms, but later it was renamed the Cape of Good Hope by the king of Portugal.

quests.name: South tip of Africa
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

quests.name: South tip of Africa
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

quests.name: South tip of Africa
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

quests.name: South tip of Africa
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70000649.name: Cuba Island
70000649.description: An island thought to be the largest in the Caribbean Sea. Development has progressed lately, and it grows crops unique to the Caribbean such as tobacco.

quests.name: The largest island in the Caribbean
The largest island in the Caribbean
The largest island in the Caribbean
The largest island in the Caribbean

70000650.name: The Land of Cockaigne
70000650.description: By Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Renowned for depicting scenes populated by peasants, he became known as Peasant Bruegel. Here we see a priest, soldier, and peasant laying around, with delicious food, doing nothing.

70000651.name: The Island of Cozumel
70000651.description: An island located to the west in the Caribbean Sea. This island has some beautiful coral reefs, and tropical fish can be seen everywhere. The sea is so clear, you can see down to 30m. It is like paradise on earth.

70000652.name: The Comoro Islands
70000652.description: Islands located between the northern tip of Madagascar and Africa. Arabic influence has made steady progress here since the Middle Ages. There are few forests since it is a very hot land with rainy and dry seasons. There are unusual plants and wildlife to be found here.

70000653.name: The Strait of Bonifacio
70000653.description: A strait south of Genoa between the islands of Corsica and Sardinia. When heading from Naples to Barcelona, it may be quicker to pass through this strait.

70000654.name: Costa del Sol
70000654.description: The 300 km of coastline centered on Malaga. In Spanish it means the Sun Coast. Its year-round mild weather makes it an ideal getaway.

quests.name: Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules
Research of the Pillars of Hercules

70000655.name: The Island of San Salvador
70000655.description: An island which on October 12, 1492 became the first port of call in the Caribbean Sea for Spain's Colon. San Salvador is the name Colon gave it, but to the native people it was known as Guanahani.

70000656.name: The Island of Sao Tome
70000656.description: An island in the Gulf of Guinea in central West Africa. The island is near the equator, giving it a tropical, rainforest climate.

70000657.name: The Shetland Islands
70000657.description: Islands to the north of Scotland. The atmosphere gives it the feel of Northern Europe because it was initially under Viking control. They do a lot of sheep herding, using small, long haired sheep dogs.

quests.name: Islands to the north of Britain
Islands to the north of Britain
Islands to the north of Britain

70000658.name: The Island of Jamaica
70000658.description: A big island located to the south of Cuba in the Caribbean Sea. Mainly mountainous, the highlands are remarkably cool. Its complex coastline and deep waters make it suitable for harbours.

70000659.name: The Scandinavian Peninsula
70000659.description: A huge peninsula in the north of the North Sea. Its western shore bears unusual geographical features. It suffers harsh winters due to its cold climate. Numerous forests mean that the lumber industry has prospered. Also purported to have ample mines.

70000660.name: The Island of Ceylon
70000660.description: A comparatively large island to the south of India. Its closeness to the equator gives it a tropical climate. Its bounteous highlands have given birth to a prosperous tea growing industry. The island also has a number of jewel deposits.

70000661.name: The Seychelles Islands
70000661.description: An island chain located between Africa and India made up of more than 100 islands. The islands are quite picturesque with many coral reefs, but can't support human life as half of them have no access to fresh water.

70000662.name: Saint Helena
70000662.description: An island that stands alone in the South Atlantic Ocean to the west of Africa. It is over 2000km from land, a truly solitary island on the wide open sea. However, if a supply port could be built on this island, the Africa sea route would be considerably shorter...

70000663.name: Socotra
70000663.description: An island to the east of Aden. It has an ancient history and holds important military value.

70000664.name: The Chagos Islands
70000664.description: Islands located near the centre of the Indian Ocean about 1600km away from India. Most of these islands are covered by coral reefs. Farming is impossible, making it highly unlikely that anyone could settle here.

quests.name: In the middle of the ocean
In the middle of the ocean

70000665.name: The Pine Islands
70000665.description: Islands running east to west to the north of Cuba. The sea is shallow and filled with beautiful coral; the climate is warm throughout the year. It is said that the beautiful white sands came from the crushed coral.

70000666.name: The Bahamas
70000666.description: A group of over 700 islands located to the north of Cuba in the Caribbean Sea. Only around 50 of those are inhabitable. The North American continent stretches away to the north.

70000667.name: The Bermuda Waters
70000667.description: An area of sea to the west of the North Atlantic. This area is home to around 150 small islands. This area has seen many shipwrecks... people call it the Devil's Sea.

70000668.name: The Isthmus of Corinth
70000668.description: An isthmus of only 7km in width connecting the Balkan Peninsula and the Peloponnese. The region has few flatlands, and what it does have are dry; however, olive farming and livestock rearing have prospered.

70000669.name: The Island of Minorca
70000669.description: An island in the eastern part of the Balearic Islands. The large island in the west is called Majorca. The name is derived from the Spanish for mayor (big) and menor (small). It is a peaceful island with a decent climate.

70000670.name: The Island of Pinos
70000670.description: A fairly large island to the south of western Cuba. Cuba has prospered through ideal farming conditions, but the Isle of Pines is not very well populated.

70000671.name: Zheng He's Logbook
70000671.description: The logbook of Admiral Zheng He from the Ming dynasty. Zheng He set sail on seven occasions, and brought the giraffe from Africa. This is only part of a fragmented logbook, we cannot decipher the complete contents.

70000672.name: Fjord
70000672.description: An intricately complicated coastline found in colder regions. Thought to be created by natural erosion, but by something other than water, as water would leave much gentler patterns. It is likely to have been created by ice.

70000673.name: The Isle of Man
70000673.description: An island in the northern region of the Irish Sea. Due to its mild climate, it has been inhabited since ancient times and there is plenty of arable land. Here you can see tailless cats, unique to the region. The people in this area speak a strange language of Celtic origin.

quests.name: A Small Island West of Britain

70000674.name: Cape Blanc
70000674.description: A cape near Arguin in West Africa. It is said that the fleet of Prince Henrique the Navigator has also been there; a cape of the southern sea, which faces the Atlantic Ocean.

70000675.name: Principe
70000675.description: An uninhabited island off the west coast of Africa. The soil is fertile and very suitable for agriculture. The temperature remains very high throughout the year.

70000676.name: Bona Confidenta
70000676.description: A ship amongst the ambassador fleet dispatched by the Russian emperor, Ivan IV. It sunk in the northwest of the Scandinavian Peninsula

70000677.name: The Island of Bioko
70000677.description: An island right on the equator on the west coast of Africa. The Bubi people live here. It is mountainous and covered with forests, and has a high temperature throughout the year as well as high rainfall.

70000678.name: The Island of Madagascar
70000678.description: A huge island located to the east of South Africa. Mountains there soar to 3000m above sea level and it has a varied climate. Due to its isolation, there are a lot of unusual plants and wildlife.

quests.name: Large island in the Indian Ocean
Large island in the Indian Ocean
Large island in the Indian Ocean
Large island in the Indian Ocean
Large island in the Indian Ocean

70000679.name: The Island of Fuerteventura
70000679.description: An island in the eastern part of the Canary Islands. It is the island closest to Africa. Most of the island is dry, and there is a beautiful white sandy beach called Puerto Blanca in the south.

70000680.name: The Mauritius Islands
70000680.description: An uninhabited island to the east of Madagascar. It is surrounded by coral reefs. The land itself is reasonably fertile, and it seems that farming is possible. The tropical climate and beautiful sea come together to create a paradise.

70000681.name: The Maldives Islands
70000681.description: Islands located around the southwest of India. There are over a 1000 islands ranging north to south. The land is fertile in its own way, and appears to be suitable for growing coconuts and so on.

70000682.name: The Yucatan Peninsula
70000682.description: A large peninsula jutting out towards Cuba. Comprised of limestone rock, it has a tropical climate with goodly amounts of rain and fairly rich soil. it is likely farming is possible. There seems to be a giant structure inland. Is there some colossal power here...?

quests.name: At the end of the Caribbean

70000683.name: The Laccadive Islands
70000683.description: Islands to the west of Southern India. This cluster is made up of about 40 islands, but they are only home to a small number of people. The people there make their livelihoods growing palm trees and fishing.

70000684.name: Long Island
70000684.description: A narrow island to the east of North America. An incredibly large island, close to 200km in length. The people who live there are known as the Algonquians.

70000685.name: The Irish Sea
70000685.description: The sea between Britain and Ireland. Its waters are calm and not so deep.

70000686.name: The Strait of Otranto
70000686.description: A gateway to the Adriatic between the Italian peninsula and the Balkan peninsula. At its narrowest point, it's about 80km wide.

70000687.name: The Arabian Sea
70000687.description: The sea between India and the Arabian Peninsula. It connects the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea and is an important point in trade for India, Arabia, and Africa. A maritime region that has prospered since ancient times, with a multitude of ships passing through.

70000688.name: The Indus River
70000688.description: A large river flowing to the west of India and on into the Arabian Sea. Small ships come and go down stream. It also provides much needed irrigation to the watershed areas. Without this river, a vast stretch of land would likely become a desert.

70000689.name: The Indian Ocean
70000689.description: A vast expanse of sea that touches both India and Africa. It provides a useful trade route from India to Africa. The ocean spreads out to surround the south of India.

70000690.name: The Island of Santorini
70000690.description: A small island to the north-northeast from Candia in Crete. There is a volcano right in the centre, and they say that a large eruption occurred many years ago. Some say that this was the location of the lost civilization of Atlantis.

70000691.name: The Orange River
70000691.description: A large river that flows from east to west in southern Africa. Apparently the watershed contains an abundance of ore deposits, but with a huge waterfall right in the middle, water transportation is very difficult.

maps.name: Unfinished Map
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

maps.name: Unfinished Map
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

maps.name: Unfinished Map
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70000692.name: Caribbean Sea
70000692.description: An area of sea that extends between North America and South America. There are a lot of islands here and the natives live side-by-side with a wealth of nature. Its ecosystem is quite different from Europe, Africa, and India.

70000693.name: The River Ganges
70000693.description: A large river that flows from the east of India into the Bay of Bengal. It is a sacred river to the Hindus. Highly fertile land extends into the watershed. Civilization has been developing here since ancient times.

70000694.name: The Crimea Peninsula
70000694.description: A peninsula projecting into the northern part of the Black Sea. The enclosed sea in the northeast is called the Sea of Azov. The climate of the southern part of the peninsula is warm and comfortable. They say the large outbreak of the Black Death started here in the 14th century.

70000695.name: The Congo River
70000695.description: A large river in Africa. It flows into the Atlantic Ocean. Going by the sheer scale of the river mouth, it would appear to have a considerable catchment area. It may be a promising route for inland explorations, but the harsh climate would make things difficult.

quests.name: Entrance to the Kingdom of Kongo

70000696.name: The Zambezi River
70000696.description: The river in Africa flowing into the Indian Ocean. As most of the areas are accessible by small ship, it is considered as an important means of transportation for the local people. There is a magnificent waterfall called Mosi-oa-Tunya upstream.

quests.name: Fishing spot close to river mouth
Fishing spot close to river mouth

70000697.name: The Bay of Saint Malo
70000697.description: A bay between the Cotentin Peninsula and Brittany. Considering the high latitude it's still relatively warm, and the coast has been known as a getaway since ancient times.

70000698.name: Amun Statue
70000698.description: A god of ancient Egypt. In the form of Amun-Ra, he became the central god of all Egyptian gods. He is also the god of the wind in Thebes, and is worshipped as the head god in the Karnak Temple.

70000699.name: Cape St. Vincent
70000699.description: A cape on the southwest edge of the Iberian Peninsula. It juts out into the Atlantic Ocean, and is often used as a landmark for sailors.

70000700.name: The Tigris River
70000700.description: A large river that flows through Persia and joins the Euphrates. Apparently civilization has prospered in this watershed since ancient times, as many unusual relics have been discovered here. Although its an arid region now, the land may have been more productive a long time ago.

70000701.name: The Island of Ibiza
70000701.description: An island in the western part of the Balearic islands. People have lived here since ancient times, and it has served as a transit point between Africa and Spain. A beautiful island with its blue sky and sea.

quests.name: Investigation at the West of Palma

70000702.name: Cape Land's End
70000702.description: A headland on the southwest of Britain. When at the tip of this long and narrow promontory, all you see in front of you is the rolling sea without land in sight. This is probably where it gets its name.

quests.name: Investigation at the West of Plymouth

70000703.name: The River Danube
70000703.description: A large river that runs through Europe and flows into the Black Sea. Thought to be close to 3000km in length. It has been used for trade and military purposes since ancient times, and a lot of cities have grown up along its banks.

quests.name: River that feeds the Black Sea
River that feeds the Black Sea

70000704.name: The River Nile
70000704.description: A large river flowing through Africa and on into the Mediterranean sea. At the same time every year it causes a catastrophic flood, but through this, fertile soil is brought to the banks of the river. It's extremely long making it almost impossible to pin point the river's source.

70000705.name: Epigraph of Victory
70000705.description: Tablet inscribed as a memorial of victory in battle by Ramses II, a major pharaoh of ancient Egypt. The relic provides a suitable memento of an individual who, beginning with the battle of Kadesh, spent his days in numerous battles.

70000706.name: The River Niger
70000706.description: A large river that flows through the centre of West Africa. It has wide curves. It's possible to sail upstream in a small ship, and it acts as an important traffic route for the area. It is believed that upstream is a city called Timbuktu that has flourished for hundreds of years, but it cannot be reached in an ocean faring ship.

70000707.name: The Hudson River
70000707.description: A large river flowing through the eastern part of North America. Its gentle currents make it suitable for sailing, and is therefore an important traffic route for the region.

70000708.name: The Island of Gotland
70000708.description: The largest island in the Baltic Sea. It is believed that people have lived here since prehistoric times. During the time of the Hanseatic League, it was important for trade. The name means God's island or God's country.

quests.name: Island of the Gods in the Baltic Sea
Island of the Gods in the Baltic Sea

70000709.name: The Gulf of Gascogne
70000709.description: Southeast part of the Bay of Biscay located to the west of France. It touches the borders of both Spain and France.

70000710.name: The Gulf of Finland
70000710.description: A long bay from east to west to the north of Riga. It's very shallow. Given its high latitude, the coastal regions are surprisingly warm.

quests.name: Investigation of bay in the Baltic Sea
Investigation of bay in the Baltic Sea

70000711.name: The Red Sea
70000711.description: An area of sea between the Arabian Peninsula and Africa. It can be found described in a passage from Exodus in the Old Testament. It says that Moses thrust out his staff and the Red Sea parted, allowing the Israelites to cross over.

70000712.name: The Persian Bay
70000712.description: An area of sea between the Arabian Peninsula and Persia. The environment is suitable for producing black-lip pearl oysters, and records show pearls have been harvested here since ancient times. The pearl is still considered to be very valuable.

70000713.name: The Bay of Bengal
70000713.description: A vast bay that stretches to the east of India. Many large rivers including the Ganges flow into here. The coast has many good natural harbours.

70000714.name: The Palk Strait
70000714.description: A strait between Ceylon and India. Because Ceylon has many special products and trade has prospered, this strait sees a lot of ships coming and going.

70000715.name: The Gulf of Bothnia
70000715.description: A vast bay in the northern part of the Baltic Sea. It's long from north to south, and many rivers flow into here. This may explain why the salt concentration is low and why it sometimes freezes in winter.

70000716.name: Great Fisher Bank
70000716.description: A wide shallow spot near the centre of the North Sea. It holds this name because it has provided excellent fishing ground since ancient times.

70000717.name: The Strait of Hormuz
70000717.description: A strait to the southeast of the Persian Gulf. Because this has been a busy strait since ancient times with ships frequently coming and going, a town called Hormuz developed near by.

70000718.name: The Strait of Mandeb
70000718.description: A strait that divides the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. It is only about 25km wide at its narrowest point, due to an island located in the middle. It is an important strait for maritime trade, and a nearby town called Aden has prospered exceedingly.

quests.name: Channel preserving clarity of Red Sea
Channel preserving clarity of Red Sea
Channel preserving clarity of Red Sea

70000719.name: The Euphrates River
70000719.description: A large river flowing through Persia. It flows parallel to the Tigris, and joins it downstream. The name of this river appears several times in the Bible. In the Apocalypse, it is said that the four angels bound in the great river will be set free. When this happens, it is said they will kill a third of mankind...

70000720.name: The Island of Maui
70000720.description: The 2nd largest of the Hawaiian Islands. Two smaller islands merged into a single island over time and formed this island.

70000721.name: North Cape
70000721.description: Also known as Nordkapp. It is a cape on the northern coast of a small island of the Scandinavian peninsula. The cliff is steep, but the view from the top is superb.

70000722.name: Taymyr Peninsula
70000722.description: A large peninsula of the seas of the Far North. There is a mountain range that runs through the peninsula, as well as a river that flows from east to west through its lowlands. Although it is covered in permafrost, there is evidence of past inhabitants.

70000723.name: Cape Chelyuskin
70000723.description: Cape at the northern most tip of the Eurasian Continent. It is an important landmark on the Northeast passage

70000724.name: Bering Strait
70000724.description: The strait that lies between the eastern edge of the Eurasian continent and the western edge of the North American continent. Except in summer, it is always covered in ice floes, and sailing through it is extremely difficult.

quests.name: Investigation: the eastern ridge of the northeastern passage

70000725.name: Wrangel Island
70000725.description: A small island in the Chukchi Sea. Many animals from the far north reside on the island. In summer time, many migrating birds can be seen.

quests.name: Biological survey of the Extreme North

70000726.name: Iceberg
70000726.description: A great tall mass of ice, bigger than most of the ice floes of the Arctic Ocean. Any ship that collides with it will sink.

70000727.name: Chukchi Peninsula
70000727.description: A peninsula facing the Bering Strait. Though a frigid land, there is evidence that people used to live here. Perhaps there are rich resources sleeping under the ice…

70000728.name: Chukchi Mountains
70000728.description: A large mountain range located at the base of the Chukchi Peninsula. There are also other mountain ranges in the area, which makes the whole region peppered with mountains

70000729.name: Greenland Shark
70000729.description: They are large sharks native to the cold waters of the North Atlantic Ocean, stocky and slow swimming. Beside fish, they also prey on seals and similar animals.

70000730.name: Taiga
70000730.description: Boreal forest that covers much of Siberia. Depending on the region, the types of conifers seem to differ, and seen from far away, the colors vary.

70000731.name: Amur Leopard
70000731.description: A large leopard that inhabits the coast of eastern Russia. Its habits are slightly different from other leopards, and Amur leopards do not carry their prey into the trees.

maps.name: The Map of the Beast of the Far North.

70000732.name: Amur Tiger
70000732.description: Large tiger that resides in the coastal region of southern Russia. It preys upon large herbivores of the region. It sometimes preys on bears as well, which makes it one of the fiercest predators.

quests.name: Tiger survey in the wintry region

70000733.name: Polar Bear
70000733.description: A bear whose whole body is covered by white fur that lives in the Arctic circle. It has a smaller head and a longer neck than other bears. Usually they are found on land, but sometimes can be found swimming.

quests.name: The bear of the frozen land

70000734.name: Narwhal
70000734.description: A type of whale that inhabits the Arctic Ocean. Most of the males have a single, long tusk. The fang looks like a horn with a spiral groove.

70000735.name: Ringed Seal
70000735.description: Small seals that reside vastly across the sea ice fields. Their bodies are rounded with black and grey spots on the dorsal side.

70000736.name: Walrus
70000736.description: Large pinniped that forms a large aggregation in the northern coasts. It is hairless and covered with blubber. Characteristic tusks are located on the upper jaw.

quests.name: Biological survey of the Wrangel Island

70000737.name: Siberian Musk Deer
70000737.description: A small deer like animal that secretes musk. Despite not having antlers, it has highly developed canine on its upper jaw.

70000738.name: Micromeryx
70000738.description: Animal thought to be a sub species to the Siberian musk deer. Its ecology is essentially the same as a Siberian musk deer. Rarely seen.

70000739.name: Clione
70000739.description: Marine animal seen in the cold currents. Its body is semi transparent, with visible internal organs. It flutters in the ocean mysteriously. Named after a Greek goddess.

70000740.name: Ladoga Lake
70000740.description: A lake located to the northeast of St. Petersburg that has become an important source of water for the city. The lake is dotted with islands, and some of the bigger ones are inhabited by humans. It freezes over during the winter.

70000741.name: Rurik's Grave
70000741.description: According to the Primary Chronicle, Rurik built the nation that became the foundation for the Russian Empire. He may have once been a Viking. Until his death, he was a ruler for his people.

70000742.name: Heimskringla
70000742.description: Meaning 'the circle of the world'. Saga thought to have been written in the 13th century. According to the saga, there are guardians at all corners of Iceland

70000743.name: Primary Chronicle
70000743.description: A tome that records the history of the Kievan Rus'. It was compiled by Nestor the Chronicler during the 12th century. Many phenomena, such as the origins of the Kievan Rus', and its main religion, are described in it.

quests.name: A tale of years gone by

70000744.name: Laurentian Codex
70000744.description: A collection of chronicles, including the Primary Chronicle, copied by the monk Laurentius. For some unknown reason, some sections are missing.

70000745.name: Hypatian Codex
70000745.description: One of the manuscripts of the Primary Chronicle, compiled in the 15th century. Not only is the original information included, but subsequent history has been added.

70000746.name: Gusli
70000746.description: Traditional string instrument of Russia. Along with the number of strings, its shapes have changed with the progression of time, from wing shape, helmet shape, to box shape. Used by the Russian bards.

70000747.name: Skomorokh's Mask
70000747.description: Artists in Russia are called 'Skomorokh'. They play instruments and sing poetry with this mask on, providing entertainment to people

quests.name: What is left behind by the instructor

70000748.name: Iconostasis
70000748.description: A wall covered by iconography. They are placed in several locations inside the Cathedral. Depending on the location, different pictures are drawn.

70000749.name: Copper Pail
70000749.description: A copper pail that was made around the 12th century. The region of production and year is engraved on it, but its original owner is unknown.

70000750.name: The Aksum Stelae
70000750.description: Remains from the once flourishing Aksumite Empire. There are more than 100 stone pillars with unique styles. From the stone room at the base of the largest one that has yet been found, it is possibly a grave for royalty.

70000751.name: Edinburgh
70000751.description: The heartland of Scotland, located in the northeast of Britain. The first king of Scotland, King Edwin, built the castle in the 7th century. The city's name comes from Edwin and Burgh meaning walled or fortified city.

70000752.name: Faro
70000752.description: A small town located in the south of Lisbon. During the time of the Reconquista, Islamic forces continued to occupy this Portuguese city to the very end. When the King of Portugal finally took control of this town in the 13th century, it marked the end of the Reconquista.

70000753.name: Gijon
70000753.description: A small city to the west of Bordeaux and on the south coast of the Bay of Biscay. Originally it is thought to have been a military base for the ancient Roman army.

70000754.name: Casablanca
70000754.description: A small city located in the northwest of Africa. Previously ruled by the Berber dynasty, it flourished as a trading town. There are no traces left of that era because it was obliterated by the Portuguese in the 15th century.

70000755.name: Montpellier
70000755.description: A small town near Marseille. It has been a university town since ancient times, and is a hot bed for medical research. Nostradamus became a master of medical science at the University of Montpellier.

70000756.name: Calvi
70000756.description: A town in Corsica to the south of Genoa. Corsica has been fought over by various powers since ancient Roman times. This town was built by Genoa.

70000757.name: Cagliari
70000757.description: A town in the south of Sardinia. Geographically attractive to many powers, it has changed rulers one after another, year after year. As a result, it has become a town in which many different cultures coexist.

70000758.name: Sassari
70000758.description: A town located in the north of Sardinia. Just like Cagliari down south, a multitude of cultures coexist here.

70000759.name: Trieste
70000759.description: A town close to Venice. It is located at the furthest point inland in the Adriatic Sea, it has prospered as a port town since ancient Roman times. It is buffeted by the powerful winds known as the Bora during the winter.

70000760.name: Zadar
70000760.description: A town in the suburbs of Venice. Previously it was the capital of Dalmatia. It faces the Adriatic Sea, and has a warm climate.

70000761.name: Ancona
70000761.description: A town located to the south of Venice. It has prospered as a port town since ancient Roman times. It was made a free city by the Pope in the 12th century.

70000762.name: Helder
70000762.description: A small town to the north of Amsterdam. It faces the North Sea, and the fishing industry there has flourished.

70000763.name: Dover
70000763.description: A town located in the southeast of Britain. It faces the Strait of Dover. It was the front line in the war against France, and defensive fortifications were built during the age of the Vikings.

70000764.name: Stained Glass of the Madonna
70000764.description: An old stained glass window depicting the Madonna. It was removed while the church was repaired and placed in storage. The stylistic features have caught the interest of a number of scholars.

70000765.name: Apollo
70000765.description: It has a red, round spot on its rear wings. We're not sure whether its because it looks like the sun, but it's only active when the sun is shining. It lives in dry grasslands in the mountains.

70000766.name: Gharial
70000766.description: This member of the crocodile family has a long thin snout. During mating season, the male will draw together a veritable harem of females. They are not often seen on land, and they mainly feed on fish.

quests.name: Those who dwell on the sacred river

70000767.name: Double Crested Basilisk
70000767.description: It lives in trees lining rivers, and when it feels under threat, it dives into the water to escape. It can sometimes be seen running across the surface of the water with its hind legs. The male has crests on its head, back, and tail.

70000768.name: Helmeted Guinea Fowl
70000768.description: Its predominant features are its spotted wings and bony crest. It has been domesticated and bred for food since ancient times. When wild, it lives in groups in open grasslands in the tropics of Africa.

70000769.name: European Mink
70000769.description: Its hair is dark brown to black, with white stripes on the lips. It is nocturnal, and eats small living things such as birds, mammals, and fish.

70000770.name: Azoth
70000770.description: A mysterious material described in books on alchemy. It was discovered in the burial chambers of the Great Pyramids of Giza. Its history and usage are unclear, but it appears to be an extremely important material in alchemy.

70000771.name: The Philosopher's Stone
70000771.description: An unidentifiable material that Paracelsus refined by using azoth. The creation method is a closely guarded secret. If an alchemist is ever successful in creating this material, they must abandon the results and leave no trace as to how it was created.

70000772.name: The Ring of the Nibelung
70000772.description: A ring made from Rheingold. It is said that the ring will bestow the riches of the world on its owner. It's uncertain whether the ring obtained by the Spanish royal family is real, but there is no doubt that the legend of a beautiful gold ring has been passed down from generation to generation.

70000773.name: Balmung
70000773.description: A sword that legend tells was wielded by the North European hero Siegfried. They say that a hero's glory and a heroic death will be bestowed on the owner. It was discovered in the misty lands at the end of the earth...

70000774.name: Dragon Slayer Crest
70000774.description: A banner bearing the crest of the heroic dragon slayer George, handed down through his descendants. If it is dyed on a sail and raised, it would be a truly heroic sight.

70000775.name: Flute of Light
70000775.description: A treasure handed down through the Egyptian royal family. It is said that if it's played by an expert, it causes confusion in people's minds, and puts an end to fighting. It was discovered in the Temple of Abu Simbel that was built by Ramses II.

70000776.name: Tristan's Sword
70000776.description: A sword thought to belong to the English knight Tristan. It was discovered at the site of his purported grave. Tristan's story is well known because of his tragic love for the Princess Iseult.

70000777.name: The Greek Fire
70000777.description: A flaming liquid used in the Byzantine empire around the 7th century. It is made by mixing sulphur and pine resin with petroleum. Said to burn with an intense flame, the fires cannot be doused by mere water. It is believed that it originally came from the east.

70000778.name: Roland's Olifant
70000778.description: A horn made from the tusk of an elephant that Roland blew prior to his death. It has minute engravings, and is valuable even as a work of art.

70000779.name: Durandal
70000779.description: A fabled sword, decorated with crystal, thought to have been a favourite of the sacred knight Roland. They say the blade can split rock. It has passed through many hands and was finally discovered enshrined in a church in Amsterdam.

70000780.name: The Tears of the Princess
70000780.description: Earrings thought to be burial goods from the time of the Old Kingdom. It was discovered while tracking down a tragic love story from ancient Egypt. The craftsmanship is exquisite, and this would surely be a treasured possession of a very high ranking individual.

70000781.name: Tombstone of Radames & Aida
70000781.description: A stone monument that appears to have been erected to mourn the death of general Radames and the handmaiden Aida from ancient Egypt. They were buried alive together in the foundations of the temple, and their last words were carved on this stone monument.

70000782.name: The Doctor's Oath
70000782.description: A slate bearing an engraving of an oath by the sacred doctor Hippocrates from Greece. It is a noble oath in which one devotes one's life to medicine. It was also owned by the noted doctor Pare who also had a large influence on doctors of that age.

70000783.name: The Treasure of Atlantis
70000783.description: Items that appear to be relics of the legendary civilization of Atlantis. The elaborate craftsmanship is quite exquisite, but above all else is the sparkling ore unlike anything we have seen before.

70000784.name: Aurochs
70000784.description: An animal that appears to be the ancestor of the domesticated cow. It stands 2m at the shoulders and the male can weigh up to 1000kg. To secure pastures for domesticated cows, these beasts were driven off, and now they are only found in a few small regions.

70000785.name: Blaubok
70000785.description: Antelopes with beautiful, blue-gray fur that live on the plains of southern Africa. With their horns, they stand at around 2m in height which is large for an antelope. The peculiar colour of their fur is highly prized, but if they continue to be hunted in this way, they are likely to become extinct.

70000786.name: The Elephant Bird
70000786.description: A huge species of bird that lives on the island of Madagascar. They stand at 3m in height and can weigh over 500kg. They lay their eggs in sandy areas, and the eggs alone can weigh up to 10kg. They rely on the heat of the sun to hatch their eggs. They are hunted for their feathers and meat, and if this continues, they will be hunted to extinction.

70000787.name: Princess Aurore's Tiara
70000787.description: The tiara used by Princess Aurora, the legendary Sleeping Beauty, during her wedding. Carried to England by her descendants, it was lost in the chaos of war. Recent investigations revealed that it had been donated to the English church. It is a wonderful piece of craftsmanship, highly valued for its artistic worth.

70000788.name: Bush Baby
70000788.description: They have big hind legs and can jump several meters. They continually wet their hands with urine in order to hold things firmly. They usually live in small family units.

70000789.name: Indian Giant Squirrel
70000789.description: Its main feature is its fluffy, huge tail that is longer than the length of its body, and it leaps between branches with a graceful, agile motion. Its staple diet is fruit, nuts, and insects. It grips the tree with its hind legs, balances using its tail, and then stoops down to eat.

quests.name: A tail longer than it's body

70000790.name: Ring Tailed Lemur
70000790.description: It has a long tail with a white and black striped pattern. A diurnal animal, it lives in groups of 5 to 30. The entire group will gather together on the branch of a tree, bask beneath the sun, and groom themselves.

70000791.name: Arctic Fox
70000791.description: Its entire body, except for its nose, is covered with thick fur. The fur of the arctic fox comes in two colours; its winter fur is pure white allowing it to disappear in the snow and ice, while the summer fur is gray and half as thick as its winter coat.

70000792.name: Caracal
70000792.description: Its name originates from the Turkish word for black ear, and its prominent features are the black ears with their decorative tufts of hair. They say that these hairs allow it to hear the smallest sound made by its prey. It can jump extremely far, and hunts small birds and so on by beating them to the ground.

70000793.name: Elk
70000793.description: It has a very large body. The male is twice as large as the female. The male has distinctive antlers and uses these to assess comparative strength or fight off outside enemies. For their diet, they prefer to eat tree leaves rather than grasses.

quests.name: The palm of a giant's hand

70000794.name: Red Kite
70000794.description: This bird tends to fly in flocks, low to the ground. Its overlapping feathers are beautiful, looking somewhat like fish scales. It bends its wings in segments and use its tail like a ship's rudder to fly in at an angle to catch their prey.

70000795.name: Egyptian Vulture
70000795.description: They use their large, broad wings to catch upward air currents and stay aloft for hours at a time. Their method of eating is unusual. They use rocks to break the shells of large eggs such as ostrich eggs.

quests.name: A bird with a practical use

70000796.name: African Fish Eagle
70000796.description: This eagle has dark brown and black feathers, a white head and chest and a distinctive yellow beak. It mainly eats fish but has been known to occasionally attack seagulls. It throws its head back and emits a high pitched shriek.

70000797.name: Bee Hummingbird
70000797.description: These are very small birds. They hold their bodies level and seem to hover in midair while using their long beaks to suck nectar. The males can frequently be seen on the lookout protecting their territory.

70000798.name: Cave-like Grave Site
70000798.description: A graveyard built underground. The first of this type of graveyard is believed to be the catacombs in Rome. There have also been some found in Syracuse, and some of the larger ones with their labyrinthine structure make it seem as if they are natural caves.

70000799.name: Lucanus Cantori
70000799.description: A large insect found deep inland in India. It has large scissor-like appendages on its head. It is attracted to light. It has a delicate body and weakens when kept by humans.

70000800.name: Blue Migrant Hawker
70000800.description: This subspecies of hawker dragonfly is found near bodies of water in Europe. It has a large body and sometimes attacks other males to defend it's own territory.

70000801.name: Emperor Scorpion
70000801.description: A large insect with a poisonous stinger on the tip of its tail. Although poisonous, it is not strong enough to kill a man, but can cause some numbness. Its entire body is covered with a hard shell.

70000802.name: Camberwell Beauty
70000802.description: A beautiful butterfly with a rich yellow fringe around its wings and blue next to that. It is so beautiful that it is known as the beautiful woman in some areas.

70000803.name: The Mississippi River
70000803.description: A large river dividing the North American continent. It's name means large river in the language of the indigenous Ojibwa people. To them its currents seemed to flow to the ends of the earth.

quests.name: A river named for its size

70000804.name: Dondra Head
70000804.description: A cape at the southern tip of the island of Ceylon. Islanders rarely venture near it.

70000805.name: Cape Saint Marie
70000805.description: A cape at the southern tip of the island of Madagascar. A giant creature that lives on the island uses the surrounding sand dunes as a place for hatching its eggs.

70000806.name: The Coins of Lydia
70000806.description: These coins are thought to be from the ancient nation of Lydia on the Anatolian peninsula. Thought to be the oldest coins in recorded history.

70000807.name: Stone Arrowheads
70000807.description: From the stone age and of a shape seen in any civilization. Perhaps the same hunting method was used everywhere.

70000808.name: Hittite Peace Talks Document
70000808.description: A document describing the battle of Kadesh between the Hittites and the Egyptians. The document describes the Egyptians and the events leading up to the cease-fire in fine detail. However, the details contained herein differ greatly from the same kind of document found in Egypt.

70000809.name: Egyptian Peace Talks Document
70000809.description: A document written by King Ramses 2 describing the battle against the Hittites at Kadesh. It records that Egypt was winning the battle when they accepted the call for a truce made by the Hittites.

70000810.name: Bronze Decoration
70000810.description: A bronze ornament unearthed on the Anatolian peninsula. Its function is unknown. The Hittites, who flourished on the Anatolian peninsula, would later discover iron forging technology.

70000811.name: Small Gold Box
70000811.description: A box made of pure gold, found in the Vergina ruins. On its surface is carved what is thought to be the Sun crest of Macedonia. It contains bones, thought to be those of someone of nobility.

70000812.name: The Bronze Statue of Poseidon
70000812.description: A bronze statue of Poseidon, said to have stood in Athens in the past. Its intricate details perfectly depict the instant of throwing his spear. The big toe of his left foot, which he is using for balance, is slightly raised, and the heal of his right foot which is set back is raised. It seems as if he could spring to life at any moment.

70000813.name: Thessaloniki's Bracelet
70000813.description: Thought to be the beloved bangle of Thessalonike, the half-sister of Alexander the Great. It is a very luxurious bangle with a sun-like motif.

70000814.name: The Dance Costume of Theodora
70000814.description: A gown which belonged to Theodora, the wife of Justinianus 1, the Byzantian Emperor. Of peasant stock, before becoming the Empress she was a dancer among other things. Justinianus 1 changed the law in order to marry her.

70000815.name: Wheel of Konark
70000815.description: Wheels at the base of the Sun Temple Konark. The entire temple looks like a chariot. It is said that the sun goddess Surya rides this gigantic chariot to the heavens.

70000816.name: Queen's Lyre
70000816.description: A lyre found at the grave of queen Puabi at the tomb of King Ur. The cattle head decoration is adorned with gold. The lavish use of lapis lazuli and shells give testimony to the richness of the time.

70000817.name: The Standard of Ur
70000817.description: A box unearthed from the grave of King Ur. Its purpose is unknown. It is thought to be a part of a military pennant or musical instrument. A war scene is depicted on one side and peace on the other side, and it is adorned with mosaics of shells and Lapis Lazuli.

70000818.name: Cornflowers
70000818.description: A flower that grows in south-eastern Europe. It blooms in a multitude of colours such as blue, white, and peach. It was used to ward off evil in ancient Egypt and well known as a flower with healing powers in Greek mythology.

ornaments.name: Cornflowers with White Urn on Table

70000819.name: Persian Yellow
70000819.description: A yellow rose from the fields of Persia. Its detailed yellow petals overlap one over the other. Its small leaves are fragrant.

quests.name: In pursut of the colour yellow

70000820.name: Clerodendrums
70000820.description: Its beautiful blue petals are thought to be as beautiful as butterflies or nymphs. When it blooms, it appears as if these are overlapping each other.

70000821.name: Bay Laurel
70000821.description: A tree said to be Daphne, a nymph appearing in Greek mythology, who turned herself into a tree in order to escape from the love of Apollo. Its leaves are widely used for cooking and to ward off evil.

70000822.name: Asteriscus
70000822.description: A yellow even-shaped round flower. Its shape is said to look like the sun or a coin.

ornaments.name: Asteriscus with White Jar on Table

70000823.name: Masked Lovebird
70000823.description: Its red beak and white-ringed eyes give it a characteristic appearance. It spends nearly all its active time in pairs. Its main diet is seeds or fruit.

70000824.name: Standard-Winged Nightjar
70000824.description: Long feathers adorn it's wings. It can fly at considerably high altitudes and mainly eats insects.

70000825.name: Crimson Topaz
70000825.description: A bird covered in tiny jewel-like feathers. It appears to hover in the air and drinks nectar.

70000826.name: Paradise Whydah
70000826.description: A bird with a tail as long as its own body. However, the tails of females are about half as long as males.

70000827.name: Eurasian Hoopoe
70000827.description: It's feathers appear to change colour from a dark green or black, depending on the viewing angle. It has a dark red beak and tail with a white spotted pattern. It moves around in groups and mainly eats insects.

70000828.name: Common Kingfisher
70000828.description: It has blue feathers that shine like jewels and a characteristic long, pointy beak. It dives into the water from its perch to swiftly catch fish. It is known to occasionally dive into the water from a motionless airborne position.

70000829.name: The Golden Throne
70000829.description: A golden throne adorned in rich cloth. The backrest contains an engraving thought to be that of the pharaoh and his queen. The two appear to be a happy couple in the carving, each wearing one of a single pair of sandals.

70000830.name: The Jewel of Baal
70000830.description: One of the gems in which it is said King Solomon imprisoned 72 demons. This stone is said to have imprisoned the demon known as Baal. Whether or not this is true is unknown. Upon closer inspection, the gem is scratched and the words sea with shoals are engraved upon it.

70000831.name: The Jewel of Astaroth
70000831.description: One of the gems in which it is said King Solomon imprisoned 72 demons. This stone is said to have imprisoned the demon known as Astaroth. Whether or not this is true is unknown. Upon closer inspection, the gem appears scratched and the word west is engraved upon it.

70000832.name: The Jewel of Asmodeus
70000832.description: One of the gems in which it is said King Solomon imprisoned 72 demons. This stone is said to have imprisoned the demon known as Asmodeus. Whether or not this is true is unknown. Upon closer inspection the stone appears scratched and the word Atlantis is engraved upon it.

70000833.name: The Jewel of Belial
70000833.description: One of the gems in which it is said King Solomon imprisoned 72 demons. This stone is said to have imprisoned the demon known as Belial. Whether or not this is true is unknown. Upon closer inspection, the gem is scratched and the words town in the north of the pine island are engraved upon it.

70000834.name: Springhare
70000834.description: Identifiable by its long, furry tail and large ears. It can easily clear 2m in a single bound. It is nocturnal and digs several nesting holes.

70000835.name: Roan Antelope
70000835.description: Both males and females sport distinctive horns and manes. It thrives in weak brush areas and moves around in groups of one male and several females or groups of several young males.

quests.name: Animal with horns and a mane

70000836.name: African Buffalo
70000836.description: Easily identified by its large body and thick horns. It typically travels in groups of 50, but sometimes several groups can join to form a large group of 2000 or more. The males fight over females or over rank.

70000837.name: Sitatunga
70000837.description: This animal lives in wet areas such as swamps. It can be distinguished by its pointed hooves and long, twisted horn and eats plants in water and on land. While eating, it is known to immerse itself in water up to its shoulders.

70000838.name: The Senegal River
70000838.description: A large river flowing from western Africa to the Atlantic Ocean. The origin of the name of this river, which delivers rich water to dry lands, is thought to be either from the Berber word Sanaja which means river or the Wolof word Sunugal which means my boat.

70000839.name: Serval
70000839.description: The word serval originates from Portuguese and means hunting dog. Its large eyes and long limbs are useful for catching prey such as rabbits and mice in the long field grasses.

70000840.name: Clouded Leopard
70000840.description: Its entire body is covered with a distinctive cloudlike pattern and it has long fangs. It is accustomed to living in trees and normally travels alone.

70000841.name: Fossa
70000841.description: It is the fiercest carnivore living on Madagascar. It typically travels alone and chases or lies in wait for prey both day and night. It is very muscular and is skilled at climbing trees.

70000842.name: Jaguar
70000842.description: Like its name which means kill prey in a single lunge, it is powerful enough to crush its prey with a single bite. Its bite is so powerful that it can rip through a turtle shell and even sometimes catch crocodiles. It is skilled at climbing trees and also a good swimmer. It typically moves about alone.

70000843.name: White Tiger
70000843.description: Except for the black striped areas, it is covered in pure white fur, and has a pink nose and deep blue eyes. It is believed to be a servant of god in India.

70000844.name: Black Lemur
70000844.description: The males have a black coat of fur while the females are red, brown, or grey. They both have long ear feathers. They eat fruits found in trees.

70000845.name: Ruffed Lemur
70000845.description: They have long fur as if they're wearing a collar. There are both black fur and red fur varieties, and they both have a loud cry. They love to eat fruit.

70000846.name: Sifaka
70000846.description: They move on land by kicking with their hind legs. Some think it looks as if they are dancing. They have incredible kicking power and are able to jump 10m between trees. They are most active during the day.

70000847.name: Indri
70000847.description: Their shrieks can be heard kilometres away in the forests of Madagascar. Their cry is thought to be a way of communicating with other members of their species. They eat young leaves, fruit, or flowers.

70000848.name: Rain Frog
70000848.description: They mostly hide in the ground and come out after rainstorms. If chased, they will puff up heir bodies and scurry back underground.

70000849.name: Golden Mantella
70000849.description: They are dressed in bright colouring to warn potential predators that they are poisonous. They are active on land and lay their eggs on land as well.

70000850.name: Carpet Chameleon
70000850.description: Their bodies look like a colourfully woven carpet. They seek out prey with their constantly moving eyes; they move in slowly and swiftly devour them. It is this behaviour that has given them the nickname servant of the devil."

70000851.name: Bremen
70000851.description: A port city located at the mouth of the Wesel River. It flourished in the 9th century as the seat of the archdiocese. It became a member of the Hanseatic League around the 14th century and flourished as a merchant city.

70000852.name: Groningen
70000852.description: A city in the north of the Netherlands. One of a handful of Hanseatic League cities in the Netherlands.

70000853.name: Danzig
70000853.description: A city built around the 10th century. It joined the Hanseatic League as well in the 14th century. With active shipbuilding commerce, it established its position as a shipbuilding city.

70000854.name: Visby
70000854.description: A Hanseatic League city on the island of Gotland floating in the Baltic Sea. Toward the end of the 13th century, it lost a political struggle with Lubeck for control over commerce in the Baltic Sea and became a member of the Hanseatic League.

70000855.name: Benghazi
70000855.description: It has its origins in a city built in ancient Greek times. It is named after a person who contributed to the prosperity of the town.

70000856.name: Odessa
70000856.description: A port city on the Black Sea. It is a trade port for the distribution of many different supplies.

70000857.name: Sevastopol
70000857.description: A port city facing the Black Sea on the Crimean peninsula.

70000858.name: Douala
70000858.description: A port town on the Atlantic Ocean Bay of Guinea. Broad, flat land spreads out from the town, but it is bordered by a mountain range to the northwest.

70000859.name: Benin
70000859.description: A port town in western Africa. It grew as a commerce centre for widespread trade throughout all of west Africa.

70000860.name: Benguela
70000860.description: A southwest African town facing the Atlantic Ocean. Due to nearby ocean currents, the surrounding land is parched and dry.

70000861.name: Natal
70000861.description: A port town on the southern African coast facing the Indian Ocean. Natal means Christmas in Portuguese.

70000862.name: Kilwa
70000862.description: A port town on the Swahili coastline in east Africa. It gradually grew as a temporary stopover for Arabian and Persian tradesman arriving on the seasonal winds.

70000863.name: Malindi
70000863.description: A port city located on the east coast of Africa. It flourished after the 7th century with the arrival of Muslim merchants and ocean commerce.

70000864.name: Socotra
70000864.description: A town located on an island in the Indian Ocean offshore from the Arabian peninsula. Sailors travelling the Indian Ocean frequently stop there.

70000865.name: Jofra
70000865.description: A port town on the Arabian Ocean coast. Heavy rains come with the monsoon season.

70000866.name: Saylac
70000866.description: A port town in the northeast of Africa just opposite the Arabian peninsula. It is located partway from the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea.

70000867.name: Jeddah
70000867.description: A port town on the west coast of the Arabian peninsula facing the Red Sea. It has flourished since ancient times as a gateway town for pilgrims visiting Islamic holy sites.

70000868.name: Portobelo
70000868.description: A port town on the Caribbean sea which serves a role as a relay point for trade with Central and South America. The name Portobelo means beautiful port."

70000869.name: Cayenne
70000869.description: A port town on the northeast coast of South America. The climate is warm and rainy all year round.

70000870.name: Pernambuco
70000870.description: A port town on the eastern coast of South America. It grew as a point for Atlantic Ocean trade.

70000871.name: Laocoon
70000871.description: Laocoon was a priest of Troy who advised against the Trojan Horse. He was attacked by large serpents sent by Athena, who sided with the Greeks, and was killed along with his two children.

quests.name: An Account of the Trojan War

70000872.name: Right Arm of Laocoon
70000872.description: The broken right arm of a statue of Laocoon unearthed in Rome. Laocoon's right arm was supposed to be extended as if reaching for the Heavens, but this arm is bent.

70000873.name: Laocoon
70000873.description: The complete statue of Laocoon unearthed in Rome. The ferocity of divine punishment is evident in his writhing body and pained facial expression.

70000874.name: Sloth Bear
70000874.description: An animal with a heavy-set body and thick, strong limbs. It is covered in long, coarse hair, has long claws and a unique white pattern on its chest. It eats a diet of fruit.

quests.name: A long journey to link dreams

70000875.name: Surinam Toads
70000875.description: An amphibian with a flat body and a triangle-shaped head. The female incubates eggs in a skin layer on her own back. After about two months, the eggs hatch and emerge as small frogs.

70000876.name: The Amazon River
70000876.description: A large river dividing the South American continent. A gigantic forest spreads throughout the basin, forming a paradise of flora and fauna. It is a mysterious realm that appeals to the heart of adventurers everywhere.

70000877.name: Bullring Ticket
70000877.description: An entry ticket once passed out at Valencia to deal with the crowds when the famous bullfighter L'Estocart appeared. They were hastily prepared, but the image of L'Estocart drawn on them made the noble women swoon.

70000878.name: Glass Perfume Bottle
70000878.description: A richly decorated, luxurious glass perfume bottle. The heads of two falcons are carved into its cap. On the bottom is written: Someday, this too must be overcome. The sword is heavy. The heart is broader than the land of Flanders and more gentle.

70000879.name: Main Engel
70000879.description: A guitar used by L'Estocart, who had quit being a popular bullfighter to become the guitarist for Michaela. Its many strings offer a complex tone, but it would seem a difficult instrument for any but the most skilled to play.

70000880.name: Note of Paschal de L'Estocart
70000880.description: Michaela, I will go to my sister's place tomorrow. I will run no further... Michaela, run no further. Your place from now is the land of the Caribbean and the turquoise sea. You can dance by yourself now without my guitar. ...the writing ends here.

70000881.name: El Camino Real
70000881.description: El camino real means royal road in Spanish. Charles V designed the red flamenco costume with Michaela in mind. Perhaps letting this go means that Charles has decided to put aside his past...

70000882.name: Chichen Itza
70000882.description: Ruins of the Mayan civilization that flourished on the Yucatan peninsula. Chichen-Itza apparently means by the spring. The Mayans spread over an extremely wide area. Their towns were centered on the pyramid-shaped temple with other buildings including a sacred spring, warrior's temple, and astronomical observatory.

70000883.name: Palenque
70000883.description: Ancient Mayan ruins shrouded in a thick forest. Beyond a building in the centre which appears to be a palace lies a temple with intricate wall carvings. Much about the Mayans could be learned if these could be deciphered.

sources.name: E Coast of Latin America(Cayenne, Pernambuco, Grand Cayman, Willemstad, Trujillo, and Caracas)

70000885.name: The Sarcophagus of Palenque
70000885.description: A sarcophagus housed in the Temple of Inscriptions in the Palenque ruins. An intricate relief is carved into its lid. It contains an uncountable number of burial items.

70000886.name: The Earring of Queen Cook
70000886.description: The queen Sak K'uk is the mother of the Palenque king K'inich Janaab' Pakal. She ruled until Pakal was old enough to ascend to the throne. A set of feminine earrings made of jade, obsidian, and porcelain.

70000887.name: The Shield of King Pacal
70000887.description: A shield thought to have belonged to the Palenque king Janaab'Pakal. Pakal miraculously returned Tikal from the brink of destruction at the hand of the Calakmul people.

70000888.name: Chan Bahlum's Crown
70000888.description: Said to belong to the ruler Chan Bahlum II, also known as Kan B'alam II, who followed after his father King Pakal. It is heroically constructed and includes a large piece of obsidian as a symbol of its strength.

quests.name: A king's blood and the god's protection

70000889.name: The Bracelets of Kan Xul
70000889.description: A bracelet of King Kan Xul, also known as K'inich K'an Joy Chitam, the younger brother of Chan Bahlum and son of Pakal. It is an intricate piece with elaborate engravings and detailed colouring.

quests.name: History hidden in lettering on a crest

70000890.name: Ancient Mayan Skull
70000890.description: One of many skull found throughout the Mayan lands. There are signs of jade implanted in teeth and they are flat and unusually shaped in some places.

70000891.name: The Ornament of Lord Water
70000891.description: An ornament of the king of Caracol. Yajaw Te' K'inich II was a king who invaded T'ikal in the war of stars.

quests.name: One aiming to become the ultimate king

70000892.name: Chacmool
70000892.description: Chac Mool means thundering paw. The Mayan people are said to have placed the hearts of sacrifices on the tray at the stomach of this statue and pray to the gods.

70000893.name: Jade Decorative Vase
70000893.description: A luxurious jade vase. Its exterior middle section is adorned in porcelain. Such a finely crafted vase must have belonged to someone of importance.

70000894.name: Relief of an Eagle and Jaguar
70000894.description: One of many reliefs carved into the walls of the palace of Chichen Itza. On the left is a jaguar. On the right is a falcon holding a heart.

70000895.name: Tetrapod Vessel
70000895.description: A bowl-shaped container with four legs. It has a lid like the head of a dog. The dog is thought to have been a companion to Mayan kings making their journey to the afterlife.

70000896.name: Tripod Vessel
70000896.description: A cylindrical container with three legs. Most are made from earthenware or porcelain. None are made from metal. Many are made with intricate engravings.

70000897.name: Celt
70000897.description: The word Celt means a ceremonial axe. Many are decorated with intricate engravings. These were used in dances to the gods or when praying to ancestors.

70000898.name: Jade Bowl
70000898.description: A large cup made from jade. The ability to make such a large cup must have meant that jade was richly available.

70000899.name: Shell Pictogram
70000899.description: A pictogram made from shell. The meaning is unknown, but the advanced technique shows a growing sense of beauty.

70000900.name: Acha
70000900.description: A rock with its surface covered in pigment. It was apparently used in the ancient game of Tlachtli."

70000901.name: Jade Mask
70000901.description: Found in a stone sarcophagus at the Palenque ruins. Thought to have belonged to king Pakal from the pinnacle of Palenque civilization, but little else is known. The face is made of jade, the whites of the eyes from shells, and the pupils from obsidian.

70000902.name: Rubber Ball
70000902.description: A rubber ball used in the ancient ball game Tlachtli. Tlachtli was played with protective gear since the ball was extremely heavy and injury could result if playing unprotected.

70000903.name: Obsidian Sword
70000903.description: A sword made of obsidian, commonly seen in Aztec weaponry. It is very sharp but also very brittle. It was probably mass-produced.

70000904.name: Obsidian Spear
70000904.description: Few metal weapons are seen in ancient Aztec weaponry. They knew how to make bronze but apparently did not use it in weapons.

70000905.name: Statue of Toltec Warrior
70000905.description: A statue of a Toltecan warrior, a civilization thought to have flourished in Mesoamerica. This kind of statue was also carved as temple pillars. The Toltecans were a warrior civilization.

70000906.name: Mesoamerican Seal
70000906.description: A cylindrical earthenware crest. It is unclear what it was used for. Perhaps used to apply pigment to the body, or rolled over uncured pottery to make an imprinted pattern?

70000907.name: Nonstriated Pot
70000907.description: A pot without any markings. Most of the pots found in Azteca are earthenware.

70000908.name: Relief Decorated Pot
70000908.description: A wide-mouthed pot with a relief drawn on it. It is made out of earthenware. This picture may tell some kind of story.

70000909.name: Yoke
70000909.description: Protective gear used in the ancient ball game of Tlachtli. Tlachtli was performed sometimes as an act of war or as a prayer dance to the gods.

70000910.name: White Patterned Earthenware
70000910.description: Geometric patterns are added to white earthenware pots. This white colour may have been made by mixing quartz.

70000911.name: Olmec Colossal Head
70000911.description: Olmec Colossal Heads, from one of the oldest periods in Mesoamerican culture. Many specimens have been found, the smallest about as tall as an adult women, while the largest are several times larger.

70000912.name: Shell Ornament
70000912.description: In the Mayan civilization, ornaments were frequently created using shells. This one is like an earring.

70000913.name: Incense Burner
70000913.description: An earthenware incense burner found in the Aztec land. Perhaps it was used as a shrine accessory.

70000914.name: Decorated Earthenware
70000914.description: An earthenware item painted with various coloured pigments. The people who made it must have possessed extremely advanced technology.

70000915.name: Statue of an Unknown Creature
70000915.description: A statue depicting an unusual creature. Neither the people of the land where it was unearthed nor Europeans have ever seen an animal that looks like it. Perhaps it is an effigy of some already-extinct animal?

70000916.name: The Relief of Yax Nuun Ayiin I
70000916.description: A royal relief said to have been brought here when Tikal came under the control of Teotihuacan. It is extremely large and completely covered with pictures.

70000917.name: The Arm of Kak Siyaj
70000917.description: Weapons thought to have been used by Siyaj K'ahk', a Teotihuacan general who was involved in the operation to take over control of Tikal.

70000918.name: Festival Mask
70000918.description: A mask used by the nobility as a burial good or as a ceremonial item. Many such masks are found in Mesoamerica and they are made from a variety of materials such as stone, clay, shells, or gemstones.

70000919.name: Skull with a Hole
70000919.description: A skull, many of which can be found in South America. Was the hole made in the skull for a ritual after the person died, or was it made while the person was alive...?

70000920.name: Clay Work Statue
70000920.description: A detailed clay statue found in the western part of the Maya region. Many types exist. Perhaps they depict various gods?

70000921.name: The Statue of Kukulkan
70000921.description: Kukulcan was the Mayan name for the Aztec God Quetzalcoatl. Also called Kukumatz by people of the highlands. He was a god who was especially revered at Chichen Itza.

70000922.name: The Statue of Chaak
70000922.description: A rain god corresponding to the Aztec god Tlaloc. He was thought to bring not only rain but various other weather conditions.

70000923.name: Cylindrical Ceremonial Cup
70000923.description: A richly decorated and coloured cylindrical cup. Thought to have been presented by nobility or kings for ceremonies.

70000924.name: Statue of a Snake
70000924.description: A snake statue, commonly seen in Maya. It is probably a rattlesnake. Rattlesnakes extend their joints each time they shed their skin and for this reason were respected by the Mayans who also respected the passage of time.

quests.name: Divine statue shaped like a snake

sources.name: E Coast of Latin America(Cayenne, Pernambuco, Grand Cayman, Willemstad, Trujillo, and Caracas)

70000925.name: The Statue of Huitzilopochtli
70000925.description: The Aztec god of war, also the sun god. This god appears in the East and sinks into the evening darkness in the West, only to again reawaken in the East. The movement of the sun is actually the movement of this god According to myth.

70000926.name: The Statue of Tezcatlipoca
70000926.description: The god of night from Aztec mythology. The name means smoking mirror. He was thought to have created the world together with Quetzalcoatl but then banished him and ruled the world by himself. He was said to have been very handsome in his human form.

70000927.name: Statue of Quetzalcoatl
70000927.description: The god of culture from Aztec mythology. This god was said to be a peace-loving god who did not demand sacrifices, which was unusual for Aztec gods. He was tricked by Tezcatlipoca's and before leaving the center vowed to return in the first year of the reed.

sources.name: E Coast of Latin America(Cayenne, Pernambuco, Grand Cayman, Willemstad, Trujillo, and Caracas)

70000928.name: The Statue of Xipe Totec
