70001231.description: This flower grows in cold regions in the Andes mountains in South America. Flowers of many colours live there. They are popular because they are cheerful and last a long time when cut. Also known as the lily of the Incas.

ornaments.name: Lily of the Incas with Table
Lily of the Incas with Vase
Lily of the Incas Vase on Table
Lily of the Incas with Urn
Lily of the Incas Urn on Table
Lily of the Incas with White Urn
Lily of Incas w/ White Urn on Table

70001232.name: Malesherbia
70001232.description: This flower can be found only in dry regions in southwest Central America. The flower petals are shaped like stars, and bloom white and purple.

70001233.name: Chilean Bellflower
70001233.description: A plant like a vine with a strong stem. This blossoms large, drooping flowers. There are many cheerful, red flowers. It is found over a wide area in the southwestern forests of the South American continent.

70001234.name: Lady's Purse
70001234.description: A low bushy plant whose bag-shaped flower petals are its main characteristic. The flowers come in a number of colors; yellow, red, orange and even some with mixed colours. They are mainly found throughout warm regions in Central and South America. The flower is also known as Lady's Purse or slipper flower. Calceolarias is Latin for small shoe.

ornaments.name: Calceolarias with White Urn on Table

70001235.name: Chilean Glory Flower
70001235.description: This plant has stems growing straight, and it blossoms bright red and orange, tubular-shaped flowers. It grows by crawling along the ground or walls, like ivy. They are quick growers, hibernate in warm regions.

70001236.name: Chilean Firebush
70001236.description: This flower is native to Patagonia in South America, a land known for its cold winds. Its deep red flowers are particularly memorable, perhaps because it is most frequently seen on snow covered plains or in places where other plants are scarce. Also known as the Chilean Firebush.

quests.name: Flower blooming in the realm of winds

70001237.name: Goldcap
70001237.description: A plant with two flowers shaped like small purses on the end of long, narrow stems. It grows in Patagonia on the continent of South American.

70001238.name: Andean Condor
70001238.description: A very large bird, some of which whose wingspan can reach up to three meters. They are often seen in flight with their massive wings spread. They build nests in the rock crevices of bluffs, and prefer to eat the meat of large dead animals. These birds live as long as 50 years.

quests.name: A giant bird elegant on the wing

70001239.name: Inca Tern
70001239.description: Sea birds that live on the west coast of South America. Some characteristics are the red beak on a dark grey body, and the white feathers that look like a beard. It lives in groups of several thousand birds, and they can often be seen perched in groups on rock faces near the sea coast. They dive straight from the sky into the sea to easily catch fish.

70001240.name: Burrowing Owl
70001240.description: An owl with an unusual underground nest. It mainly makes its own nest using a hole burrowed into the ground by other animals. It runs like a chicken with its long legs, and is active during the day, and has many other characteristics not seen in other owls. It is found throughout the grasslands of the New World in South and North America.

quests.name: Bird that lives on the ground

70001241.name: Booted Racket-Tail
70001241.description: A small bird with beautiful tail feathers. One characteristic of the males is the tail feathers that appear to have a racket attached to the tip of a long stick, and that is said to attract females. The feathers are fluffy around its legs, like birds that live in colder regions. It lives only in one region of the Andes mountains in South America.

70001242.name: Sword-Billed Hummingbird
70001242.description: A small bird with a long beak. The beak, shaped like a spear, takes up almost 40% of its body length. It uses its long legs instead of its beak to groom itself. It flies silently through the sky and drinks the nectar of flowers.

70001243.name: Pygmy Marmoset
70001243.description: A very small monkey. It grows no larger than the palm of your hand. It likes living in forests along rivers and survives mainly by eating tree sap. It chirps like a bird.

quests.name: A monkey in the palm of your hand
A monkey in the palm of your hand

70001244.name: Emperor Tamarin
70001244.description: A small monkey that has made its habitat in the tropical forests in the north of South America. It gets the name Emperor from its fine whiskers. It lives in the trees and eats fruit.

quests.name: Little old man of the forest

70001245.name: Chinchilla
70001245.description: An animal slightly bigger than a squirrel. Perhaps because it lives at high altitudes and colder regions, it has a soft, and very dense coat. It is nocturnal and lives in the rocks of mountains.

70001246.name: Darwin's Frogs
70001246.description: An unusual frog that raises its young in its mouth. When the eggs have grown, the baby frogs jump from the father's mouth. A characteristic is its pointed head and nose.

70001247.name: Giant Tortoise
70001247.description: A land turtle whose shell can grow to be over a meter in diameter. It looks like a pile of rocks. It lives a long time…with some living for over one hundred years. They have no natural enemies, and are not afraid of man.

70001248.name: Marine Iguana
70001248.description: A large and unusual lizard that lives in the sea. Spike-shaped scales grow like a crest on its back, and it has a rough black skin that resembles rocks. They skillfully use their long, flat tails to swim and they eat seaweed. They live in groups on sea coasts and can often be seen sunning themselves.

quests.name: Lizard that lives in the sea

70001249.name: Land Iguana
70001249.description: A large lizard with a 1-meter long body. Distinguished by its amber body and fat tail. Herbivorous, it mainly feeds on cactuses. Quiet by nature.

70001250.name: Spectacled Bear
70001250.description: A bear that lives in South America. Its face has white patterns resembling eyeglasses. It's as large as a man, and lives in high-altitude forests, some as high as 2,000 meters. It is nocturnal and good at climbing trees.

70001251.name: Guanaco
70001251.description: This animal lives in mountain regions and grassy wastelands. On its sides and back, it has a bright ginger colour, and from its head to its chest, it has soft, white fur covering its body. Although it has a quiet nature, it is tirelessly curious. Since ancient times, it has been used by natives as a beast of burden.

70001252.name: Vicugna
70001252.description: A bronze-coloured animal living high in the Andes. It looks like a camel, but it's smaller at just 1.5 meters; it has long, white hair growing from the base of its neck that looks like a beard. Its fine and very soft fur commands a high value and is much prized.

70001253.name: The Drake Passage
70001253.description: Admiral Francis Drake of England is said to have discovered this strait. The waves of adjacent waters are high and the forceful winds never drop, making this known as a difficult area to sail. Moreover, it is covered in ice through the winter.

quests.name: The second circumvention of the globe

70001254.name: Cape Horn
70001254.description: The cape at the south end of the South American Continent. Admiral Francis Drake discovered this cape. The name Cape Horn was given by the Dutch sailor Willem Schouten who successfully passed through the waters off the cape.

70001255.name: The Andes
70001255.description: A mountain range on the western edge of the South American continent. 6,000m high peaks continue from the north to south end of the South American continent. It is cool and pleasant near the equator in the north, and there is some agriculture, albeit small in scale.

70001256.name: Punta Parinas
70001256.description: The cape at the westernmost tip of the South American continent. It is very dry there because of the cold air currents that flow nearby and quite barren.

70001257.name: The Gulf of Panama
70001257.description: The bay spreading out south of the Isthmus of Panama. The Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean sea spread to the north of the isthmus. If there were a way to get through the isthmus more easily, the area would be busy with traffic from the north and south.

70001258.name: The Gulf of Tehuantepec
70001258.description: The gulf spreading out south of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Central America. They say many civilizations have prospered along this coast since ancient times.

70001259.name: Terraced Fields
70001259.description: Gently inclined fields built into the base of the inclined mountain in a step shape. This is a common sight in agriculture in the highlands along the Andes Mountains.

70001260.name: Rapa Nui
70001260.description: A solitary island far off in the sea that exists on the east side of the Pacific Ocean. Massive icons tower along the coast; this must be the island from where you can see the stars. Rapa Nui means big island in the native language.

70001261.name: The Galapagos Islands
70001261.description: A string of volcanic islands located just below the equator. There are many animals living there that cannot be found anywhere else on earth.

70001262.name: Uluru
70001262.description: A large rock called Uluru by the aboriginal people of Australia. It is sacred to them. They believe that spirits dwell inside and gather around when there are rituals.

70001263.name: Ancient Boomerang
70001263.description: A boomerang used by the aboriginal tribes for hunting. They are made of wood and polished smooth. They cut down on air resistance and fly beautifully. The natives are said to have lived on this big area of land as hunters and gatherers.

70001264.name: Kupe's Wood Spear
70001264.description: A wooden spear bearing the name of Kupe. Kupe is said to have discovered Aotearoa and then returned to Hawaiki. He then convinced many to follow him and then guided the group to Aotearoa from Hawaiki. He was one of the ancestors of the Maori people.

70001265.name: Legendary Canoe
70001265.description: Canoes said to have been used to move from Hawaiki to Aotearoa. It has been preserved and seems very old. Perhaps this is one that they actually used to move.

70001266.name: Ancient Hook
70001266.description: Fish hooks used by the people who lived along the coast. They were made by polishing wood. Because they were used in sea water, they rotted away quickly, but there are some that still remain in good condition. The natives that used them are said to have been skilled in working with wood.

70001267.name: Didgeridoo
70001267.description: A wooden flute the Australian aborigines used in ceremonies. It has different names, such as Idaki or Mago, depending on the region. They used the wood of Eucalyptus whose insides had been eaten away by termites. Sound is made by placing the lips and vibrating them at the end of the cylinder.

70001268.name: Hunting Sticks
70001268.description: A set of sticks used to keep rhythm for the didgeridoo during the ceremonies of the Australian aborigines. Clapsticks were held by the singer who was singing the ceremonial songs.

70001269.name: Ancient Rock Art
70001269.description: Rock paintings drawn in the caves aboriginal Australians live in. They have been drawing them since time immemorial. It's said that it's a way for them to express their unique world-view, called 'Dreamtime.'

70001270.name: Washikuku Ceremonial Pottery
70001270.description: Pottery used in rituals in the Washikuku region. No liquids were ever put in them. It was a object of worship similar to an idol. The same face is painted on the front, back, and both sides. Its round pupils and somewhat smiling mouth are designs not often seen in Europe.

maps.name: Festival Clay Pot Map
maps.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001271.name: Pedestal with a Statue of a God
70001271.description: A pedestal for a spiritual hall. During gatherings, sound was produced by hitting it. All of the many tribes, both large and small, in New Guinea had a spiritual hall for spirit worship.

maps.name: Festival Pedestal Map
maps.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001272.name: The Statue of a Spirit
70001272.description: A statue of a spirit worshipped by the tribes in New Guinea. On this island, spirits are honoured and embodied in wooden icons.

quests.name: Elemental faith of New Guinea
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001273.name: Spirit Mask
70001273.description: Spirits in New Guinea are said to only be visible by adult males that have completed a ritual. For that reason, they wear masks to show women and children that the spirit has descended.

quests.name: Elemental loss
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001274.name: The Eternal Stars
70001274.description: Black opals found only in Australia. The land is black, creating even more contrast between the hues and colours. Its beauty is like a moonless night filled with shining stars; it makes you feel as though you're being pulled into the sky, all alone on a moonless night.

70001275.name: Bahinemo Warrior's Shield
70001275.description: A shield used by the Bahinemo tribe of New Guinea when battling other tribes. Many tribes live on the islands and never stop fighting. The pictures and paint are meant to intimidate their enemies. Each tribe and people have different drawings.

quests.name: The people who live in New Guinea
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001276.name: Warrior's Headdress
70001276.description: Head decorations worn by warriors of the tribes of New Guinea in battle. This headware is made from special feathers of the bird-of-paradise. These special feathers only appear during a certain period. This headdress, the chest decorations that hold the blessings of the spirits, and the body paint are said to increase morale.

maps.name: Headgear Map
maps.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001277.name: Stone Axe
70001277.description: A weapon that uses stone at the top of an axe. Similar weapons have been found in all regions around the world from ancient times. Metals were not used in New Guinea; weapons for fighting were made from stone, bone, and wood.

70001278.name: Water Drums
70001278.description: An instrument used in rites of passage when boys become men. A hole is dug in the ground and filled with water. The drum is placed on it to vary the sound by raising and lowering it in the water.

70001279.name: Abelam Tribe Brooch
70001279.description: Chest decorations worn when battling with other tribes. Men decorate themselves to look very masculine and to show their pride to others, using feathers, leaves, shells, and animal fangs.

quests.name: Pride of each of them
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001280.name: Slit Drum
70001280.description: An instrument that produces sound by hitting a hollowed out log. It can be found everywhere across the world. New Guinea's slit drum is used in rituals and to signal friends.

70001281.name: Beautiful Shell Stone
70001281.description: Shells that have been made into gems. There are many colours such as white and black.

70001282.name: Stone Shaped like a Fish
70001282.description: A stone that looks like two fish are trapped. How long would it take for fish to be like this?

70001283.name: Banksia
70001283.description: A plant with large quantities of nectar. It is a precious source of food for animals that live on nectar. The fruit is extremely hard; it cracks when burned such as in a forest fire and drops its seeds on the ground.

70001284.name: Grevillea
70001284.description: An evergreen that grows in Australia. The leaves and flowers are delicate, and the flowers are red and white.

70001285.name: Wattle
70001285.description: A tree that lives in the highlands on the coast of Australia. It has thorns and can grow as high as 10 meters.

70001286.name: Blue Orchid
70001286.description: A large, blue-ish purple flower. It loves the sun and will bloom even in the desert.

ornaments.name: Orchids with White Urn on Table

70001287.name: Southern Cassowary
70001287.description: A large bird that stands 1.7 meters tall. It cannot fly because its wings are too small for its body. On the other hand, it has well developed legs. It can kick hard enough to kill a man.

quests.name: Animal that does not show itself
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001288.name: Emu
70001288.description: A large bird that stands 2 meters tall. Its wings are so tiny that it cannot fly. It is completely covered in a grey-brown coat.

quests.name: Big animal living on south east continent

70001289.name: Kiwi
70001289.description: This bird has a very long beak (as long as 60 cm) compared to its body. It uses that beak to search underground for worms and insects. It makes calls that sound like a flute, which where it gets its name.

70001290.name: Kagu
70001290.description: A bird that lives in New Caledonia. When threatened, it raises its crest and spreads its wings to intimidate its enemies. Although it has large wings, it can't fly.

70001291.name: Rainbow Lorikeet
70001291.description: A brightly coloured bird. Individuals vary in appearance and make a lot of noise when in groups.

70001292.name: Galah
70001292.description: A bird that lives in groups in all regions of Australia. Its body is orange, its wings are grey, and its tail is black. It eats fruit and insects.

70001293.name: Cockatiel
70001293.description: A bird whose characteristics are its long crest and the orange fluff under its eyes. It raises and lowers its crest depending on the situation.

70001294.name: Sulphur-Crested Cockatoo
70001294.description: A bird whose body is covered in white feathers, but has yellow crest feathers. When excited it raises its crest and emits a surprisingly loud cry. Larger groups can have several hundred birds.

quests.name: Clearly black and white
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001295.name: Crimson Rosella
70001295.description: A bird whose body is bright red and cheeks are blue. It stands out against its surroundings and so builds its nest in safe places like the hollow of a tree.

70001296.name: Kakapo
70001296.description: A bird whose name in the native language means night parrot. It can fly, but it is particularly active when night falls.

70001297.name: Kea
70001297.description: A bird that lives high in the mountains near the border of forests. It is covered in olive-colour green feathers, but the underside of its wings are a pretty orange colour. It is very friendly to humans.

quests.name: Creature that does not fear man

70001298.name: Brown Hawk Owl
70001298.description: A small, stout owl. It becomes active at night-fall, and eats insects and mice.

70001299.name: Lyrebird
70001299.description: A bird with uniquely shaped tail feathers, like a lyre. When in mating season, it attracts females by shaking its tail and calling. Most surprising is its voice. It not only sings like a bird, but it can also mimic a wide variety of sounds.

70001300.name: Gouldian Finch
70001300.description: A bird that lives in Australia. The colour of its head varies according to the individual, and it uses termite mounds for its nest.

70001301.name: Raggiana Bird of Paradise
70001301.description: A bird that lives around New Guinea. Males have beautiful decorative feathers. In mating season, males attract females by gathering in one place to dance. Females watch the dancing males and select one as their mate.

quests.name: State of love affairs
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001302.name: Frill-necked Lizard
70001302.description: A lizard that lives in Australia. Its body can reach 1 meter, including its long tail. It has a distinguishing frill around its neck. This fans out when it encounters an enemy and it attempts to intimidate by opening its mouth widely. Then, when its enemy backs off, it runs away on two legs.

quests.name: Lizard that walks on two legs

70001303.name: Crocodile Lizard
70001303.description: A lizard with a triangular, bony head. One male lives with several females, and hides in fallen leaves.

maps.name: Armoured Animals Map
maps.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001304.name: Echidnas
70001304.description: A mole with fat, hard spikes. It uses its spikes to protect itself from enemies. It digs into the ground to hide itself, and only the spikes on its back can be seen.

70001305.name: Quoll
70001305.description: A marsupial that looks like a cat. It is nocturnal and eats insects and small animals.

70001306.name: Numbat
70001306.description: A marsupial that eats ants. It uses its large, front-leg claws to destroy ant nests.

70001307.name: Bandicoot
70001307.description: A marsupial that looks like a mouse, and has a long nose. It's nocturnal and eats insects.

70001308.name: Southern Marsupial Mole
70001308.description: A marsupial that looks like a mole. It lives in the desert and moves by digging into the ground. It eats any living thing it finds.

70001309.name: Coffin in the Catacombs
70001309.description: Coffin placed in the Catacombs.In Catacombs, bodies, both with and without coffins, were often laid to rest in holes dug out of the walls.

70001310.name: Common Brushtail Possum
70001310.description: A marsupial that looks like a fox. It lives in trees and eats plant leaves, flowers, and bird's eggs.

70001311.name: Greater Glider
70001311.description: A flying marsupial. It has long claws and opposable fingers which allow it to firmly grasp branches. It uses its large ears and forward facing eyes to determine distances. It can fly over 100 meters through the air, even in the dark.

70001312.name: Common Striped Possum
70001312.description: A black and white striped marsupial. It sprays a sickeningly smelly liquid. They eat fruit and so on.

maps.name: Squirrel-like Animal Map
maps.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001313.name: Sugar Glider
70001313.description: A flying marsupial. It has a tail covered in long, soft fur. When flying through the air, that fur acts as a rudder. It lives in small groups and eats tree sap and seeds.

70001314.name: Eastern Long-Neck Turtle
70001314.description: A long-necked aquatic turtle. Its long neck cannot even fit inside its shell.

70001315.name: Platypus
70001315.description: An animal that has the body of an otter and a beak like a duck. It lays eggs and suckles its hatchlings. Males can inject their enemies with poison from large spurs on their hind legs.

70001316.name: Tasmanian Devil
70001316.description: A meat-eating marsupial. It eats anything from insects to small mammals, and even creatures as large as wallabies. It often fights for food, and when excited, its skin flushes red.

70001317.name: Koala
70001317.description: A marsupial that lives most of its life in Eucalyptus trees. When the young grow to a certain age, they spend their time clinging to their parent's backs. They mainly eat Eucalyptus leaves.

quests.name: On the backs of our fathers

70001318.name: Wombat
70001318.description: A marsupial that live in holes burrowed in the ground. Its pouch faces backward so that dirt doesn't get inside. It is very strong and can sometimes kill predators.

70001319.name: Wallaby
70001319.description: A marsupial with a fat tail and large hind legs. It places its young in its pouch and can jump several meters in one bound. It eats fruit at night and lives in large groups.

70001320.name: Kangaroo
70001320.description: The largest marsupial. Twice the size of a wallaby, this animal can jump up to 8 meters in one bound. It lives in groups. The males frequently fight. When they do, they rear back on their large tails for support while kicking out with their powerful legs.

70001321.name: Tasmanian Tiger
70001321.description: A marsupial that eats meat and looks like a wolf. It eats large mammals like kangaroos and wombats.

70001322.name: Crocodile
70001322.description: A creature with a characteristically long snout. The body is approximately 2.5 meters, and it can move very quickly on the ground.

quests.name: Crocodiles of the south east continent

70001323.name: Taipan
70001323.description: A snake that can grow longer than 3 meters. When it finds its prey, it attacks very quickly and kills with its deadly poison. Even humans are likely to die if bitten.

70001324.name: Tiger Snake
70001324.description: A snake with characteristically bright yellow lined patterns. It has a powerful venom and uses it while hunting prey.

70001325.name: Fairy Penguin
70001325.description: A small penguin. It nests in holes in the ground or on rock ledges, with the males and females taking turns keeping the eggs warm. It frequently dives into the water to catch fish.

70001326.name: Sea Dragon
70001326.description: An animal that looks a lot like seaweed. It protects itself by pretending to be the surrounding seaweed. It eats small shrimp and fish.

70001327.name: The Bay of Plenty
70001327.description: The bay at the north of Aotearoa. It has capes on both the east and west. The waves are quiet, and there is an abundant amount of fish to be caught.

70001328.name: The Tasman Sea
70001328.description: The sea across the southeast of Australia. There are warm currents nearby, so it's a pleasant temperature on the coast, but it is very windy.

70001329.name: Aotearoa
70001329.description: The island southeast of New Guinea. There are two large islands to the north and south, but in particular the island to the north is called Aotearoa. Aotearoa means the land of the long, white cloud in the Maori language.

70001330.name: New Caledonia Island
70001330.description: A narrow and long island east of Australia. The island is surrounded by coral, with mountains inland. It has a mild climate. The sandalwood that grows there has drawn the attention of a number of merchants.

70001331.name: Van Diemen's Land
70001331.description: An island in the southern part of the southeast region of Australia. Tasman discovered the island and named it after the Governor of the East India Company, Anthony van Diemen. The island has a plethora of animals, making it a much coveted land for biologists.

quests.name: Footsteps of those who came before

70001332.name: The Great Australia Bight
70001332.description: A bay expanding south of Australia. The long coast line extends 1,000 kilometres, and the wide shoals continue on. The bluffs that project into the sea along the coastline of the bay continue in some places for several hundred kilometres. It seems that the bluffs were created by the strong winds that blow up from the south.

70001333.name: Kangaroo Island
70001333.description: An island southeast of Australia. It was discovered by Mathew Flinders of England. Many varieties and types of animals live here. The land itself is diverse, and inland there are caves and deserts, as well as one gargantuan boulder.

70001334.name: The Spencer Gulf
70001334.description: A bay with sharp angles located south of the southern coast of Australia's Eyre Peninsula. Near the bay, they say that there is a plentiful vein of silver.

70001335.name: Eyre Peninsula
70001335.description: A peninsula belonging to the southeast region of Australia. In the sea nearby, you can often see whales and sharks. It is also home to many seals, sea lions, and dolphins.

70001336.name: Shark Bay
70001336.description: A bay spreading out to the west of Australia. The seawater in the bay has an extremely high salt content, so only a certain type of seaweed can live there. Although it is a narrow piece of land, you can find many areas with unique environments, such as a beach made entirely of white shells.

70001337.name: The Great Sandy Desert
70001337.description: A desert covering a large part of the northwestern region of Australia. Much of the western area of inland Australia is dry, making it mostly desert. Annual rainfall is very low, and there is even saltwater lakes.

70001338.name: Cape Levique
70001338.description: A cape northwest of Australia. The southern portion is slowly becoming desert. The seacoast line extending south southwest is 100 kilometres long, and there are blue seas and beautiful silver-white beaches.

70001339.name: Kimberley Plateau
70001339.description: A plateau northwest of Australia. Inland, there are canyons and steep mountains. The seacoast line is complex.

quests.name: Investigation - north west coast of Continent

70001340.name: Tiwi
70001340.description: An island in the northern part of Australia. After passing Van Diemen's bay, you come to Amhem Land. Melville island to the east and Bathurst island to the west are collectively known as Tiwi. The Tiwi people live there and protect their unique culture.

70001341.name: Arnhem Land
70001341.description: The northernmost peninsula in Australia. The central part is mountainous, but the coastal areas are relatively flat. Many rock paintings believed to have been drawn by the Aboriginal Australians remain on this peninsula.

70001342.name: Groote Eylandt
70001342.description: An island north of Australia. In Dutch, it means large island. As suggested by its name, this is the largest island in the Gulf of Carpentaria.

70001343.name: Mornington Island
70001343.description: An island at the far south of the Gulf of Carpentaria, northeast of Australia. There are also inlets to several mid-sized rivers in the south making it a good fishing spot.

70001344.name: The Gulf of Carpentaria
70001344.description: The bay northeast of Australia sandwiched between Amhem Land and the Cape York peninsula. Although it covers an expansive area, the water is shallow overall. The seacoast is covered in mangroves. Crocodiles live in the river that feeds into the bay. It would probably be difficult to build a harbour...

70001345.name: Cape York Peninsula
70001345.description: A projecting peninsula in the northeast of Australia. The northern point is called Cape York and is the northernmost point of Australia. To the east is the Coral Sea and to the west is the Gulf of Carpentaria. There are many unusual animals living there.

70001346.name: Fiji Islands
70001346.description: The island chain located east of Vanuatu. There are more than 300 islands of varying sizes ranging from large to small. The largest is Vetileb Island in the southwest. Abel Tasman from the Netherlands was the first European to discover the northern region of the Fiji islands.

quests.name: Selection of the site for 2nd supply port

70001347.name: Koro Sea
70001347.description: An inland sea surrounded by the islands of Fiji. Although called an inland sea, its waters are deep. With the shoals of the surrounding islands covered in coral reefs, this inland sea creates a fantastic scene that mesmerizes all who gaze at it.

quests.name: Investigation of sea around Fiji islands

70001348.name: The Coral Sea
70001348.description: A marine region located on the east coast of Australia with abundant coral, making it an extremely beautiful sea. There are innumerable islands. It is the breeding grounds for sea turtles and migratory birds.

70001349.name: Clarence Strait
70001349.description: The straits in northern Australia between Amhem and Bathurst Islands and Melville Island. It has a tropical climate. The area is hot all year long and is subjected to strong winds and heavy rains that are typical of the tropics.

quests.name: Shallows right in front of you

70001350.name: Vanuatu
70001350.description: An island chain located far to the east northeast of Australia, and north northeast of New Caledonia. Half of the islands are volcanic. The islands are mountainous and the highest peak is Mount Tabwemasana on the island Espiritu Santo. Each island has developed its own unique culture.

70001351.name: The Solomon Sea
70001351.description: The sea spreading out east of New Guinea. The area is surrounded by islands, and it is said that the people that live on the islands have interacted with each other since antiquity. In the rainy season, the weather can suddenly change to heavy rains and strong winds, but at other times, the sea is said to be quiet with coral reefs developed in the area.

quests.name: Investigation - sea to east of New Guinea

70001353.name: The Azores
70001353.description: A town on a volcanic island located in the centre of the Atlantic Ocean. After being discovered in the first half of the 15th century by the Portuguese, many people have emigrated here from the various countries in Europe. It became a base for long voyages to the New World.

70001354.name: Nassau
70001354.description: A town on the New Providence Island south of the Florida peninsula and north of the West Indies. The area became known as the West Indies because when they were discovered by Cristobal Colon at the end of the 15th century, he mistakenly thought they were in India.

70001355.name: Grand Cayman
70001355.description: A town on the largest of the Cayman Islands, in the western area of the West Indies. Shipwrecked sailors and pirates began living there.

70001356.name: Willemstad
70001356.description: A town located at the southern most edge of the Caribbean Sea, southeast of Curacao Island. It was discovered at the end of the 15th century by Alonzo de Ojeda and Amerigo Vespucci.

70001357.name: Veracruz
70001357.description: The name of the town means the true cross in Spanish. At the beginning of the 16th century, Hernan Cortes landed here. It became the main gateway for trade in the Gulf of Mexico.

70001358.name: Merida
70001358.description: A town located at the northeast edge of the Yucatan Peninsula which is covered with a tropical rain forest. The ancient Mayan civilization prospered here.

70001359.name: Trujillo
70001359.description: A town adjacent to the Gulf of Honduras in the Caribbean Sea. Cristobal Colon discovered it on his fourth voyage. The name Honduras means deep in Spanish. It is taken from the time Cristobal Colon reached land, he dropped anchor, but it didn't reach the bottom.

70001360.name: Maracaibo
70001360.description: A town adjacent to lake Maracaibo, the largest salt water lake in South America, and the bay that connects the Caribbean Sea and Atlantic Ocean. Occasionally, silent lightening occurs at this lake.

70001361.name: Bahia
70001361.description: Bahia means bay. A South American town adjacent to the Atlantic Ocean and located on a peninsula that envelopes Todos os Santos (All Saints' Bay).

70001362.name: Rio de Janeiro
70001362.description: Discovered at the beginning of the 16th century by the adventurer Caspar de Ramos, this large bay was mistaken for the mouth of a river and given the name Rio de Janeiro, which means the January River.

70001363.name: Buenos Aires
70001363.description: The name of the town means good air or fair winds. It is located on the east coast of South America at the inlet to the river Plate with its wide and fertile plains. There are four seasons. The Wichi people live here.

70001364.name: San Antonio
70001364.description: A warm port town on the east coast of South America south of Buenos Aires in the San Martias Gulf. Further south is an arid region called Patagonia.

70001365.name: Caracas
70001365.description: A town on the east coast of South America east of Maracaibo. The name of the town comes from the Caribbean and Caracas people that lived there.

70001366.name: Pegu
70001366.description: A town located on the east coast of the Bay of Bengal. It was built by one of the peoples that live in southeast Asia, the Hmong. It is the capital of the Pegu dynasty.

70001367.name: Banda Aceh
70001367.description: A town located at the north edge of the island of Sumatra. It is the capital of the Aceh Empire which had broken off from the Majapahit Empire.

70001368.name: Malacca
70001368.description: The capital of the Malaccan Empire, a nation of Islamic Malay people. Malacca was created when the prince of the Sailendra dynasty escaped the invasion of the Majapahit Empire and built a town in that spot.

70001369.name: Palembang
70001369.description: A town on the northern coast of the southern region of Sumatra. It was the capital of the Sailendra dynasty that established trade between the east and west.

70001370.name: Jakarta
70001370.description: A town located on the northwest coast of Java. Originally there was a small settlement of the Sunda people called Sunda Kelapa at this location. The Sunda people built the Pajajaran Empire and even withstood invasions by the Majapahit Empire.

70001371.name: Surabaya
70001371.description: A town located on the northeast coast of Java. It came under the rule of the Majapahit Empire and build the golden age of Hindu culture.

70001372.name: Pattani
70001372.description: The capital of the Pattani Empire, a nation of Islamic Malay people. The Malay here were the first in the Malay Empire to convert to Islam.

70001373.name: Lop Buri
70001373.description: A town in the Chao Phraya River basin. Until the 10th century it was called Rauo. It was known as a city of the Khmer race Hmong people and thrived as an important capital of the Ayutthaya kingdom.

70001374.name: Gia Dinh
70001374.description: A town built in the Mekong river valley. For many years it was under the rule of the Chenla Empire. It is said that the ancient capital of the Chenla Empire is upstream.

70001375.name: Brunei
70001375.description: The center of the Kingdom of Brunei, Islamic t3aachings have spread throughout the area. It is rich in natural resources such as petroleum and ore.

70001376.name: Banjarmasin
70001376.description: A port on the south coast of Borneo Island, it fell under the control of the Majapahit Kingdom in the 14th century. At present, it is controlled by Islamic forces. The Dyak people who were the original inhabitants live on the outskirts.

70001377.name: Makassar
70001377.description: A town located south of Celebes Island. It prospered during the Gowa Kingdom and Tarro Kingdom as an intermediate port for trade.

70001378.name: Run
70001378.description: A town on Run Island, south of the Banda Islands. Nutmeg is produced here. It is a noted centre of trade.

70001379.name: Manila
70001379.description: A port town located south of the Luzon Islands. There is a Malay settlement and trade has prospered here. In the latter half of the 16th century, it was occupied by the Spaniard Legazpi.

70001380.name: Ambon
70001380.description: A small island located south of the Molucca Islands. One of the towns produces spices such as clove. Europeans continued advancing into this region in search of spices.

70001381.name: Ternate
70001381.description: The capital of the Kingdom of Ternate, located in the northern part of the Molucca islands on Ternate Island. In recent years, Europeans have come here in search of the valuable spices produced on the island. They even built a town.

70001382.name: Valparaiso
70001382.description: A port town that prospered due to the ships that anchored there while sailing through the Straits of Magellan. The name of the town means valley of heaven."

70001383.name: Copiapo
70001383.description: An oasis town, located in the south of the wide desert that stretches south to north. There is little rain, so water is precious.

70001384.name: Lima
70001384.description: A colony developed as a base for Europeans to investigate the Incan empire. Many sailors visited this town, and it became a centre for trade.

70001385.name: Lambayeque
70001385.description: A cultural centre that flourished before the Incan empire grew. It is blessed with a mild climate all through the year, so it is easy to live here.

70001386.name: Tumbes
70001386.description: A town that Francisco Pizzaro visited when he was heading toward the Incan empire. It is said that seeing Pizzaro shining in the sunlight, clad in his armour, they thought he was holy and welcomed him with open arms.

70001387.name: Panama
70001387.description: A port town located on the border of North and South America. The fishing industry is strong here, just as its name (a place abundant with fish) suggests. A variety of animals live in the tropical rain forest that spreads out around the town.

70001388.name: Guatemala
70001388.description: One of the port towns in central America adjacent to the Pacific Ocean, known for its coffee production. The coast is a tropical lowland, and the difference in temperature with the inland highlands is striking.

70001389.name: Acapulco
70001389.description: A town adjacent to the Pacific Ocean and at the foot of the mountains. The temperature is high all year long. Its climate is permanently summer. Because of the silver trade, there was no end to the traffic of cargo ships heading toward Europe.

70001390.name: Samarai
70001390.description: A town located southeast of New Guinea. Its high temperature and humidity give it a tropical rain forest climate. There is a high level of annual rainfall and little temperature difference throughout the year.

70001391.name: Guam
70001391.description: A town on Guam located at the southern most edge of the Mariana Islands. It is always summer here with high temperatures and high humidity, allowing people to swim year round. Also, Magellan visited here while sailing around the world.

70001392.name: Kakadu
70001392.description: A town located on the north coast of Australia. The name originates with a name of the native people, Gagudju. Around the town are marshes, with a lot of animals and plants. There are also many wall paintings in the area around Kakadu. It seems people have lived here since ancient times.

70001393.name: Hobart
70001393.description: A town on the southern coast of Van Diemen's Land, an island in the southern part of Australia. Located at the inlet to the River Derwent, it was as an important base for fishing due to its good topographical conditions.

70001394.name: Wanganui
70001394.description: A town located on the south coast of Aotearoa. The Maori have lived here from antiquity and this was a base for trade. In the Maori language, Wanganui means large port.

70001395.name: Atlantic Blue Marlin
70001395.description: This fish lives in the ocean and is said to be the largest of the marlins.

70001396.name: Black Marlin
70001396.description: A large marlin with a fat, short beak.

70001397.name: Indo-Pacific Sailfish
70001397.description: A comparatively small marlin, but it has a beautiful body due to its great back fin.

70001398.name: Mediterranean Billfish
70001398.description: A marlin unique to the Mediterranean sea. Compared to other marlins, the beak of its upper jaw is short.

70001399.name: Atlantic Tarpon
70001399.description: This fish has large eyes like a herring, and a shiny silver body. It is a large and ferocious fish.

70001400.name: Nile Perch
70001400.description: A relative of the perch found widely throughout the Nile river basin. The larger ones can be heavier than 200 kilograms.

70001401.name: Patagonian Toothfish
70001401.description: This fish lives in the southern seas. It has an extremely large mouth and looks like cod.

70001402.name: European Catfish
70001402.description: A giant catfish with an extremely long pair of whiskers on its upper jaw. When it reaches adulthood, it can be 5 meters long.

70001403.name: Beluga
70001403.description: A large sturgeon found in the Black Sea. It can grow to over 6 meters and weigh several tons.

70001404.name: Baltic Sturgeon
70001404.description: A sturgeon with a brown body and a distinctive faint gold tint. It is found throughout northern Europe.

70001405.name: African Arowana
70001405.description: An arowana that lives in the Nile river. Its features are its small mouth and black rouge-coloured body.

70001406.name: Black Arowana
70001406.description: This fish is black while young, but grows into a beautiful silver colour. It also has an orange pattern on its fins.

70001407.name: Piraiba
70001407.description: This is a particularly large catfish living in the Amazon river. Its whiskers can be twice the length of its body.

70001408.name: Zungaro Zungaro
70001408.description: This is a giant, gluttonous catfish that is said to even eat humans.

70001409.name: Tambaqui
70001409.description: A black coloured fish. It grows to be over 1 meter in length. It is a relative of the piranha.

70001410.name: Black Pacu
70001410.description: A grey-coloured relative of the piranha. It is omnivorous and even eat nuts.

70001411.name: Fahaka Puffer
70001411.description: A blowfish that lives in the Nile river. Unusual for this type of fish, it lives in freshwater.

70001412.name: Pink Cusk-Eel
70001412.description: A giant fish that can be up to 2 meters in length. It lives in the deep ocean in the southern hemisphere. A type of brotulidae.

70001413.name: Amazonian Freshwater Stingray
70001413.description: A small freshwater stingray that lives in river basins in South America. It has poisonous barbs on its tail.

70001414.name: Sawfish
70001414.description: A ray with a saw-like snout. It is said that it will cut a hole in the bottom of a ship and eat the corpses of people who drown.

70001415.name: Electric Numb Ray
70001415.description: This ray has a pair of internal organs that produce electricity on the left and right sides that it uses to shock and paralyze its prey, such as small fish and shrimp.

70001416.name: Snook
70001416.description: A fish that looks like a perch with a characteristically long and narrow jaw that projects from its low body. It can grow to be over 1 meter in length.

70001417.name: Striped Bass
70001417.description: A type of perch that has stripes on its body and lives in freshwater, brackish water, and seawater.

70001418.name: Great White Shark
70001418.description: With a giant body and ferocious temperament, this shark is a feared tyrant of the sea. It is known as a man-eater.

70001419.name: Mako Shark
70001419.description: This shark lives in the open sea and catches its prey by swimming at high speed. It is known as a man-eater.

70001420.name: Halibut
70001420.description: A giant flounder that can grow to as long as 3 meters. It lives in the Arctic ocean.

70001421.name: Blue-Tooth Groper
70001421.description: The large bump on the head of this fish is its biggest characteristic. It is a relative of the wrasse and can to be over 1 meter.

70001422.name: The Mask of Barong
70001422.description: A mask made in the shape of Barong, Beast King of spirits of the island of Bali east of Java. On Bali, Barong is believed to protect against plague. The mask is considered to be an avatar of the god, and kept carefully in its own shrine.

quests.name: Endless battle between good and evil

70001423.name: Capitoline Wolf
70001423.description: A bronze statue of the brothers Romulus and Ramos suckling on a wolf. The brothers appear in the myth about the founding of Rome. The statue of the twins was recently added by Antonio Del Pollaiuolo, but the statue of the wolf is from the Etruscan era.

70001424.name: Venus of Urbino
70001424.description: A piece by Tiziano. In the front, Venus is lying down, provocatively looking out at the viewer. The puppy curled up at her feet is a metaphor for obedience and virtue, and the rose in the hand symbolizes love. The maid searching the clothes cabinet to the rear gives the goddess a more worldly feel.

70001425.name: Sleeping Venus
70001425.description: A piece by Giorgione. commissioned by the royal family of Venice as a wedding present. Giorgione influenced his student Tiziano who later drew a similar picture. Innocent beauty oozes from the sleeping Venus in her tranquil state.

70001426.name: Portrait of a Man in a Turban
70001426.description: A piece by Jan van Eyck. Opinions differ, but it is thought that this was drawn by Eyck himself. He improved upon the drawing techniques used until then, and made it possible to draw fine parts as evinced by this drawing. He was successful in expressing deep, varied forms of light and darkness.

70001427.name: Maesta
70001427.description: An alter piece by Ambrogio Lorenzetti. One of the pieces depicting a solemn virgin Mary that Lorenzetti spent his entire life perfecting. Of the paintings he did of Jesus and the virgin Mary, this one is of particularly high value. Their mutual line of sight impresses upon the viewer that the mother and child had a deep love for one another.

70001428.name: David with the Head of Goliath
70001428.description: A piece by Guido Reni. It tells the bible story of the shepherd boy David felling the giant Goliath with his sling and taking his head. While composed in the classical tradition, Reni's unique touch can be seen in various portions of the painting.

70001429.name: St.Veronica
70001429.description: A piece by Roberto Campin. He was one of the first painters to use oil-based colours. This work shows Saint Veronica wiping the face of Jesus and the image of Jesus appearing on the cloth.

70001430.name: Wolverine
70001430.description: This animal has a short and stocky body. It uses its muscular jaws to bite through frozen meat or bone. It can travel quickly over soft snow without sinking in.

70001431.name: Ternate Island
70001431.description: An island that produces the precious spice called clove. On this island is the Sultanate of Ternate, which has accumulated immense wealth due to the clove trade. Ternate is a fierce rival of the Sultanate of Tidore and they are continually looking for an advantage over the other.

quests.name: Small island that makes great wealth

70001432.name: Halmahera Island
70001432.description: An island located east of Ternate. The north is under the control of the Sultanate of Ternate; the south is under the control of the Sultanate of Tidore. The island is covered by a dense forest jungle. Population is low due to the frequency of febrile disease in the area.

70001433.name: Mekong Delta
70001433.description: Located at the inlet of the Mekong River, this marshy area has innumerable islands. In the same way as a delta, sand conveyed by the Mekong river built up over time to form the islands. For this reason, many of these small islands are rather flat and will be submerged during the rainy season.

70001434.name: Sulu Archipelago
70001434.description: Islands on the northeast coast of Borneo. This primarily Islamic kingdom was established in ancient times and gradually spread it's influence over the nearby islands. Because the Spanish have begun using Manila as a base in recent years, this kingdom has been encouraging pirates in order to resist being overwhelmed.

70001435.name: Palau Islands
70001435.description: A group of islands located east of the island of Mindanao. Since it is made up of very tiny islands it is not suitable for agriculture. The island people have learned the position of these islands and there is a frequent exchange of resources between the different islands.

quests.name: Plan to Sail Across the Pacific

70001436.name: Bali Island
70001436.description: An island located east of the island of Java. Although there is an increasing number of countries converting to Islam, a unique Hindu religion is spreading on the island of Bali.

70001437.name: Kuching
70001437.description: A town located on the west coast of the center part of Borneo. It is under the control of the Kingdom of Brunei, which is centered on Brunei in the northeast. Kuching means cat in the native language.

70001438.name: Davao City
70001438.description: A town located at the south coast of Mindanao. The stable climate in Mindanao is perfect for agriculture. Furthermore, with mountains on the sea side, Davao is not subject to the influence of storms.

70001439.name: Dili
70001439.description: A town located on the northern coast of the eastern part of Timor. Known for its sandalwood industry, Timor has long been visited by many merchant ships. In recent years, European merchant ships have become more common.

70001440.name: Jambi
70001440.description: The Jambi people's town in Central Sumatra. Surrounded by a tropical rain forest, traffic in lumber is prospering. It is heavily influenced by Islam, but you can still find Buddhist structures outside of town, resulting in a mixed history and culture.

70001441.name: Jolo
70001441.description: In the second half of the 15th century, an Islamic country called the Sultanate of Sulu was created, centered on this island. In recent years, the Spanish has advanced into this area, but the Sultanate of Sulu is still strongly resisting them.

70001442.name: Buffalo Fish
70001442.description: A fish with a large beak and which kicks up excrement like a cloud. It is related to the swimming parrot fish.

70001443.name: Oriental Flying Gurnard
70001443.description: A fish with a large, beautiful pectoral fin. It glides through the water using its pectoral fin.

70001444.name: Giant Grouper
70001444.description: A giant grouper found throughout the south Pacific and Indian oceans. It can reach up to several meters in length.

70001445.name: Emerald Bass
70001445.description: A relative of the grouper with a brightly coloured body.

70001446.name: Giant Australian Cuttlefish
70001446.description: A large sepiida that lives in southern oceans. It camouflages itself in its surrounding environment like a chameleon.

70001447.name: Barramundi
70001447.description: A species of giant perch found from southeast Asia to Australia.

70001448.name: Red Emperor
70001448.description: A relative of the star snapper or lutjanus stellatus that lives around Australia. It is quite delicious.

70001449.name: Mangrove Red Snapper
70001449.description: A relative of the lutjanus stellatus often found in tropical mangrove forests. It is red coloured and has sharp teeth.

70001450.name: Red Sunfish
70001450.description: This fish is found throughout tropical areas and temperate seas. It has a large disc-shaped body that can grow to over 2 meters in size.

70001451.name: Isla Grande Tierra del Fuego
70001451.description: An island located at the southern edge of the South American continent. Fuego is Spanish for flame. The original inhabitants, the Yahgan, were half naked, even though the island is extremely cold. For that reason, they never let their fires go out, so the name was given to the island.

70001452.name: Tahiti
70001452.description: An island northeast of Aotearoa. You can find black sandy beaches on the coast there. The people that live on this island have elaborately designed tattoos, like the people on Aotearoa. Their languages are also very similar. I wonder if this is Hawaiki?

70001453.name: Glacier
70001453.description: Glaciers are formed out of snow that accumulates between mountains and then repeatedly melts and freezes or that turns to ice due to its own weight and which compacts over the space of many years. Glaciers move down at an extremely slow speed.

70001454.name: The Sahara
70001454.description: An expansive desert that covers the northern portion of the African continent. In Arabic, it means rough land. Pottery has been unearthed in many locations so we can see that people have been living here in the desert since ancient times. Caravans using camels promoted trade throughout the desert.

70001455.name: Solomon's Ring
70001455.description: A ring said to have been owned by Solomon, the son of David, king of ancient Israel. It is said that the person who wears this ring can talk to animals.

70001456.name: The Ten Commandments
70001456.description: Stone tablets inscribed with the ten commandments said to have been given to Moses by God, in the Old Testament. The Bible says that they were stored in the Ark of the Covenant.

70001457.name: The Clay Tablet of Zerubbabel
70001457.description: Clay tablets written with wedge-shaped characters. As it is not stone, it is thought that it was not meant to be permanent. The name of Zerubbabel, King of the Kingdom of Judah and the one who orchestrated the reconstruction of the Jerusalem temple, can be found on the tables.

70001458.name: Warrior's Tomb
70001458.description: A tomb on the outskirts of Beirut. An epitaph is inscribed, but it is no longer legible due to erosion. Because there are rusted weapons buried in the vicinity, it is thought to have been the tomb of a warrior.

70001459.name: Ahu Tongariki Moai
70001459.description: The 15 Moai statues on the northeast side of the island of Rapa Nui. All 15 statues are facing the same direction. They are some of the larger Moai on the island at around three times the height of a grown man.

quests.name: Investigation of statues of Rano Raraku

70001461.name: The Santa Maria
70001461.description: The Nao that served as the flag ship for the first voyage of the explorer Cristobal Colon. On Christmas of 1492, after crossing the Atlantic Ocean, Colon ran this ship aground on a hidden reef on Hispaniola Island. Crippled, it sunk.

70001462.name: The Capitana
70001462.description: The caravel that served as the flag ship for the magnificent fourth voyage by Cristobal Colon. One year after being shipwrecked in a collision with the Bermuda, it was salvaged by Diego Mendes and then abandoned in the Santa Gloria Bay.

70001463.name: Vincente Pinzon Expedition Ship
70001463.description: A caravel belonging to the group of ships owned by Vicente Yanez Pinzon who sailed to South America. After reaching Saint Roche Cape, the fleet ran into a storm and was shipwrecked its way to Palos after passing the Windward Passage.

70001464.name: Saint Raphael
70001464.description: A carrack commanded by Paolo da Gama, brother of Vasco da Gama. Faced with a severe shortage of crew members due to scurvy, Paolo abandoned this ship on the southern coast of Mombasa on his way back from finding a passage to India.

70001465.name: Agostino Barbarigo's Trade Ship
70001465.description: One of the vessels of the galley trading fleet commanded by Nicolo Barbarigo. After leaving Alexandria, and on route to Venice for Christmas, it was sunk near Urbo Island.

70001466.name: The Anne
70001466.description: A trade ship that was shipwrecked off the shores of the Peloponnese peninsula. After delivering pilgrims to Jaffa, it was shipwrecked on its way back to England.

70001467.name: The Conceicao
70001467.description: The official name is the Nossa Senhora da Conceicao. An east Indian trading vessel from Portugal; it carried the king's treasure to India. It sank near the Chagos Islands.

70001468.name: The Saint Benedict
70001468.description: An east Indian trading vessel from Portugal. It sank near the rocky reef of Pedro dos Valcos off the southeast coast of Africa.

70001469.name: The Estrela
70001469.description: Nossa Senhora da Estrela. An east Indian trading vessel from Portugal that was shipwrecked in the northwest of Ascension Island in the Atlantic Ocean.

70001470.name: The Appian Way
70001470.description: A road built during the time of the Roman Republic that extended from Rome to the south eastern coast of the Italian peninsula. Among Roman roads, this is the oldest and said to be the most beautiful.

quests.name: Do all roads lead to Rome?

70001471.name: Equestrian Spear of Guesclin
70001471.description: A lance said to have been used by a French soldier active at the beginning of the Hundred Years' War. Guesclin was born the son of a castellan in the Bretagne region. As a youngster he was a rough child that liked playing war and jousting matches, and later he beat the English army with agile tactics using mercenary soldiers.

70001472.name: Kanishka's Reliquary Container
70001472.description: A container holding the bones of King Kanishka who brought about the greatest period of prosperity for the Kushan Empire. The cover of the bronze container has Brahma-Deva and the three images of the Sakra devanam Indra mounted on it. The statue is from the earliest period of Buddhist designs created in the Ghandharan region.

70001473.name: Nilometer
70001473.description: Facilities for measuring water level setup all around the Nile river. Once a year, the Nile river floods the region dealing a heavy blow to farms downstream, so it is necessary to detect the flood as early as possible. However, it is said that these floods bring rich, black earth from downstream.

70001474.name: The Bread of Pompeii
70001474.description: Bread found in Pompeii after the city was destroyed by a volcanic eruption. This bread was covered by volcanic ash and miraculously preserved. It is dried and completely black, and appears to have been cut with a knife into eight equal parts. Perhaps they were just about to have dinner...

70001475.name: The Little Street
70001475.description: A landscape by Vermeer. It is said to have been a picture of his hometown of Delft, where he spent the majority of his life. He drew everything, including the minutest detail; he drew the seams between bricks, and the bolts on the doors. Extremely realistic, it looks as if he's captured an instant of time.

70001476.name: Judith
70001476.description: A painting by Giorgione. He used the Book of Judith from the Old Testament as his subject. In her right hand is a sword, and at her feet is the head of the enemy leader Holophernes. There is no feel of presence from Judith's facial expression, colours or touch, but there is a feeling of holiness and solemnity projected.

70001477.name: Banquet for the Prodigal Son
70001477.description: A painting of a figure by Rembrandt. Said to be based on the Biblical story of the Prodigal son spending money on prostitutes. The dark and unclear touch which is uncharacteristic of Rembrandt gives the impression he is actually looking at something realistic beyond his subject.

70001478.name: The Samoa Islands
70001478.description: The island chain located northeast of the Fiji Islands. There are two main islands; Savai'i and Upolo. Both islands are volcanic with beautiful coral reefs lining the coasts.

70001479.name: Lewis Chessmen
70001479.description: A chess piece carved from a walrus tusk. Given its shape, it is thought to have been created in the 12th century in Norway or Sweden.

70001480.name: Pounamu Axe
70001480.description: Pounamu is the Maori word meaning jade. The Maori did not have iron, but they carved axes, clubs, and neck decorations out of jade due to its hard consistency. This axe was used in ceremonies and has a blade made of Pounamu.

70001482.name: The Bismarck Archipelago
70001482.description: Islands in the waters northeast of New Guinea. The largest island is New Britain that stretches from the south to the east of the archipelago. Most of the islands are volcanic and damage from eruptions is common.

70001483.name: The Bass Strait
70001483.description: The strait between the Australian continent and Tasmania. It is known as a difficult area to sail due to the narrow passage and shallow waters. The formation of these straits is part of the oral traditions of the native inhabitants.

quests.name: Between the island and the land

70001484.name: The Jelling Stones
70001484.description: Stone markers erected by Harald the Bluetooth, the king of Denmark in the 10th century. These markers tell in Runic letters the great accomplishments of Harald the Bluetooth who unified Denmark, conquered Norway, and converted the Danish people to Christianity.

70001485.name: The Great Sphinx of Giza
70001485.description: A giant statue sitting next to the pyramid at Giza. It has the head of a pharaoh and the body of a lion. In ancient Egypt it embodied the glory of the great pharaoh. On the other hand, in Greek mythology, it was considered a monster, with the face of a woman, the body of a lion, and the wings of a falcon.

70001486.name: Poi
70001486.description: A tool constructed of a ball filled with thistles and woven flax tied to a rope. Used by women during the unique Maori dance called the Haka. Also, the Poi is considered a lucky item indicating fertility.

70001487.name: Terme del Foro
70001487.description: A public bathhouse built in Pompeii, one of the ancient Roman cities. It has several bathrooms with different water temperatures as well as changing rooms.

quests.name: Additional Survey of the Ruins of Pompeii
Additional Survey of the Ruins of Pompeii

70001488.name: Tophet
70001488.description: One of the ruins of ancient Carthage. Thought to be a place of worship for deities such as Baal Hammon and Tanit, the site is full of gravestones.

quests.name: Customs Related to a Holy Place

70001489.name: Nautilus
70001489.description: A mollusc that resembles the face of a person wearing a suit of armour. It captures its prey using its dozens of tentacles. It moves by shooting water out of what is thought to be its mouth.

70001490.name: Sea Lily
70001490.description: A creature found in the sea. It sinks its roots on the floor of the deep ocean and gently rock in the waves. It looks more like a land plant than a sea plant such as sea weed. But as it is mobile and can move through the sea, it is highly likely that it is an animal.

70001491.name: Moray Eel
70001491.description: It lives in warm, shallow waters. It is long and narrow with small fins, and looks like a fat snake. When an enemy approaches, it will open its mouth wide to intimidate them and can bite with very sharp teeth. There is no fixed body pattern or colouring and there are many different types.

70001492.name: The Gerona
70001492.description: The official name is La Gerona. Part of the Spanish fleet sent to attack England. The fleet was beaten by the British Navy. The Gerona hit a rocky reef off the Irish coast while trying to escape and sank.

70001493.name: Saint Paul
70001493.description: A large, sturdy Portuguese ship, and one of the east Indian trade vessels. While heading toward India, it took the passage east of Madagascar but was blown by winds along the way and was shipwrecked off the west coast of Sumatra.

70001494.name: The Chagas
70001494.description: The official name is Las Cinque Chagas. An East Indian Trading vessel out of Portugal. On its way back from India, it was attacked by English pirates near the Azores and sunk.

70001495.name: Cape Leeuwin
70001495.description: A cape on the southwestern part of Australia. It has a beautiful landscape with a sweeping view of the Indian Ocean and the Antarctic Ocean. The surrounding land is abundantly green, even though it is found on the drought struck western side of the Australian continent. The area is rich in mineral resources.

quests.name: Aim for the south west tip

70001496.name: Cephalotus
70001496.description: Endemic to Australia, this carnivorous plant has multiple leaves shaped like small bottles with lids. Insects fall into the bottle shaped leaves and dissolve inside after some time. The plant might derive its nutrition from insects.

70001497.name: Common Sundew
70001497.description: This plant lives in warm bogs. The leaves exude a sticky liquid from the many hairs that grow on it. Insects get stuck on the sticky liquid and the leaf slowly contracts to close in around the insect. The insect, trapped inside, is slowly dissolved.

70001498.name: Moa
70001498.description: A flight-less bird that lives in the forest of Aotearoa. At first glance it looks like an ostrich, but there are no wings. It can grow to be a giant of over 4 meters tall. Reports indicate a sizable population at one time, but as people began to live on the island, its numbers have dramatically reduced.

70001499.name: Haast's Eagle
70001499.description: A large eagle living in Aotearoa. Large specimens can have a wing span of 3 meters, making it one of the largest eagle types. It seems to mainly eat moa. Its numbers have dwindled due to the drop in moa numbers.

70001500.name: Red Panda
70001500.description: This animal lives in mountain forests from India to southeast Asia. Its fur is bronze-coloured, its four legs and stomach are black and its face has white patterns. Its tail is fluffy and has ringed stripes. It is good at climbing trees and sleeps in the trees during the day. The name panda comes from one that eats bamboo in the local language.

70001501.name: Crocodile Monitor
70001501.description: A large lizard that can grow to exceed 4m. Its body is slim, but also long. Its tail makes up two thirds of its size. It lives in the trees and has a ferocious temperament, so it is known as the crocodile of the forest.

quests.name: Dragon that lives in the forest
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70001502.name: Saw Shark
70001502.description: This shark has narrow features from its eyes to its mouth, and has varying sizes of saw-like projections around the edge. It mainly lives at the bottom of warm seas, and gets its food by sticking its long and narrow mouth into the silt at the bottom. Although it appears aggressive, it's actually quite timid. It is quite delicious.

70001503.name: Kahawai
70001503.description: A fish that lives in the sea near Aotearoa. It looks like a cross between a perch and a salmon. Large specimens can be as long as 90 cm. It's meat is thick with fat and delicious.

70001504.name: K'gari
70001504.description: A town located on the east coast of Australia. It means heaven in the native language. The name is certainly apt, with its sandy beaches stretching 100 km north to south, and a lake with the clearest water in the world found in its inland forest region.

70001505.name: Pinjarra
70001505.description: A town located near the southwest coast of Australia. The town's name comes from the local language indicating the low humidity of the nearby region. With the inland southwest region of Australia having mines with abundant amounts of iron and gold, this town has become a point of interest as the port for these exports.

70001506.name: Octopus Amphora
70001506.description: A pot found in the ruins of the island of Crete. The pot is a type of amphora and was used for carrying and storing alcohol and oil. The pictures are drawn with a sophisticated style and with graceful lines. Living things from the sea, such as octopi, are food and symbols of wealth for island people who are surrounded by the sea.

quests.name: A shadow from the age of king Minos

70001507.name: Stone Pillar of the Celtic Cross
70001507.description: A cross similar to many found in ruins on Ireland. The cross is carved from a large stone with a circular ring, and has Celtic designs all over it. They say a circular ring was placed on the crucifix because the cultures joined after the Celts came in contact with Christianity.

70001508.name: Tara's Brooch
70001508.description: A brooch created in Ireland in the 8th century. This penannular gold brooch has gems and is carved with Celtic designs. It was used to pin a cape, similar to those worn by monks. It is said to be the crown jewel of Ireland's goldworks.

70001509.name: Baroque Pearl Pendant
70001509.description: A pendant combining carved, luxurious designs and an unusually shaped pearl. The designs have natural, animal, and mythological themes. The baroque name comes from the Portuguese for distorted pearl.

70001510.name: The Witte Leo
70001510.description: A Dutch East Indian trading vessel whose name means white lion. It was attacked by a Portuguese carrack on its way back home while filled with spices from East Asia, and sunk off Saint Helena.

70001511.name: The Solenn
70001511.description: A Swedish vessel that participated in the battle between Poland and Sweden that erupted in the Danzig sea. It was attacked by the Polish fleet's flagship. When it seemed that it was about to be seized, explosives were used to sink it.

70001512.name: The Bom Jesus
70001512.description: A Portuguese vessel used tor trade with East Indian. On the way from Lisbon to India, it ran aground on hidden coral east of Madagascar and sank.

70001513.name: Arco Di Constantino
70001513.description: An arch built to celebrate a triumphal return after battle in the time of the Roman Empire. It is said to commemorate Constantine I's victory over Maxentius.

70001514.name: Trireme of the Ancient Greek Navy
70001514.description: A ship used by the ancient Greeks during the Persian wars. The oars were arranged in 3 tiers, giving it great mobility. It successfully out sailed the great Persian navy.

70001515.name: The Spear of Baibars
70001515.description: A spear said to have been owned by Baibars, a Sultan of the Mamluk dynasty. Baibars won many battles against the Crusaders and Mongols and had many great achievements such as creating an infrastructure for domestic affairs. Baibars himself was a great warrior, and is said to have particularly excelled at horsemanship.

70001516.name: Sumerian Chariot
70001516.description: A chariot created by the city-state Sumeria of ancient Mesopotamia. It had four wheels and no spokes in the wheels; it was pulled by a mule and the person riding it would wield his spear for battle.

70001517.name: Hittite Chariot
70001517.description: A chariot created by the ancient Hittite kingdom of Anatolia. Wit had two wheels and six-spokes in the wheels; it was pulled by a horse and the person riding it would wield a bow in battle.

70001518.name: Gladiator's Helmet
70001518.description: Gladiators were fighters that fought in front of crowds in arenas in ancient Rome. Many prisoners taken in battle became gladiators, but some citizens of Rome also became gladiators. The tyrannical and famous Emperor Commodus also wanted to be a gladiator.

70001519.name: Golden Breastplate
70001519.description: A breastplate thought to have been taken as a war trophy when the Carthaginian army fought the Roman army. Even elite Roman soldiers of the day were only given bronze equipment, so only people with a high rank wore this.

70001520.name: Sculptured Group of Soldiers
70001520.description: Bronze statues of soldiers unearthed from the Obelisk of Byblos. It is thought to have been a gift from Egypt. Egypt imported Lebanese cedar for creating mummies and as building material. It is said they made many such offerings in order to keep Emperor Byblos happy.

70001521.name: Phoenician Glass Jar
70001521.description: The Phoenicians were very talented, and created many artworks for trade. They made many glass products from their silicon rich sand. It is thought that they learned glass production from Egypt, which indicates a close relationship with the same.

70001522.name: Crystal Pitcher
70001522.description: A crystal carafe given to a Caliph of the Fatimid dynasty. It is made so thin you can hardly believe that it is made of crystal; the carvings are exquisite. You can clearly see the high technology of Islam.

70001523.name: Ancient Greek Clothing
70001523.description: Clothing worn by the ancient Greeks, called chiton. Chiton was a single piece of cloth held together by a pin. The Doric style involves wrapping the cloth around the body, while the Ionic style has the sides sown up and worn like a pull on. An overcoat called a Chlamys was draped over this.

70001524.name: Civic Crown
70001524.description: One of the ancient Roman compensation systems; a crown given to a citizen who saved the life of a Roman citizen. A crown made of gold was bestowed for other reasons, but this civic crown made of oak leaves was the higher honor. Only those who had received this award were granted permission to make gold versions of this award.

quests.name: Proof of having saved a Roman citizen
Proof of having saved a Roman citizen
Proof of having saved a Roman citizen
Proof of having saved a Roman citizen

70001525.name: Golden Horn Chain
70001525.description: A thick chain laid by the Byzantine Empire to hinder the advancement of the Ottoman military ships in the Constantinople wars. The Ottoman army was unable to break these chains. But they dealt the Byzantine Empire a heavy blow by carrying their ships overland in a surprise attack.

70001526.name: Rhomphair
70001526.description: A sword with a long handle and blade used by the ancient Thracian people. The blade was sometimes curved and could be used to slash.

70001527.name: The Atacama Giant
70001527.description: A geoglyph of approximately 80 meters in length. It was drawn by using black stones to create the contours then digging out the inside to make it flat. The land was not level and the drawing was created on the side of a slope...perhaps this glyph had some intended purpose.

70001528.name: The Relief of Viracocha
70001528.description: Viracocha is the sun god worshiped by the Incan Empire. He is drawn as a large man with white skin and a beard and is said to have given civilization to the people. After doing so, he disappeared across the water from the edge of the lake of Cuzco.

quests.name: The god descended upon a lake

70001529.name: The Royal Inca Mummy
70001529.description: In the Incan Empire, the bodies of the royal family were mummified and retained their authority even after death. That is why there was little revolt against the king in the Incan Empire. The mummy was dressed in the same clothes they wore when they were alive, were given food, and said to communicate with the other mummies of kings.

70001530.name: The Statue of Mictlantecuhtli
70001530.description: According to Aztec mythology, Mictlantecuhtli is the ruler of the underworld. He was drawn as a scary figure, for example as a bloody skeleton with protruding teeth.

quests.name: God who sleeps in Aztec underworld

70001531.name: Tapac Yauri
70001531.description: A stave said to have been given by Inti, Incan god of the sun, to the first Emperor of the Incan Empire. Inti ordered them to build a temple to the sun where the stave sank into the ground. The stave was said to have landed in none other than Cuzco, the capital of the Incan empire.

70001532.name: The Statue of Lanzon
70001532.description: An idol with the head of a jaguar, hair of snakes, and the body of a human. To the Incan people, the jaguar was a deity, but it was never drawn combined with a human. Perhaps some other tribe in the vicinity of Lima had a high civilization prior to the Inca.

70001533.name: The Gold Mask of Naymlap
70001533.description: Before the Incan Empire, there was a city state with a highly developed civilization in the vicinity of Lambayeque. Naymlap is the legendary king described in the legends of this city state. It was said that he appeared with a fleet of ships from the south, and after he died, he grew wings and flew away.

quests.name: Gold in the shape of a god
Gold in the shape of a god
Gold in the shape of a god

70001534.name: The Shroud of Turin
70001534.description: The linen shroud said to have wrapped the body of Christ. You can clearly see the shape of the body of a scarred man in the shroud. Surprisingly, the scars match perfectly with the description of Jesus' death found in the Bible.

70001535.name: The Statue of Nonmo
70001535.description: Nonmo is the god of creation for the Dogon people that live in the northeast area of Africa. The upper torso is human, the lower is depicted as that of a snake.

70001536.name: Pachamama Statue
70001536.description: A goddess that represents mother earth in the native language. The god of fertility and the mother of all creation. After the spread of Christianity, it became identified with the Virgin Mary and became the subject of worship.

quests.name: The Andes' mother god of the Earth

70001537.name: The Book of Enoch
70001537.description: One of the Apocrypha of the Old Testament. Enoch was the great grandfather of Noah, and has the meaning he who follows. According to the Book of Enoch, Enoch was taken into heaven by God and was then transformed into the angel Metatron.

70001538.name: The Septuagint
