70001538.description: A generic name for the Bible as translated from Hebrew into Greek. The Greek bible was started since many Jews had not learned Hebrew due to the expeditions of Alexander the Great.

70001539.name: Gold Discus
70001539.description: A gold raft said to be used in rituals by the Chibcha people. In the ritual, the chief of the people would paint himself in gold dust on a moonlit night and jump from the raft into the lake.

70001540.name: Gold Ornament of Royal Chimu
70001540.description: A burial accessory of the royal family of the Chimu Dynasty that existed in the Andes mountains prior to the Incan Empire. Their high level of metallurgical technology predated the Incan Empire.

70001541.name: Saint's Body Brought to Venice
70001541.description: A painting representative of the St. Mark paintings, a series drawn for the Scuola Grande of San Marco chapel. People are drawn by the intense contrast. The painting gives a sense of tension by combining an adept use of perspective and realism.

quests.name: Painting of faithful saveing Saint Mark
Painting of faithful saveing Saint Mark
Painting of faithful saveing Saint Mark

70001542.name: Saliera
70001542.description: A gold salt cellar with impressive carvings. A work by the artist Benvenuto Cellini a representative artist of the Renaissance. It is called the Mona Lisa of sculpture because of its extremely lush and exquisite carving.

70001543.name: Painters, Sculptors, & Architects
70001543.description: A history of artists described by Giorgio Vasari. The full title is Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects. The lives of 133 artists are described. He was multi-talented and worked as a writer, painter, and architect and his evaluation of artists was revered. This is first class material for art historians.

70001544.name: Durer's Rhinoceros
70001544.description: A wood engraving by Albrecht Durer. It was drawn in minute detail as though it were sketched, but Durer himself had never seen a Rhino. This piece alone is proof of Durer's incomparable imagination and expressiveness.

quests.name: Imaginative power far beyond the norm
Imaginative power far beyond the norm
Imaginative power far beyond the norm

70001545.name: The Vitruvian Man
70001545.description: Da Vinci rethought the perspective on people shown by Vitruvius, the ancient Roman architect, and represented it graphically. Da Vinci uses this drawing to try to draw people realistically.

70001546.name: The Baptism of Jesus
70001546.description: A painting by Da Vinci's mentor, Andrea del Verrocchio. However, Da Vinci drew the background and the little angel in the left side of this painting. Verrocchio was so taken by the beauty of the angel that he is said to have never painted again.

70001547.name: Dutch Proverbs
70001547.description: A work by Pieter Brueghel the Elder. He drew over 90 proverbs that were told in the Netherlands. For example, there is a man that has spilled his porridge at the bottom right. This proverb means, Once something is done it cannot be undone.

quests.name: Collection of proverbs using no text

70001548.name: Melancholia
70001548.description: A copper engraving said to be a representative work of Albrecht Durer. There are a variety of objects used in daily life in this painting such as spheres and polyhedrals to hourglasses and scales. Only Durer himself knows what these represent.

70001549.name: Equestrian Statue Gattamelata
70001549.description: Gattamelata was a condottiere active in the latter half of the 12th century to the first half of the 13th century. He had many military glories such as defeating Venice in the battle with Visconti. This bronze statue pays tribute to his glories, and was made by Donatello.

70001550.name: Salome's Veil
70001550.description: This is thought to be princess Salome who appears in a passage from the Bible. When offered a reward for her beautiful dance using veils, she asked for John the Baptist's head on a platter.

70001551.name: Hair Ornament of Sarka
70001551.description: Sarka is a woman found in the legends of Bohemia. Betrayed by her lover, she swore revenge on all men, but in the end she fell in love again. A long time saying of Bohemia is long-haired women have a vicious temper. This matches with the legend of Sarka.

70001552.name: Arabesque Water Bottle
70001552.description: A drinking flask for pilgrims to the holy land, made during the Dawla al-Mamalik era. A drinking flask was essential for the pilgrims, but this is also a wonderful piece of art.

70001553.name: Sakuntala
70001553.description: A drama written by Kalidasa during the Gupta Empire based on the Mahabharata. The Sanskrit title translates roughly to The Recognition of Sakuntala.

70001554.name: Black Prince's Ruby
70001554.description: This gemstone known as spinel, not ruby, is over 100 carats. It is said that Edward the Black Prince received it as a reward when he aided the Kingdom of Castile during their civil war.

70001555.name: Kohinur
70001555.description: A large diamond whose name means Mountain of light in Persian. It is said to have been more than 800 carats in size. It was owned by generations of Indian kings, but after the change in the Mughal Empire to the Safaviyan Dynasty it was lost.

70001556.name: Newly-wed Sari
70001556.description: Clothing worn by Indian women by wrapping it around their bodies. In India, it is convention that newly wed brides may only wear a red sari.

70001557.name: Jewelled Armour
70001557.description: A suit of armour decorated with silver, gold, and jewels. Its weight and strength make it impractical to use. An aristocrat indulging in extravagance.

70001558.name: Longbows
70001558.description: A bow, developed since ancient times through hunting and war. It's called a longbow, 1.2 metres in length and is distinct from the short bow, used by nomads on grassy plains. In the Battle of Crecy, the longbow men positioned on high ground rendered the cavalry helpless.

70001559.name: Laurel Wreath
70001559.description: A crown made of plaited laurel branches with leaves. According to Greek mythology, Daphne, who refused Apollo's advances, turned into a laurel tree. The disappointed Apollo made a crown from the branches and wore it all his life.

70001560.name: Arabian Furniture
70001560.description: This first class piece of furniture is adorned with the crowded geometric and floral designs characteristic of arabesque. Both the cushioning and outer fabric are of the highest quality. It gives a sense of the high quality workmanship in Islamic culture.

quests.name: Furniture of the world of Islam

70001561.name: Tapu y Alca
70001561.description: This means green stone in the Quechuan language and refers to raw emerald stones. The chief of the Chibcha tribe in the northern Andes used it in rituals.

70001562.name: The Cutlass of Mamluk
70001562.description: A cutlass is a sword with a curved spine. It is small and easy to handle; famous for being the pirates' weapon of choice. They say that it was also used by the Mamluk cavalry, who were known for their spear handling and archery.

70001563.name: Silver and Ruby Earrings
70001563.description: Earrings that a wealthy merchant gave his wife as a present. Silver and rubies are difficult to come by in Europe. An aristocrat must have had this made.

70001564.name: Quipu
70001564.description: The method of recording information in the Incan Empire. Numbers were recorded as knots in string. Only experts could decipher it and the messengers were known as Chasquis.

70001565.name: Quena
70001565.description: A flute made from bamboo, reeds, or animal bone. It is essential for music in Incan ceremonies and as such, is quite a powerful instrument. Although easy to make, it is very difficult to play.

quests.name: Festival flute of the New World

70001566.name: The Divine Comedy
70001566.description: An epic poem by the Italian poet, Dante Alighieri. It is comprised of three parts, Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise. The main character is Dante himself who journeys through hell and purgatory, finally arriving in heaven. It is regarded as a masterpiece of classical Italian literature.

70001567.name: Calafate
70001567.description: A tree found in Patagonia in South America. It gives bloom to numerous small flowers with purple seeds. It is said that one who eats calafate seeds will return to the land of the calafate.

70001568.name: Cantuta
70001568.description: A tree that grows wild in the high reaches of the Andes. It puts forth brilliantly coloured, bell shaped flowers of red and yellow. The local name for it is sacred flower of the Incas.

70001569.name: Titan Arum
70001569.description: A large flower that easily stands taller than a person, at 3 metres, with a diameter of up to 1.5 metres. It grows in the rain forests of Indonesia on the island of Sumatra. It blossoms for only a few days every few years. The stench of this flower has earned it the name corpse flower.

70001570.name: Edelweiss
70001570.description: An alpine plant that grows in the mountains in Europe. The white petals of this star shaped flower are covered in cilia, such that it appears to have a frosting of snow. It doesn't break apart when it withers and leaves behind a clean white flower. Adored locally as a noble flower because of its rarity.

ornaments.name: Edelweiss with White Urn on Table

70001571.name: Titan Beetle
70001571.description: The titan beetle. As large as an adult's palm, with sharp mandibles and hooks. The larvae is half as large again. There are no other beetles in its genus. It inhabits the South American rain forest.

70001572.name: Lantern Fly
70001572.description: An insect that lives in the Yucatan Peninsula. Its open wings resemble a moth's, but the body is like a cicada. It has an unusually large head, which when viewed from the side, looks like an alligator.

70001573.name: Giant Fiddler Beetle
70001573.description: An insect that inhabits the tropical rain forests of South East Asia, and looks like a violin. It's large among insects, about 10cm long. It is often found near a particular type of mushroom.

70001574.name: Leaf Insect
70001574.description: An insect which resembles the leaves of a plant. This is a characteristic of the adult female and even the eggs it lays look like plant seeds. It prefers to feed on the leaves of fruit trees in southern countries and inhabits the tropical forests of Australia, South-east Asia, and India.

70001575.name: Man-Faced Stinkbug
70001575.description: A type of Pentatomoidea that inhabits South East Asia. Upside down it looks like a face. Individual beetles look like they are either laughing or crying.

70001576.name: Black Swan
70001576.description: The black swan. Unlike the migratory white swan, it spends its whole life in one place. It nests by the water's edge in lakes and marshes, primarily in Australia and Aotearoa.

70001577.name: Naked Mole Rat
70001577.description: A hairless rat with large front teeth. A single adult looks like a mammalian infant. It lives in groups in underground burrows. The child bearing female and the worker male occupy distinct roles in the community. It inhabits arid regions of East Africa.

70001578.name: Degu
70001578.description: An animal twice as large as a rat that resembles a squirrel. It appears to socialize through diverse calls, as though it is singing. It inhabits rocky cliffs in the cold, high reaches of the Andes.

70001579.name: Beaver
70001579.description: A type of animal that resides in the watersides of woods in North America. Having webs on their hands, they mostly live around the waters. The beaver works as a keystone species in an ecosystem by creating wetlands that are used by many other species. Next to humans, no other extant animal appears to do more to shape its landscape. Their colonies create one or more dams to provide still, deep water to protect against predators, and to float food and building material.

70001580.name: Wisent
70001580.description: A large land animal that lives in the deep forests of Europe. It resembles a cow, but is taller, at just under 2 metres. It can be seen on grassy plains, near places with lots of water, and on hills. It has been hunted since ancient times. Numbers are falling due to years of hunting and deforestation.

70001581.name: Quagga
70001581.description: This animal lives in arid regions of South Africa. The front portion of its body has the same design as that of a zebra. From the stomach to the rear it is a dark brown and its four limbs are white. It's name comes from an attempt to mimic its cry. Herds of these used to cover the savanna, but the numbers have decreased with the advent of colonies.

70001582.name: Electric Catfish
70001582.description: A catfish that produces electricity. It has small round eyes and a tubular body. Although it appears quite charming, it uses its sting to emit a powerful jolt of electricity to stun and then eat prey such as small fish and crabs. It lives in freshwater lakes and the Nile River in North Africa.

70001583.name: Nile Bichir
70001583.description: A fish with a tubular body, covered in scales like a snake, with about 15 spines on its dorsal fin, a large caudal fin, and pectoral fins. It is about a metre in length and many are dark reddish-brown with deep green specks. A rare sight in tropical African rivers as well as the Nile.

70001584.name: Red Bichir
70001584.description: A fish with a flat head and a fat, tubular body covered in hard scales. With a wing-like dorsal fin, it has a unique appearance. It can live for over ten years. It inhabits the upper reaches of the Nile and other tropical African rivers.

70001585.name: Plecostomus
70001585.description: A freshwater catfish that live in the Amazon in South America. It eats the moss that grows on rocks and drift wood. It possesses a peculiar beauty, coming in a variety of body shapes, colours, and speckled designs. Despite its appearance, it has a pleasant taste.

70001586.name: Dorado
70001586.description: A large freshwater fish that resembles a shiny, gold salmon. An adult grows as long as a metre. From its appearance, it was given the Spanish name for gold, dorado. It has sharp teeth, powerful jaws, and a fierce temperament, leading it to also be known as the river tiger. It can be seen in South American rivers.

70001587.name: The Gulf of Guayaquil
70001587.description: A gulf on the North-west coast of the South American continent. On the southern shore is the city of Tumbes. Off the coast of the bay a warm current from the north and hits a cold current from the south.

70001588.name: The Humboldt Current
70001588.description: A cold current that flows from the southern tip of the South American continent, north along the western coast, up to the Gulf of Guayaquil. It is slow and extremely cold. Fish travelling north on this current make wide areas along the south-western coast of South America fertile fishing grounds.

70001589.name: The Atacama Desert
70001589.description: A long and narrow desert stretching north-south in the center of South America's west coast. Some areas only see rainfall once every few decades, making it prominent among the world's arid regions. One cannot see any vegetation, yet it is rich in mineral resources like copper, silver, and saltpetre.

70001590.name: Potosi Silver Mine
70001590.description: A mountain boasting massive deposits of silver ore in a corner of the Andes surrounded by mountains reaching over 4000m. Under these conditions, the possibility of mining and transporting silver is remote.

70001591.name: The Azuero Peninsula
70001591.description: A peninsula to the west of Panama Bay. The earthenware and gold work unearthed there distinguish this place from other regions. It appears that people lived here in ancient times and developed an independent culture.

70001592.name: Huayna Picchu
70001592.description: The peak on the northern side of Machu Picchu. In contrast to Machu Picchu, which means, old peak, Huayana Picchu means, young peak. Similarly, where Machu Picchu has a temple dedicated to the sun god, Huayana Picchu has a temple dedicated to the moon deity.

70001593.name: The Isthmus of Panama
70001593.description: An isthmus in Central America. At its narrowest point, there is only 64km between the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. Although it is not an unreasonable distance to build a canal, it is mountainous country with high rainfall and covered in dense forest. On top of that, construction would not be easy in a land with illnesses that produce high fevers.

quests.name: Place where north and south divide

70001594.name: The Darien Mountains
70001594.description: The mountain range that stretches from the north-west coast of South America to Central America. It is hot and humid and the densely forested mountains are constantly covered in mist. A veritable paradise of flora and fauna, with over 1000 varieties of orchid.

70001595.name: Buenaventura Bay
70001595.description: A bay south of Panama, on the north-west coast of South America. Mangrove forests grow to the south of the bay. The cold ocean current from the south turns west at a point south of the bay, resulting in relatively high humidity.

70001596.name: The Cordillera Occidental
70001596.description: A branch of the Andes. The Occidental range branches off the Andes, north of Copiapo, to the vicinity of Tumbes. The active volcanoes in this mountain range set it apart from the Andes.

70001597.name: Margarita Island
70001597.description: An island to the east of Caracas. On Colon's third voyage, he discovered Venezuela. Spain was quick to begin construction of a base on Margarita Island. The seas close to the island are rich in pearls, resulting in frequent pirate attacks.

70001598.name: The Bosphorus
70001598.description: The northernmost of the two channels separating Europe and the Anatolian Peninsula. During the battle of Constantinople, a fierce battle was fought over the Golden Horn in order to control the fast flowing waters of the channel. The Turkish army built fortresses along both shorelines as the first line of attack.

quests.name: Ebb and flow within a narrow sea
Ebb and flow within a narrow sea
Ebb and flow within a narrow sea

70001599.name: The Salar de Atacama
70001599.description: An expansive salt lake in the Atacama desert. The rocks on the shoreline are salt and look as though they have been dyed white. This lake is a place where flamingos come to rest their wings.

70001600.name: The Moon Valley
70001600.description: A belt of rock salt in the Atacama desert. There is absolutely no vegetation, and valleys are formed by hills of rock. They say that someone once said it looks like the moon in the sky, and this has stuck ever since.

70001601.name: El Tatio Geyser Field
70001601.description: A group of geysers in the Atacama desert, at an altitude of 450m. Hot water spouts from the earth and steam rises into the sky. It is truly an amazing place.

70001602.name: Lake Titicaca
70001602.description: A lake 3800m above sea level. It is called the lake in the sky. The story goes that the god of creation, Viracocha, came down to earth to make it. Around the lake are many ancient ruins.

quests.name: Lake upon which a god descended

70001603.name: The Buen Jesus
70001603.description: The ship of Captain Francisco de Ibarra and one of Spain's New World trading vessels. It was attacked and sunk by a Dutch naval commander, Oliver van Noordt, in the sea off Valparaiso.

70001604.name: The Shipwreck of Canete
70001604.description: A Spanish trading vessel on a return voyage from South America. It was sunk in a battle with a Dutch ship commanded by Captain Spielbergen.

70001605.name: The Flamengo
70001605.description: A vessel of the Portuguese East India Company. It hit a storm off the Cape of Good Hope on a return voyage and sank off San Tome.

70001606.name: Magellan American Adventures
70001606.description: A book thought to have been written by Magellan in South America during a break between voyages. It records information about the local natives.

quests.name: Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World
Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World
Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World
Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World
Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World
Records of a pioneer upon reaching west shore of New World

70001607.name: The Note of Admiral Colon
70001607.description: A segment of a report written by Admiral Colon upon his arrival at Portobelo. It appears to have been lost somehow during his investigation of the area.

70001608.name: Priest's Necklace
70001608.description: A necklace to be worn only by priests. It is finely crafted and has high value as a work of art, as well as important spiritual significance.

quests.name: Faith of the city of gold
Faith of the city of gold
Faith of the city of gold
Faith of the city of gold
Faith of the city of gold
Faith of the city of gold

70001609.name: Missionary Relic
70001609.description: An article from a deceased missionary who spread teachings in a foreign land. It is well known in Europe.

quests.name: Investigation of ideals in the region
Investigation of ideals in the region
Investigation of ideals in the region
Investigation of ideals in the region
Investigation of ideals in the region
Investigation of ideals in the region

70001610.name: The Robe of El Dorado
70001610.description: Robe that was brought back by a valiant adventurer who infiltrated a land thought to be El Dorado. It has clearly been made with superb skill and high quality material.

quests.name: Search for treasure of the city of gold
Search for treasure of the city of gold
Search for treasure of the city of gold
Search for treasure of the city of gold
Search for treasure of the city of gold
Search for treasure of the city of gold

70001611.name: Gold Earrings
70001611.description: Gold earrings that can be taken back home. As they are made by the unique skills of this area, they will be highly valuable in Europe.

quests.name: Pursuit of the missing investigation team
Pursuit of the missing investigation team
Pursuit of the missing investigation team
Pursuit of the missing investigation team
Pursuit of the missing investigation team
Pursuit of the missing investigation team

70001612.name: Mara
70001612.description: A rat that inhabits grassy plains in South America. It hops about. Male and female always move about together and remain so all their lives. The male is subservient to the female.

quests.name: Search for animal on west shore of New World
Search for animal on west shore of New World
Search for animal on west shore of New World
Search for animal on west shore of New World
Search for animal on west shore of New World
Search for animal on west shore of New World

70001613.name: Fringe-Lipped Bat
70001613.description: A bat that lives in the tropical rain forests of Central America. It takes its name from the wart-like protrusions on its lips and muzzle. It is known to eat frogs and its large ears are able to distinguish which frogs are poisonous just by the frog's call.

quests.name: Animal that does not succumb to poison
Investigation of ecology in the region
Investigation of ecology in the region
Investigation of ecology in the region
Investigation of ecology in the region
Investigation of ecology in the region
Investigation of ecology in the region

70001614.name: Cape Deseado
70001614.description: A cape on the west coast of the South American continent. The land formation here is very distinct from other areas, with fjords created by glaciers.

quests.name: Signpost to west shore of New World
Signpost to west shore of New World
Signpost to west shore of New World
Signpost to west shore of New World
Signpost to west shore of New World
Signpost to west shore of New World

70001615.name: The Chagres River
70001615.description: A river running from the South American inland to the Caribbean. If the river could be used to cross the isthmus, it could make passage much easier.

70001616.name: Tizona
70001616.description: The famous sword in The Lay of the Cid, was valued at 1000 marcos of gold and picked up by a Moroccan, General Bukal. The name means burning stick.

70001617.name: Colada del Cid
70001617.description: The famous sword in The Lay of the Cid, valued at over 1000 marcos of silver, acquired in a victorious battle with the Count of Barcelona.

70001618.name: Madonna in Garland Flowers
70001618.description: A collaborative work by Rubens and Jan Brueghel. Brueghel painted the wreath and Rubens the figures. It is classified as a still life by Brueghel, or Flower Breughel, and is a work that brings out the best of their respective talents.

quests.name: The correct station for an artist

70001619.name: Buffoon Playing a Lute
70001619.description: An individual portrait by Frans Hals. Hals was prolific in painting portraits that bring out individual character. With some influence from the Caravaggio style shading of mainstream genre works, the lively strokes bring out playful expressions.

70001620.name: The Music Lesson
70001620.description: By Vermeer. In this work, he uses perspective to distort the composition. In the mirror up high, the face of the lady at the instrument is directed towards the adjacent man. The inscription on the virginal reads, Music: companion of joy, balm for sorrow.

70001621.name: El Cantar de Mio Cid
70001621.description: Or the Lay of the Cid. A lyrical poem that depicts El Cid as the hero of the Reconquista. A blend of drama and history. The original manuscript was lost and various parts are missing from copies, so the actual title and author is unknown.

quests.name: Hero talked of since olden times

70001622.name: Cave of the Hands
70001622.description: Cave paintings by the indigenous people. It means, cave of many hands. In addition to hand patterns in red pigment, there are also depictions of local wild animals.

70001623.name: Ostracon
70001623.description: A fragment of pottery with inscriptions of letters and symbols. In Greek, it is an ostracon. It was used in voting to banish dictators. There are those who believe that this system led to the decline of Athens.

70001624.name: Kerch Vase
70001624.description: A pot made for a flourishing kingdom near Kaffa. The kingdom that imported these also produced imitations.

70001625.name: The Additions to Daniel
70001625.description: A portion of the Catholic canon, called by some the oldest mystery. The Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Holy Children, Suzanna, and Bel and the Dragon. The authorship of these chapters is unknown.

70001626.name: The Upanishads
70001626.description: One of the Hindu scriptures. Philosophical writings that have been called esoteric. The name is Sanskrit for passing wisdom down, with the implication being from teacher to disciple.

70001627.name: The Statue of Chico Quaja
70001627.description: The goddess of fields and waterways in Andean mythology. Believed to be the wife of the water god Pariacaca in a deified state.

quests.name: Theft of the goddess of fields

70001628.name: The Huarochiri Manuscript
70001628.description: A book by a missionary on mythology and traditions passed down in the Andes. Many myths are recorded, beginning with a fight between the water god Pariacaca and the fire god.

70001629.name: Adam and Eve
70001629.description: A copper engraving depicting a man, a woman, and animals, in a garden paradise. The earliest of Durer's four great copper engravings. The theme is original sin. It employs the proportions of the Vitruvius man and presents an early engraving of the ideal form.

70001630.name: The Four Holy Men
70001630.description: A painting by Durer of four apostles. You can almost hear the rustle of the clothing painted in vivid red and white. In the Christian religion, red is affection and white represents purity.

70001631.name: St. Mary of the Friars
70001631.description: One of Rubens altar pieces. It depicts the Virgin Mary ascending to Heaven at the end of her life. The figure ascending skyward and surrounded by angels could only be the Holy Mother.

70001632.name: Encyclopedia of Medical Science
70001632.description: An encyclopedia of medical knowledge written by Al Razi. In the Greek, Arabic, and Indian compilations, the authors' experiences and opinions have also been added. Surgical tools are also recorded.

70001633.name: Santur
70001633.description: Steel strings stretched over a box made of walnut. It is played by striking the strings with a light weight wooden rod called a Mezrab. The clarity of sound fascinates all who hear it.

70001634.name: The Historical Library
70001634.description: A book by the historian Diodorus in three parts and forty-two volumes. Volumes one to five are a collection of the worlds' mythology. Volumes eleven and twelve deal with historical eras. The rest of the volumes are missing.

70001635.name: Dirham Silver Coins
70001635.description: A silver coin made during the Sassanid Empire. On one side is the bust of the king facing right. The other is engraved with sacred fire that they worshiped.

70001636.name: Isola Bella
70001636.description: A small island located in the north of Syracuse on Sicily. The water clarity of the surrounding sea coupled with the shape of the island creates breathtaking beauty.

70001637.name: Zurna
70001637.description: Traditional woodwind instrument of the Ottoman Empire. It emits a loud sound and is used in the military and during religious festivals to accompany dancing. It is not suitable for playing indoors.

70001638.name: Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam
70001638.description: A collection of quatrains written by Omar Khayyam. In Persian, it means 'quatrain.' It continues to sing hymns in praise of fine wine and wine maidens, advocating for an ephemeral hedonism.

70001639.name: Seven Sessions
70001639.description: A literary work by Rumi, called the Seven Sessions in English. A collection of Islamic tales. Rumi left many poetic works. This tale is written in prose.

70001640.name: Nazar Boncugu
70001640.description: A Turkish amulet made of glass in the shape of an eye. The eye is meant to represent Medusa's eye. In Turkey, evil intent is thought to be emitted from the eyes. When the holder of the amulet comes near danger, it is reflected back and dispersed.

quests.name: Medusa's eye, guardian of the people

70001641.name: The Constitution
70001641.description: Book of government. A book written by the famous vizier to the Seljuq Empire, Nizam al-Mulk. At the request of the sultan, he wrote an anecdotal and easy to understand study of sovereignty.

70001643.name: Skull of Horse-like Elephant
70001643.description: A skull of an animal which has a long face like a horse and tusks like an elephant.

70001645.name: Nigella
70001645.description: A plant that flowers along the Mediterranean coast. It has aromatic black seeds that smell like strawberries and brightly coloured flowers. The seeds can also be used as a spice.

70001646.name: Driver Ant
70001646.description: This species of ant lives in places like the savannah, and are frequently on the move in search of food. The head is larger than other ants, with vestigial eyes. They move about in colonies of a million, eating any animals in their path right down to the bone.

70001647.name: Chilean Rose Tarantula
70001647.description: A spider that inhabits South America. It normally has a light brown, sober appearance, but it is extremely beautiful immediately after moulting. It has a relatively quiet disposition.

70001648.name: Bullet Ant
70001648.description: An ant 3cm long. It lives in colonies but as their bodies are large, they move about alone. They possess a strong poison that can be lethal. Individually speaking, it is the strongest of all insects.

70001649.name: Water Stick Insect
70001649.description: Also known as water stick-insects or waterscorpions, though it bears no relation to a scorpion. It feeds on insects and small fish, dissolving its captured prey with digestive fluid and sucking the juices. It has wings and can fly.

70001650.name: Bali Starling
70001650.description: It lives only in the north-west of Bali island. It has white wing feathers and black-tipped tail feathers. It has beautiful eyes that appear to be ringed with blue make up. It lives in hollow trees in nests made of grass and twigs.

70001651.name: Resplendent Quetzal
70001651.description: A bird that inhabits mountainous forests in Central and South America. It's body is 35cm long. If the decorative feathers of the male are included, its length can reach 90cm. It was used by the Aztec gods as a messenger. With its brilliant dark green feathers, it is indeed a divine, rainbow coloured bird.

70001652.name: Tomato Frog
70001652.description: It inhabits the forest in the north-west of Madagascar Island, usually nestling underground or in fallen leaves. It does not spend a lot of time in water and moves about slowly. It is few in number, as its habitat is limited.

70001653.name: Hermann's Tortoise
70001653.description: A tortoise that inhabits the southern part of Europe. It lives on dry plains and, despite being omnivorous, mostly feeds on leaves and fruit. Although opinion differs, it is said to be the model for Aesop's fable of the hare and the tortoise.

quests.name: Turtle that could beat the hare

70001654.name: Candiru
70001654.description: A catfish that inhabits the Amazon river basin. About 10cm long. It enters the gills of larger fish to eat them and suck the blood. It's own gill covers have sharp spines that allow it to maneuver. It has a flattened head in order to enter the gills more easily.

quests.name: Blood suckers of the Amazon river

70001655.name: Pelagic Thresher
70001655.description: It inhabits tropical areas of the Pacific. It's characteristic tail is almost as long as its body, which it uses like a whip to strike smaller fish. It can leap above the surface and has a rather docile character.

70001656.name: Mount Nemrut
70001656.description: A mountain rising to a height of 2000m in eastern Turkey. Apparently, carvings of deities line the summit.

70001657.name: Mount Lebanon
70001657.description: A mountain near Beirut. Accumulation of snow has earned it the name Lebanon, from the Aramaic word meaning snow. Many Lebanese cedar tress used to grow there, but were largely cut down by the ancient Egyptians in order to build the pyramids.

70001658.name: Istria Peninsula
70001658.description: A peninsula south of Trieste. It is the location of a ancient Roman city-state called Buje. There are said to be the preserved remains of ancient Roman temples.

quests.name: Initial investigation of an ancient city

70001659.name: The Kerch Strait
70001659.description: A narrow channel linking the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. There was once a flourishing city near here during the ancient Bosporan Kingdom.

70001660.name: The Benguela Current
70001660.description: A cold current flowing north along the west coast of Africa. A breeding ground for fish and catches are plentiful. There is some secret about the tides.

70001661.name: Nevado Pariacaca
70001661.description: A mountain in the Andes range. It is said that the mountain is the water god Pariacaca in a changed appearance and given how the snow accumulates at the top, it can be understood why the natives thought so. Ice from this mountain is apparently transported all the way to Lima.

quests.name: The mountain that she stares at

70001662.name: The Inscription of Merneptah
70001662.description: An epigraph left over from the time when Merneptah ruled as Pharaoh of Ancient Egypt. It has been severely damaged and is difficult to read, but there is a section that reads, sheken canal and, eddi canal.

70001663.name: The Statue of Anuket
70001663.description: An image of the goddess that causes the waters of the Nile to rise. This goddess, who carries a staff of papyrus and wears a cap with wings, gave the blessing that allowed Egypt to flourish.

quests.name: Statue that overlooks the Nile river

70001664.name: The Codex Leicester
70001664.description: A book in Da Vinci's own handwriting. An extensive work, that inquires into astronomy and medicine, and also has drawings and sketches. However, all the letters are written in mirror image, making it difficult to read.

70001665.name: Nile Monitor
70001665.description: A creature that resembles a lizard and is longer than a person is tall. It is carnivorous and even feeds on crocodile eggs and young. Although Nile is part of its name, there have been sightings of it elsewhere.

quests.name: A dangerous animal near the water
A dangerous animal near the water
A dangerous animal near the water

70001666.name: The Great Bitter Lake
70001666.description: A relatively large lake located between Cairo and Suez. There are smaller lakes in the vicinity and together they make up part of the Suez Canal.

70001667.name: The Martinenga
70001667.description: A Venetian trading vessel. It sank near the Bosphorus strait during a return voyage from Istanbul.

70001668.name: The Salvetta
70001668.description: A Venetian trading vessel. It was sunk by pirates whilst navigating the seas off Beirut.

70001669.name: The Shipwreck of Aboukir
70001669.description: A Catalonian trading vessel. It went down in the Abu Qir Bay, north-east of Alexandria.

70001670.name: The Ruins of Copan
70001670.description: The ruins of a large Mayan city discovered when the river flooded after high rainfall. It has stone carvings and wall paintings that distinguish it from other Mayan ruins. One can appreciate a high level of skill in the carvings.

quests.name: In the depths of the town

70001671.name: Ancient Arena
70001671.description: A ball court called a tlachtli where ancient Mayan ball games were performed. Ball courts can be seen at other Mayan ruins but the one at Copan is of the highest class. One is given a glimpse of its power and influence at that time.

70001672.name: Remains of a Palm Oil Plant
70001672.description: A place where palm oil is made for use in ceremonies. The oil is created on the stone platforms and stored there when not in use.

70001673.name: Nan Douwas
70001673.description: The most majestic of the Nan Madol ruins.. Also called, inside the mouth of the chief. It is a holy space and the approach to the shrine is separated for the nobility and commoners.

70001674.name: Relief of the Stairs
70001674.description: A large stairway showing the history of the Copan kingdom written in hieroglyphics. The stairway was severely damaged by river floodwaters. It will take a great deal of work to decipher the script.

70001675.name: Mano
70001675.description: A mano is a tool for grinding corn. The ground corn is then kneaded into a flour to be eaten. This tool has been used in the preparation of food since ancient times.

70001676.name: Red Stained Bone
70001676.description: Human bones that were dyed red and left with an enormous number of burial items. The extravagance of the burial items, along with evidence of a post-burial ceremony, suggest that this was for the founder of the Copan kingdom or someone of similar stature.

70001677.name: The Sakau Stone
70001677.description: Sakau is a drink made out of pulverized tree roots. People would make the drink here, before attending the ceremonies.

quests.name: Sound of stone in the ruins

70001678.name: The Royal Necklace
70001678.description: A jade necklace discovered at the Copan ruins. It has a piece of cord passing through a jade rod over 10cm long. At the midpoint is a hole into which another jade rod is attached, forming a T. This was the mark of the royal family.

70001679.name: Frangipani
70001679.description: A flower seen in southern lands. It has a sweet fragrance and bold-coloured petals and is often used as a hair ornament. The stalk breaks readily, secreting a white latex, which is used to make poison as well as medicine.

quests.name: A flower to go in your hair

70001680.name: Blue-Footed Booby
70001680.description: A bird 80cm tall with brilliant blue-green legs. The male faces the female and attracts her attention by raising its legs alternately and extending its wings. It mainly inhabits the Galapagos archipelago.

70001681.name: Galapagos Penguin
70001681.description: A rare penguin that lives in the tropics. At a height of about 35cm, it is smaller than other penguins. It has a characteristic forward leaning posture. It only inhabits the Galapagos archipelago.

70001682.name: Vampire Finch
70001682.description: A type of finch. It pecks at the base of the wings of a specific bird and sucks the blood that flows out. It inhabits part of the Galapagos archipelago.

70001683.name: Lava Lizards
70001683.description: A small lizard that can be often seen in the islands of the Galapagos archipelago. Its appearance is slightly different from island to island. The male is larger than the female, which has a characteristic red colouring around its throat.

quests.name: Lizard with a bright red face

70001684.name: Pink Land Iguana
70001684.description: A large pink lizard about 1m long. It only inhabits certain volcanic areas of islands in the Galapagos archipelago and is rarely sighted.

70001685.name: Sally Lightfoot Crab
70001685.description: A totally red crab that is often seen on the beaches of the Galapagos archipelago. It moves unlike regular crabs, jumping from rock to rock and walking forwards. It clings to rocks, feeding on seaweed by cutting it with its claws.

70001686.name: Hiva Oa
70001686.description: A town on the island of the same name in the southern part of the Marquesas islands. A volcanic island with a unique mountain range. Although part of the tropics, it is cooled by the southern equatorial ocean current and has a pleasantly warm climate all year round.

70001687.name: Mt. Nahna Laud
70001687.description: A mountain situated almost in the centre of Pohnpei island. At 800m, it is the tallest mountain on the island. There are many waterfalls.

70001688.name: Kepirohi Waterfall
70001688.description: A waterfall that flows from the tallest mountain on Pohnpei island. The high volume and intensity of the waterfall is due to the large rainfall on the island. Eels live in the basin at its foot.

70001689.name: Pohnpei
70001689.description: A small island with a name that means, stone altar. It is covered with mangroves and mountains rise in the centre. Rocks that resemble buildings can be seen deep within the forest.

70001690.name: The Marquesas Islands
70001690.description: An island chain in the South Pacific, 1500km north-east of Tahiti. The local inhabitants call the archipelago, Te Henua Enana.

70001691.name: Lake Darwin
70001691.description: A salt lake on the largest island in the Galapagos archipelago. The surface of the lake is higher than sea level and despite a lack of rainfall, the lake does not dry up.

70001692.name: Azuchi Castle
70001692.description: Japanese castle with seven-storied keep. Its magnificent figure testifies of the power of its builder. Its keep has not been in use since the fire.

70001693.name: Jomon Ware
70001693.description: Clay pot discovered in Japan distinguished by its cable-stitching. Fragile and easily broken. Believed to have been made in a period when techniques to fire pottery were not fully developed.

70001694.name: Yayoi Ware
70001694.description: Thin and tough clayware discovered in Japan. Designs and decorations are sparse. Appear to have had a more practical use. Various usages for cooking and storage, and made in several shapes to match usage.

70001695.name: Haniwa
70001695.description: Unglazed pottery made in Japan. Made to look like people, horses, houses and also cylindrical shapes. Were often placed around the grave of persons of influence, or within the tomb.

70001696.name: Dogu
70001696.description: Clay pottery in roughly human form discovered in Japan. It's odd figure somehow gives off a sense of femininity. Some appear to have been intentionally destroyed, but for reasons unknown.

70001697.name: Jomon Dwelling Site
70001697.description: Remains of a dwelling site of ancient Japanese peoples. Ground is uprooted to form a floor, with pillars placed therein. This area was once a settlement, and other traces can be found in the area.

70001698.name: Gold-lacquered Writing Box
70001698.description: Box made in Japan to store ink slabs and brushes. It's lacquering techniques show a high level of skill. Drawings were done on the object with lacquer and then metal powder like gold dust sprinkled on before the lacquer dried.

70001699.name: Sugawara's Shrine
70001699.description: A shrine dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane. Sugawara was once believed to have brought a curse upon the imperial family for their treatment of him before he died. To alleviate that curse many such shrine's were built. Sugawara is now revered as the patron god of academia.

70001700.name: Ancient Wood Strip
70001700.description: Kifuda (Wood tag) with writing on it, discovered in Japan. There were no means to make paper in this period, so similar objects can be found in China. The writings give insight into the daily lives of the people from that time.

70001701.name: Lacquered Paper Writings
70001701.description: Paper soaked in lacquer that did not decompose even buried in soil. The lacquer must be sealed with a paper cover when sealed. However, paper was valuable during the time, and writings that were no longer needed were used as covers.

quests.name: Clump That Lies in the Earth

70001702.name: Bronze-gilted Urn
70001702.description: A spherical gilded bronze vessel approximately 25cm in diameter, containing human remains and made during the Asuka Period. Inscriptions were carved into the lid and on the vessel in praise of the dead.

70001703.name: Decorative Sutras
70001703.description: A genre-painting drawn on decorated fan-shaped paper, with the Lotus Sutra written on it. Displays the gaiety of noble culture in the Heian period, and is also valued for its artistic merits.

70001704.name: Mandala Painting
70001704.description: A religious painting of Japan. A mandala is an expression of Buddhism's world view. Depicts the state of the Pure Land centered on Amitabha.

70001705.name: Tile Fragment
70001705.description: Beautifully-coloured and European-made tile fragment. Though it was to be originally used in the church corridor, it seemed to have fallen into the basement.

70001706.name: Kukai's Khakkhara
70001706.description: Staff once possessed by the Japanese monk, Kukai. When moved, the rings on top touch and make sound. This sound is said to expunge all worldly desires.

70001707.name: Kenkairon
70001707.description: Book written by the Japanese Buddhist priest, Saicho. Criticizes the inequality of the Buddhist system at the time, and expresses the correctness of his own Buddhist thoughts.

70001708.name: Catacomb Bones
70001708.description: Human remains buried under a church in Lima. The skull and other bones are arranged like an eye-catching painting. The bones are mostly undamaged and remain intact.

70001709.name: Torii
70001709.description: Stone Gate located in the west of Shitennoji. On the upper part is written, Here is the entrance to paradise. In Japan, holy grounds and secular worlds are divided by these gates.

70001710.name: Chinese Guardian Lions
70001710.description: A pair of statues often seen around Japanese temples. An unimaginable beast, shaped vaguely like a dog. One of the two has its mouth open while the other has its mouth closed. Endeared by the people as guardian gods.

70001711.name: Bell of Dojoji
70001711.description: Dojoji is an old temple said to have been constructed in the Nara Period. There is a legend of the hanging bell that a Buddhist priest was chased by a woman and hid in the bell, and after the woman transformed into a serpent, she heated up the bell, killing him inside.

70001712.name: Kagura Bells
70001712.description: Bells used in Japanese Shinto rituals. These bells are held in the hand during the dance called Kagura. The sound it makes is said to call the gods.

70001713.name: Takkoku no Iwaya
70001713.description: Temple built in the northeast region of Japan in remembrance of the victory of the Shogun, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. Dedicated to Vaisravana. Appears as if half the building is buried in the cliff.

70001714.name: Shikigami Talisman
70001714.description: Talisman to call Shikigami.Shikigami are essences said to cause mysterious phenomenon at Onmyoji's command. Shiki means to use.In the past, the masters of Onmyodo supposedly used these talismans to call forth Shikigami….

70001715.name: Mountain Hermit's Tools
70001715.description: Set of tools used in training by the practitioners of mountaineering asceticism. Mountaineering asceticism is a Japanese religion that combines mountain worship, Buddhism, and Shinto. The practitioners wear these tools on their body, and performed ascetic practices in the mountains.

70001716.name: Itsukushima Decorative Sutras
70001716.description: 33-volume Buddhist scriptures kept up in the Itsukushima Shrine. Heike, having once reached full prosperity in Japan, made it as a prayer to the prosperity of the tribe. Has a brightly ornate design.

70001717.name: Flag of the Yatagarasu
70001717.description: Flag that bears a drawing of a three-legged crow. In Japanese mythology, this crow is god's messenger. The name in Japanese means eight-span crow, with eight-span being a length common in Japanese mythologies.

70001718.name: Magatama for Spirit Pacification
70001718.description: Special magatama used by Japanese Onmyoji in rituals. In Japanese Shinto, spirit pacification is the act of attaching a restless spirit to a living body.

70001719.name: Shimenawa of Rock Cover
70001719.description: Shimenawa is straw rope covered with cut white paper. Used to protect against evil or as a means to call the gods. In Japanese mythology, after the sun goddess, Amaterasu, was pulled out of the heavenly rock cave, a rope was wrapped around the cave entrance to seal it so she couldn't hide in it again...

70001720.name: Sesshu's Shan Sui
70001720.description: Japanese ink painting made by the Zen Buddhist, Sesshu. Characterized by its calm-like composition. The scenes of autumn and winter are expressed with strong brush strokes.

70001721.name: Animal Caricatures
70001721.description: Japanese picture scroll depicting personified animals. Expresses the daily life of the people at the time by using the figures of lively animals.

70001722.name: Kano Motonobu Landscape Painting
70001722.description: Painting from the Daisen-in of the Daitoku-ji in Japan. Drawn on an eight-paneled sliding screen. Painted by the artist, Kano Motonobu. Its central subject is a large pine tree, with a few flowers and birds added.

70001723.name: Sesshu Landscape Art
70001723.description: Japanese ink painting made by the Zen Buddhist, Sesshu. Amanohashidate is one of the foremost aesthetic landscapes in Japan. Sesshu drew that landscape with strong and free brush strokes.

70001724.name: Scenes in & around Kyoto
70001724.description: A painting on a folding screen by the Japanese artist, Kano Eitoku. A drawing looking down on the city and outskirts of the Japanese capital. This work is particularly admired within the works of this style.

70001725.name: Tawara Sotatsu Folding Screen Painting
70001725.description: A painting on a folding screen by the Japanese artist, Tawaraya Sotatsu. On the one side the thunder god is depicted on the left sounding out a dram while the wind god is depicted on the right manipulating the wind..

70001726.name: Hasegawa Tohaku Folding Screen Painting
70001726.description: A painting on a folding screen by the Japanese artist, Hasegawa Tohaku. Ink painting of a forest in a mist drawn boldly and in detail.

70001727.name: Tale of Genji Handscroll
70001727.description: A Japanese picture scroll following the Genji Monogatari. Designed to allow the reader to enjoy the story both in words and art. After each section of text, a picture of one portion of that text is included.

70001728.name: Temple Miracles Scroll
70001728.description: A Japanese picture scroll depicting the miraculous events surrounding a temple and the priests there. It beautifully records the attitudes of those who sought faith, both rich and poor.

70001729.name: City Scenery Scroll
70001729.description: A Japanese picture scroll showing the life of people living in the capital. Clothing, town layout, festivals, all are depicted in a lively manner. This is not only a work of art, but an important historical resource depicting the culture of the time.

70001730.name: Battle Picture Scroll
70001730.description: 12-volume picture scroll based on the Taiheiki. Work that vividly depicts the events surrounding the strife of Japan's Northern and Southern courts, mixed with pictures of battle.

70001731.name: Chinese Folding Screen
70001731.description: Folding screen picture depicting nature. A furnishing used in the mansions and royal courts of the Heian nobles.

70001732.name: Vivid Wall Painting Fragment
70001732.description: Part of a wall painting that decorated the interior of the Palenque Ruins. Though only a fragment, it is decorated with fine carvings. And though faded, there remains evidence that it was mostly covered in red with details in green, blue, and yellow.

70001733.name: Tale of Genji
70001733.description: Full-length novel written by Lady Murasaki. Set in the imperial court during the Heian period. A sentimental love story that describes the glamorous life of the aristocracy and their complex inter-relations.

70001734.name: Anthology of Tales from the Past
70001734.description: A Japanese book that collects over a thousand fables from Japan, India, and China into one volume. Every story in the anthology starts with the line. Now long ago.

70001735.name: A Collection of Tales from Uji
70001735.description: Collection of Japanese fables, both Buddhist and secular. Compared to other fable collections, the stories are less moralistic and more whimsical.

quests.name: Prophetic Dream and Collection of Tales

70001736.name: Kokin Wakashu
70001736.description: The first collection of waka poems collected by order of the emperor.Both past and present waka poems can be found in this collection.

70001737.name: Collection of Ten Thousand Leaves
70001737.description: A collection of approximately 4500 waka poems. A variety of works are collected, regardless of the authors' statuses and locations. Considered the oldest poem collection currently existing in Japan.

70001738.name: The Ten Foot Square Hut
70001738.description: An essay penned by Kamo no Chomei. A deeply emotive work of literature that expresses melancholy for the impermanence of the human world. It describes the natural disasters that befell the age, and the author's decision to live life in a secluded tea hut.

70001739.name: 5-Stringed Biwa
70001739.description: Biwa decorated with mother-of-pearl in-lay. The embedded seashells and tortoiseshells are gorgeous. In a certain storehouse, there is kept a lovely 5 string biwa thought to have been sent to Japan from India. Further details are scarce. There are few who are allowed to see it.

70001740.name: The Pillow Book
70001740.description: Essays written by Sei Shonagon in the Heian period. Subjects include the nature of each season, activities of the Imperial court, and human events. Filled with wit and the sensitivity of the author on every page.

70001741.name: Seal of Tenka Fubu
70001741.description: Seal engraved with the characters Tenka Fubu. In recent times, seals such as this were used in place of signatures in Japan. It's believed that it represented the political beliefs of the user, but the details are unclear.

70001742.name: Taiheiki
70001742.description: Story based on the strife between the northern and southern courts in Japan. As it's a war chronicle, accounts of battle are numerous.Takes a critical stand towards the societal climate of the time.

quests.name: War Story that Calls for Peace

70001743.name: Fushinjo
70001743.description: Letter from Kukai addressed to Saicho. A famous Japanese writing in the Chinese style. Kukai is also known for his penmanship, and this letter is considered his masterpiece.

70001744.name: Tortoiseshell Comb
70001744.description: Comb made from tortoiseshell. The tortoiseshell is engraved with fine ornamentation. Japanese women use it not only to comb their hair, but as a hair accessory as well.

70001745.name: Kyoto Doll
70001745.description: Doll made around Sakai in Japan. Often delivered to Edo as a souvenir. It is said to have originally been created as protection for children. The dolls were said to take the child's place in case of something bad happening.

70001746.name: Deerskin Mari
70001746.description: Hand ball used in the game, Kemari. Kemari was a Chinese game that grew popular in Japan. A number of people kick the Mari in succession so it does not hit the ground. Popular among nobles and samurai.

70001747.name: Azuchi Castle Roof Tile
70001747.description: Black roof tiles that shingle the roof of Azuchi Castle. It has a three way emblem on its front, and gold leaf applied to its concave part. There are traces of its burning from a fire.

70001748.name: Todaiji Aromatic Wood
70001748.description: Quality incense stored in the Shosoin in Todaiji. The shosoin stored much fragrant wood, including aloeswood, musk, and sandalwood. It was used not just for its fragrance, but as a medicine as well.

70001749.name: Missionary's Epistle
70001749.description: Letter written by the Portuguese missionary, Gaspar Vilela. In the letter he describes Sakai, the port city of Japan, as comparable to Venice.

70001750.name: Jomon Sugi
70001750.description: Giant tree of Yakushima. Grows to nearly 30m tall, and 16m wide. A roundly winding trunk is said to possess great vitality.

70001751.name: Red Spider Lily
70001751.description: Flower that grows throughout East Asia that opens its petals in a radial pattern. Also called 'Manjusaka'. Poisonous and often planted to keep away dangerous bugs.

70001752.name: Beach Vitex
70001752.description: Seaside plant tht grows throughout comparatively warm regions across East Asia to Australia. Its fruit is used as a herbal medicine. The branches and leaves are fragrant and used as an ingredient in incense.

70001753.name: Mophead Hydrangea
70001753.description: Plant native to Japan that bears small flowers that blossom closely to each other. The colour of the flower depends on the dirt and the number of days since it has blossomed. Large decorative flowers surround the small flowers in the center. It appears as a picture frame.

70001754.name: Tsukiyotake
70001754.description: Poisonous mushroom that grows in dead broad-leaf trees. When accidentally consumed it causes a hallucinogenic symptom of blue vision. It has been known in Japan as a poisonous mushroom since ancient times and also appears in Anthology of Tales from the Past.

quests.name: Ignis Fatuus of the Far East

70001755.name: Hime-Hama-Nadeshiko
70001755.description: Plant endemic to Japan living along the coast, beaches, and rocky places. Its magenta flowers bear strong winds as they grow on the rocks.

70001756.name: Japanese Bellflower
70001756.description: Plant that grows in sunny fields and mountains in East Asia. The buds blossom in to star-shaped flowers with the petals connected, appearing like balloons. The roots are used as herbal medicines.

70001757.name: Upright Hypericum
70001757.description: Plant that bears a yellow flower in the summer and grows in the grass and the hills in East Asia. Eating the plant will produce skin irritation when under direct sunlight. Generally used as an herbal medicine or ointment.

70001758.name: Hinoki Cypress
70001758.description: Evergreen tree that grows in Japan and Taiwan. Grows well in dry places. The wood is highly durable, lustrous, and aromatic. Renowned as a high-grade building material.

70001759.name: Adonis Amurensis
70001759.description: Plant inhabiting mountain forests. Golden flowers blossom at the beginning of spring. Instead of producing nectar, by gathering sunlight and creating a warm place, it attracts insects and encourages pollination.

70001760.name: Stylogomphus Suzukii
70001760.description: A special-type of Japanese dragonfly with a small, thin body. Lives in mountain areas and mountain streams in hilly areas. Its Japanese name comes from the male's white tip on the tail.

70001761.name: Higurashi
70001761.description: Cicada that lives in dusky forests in East Asia. Its Japanese name comes from its tendency to chirp as the sun sets.

70001762.name: Jakou Ageha
70001762.description: Butterfly that widely inhabits East Asia. Has long slender wings that stretch backwards. Males have velvet-like lustrous black wings, while females have relatively subdued brown wings.

70001763.name: Great Purple Emperor
70001763.description: Butterfly that is dispersed across East Asia. Males have lustrous blue-purple wings. Has great flying ability and the sound of its fluttering wings can be heard when nearby.

70001764.name: Japanese Luehdorfia
70001764.description: Bright butterfly with yellow and black spots that only inhabits Japan. When the larva matures in the summer, it pupates under a fallen leaf and passes the winter there.

70001765.name: Japanese Ground Beetle
70001765.description: Japanese indigenous insect living in flatlands and mountainous lands. It sticks its head into a snail's shell and melts it with digestive fluids.

70001766.name: Attacus Atlas
70001766.description: Large moth dispersed across a wide area from India to East Asia. Its farthest dispersion north is Japan. It has no mouth and does not feed after emerging as a butterfly.

70001767.name: Okinawa Rail
70001767.description: Bird that only inhabits the forest regions in the north of the main Okinawan island. Has small wings and is flightless. However, its legs are well developed and it can run around thickets.

70001768.name: Japanese Crane
70001768.description: Birds that inhabits marshy areas of East Asia. A portion of them spend the winter near human habitations. Red and black appears on its slender white body. That exquisite form appears in many of the works of art in the East.

70001769.name: Lidth's Jay
70001769.description: Crow with a healthy colour that inhabits the small islands south of Japan. Characterized by its lazuline wings, white beak, and red-brown body. Despite its beautiful appearance, its chirp is raucous and noisy.

quests.name: Blue Bird of the Far East

70001770.name: Copper Pheasant
70001770.description: Bird that inhabits the forest lands south of Japan's mainland. Males beat their wings against their breasts, producing sound. Their long tail feathers is viewed as a symbol of longevity and is often used in literary works.

70001771.name: Black-tailed Gull
70001771.description: Seabird that inhabits the waters near Japan. Though a type of gull, it does not migrate according to the seasons. Its cry is said to be similar to a cat.

70001772.name: Bush Warbler
70001772.description: Small bird found across East Asia. It has a beautiful chirp that can be heard from the beginning of spring until summer and is thus called a harbinger of spring. Unlike its beautiful face, its wing colour is very simple. It is very alert and rarely seen.

70001773.name: Long-tailed Cock
70001773.description: A type of chicken native to Japan. Said to have been born of mutation. Some of the feathers of the male cock's tail do not molt, thus they grow extremely long.

70001774.name: Japanese Pheasant
70001774.description: Bird indigenous to Japan that lives in bright forests and grasslands. The male is a lustrous green colour from its breast to its stomach, and bright red around its eyes.

70001775.name: Japanese Crane
70001775.description: Bird dispersed across East Asia. Nearly its whole body is white, but its wings and the backside of its tail feathers are safrano pink. When it grows menacing, the feathers behind its head stand up like a crown.

70001776.name: Ishikawa Frog
70001776.description: Frog that inhabits Amamioshima and Okinawa. Its body looks like purple jewels studded in green land. It is called the most beautiful frog in Japan.

70001777.name: Forest Green Tree Frog
70001777.description: Frog endemic to Japan. Primarily dispersed in Honshu and Sadogashima. Unlike most frogs that lays eggs in water, they lay their eggs on tree branches that hang out over the water.

70001778.name: Japanese Dormouse
70001778.description: Small 6-8cm animal like a mouse that only inhabits Japan. It hibernates in groups for nearly half of a year. When attacked it leaves its tail hair behind as it escapes, but its hair does not grow back.

70001779.name: Yakushima Deer
70001779.description: A type of deer inhabiting Yakushima. One size smaller than the deer on the Japanese mainland. The horns are usually split into only two branches, which is also one less than deer on the mainland.

70001780.name: Yakushima Macaque
70001780.description: Small monkey that inhabits Yakushima. Its body hair is rough and slightly long. The hair on the head of an adult male is split left and right from the center.

70001781.name: Japanese Copperhead
70001781.description: Fat and skinny snake seen all over Japan. It is poisonous, but not that fierce. Its skin and meat has nutritional value and can be used in medicine.

70001782.name: Japanese Serow
70001782.description: Antelope endemic to Japan that lives in forests. Both males and females have horns but neither regrow. Its fur is insular and durable, and highly valued.

70001783.name: Japanese Giant Salamander
70001783.description: A fat, lizard-like creature that primarily lives upstream in the rivers of western Japan. Some grow over 1m long. It moves slowly on land, but is quite the adroit swimmer.

quests.name: Giant Shadow lying in the Mountain Current

70001784.name: Chin Dog
70001784.description: Dog that is said to have come to Korea and Japan from China. Only about 25cm in height. Its coat is fine and lustrous. It's a calm and docile animal. A pet dog that can be raised indoors.

quests.name: A Pet Dog that is Easy to Raise

70001785.name: Japanese Lates
70001785.description: Fish that inhabits a small range from off the shore of Tosa to the eastern shore of Kyushu. It's a large fish over 1m in length, it prefers living near the mouth of rivers rather than the open ocean. Its eyes will look red when hit with light at a certain angle.

70001786.name: King Crab
70001786.description: Creature living in certain coastal regions of East Asia and Southeast Asia. There are rocks that bare a similar pattern.

70001787.name: Japanese Bullhead Shark
70001787.description: Shark that lives in warm waters near Japan. It has a tame temperament and does not attack humans.

70001788.name: Giant Beaked Whale
70001788.description: Whale that lives in relatively warm waters in the northern Pacific Ocean. About 10m in length. Its head is shaped like a hammer.

70001789.name: Spotted Garden Eel
70001789.description: Fish that inhabits the bottom of shallow waters. Often seen peeping its head out of the sand from its pod, facing in the direction of the flow of the tide.

70001790.name: Nagasaki
70001790.description: City located in the northwest of Kyushu. Has been developed as a port town for ages due to its intricate coastal lines. Trade with East Asia and the countries of Europe is flourishing.

70001791.name: Sakai
70001791.description: Port town flourishing in trade that faces Osaka Bay. Land with a free atmosphere, where merchants gather. Even the influential leaders of Japan are paying attention to the excellent economic structure of this city.

70001792.name: Edo
70001792.description: A city on the Pacific coast that has developed rapidly in recent years. The city is being carefully planned by its influential leaders and is carrying out such projects as filling in the gulf to make residential land.

70001793.name: Mt. Fuji
70001793.description: Active volcano that represents Japan, with majestic plains surrounding it. There are records of volcanic activity and it may erupt again hereafter. Has been an object of worship since ancient times and has been called a sacred mountain.

70001794.name: Mount Osore
70001794.description: Mountains in the north of Tohoku. Called a mountain, though technically it is not one. Revered as a sacred site by the local people. It's said that people's spirits go there after dying.

70001795.name: Iki Island
70001795.description: Island located in the Genkai Sea in the northwestern part of Kyushu. Due to the warm Tsushima current, the climate is comparatively warm. Since ancient times it has been a relaying point to connect Korea and Kyushu.

70001796.name: Yakushima
70001796.description: Island in the south of Kyushu. There are mountains that exceed 1000m, and it rains often. Its abundant nature supports a variety of living organisms.Also called the Galapagos of the east.

70001797.name: Mount Aso
70001797.description: Volcanic cluster located in a large low-lying depression in the central part of Kyushu. This low-lying depression was likely created by past volcanic activity. The surroundings are blessed with spring water and farming is performed on the flatlands.

70001798.name: Kii Mountains
70001798.description: General name for the mountains and holy sites that exist in the Kii region of Japan. The terrain is rugged, thus it has prospered as a training site for monks practising mountain asceticism and mountain Buddhism.

quests.name: Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island
Studying the Mountain on an Island

70001799.name: Mount Koya
70001799.description: Part of the mountains that form the Kii Mountain Range. Kukai practiced asceticism here in the Heian period. Called a mountain, though technically it is not one. A sacred site of Japanese Buddhism where many monks visit every year to practice asceticism.

70001800.name: Kujukuri Beach
70001800.description: Sandy beach on the Pacific coast of Japan. Coastal part is blessed with fisheries. The name means a beach that stretches afar.

70001801.name: Tottori Sand Dunes
70001801.description: Coastal dune located in the central region of Japan. Though it has the appearance of a small desert, rain and snow fall, and many plants and animals unique to the dunes can be seen.

70001802.name: Iwami Ginzan Mine
70001802.description: Mountain located in central Japan. The area produces massive amounts of silver and has gathered attention from various fronts. The silver is sometimes called Soma silver, named for the town nearest the mine itself.

70001803.name: Ryukyu
70001803.description: A series of islands, starting with the main island of Okinawa. Under the rule of the Ryukyu king. Has contact with China and Japan. Ships frequently come and go through here.

70001804.name: King Muryeong's Tomb
70001804.description: Tomb of the 25th Paekche King, King Muryeong. It's said that King Muryeong, in order to restore the power of Paekche, built close relations with China and Japan.

70001805.name: Gyeongbok Palace
70001805.description: An exquisite palace that was built for the royal family during the Joseon Dynasty. The name was given with the hope that the king, his descendants, and all of the citizenry would be blessed with great peace.

70001806.name: Changdeok Palace
70001806.description: Imperial villa of the Gyeonbok Palace. Rather than trying to create an artificial dignity or solemnity like other palaces, this villa was adapted and built to the natural terrain.

70001807.name: Three Stone Buddhas
70001807.description: Stone Buddha believed to have been created during the early period of the Silla Dynasty. Buddhism was strong in Silla at that time and many stone statues still remain. The oldest stone Buddha of Korea has a legend that says that drinking a scraping from the Buddha's nose will cure any illness. the Buddha is said to no longer have a nose.

70001808.name: Seokguram
70001808.description: Buddhist relic from the Silla period. Its interior is dome-shaped, but it is not built by digging out a cave, but through piling stone and packing earth. The building techniques of the Silla period appear to have been quite advanced.

70001809.name: Bulguksa Temple
70001809.description: Remains of a Buddhist Temple said to have been constructed in the Silla period. A temple divided into 3 areas by stone walls was placed on the top of hardened earth. Said to have been destroyed during the reign of the fourth Joseon king, Sejong.

70001810.name: Stone Beasts
70001810.description: Mysterious beast statues placed at a ruins of the Paekche era. Looks as if they are protecting the site.

70001811.name: Gwanggaeto Stele
70001811.description: Stele built by the King of Goguryeo, King Jangsu. The Stele has an inscription of the achievements of his father, the 19th Goguryeo king, Gwanggaeto.

70001812.name: Samguk Sagi
70001812.description: Book that details the history of ancient Korea. Records the history of Silla, Paekche, and Goguryeo across 50 volumes. It's said that it took a Confucian scholar of Goryeo two years to compile it.

quests.name: History of the Three Kingdoms of Korea

70001813.name: Samguk Yusa
70001813.description: 5-volume historical book said to have been compiled by the high priest of Goryeo, Iryeon. Unlike the Samguk Sagi, it also includes records about Buddhism, folklore, and oral traditions.

70001814.name: Annals of Hwarang
70001814.description: Book said to have been written by Kim Daemun of Silla. The Hwarang were young males trained in the military arts during the Silla period. In times of war, they would stand at the front line and fight for their nation.

70001815.name: Coloured Bark Trappings
70001815.description: Bark of white birch used as mud guards for horses. If you look carefully, you can see something drawn on it. It was likely quite colorful once.

70001816.name: Gaya Tanko Armour
70001816.description: Iron Tanko Armour made in the Gaya period. Tanko armour is armour made to primarily protect the trunk of the body. Triangular iron plates are set in place with nails and then wrapped around the chest.

quests.name: Relic of the Country of Steel

70001817.name: Ancient Iron
70001817.description: A rotting lump of iron. During the Gaya Period, iron bars were apparently used as currency.

70001818.name: Hearth-shaped Pottery
70001818.description: Clayware shaped like a Hibachi. Often used in the Gaya period. As the pottery-making technology developed they grew larger, and were decorated with various patterns, such as triangular and half-circle patterns.

70001819.name: Duck-shaped Pottery
70001819.description: Clayware modeled after an animal. From the Byeonhan confederacy of ancient Korea.There were many types, such as those shaped like ducks, horses, houses and ships. Created mainly to store in the tombs with the dead.

quests.name: History of the Country of Steel

70001820.name: Bronze-gilt Incense Burner
70001820.description: Large incense burner discovered in what is believed to be the tomb of the Paekche king. Adorned with dragon, bee, and phoenix decorations, it displays the fine quality of Paekche crafts.

70001821.name: Jungwon Goguryeo Stele
70001821.description: Stele believed to have been built in the Goguryeo period. It is covered in lettering on all four sides. It appears to detail the relationship between Goguryeo and Silla, but it is heavily damaged and difficult to read.

70001822.name: Cheomseongdae
70001822.description: Tower-like structure said to have been built at the end of the Silla period. According to tradition, this is an astronomical observatory, used in star-gazing.

70001823.name: Gochang Dolmen Site
70001823.description: A large-scale, historical dolmen on the west coast of the Korean peninsula. It is made from a variety of large and small stones with different shapes. Total is over 400.

70001824.name: Jeong Do-Jeon's Death Poem
70001824.description: Jeong Do-jeon was a scholar and politician at the end of the Goryeo dynasty to the early Joseon Dynasty. Gained the confidence of Yi Dan. Right after planning the dispatch of troops to Liaodong, he was assassinated by a political enemy. This poem is said to have been composed then.

quests.name: Studying the Beginning of the Joseon Dynasty

70001825.name: Silla Wood Strip
70001825.description: Considerably worn wood strip. Often found in any areas where Silla relics can be found. It appears to be a record of events that once happened in this area, but damage has made it illegible.

70001826.name: Eulji Mundeok's Prose
70001826.description: Eulji Mundeok was a Goguryeo warlord. When the Sui Army attacked, Eulji Mundeok sent this poem urging for peace. When the Sui Army let their guard down, he launched a counter-attack, drove out the Sui Army and protected the nation.

70001827.name: Tomb of Kim Yushin
70001827.description: Tomb of the Sila warlord, Kim Yushin. Kim Yushin was a Hwarang, and gained the total confidence of King Muyeol. He achieved the great accomplishment of unifying the three kingdoms, but passed away just before his work was completed and was buried here.

70001828.name: Woodprints of Tripitaka Koreana
70001828.description: The Tripitaka is a collection of sutras. With the impending invasion of the Khitan, their creation was started in Goryeo as a prayer for national safety. They were completed in the mid-13th century. There are said to be over 80,000 printing blocks.

70001829.name: Buddha in Seokugram
70001829.description: Statue enshrined in Seokugram. Glass is embedded in its forehead, and when sun light fills the temple, the glass shines. It seems that in the Silla period, not only masonry, but sculpture work also was very advanced.

70001830.name: Gilt-bronze Standing Bodhisattva
70001830.description: Bodhisattva statue often seen in Korea. There are many methods of making the statues, such as painting a wooden figure with bronze, or through casting.

70001831.name: Paekche Reliquary Container
70001831.description: Sarira recepticle from a time when Buddhism flourished in Silla. Stored at a certain temple, the item itself is a type of nested container. The outer bronze recepticle contains a silver recepticle, and within that is a golden recepticle.

70001832.name: Dol Hareubang
70001832.description: Stone statues, their name meaning Stone Grandfather. Originally made on Cheju Island. Placed on the corners of town and at the entrances of buildings as a protection against demons.

70001833.name: Jiuquan Rock
70001833.description: Mysterious rock that often appears in Korean mythologies. It's said that if you pour water into a crater of this rock, it will eventually turn into wine.

70001834.name: Broken Sword Fragment
70001834.description: Sword fragment left behind by Yuri, the son of the first king of Goguryeo, Jumong. Raised without knowing his father, Yuri's mother told him the words of his father. Whoever finds the hidden sword is my son. Yuri found the sword and became the second king of Goguryeo.

70001835.name: Giant Motted Eel
70001835.description: Fish that grows to twice the length of a normal eel. However it is a different species than eel, and can be identified by its slightly stodgy body and mottled pattern.

70001836.name: Ahn Gyeon Ink Painting
