70001836.description: Ink painting by the Korean artist, Ahn Gyeon. Painting depicting a dream of the Peach Blossom Land by Ahn Pyeong Dae Gun, the third son of Korean king Sejong. Ahn Gyeon is said to have finished this work in a mere three days.

70001837.name: Goryeo Buddhist Painting
70001837.description: Buddhist painting often painted in the Goryeo Dynasty. During this period, Amitabha, Yoryu Kannon, and Ksitigarbha were popular and are often seen in works.

70001838.name: Sin Saimdang Folding Screen
70001838.description: Folding screen said to have been drawn by the Korean artist, Sin Saimdang. Influenced by Ahn Gyeon, it features a very sophisticated painting style. Devoid of humans and animals, the grass and insects are beautifully depicted.

70001839.name: Sin Saimdang Painting
70001839.description: Drawing by the Korean artist, Sin Saimdang. The eye is drawn to its vibrant colours and its delicate styles. Pictures of plants and insects like this must have been a joy for Korean artists to draw.

70001840.name: Gang Huian Ink Painting
70001840.description: Ink painting by the Korean painter, Gang Hui-an. Gang Hui-an studied art in China and was particularly praised for his depictions of bamboo. He also masterly depicted landscapes, plants and figures.

70001841.name: Li Gonglin Painting
70001841.description: Drawing of a tiger drawn by the artist, Li Gonglin.Though realistic, the face is slightly comical, giving the tiger a sense of friendliness.

70001842.name: Ahn Gyeon Landscape Painter
70001842.description: Ink Painting painted by Korean artist, Ahn Gyeon. A depiction of late spring, one of the eight scenes that express the seasons. The eight scenes are Early Spring and Late Spring, First Summer and Late Summer, First Fall and Late Fall, First Winter and Late Winter.

70001843.name: Sinmungo
70001843.description: Drum set in front of the gates of the Korean Palace. Used to petition an audience with the King. Decorated with an eye-catching and colourful design. Its colouration is reminiscent of Yangban clothing.

70001844.name: Paekche King's Sword
70001844.description: Sword discovered in the ruins of Paekche. The handle is decorated with a dragon. It was clearly used by the king himself.

quests.name: Traces of The King of Paekche

70001845.name: Paekche King Crown Accessory
70001845.description: Object discovered in a ruins in Paekche. Used possibly for decorating crowns. Believed to have been used by Muryeong before his death. Made of gold and very luxurious.

70001846.name: Paekche King Magatama
70001846.description: Magatama discovered in a ruins in Paekche. It stands out with its beautiful ornamentation.

70001847.name: Goryeo Celadon
70001847.description: Celadon pot made often in the Goryeo Period. Its jade-like colours are beautiful. It is considered to be a masterpiece of the area.

70001848.name: Goryeo Geography Book
70001848.description: Book compiled by an envoy from China upon visiting Kaesong. It describes the envoy's visit to the Goryeo temple known as Anhwa Temple.

70001849.name: Dongui Bogam
70001849.description: 25-volume medical book written by Heo Jun. This medical book, influenced by Taoism, is fundamentally based on Li-Zhu medicine in China, but also weaves in many unique Korean schools of medicine. It will surely contribute to the future development of medicine.

70001850.name: Silla Crown
70001850.description: Golden crown thought to be from the Silla period. It's ornate decoration and detailing draws the eye. Wonder if there was plenty of gold at that time.

70001851.name: Lazuline Cup
70001851.description: Cup often excavated in the green areas of Silla. Made of beautiful lazuline glass. Though it has no special embellishments, it draws the eye.

70001852.name: Gyeongguk Daejeon
70001852.description: Code of laws that form the basis of government in the Joseon Dynasty. Also has rules recorded for economics, culture, military and other facets of the nation. Has undergone a number of revisions.

70001853.name: Joseon Gyeonggukjeon
70001853.description: Code of laws used previous to the Gyeongguk Daejeon. Jeong Dojeon formed the foundation of the Joseon Dynasty by penning this code of laws.

70001854.name: Buddha's Nonsense
70001854.description: A critique by the politician, Jeong Dojeon. Jeong Dojeon was entrusted with power by the progenitor of the Joseon dynasty, Yi Seong-gye. It is said that this critique established the foundation of Confucianism-centered policy.

70001855.name: Hunmin Jeong-eum
70001855.description: Book said to have been compiled under the command of the fourth king of the Joseon dynasty, Sejong. Written about the characters of the Korean language, called Hangul.

70001856.name: Amhaengeosa's Disguise Tools
70001856.description: An amhaengeosa was a royal agent who spied on local officials in the Joseon dynasty. They disguised themselves in the clothing of the local area and performed investigations. To obtain more information, they used various disguise tools.

quests.name: The Dance of a Righteous Messenger

70001857.name: Joseon Officer Cap
70001857.description: Special cap worn by the Yangban of Korea. Yangban were divided into scholarly officials and military officials. This is the cap of a military official.

70001858.name: Dancer's Folding Fan
70001858.description: Folding fan used in a Korean dance. There is a wide variety of types, from those that are beautifully adorned, to those that have a simple pattern.

70001859.name: Jeongipum Pine Tree
70001859.description: Pine tree with widely-spread, large branches. The tree's life is said to be in the hundreds of years and it is much admired by the people. It's said that when the 7th king of the Joseon Dynasty, Sejo, walked past one of these trees, the outstretched branches lifted and opened a path.

quests.name: Flora that pay respect to the king

70001860.name: Orange Spider Lily
70001860.description: Plant that grows in the sunny forests of Korea and Japan. It blossoms in early spring, but it begins to wilt in summer. It bears an adorable flower, but it is toxic.

70001861.name: Korean Rhododendron
70001861.description: Plant that blossoms with a peach-coloured flower in the spring mainly in Korea. Endeared by the people as a harbinger of spring.

70001862.name: Plum
70001862.description: Plant dispersed widely through Korea, Japan, China and all of East Asia. It bears a white flower at first spring and its fruit has an acidic flavour. Loved by people since ancient times.

70001863.name: Syringa Dilatata
70001863.description: Plant much prized by Deoksugung of the Jeosung dynasty. Flowers with a light peach-colour blossom in tight clusters.

70001864.name: Viola Diamantiaca
70001864.description: Plant that inhabits the Korean peninsula and northeast China. Grows well in areas with lots of sunshine. Like other violets, the flower is rather plain.

70001865.name: Rose of Althea
70001865.description: Plant admired in Korea as a symbol of the prosperity of the country. Several flowers blossom on one branch, and it appears as if flowers continue to blossom even when one wilts, giving a sense of eternity. Bark and flowers are dried to make medicine.

70001866.name: Forsythia
70001866.description: Highly-fertile plant that inhabits Japan, Korean and China. Bears a yellow flower in early spring that bear sharp leaves around the time they wilt.

70001867.name: Dragon Swallowtail
70001867.description: Butterfly that inhabits the Korean Peninsula. Has long protuberances connected to it's lower wings. Flies gently and low to the ground.

70001868.name: Callipogon Relictus
70001868.description: Long-horned beetle that primarily lives on the Korean peninsula. Large ones can exceed 10cm in length. Can be seen in the summer in a tree called a hornbeam.

70001869.name: Dilipa Fenestra
70001869.description: A type of Nymphalidae inhabiting the regions of Korea. Characterized by the holes at the front tip of the wings that seem to have been cut out.

70001870.name: Purpuricenus Lituratus Ganglbauer
70001870.description: Long-horned beetle with a garish outer appearance that is found around East Asia, including the Korean peninsula and Japan. Distinguished by it red wings dyed in a black pattern.

70001871.name: White-bellied Woodpecker
70001871.description: A kind of woodpecker inhabiting a wide range from Korea to China and India. Builds its nest in massive dead trees.Characterized by its red feathers on the top of its head and on its cheeks. The eyes are also drawn to its black upper half and its white lower half.

70001872.name: Crested Shelduck
70001872.description: Bird that inhabits marshy areas from Korea to northeast China. There is a design on its crown.

70001873.name: Common Magpie
70001873.description: A type of crow that inhabits a part of Japan and the Korean peninsula. Produces a clicking noise when it chirps. Its wings' white pattern is striking when flying.

70001874.name: Ito
70001874.description: Freshwater fish that lives in the northernmost parts of Japan. Swims downstream like the salmon. The largest fish among those that live in the freshwaters of Japan, it eats not only other fish, but snakes and mice as well.

70001875.name: Black-faced Spoonbill
70001875.description: A kind of heron often seen in northwestern part of the Korean peninsula.All of its feathers are white with only its face and beak black. In the summer, its neck turns yellow and a yellow crown grows on the back of its head.

70001876.name: Korean Fur Squirrel
70001876.description: Squirrel that lives in the woodland areas of the Korean peninsula. Characterized by the long tufts at the tip of its ears. Like other squirrels, it eats leaf buds and nuts.

70001877.name: Copper-winged Bat
70001877.description: Bat that inhabits dark places, such as caves. Though most bats bear somber colours, this bears an orange colour.

70001878.name: Korean Water Deer
70001878.description: Deer found from Korea to the north of China. Neither males nor females have horns. Its upper-canine teeth are developed and are extended. Due to its alertness, it is very rarely seen.

70001879.name: Korean Jindo Dog
70001879.description: Average-sized dog often seen in the regions around Korean peninsula. Originally from the island of Jindo, thus the name. Its curled tail is quite adorable.

70001880.name: Northern Snakehead
70001880.description: Large, carnivorous, freshwater fish found widely from Korea to China. Lives in ponds with plenty of plants. Has a large mouth and sharp teeth.

70001881.name: Hwangssogari
70001881.description: Hwanssogari's are normally brown. Yellow specimens are rare.

70001882.name: Cyprinid Fish
70001882.description: Freshwater fish that inhabits the rivers of Korea. It has the peculiar trait of dying soon after it's partner dies, as if following them into death.

70001883.name: Iksookimia Koreensis
70001883.description: Freshwater fish that lives around Korea. Beautiful loach with a black-on-white pattern.

70001884.name: Silurus Microdoesalis
70001884.description: Rare catfish living in the mountain streams of Korea. In Korean, its name means Mountain Catfish.

70001885.name: Hanyang
70001885.description: Means, land north of the hand river. The capital during the Paekche dynasty was here, so many relics can be discovered.

70001886.name: Busan
70001886.description: Was originally a fishing village, but has developed into a center of trade.

70001887.name: Pohang
70001887.description: Located on the east coast of the Korean Peninsula. Beautiful mountains stretch out near the city.

70001888.name: Kumgangsan
70001888.description: Mountains with peaks that line the east, west, north and south. The father of Jeong Dojeon, the politician of the first rule of the Joseon dynasty, was said to have trained in these mountains for 10 years.

70001889.name: Kowloon Falls
70001889.description: Waterfall in Kumgangsan. Kowloon, meaning nine dragons was originally called waterfall basin before its name was officially established as Kowloon.

70001890.name: Cheju Island
70001890.description: Island that lies to the south of the Korean Peninsula. It's said that there was once a singular dynasty here.It seems that this island is home to a culture different from that of the Korean Peninsula.

70001891.name: Cheju Current
70001891.description: Current that flows between the Korean Peninsula and Cheju. Connected to the Tsushima Current. The islands on the current have a warm climate.

70001892.name: Hallasan
70001892.description: Volcano located in the near-center of Cheju Island. At the peak there is a lake which can be found in numerous legends. According to records, there was an eruption in the time of the Goryeo Dynasty.

70001893.name: Longtooth Grouper
70001893.description: Fish that grows over 1m in length, large even for the serranidae family. As it is nocturnal, it hides under rocks during the day, and in the night, slowly searches for food along the seabed.

70001894.name: Cornetfish
70001894.description: Long and slender fish with a long and uniquely-shaped mouth. Though its body is red, its meat is white and surprisingly delicious. Often escapes even when imagined to have been caught, likely due to its appearance.

70001895.name: Baengma River
70001895.description: River that flows through the land fought over once by Paekche and Silla. Its wide and tranquil flow and its white sandbar and green mountain ranges are harmoniously arranged to form a beautiful landscape.

70001896.name: 96-Letter Lithograph
70001896.description: Lithograph carved to the brim with some kind of figures. Based on the overall conformity of style, it is very likely lettering. It may be a carving of the history of the Palenque dynasty.

70001897.name: Yongduam
70001897.description: Rock shaped like a dragon head on the coast of Paekche. According to legend, a dragon living in Baengnokdam tried to escape from the ocean, but angered the Emperor of Heaven and was turned into stone.

70001898.name: Fort San Domingo
70001898.description: Red castle built by the Spanish. Abandoned since Koxinga pacified Taiwan. Has a gaudy exterior, but a strange air rises from underground….

70001899.name: Fort Zeelandia
70001899.description: Fort built on Taiwan by the Dutch. A strong castle made of stone, it commanded a port where a large number of ships could anchor.

70001900.name: Yingge Rock
70001900.description: Massive rock on a mountain in Taipei. There is a legend that a miasma-producing eagle was shot down by Koxinga and was turned into stone.

70001901.name: Puyuma's Moon-shape Monolith
70001901.description: Pillar about 20cm thick that remains in the location of an ancient dwelling in Taiwan. There are various theories, such as that it was for a shrine, or the wall of a building.

quests.name: Stone Pillar Standing in the Earth

70001902.name: Zhuge Liang Crossbow
70001902.description: Repeating bow invented in the Ming Dynasty. By storing 10 bows in the top part of the bow, rapid fire becomes possible. Thought to have been named after Zhuge Liang, the strategist of the Three Kingdoms era.

70001903.name: Taiwan Island Map
70001903.description: A full-island map of Taiwan. Many maps of Taiwan depicted three islands, but this island depicts Taiwan as one island.

70001904.name: Fort Zeelandia Map
70001904.description: Map of Fort Zeelandia drawn from above. The artist is unknown, but it has been preserved beautifully.

70001905.name: Skull of Tsuochen Man
70001905.description: Remains of a race that lived in Taiwan long, long ago. Many bone instruments have been found in the area, so it has been surmised that they were alive during a time when hunters were prevalent.

70001906.name: Bronze Statue of Zhongtan Yuanshuai
70001906.description: Statue of a god worshipped in Taoism. Stored in Taipei. Zhongtan Yuanshi is also called Nezha, and is shown carrying a magic sash and a flaming spear.

70001907.name: Firewalking Mikoshi
70001907.description: Mikoshi that has been handed down through Taiwan since ancient times. Used in purification rituals. It's said that when walking across hot ash while carrying this mikoshi, all impurities are extracted, and all calamities will be prevented.

70001908.name: Hok Tek Tjeng Sien Statue
70001908.description: The statue of a god that was born from the beliefs of abundant crops and the wishes of accumulating fortune. Mainly recognized as the god who gives wealth to people, this god is quite popular in Taiwan.

70001909.name: Mazu Statue
70001909.description: A statue of a Taoist goddess believed to be a divine protector of fishermen and sailors. When immigrants move from the mainland to Taiwan, they say thanks be to Mazu.

70001910.name: Earthen Ware with Human Face
70001910.description: A pot found in Taiwan with a human face depicted on its mid-section. The expressiveness of its lightly-drawn eyebrows and almond-shaped eyes is proof that the people of this time period had highly-developed pottery skills.

70001911.name: Jew's Harp
70001911.description: Small Jew's harp of the Taiwanese natives. Made from bamboo or metal. Has many valves producing unique tones.

70001912.name: Hokutolite
70001912.description: Kind of ore produced in Taipei. Is said to have a wide array of medical benefits.

70001913.name: Tainan Map
70001913.description: Tainan map showing the routes and ports occupied by the army of the Netherlands. Offered to Koxinga by Zheng Zhilong's subordinate, He-Bin. Greatly helped in the safe landing on Taiwan.

70001914.name: Man-Beast Ear Ornament
70001914.description: Ear Accessory exhumed from a Taiwanese settlement. A beast rides on the head of two humans, symbolizing the relationship between humans and divine beasts.

70001915.name: Zheng Copper Stamp
70001915.description: Metal stamp engraved with the name Zheng. Believed to be used by Zheng as a proof of identification when trading.

70001916.name: Tamsui Dictionary
70001916.description: Language dictionary used in Tamsui, compiled by a Spaniard. Used to promulgate Catholicism among the natives and immigrants to Taiwan.

70001917.name: Lazuline Bead Necklace
70001917.description: Necklace handed down as a family treasure among part of the native tribes of Taiwan. It was believed that a sacred power resided in the beads, and they were often used in rituals to heal illness.

70001918.name: Tatara
70001918.description: Traditional ship passed down by native Taiwanese people living on Orchid Island. Shaped like a gondola and unstable. Used by friends for fishing.

70001919.name: Snorkel Viper Pot
70001919.description: Earthen pot modeled after a Snorkel Viper. In the systems of the Rukai and Paiwan native peoples of Taiwan they were symbols of social status and were not owned by commoners.

70001920.name: Longan
70001920.description: Plant in Taiwan, the south of China and other warm regions with a pale-yellow small flower in early summer. Immediately thereafter, a fruit of 2cm in diameter blossoms. When cut in half, it looks like the eye of a dragon.

70001921.name: Awkeotsang
70001921.description: Precious plant that only inhabits the mountains in Taiwan. A treat called Awkeotsang is made from this fruit.

70001922.name: Sugar-apple
70001922.description: Plant brought into Taiwan by the Dutch. Its Taiwanese name, Sakya, comes from the surface of the fruit's similarity to the head of a Sakyamuni statue.

70001923.name: Easter Lily
70001923.description: Plant that's dyed red and often seen in the mountains of Taiwan. It takes about one year to blossom, and it grows proliferously in wasteland.

quests.name: Lilly That Blooms in Waste Land

70001924.name: Flamegold
70001924.description: Plant that bears a yellow flower and mainly inhabits Taiwan. Its peach-coloured tuft of fruits is so small it is often mistaken for a flower. Said to foretell autumn.

70001925.name: Mahonia
70001925.description: Shrub resistant against drying found across Taiwan and the south of China. Small yellow flowers blossom around its trunk. The leaves are green and ragged, and turn in to stiff needles at the tip.

70001926.name: Griffith's Ash
70001926.description: Plant with a small white flower that populates India and Taiwan. Has a special fragrance, and the petals have a special luster. Has a small fruit in the fall.

70001927.name: Common Rose
70001927.description: Butterfly with red and white-spotted black wings that lives from the south of China to India. Ingests poison into its body from the grass it eats while in larva form. This poison protects it from enemies.

70001928.name: Common Mormon
70001928.description: Butterfly with white spots cleanly lined along its wings that lives in southern China. It has no poison, so it is defended from enemies by its similarity in colour to the Common Rose.

70001929.name: Spangle
70001929.description: Butterfly that inhabits a vast region, including Taiwan and China. Possesses lustrous black wings, but the male's hind wings can change colour over time. Prefers darker areas than other butterflies.

70001930.name: Common Map
70001930.description: Butterfly with complex, black vein patterns on a white wing. Mainly inhabits East Asia. Has a habit of holding out its wings horizontally. Cautious around humans. Will escape when you draw near.

70001931.name: Long-armed Chafer
70001931.description: A gold beetle that lives around Taiwan and China. The front legs for a male are exceptionally long.It's reproductive ability is low, and it is rarely seen.

70001932.name: Taiwanosemia Hoppoensis
70001932.description: Cicada that only inhabits Taiwan and is characterized by its small body and red eyes. Chirps often during the morning and evening and can be heard from far away.

70001933.name: Taiwan Yuhina
70001933.description: Small bird, about 15cm in length, inhabiting Taiwan. Characterized by its dark brown, crown-like head and its round eyes. Friendly, and will often approach right up to humans.

70001934.name: Swinhoe's Pheasant
70001934.description: Large bird that inhabits Taiwan. About 70cm in length. Very alert, and rarely lets itself be seen.

quests.name: One More Time For Taiwanese Investigation

70001935.name: Taiwan Magpie
70001935.description: Large bird that only inhabits Taiwan. Characterized by its red beak, striped tail, and blue body. The two feathers on its tail slightly flutter as it flies.

70001936.name: Formosan Whistling-thrush
70001936.description: Bird that only inhabits Taiwan. Its body is about 30cm in length, but its tail is short. Characterized by its strong legs and beak.

70001937.name: Collared Bush-Robin
70001937.description: Small bird about 12cm in length. Lives in mountains with high elevation. Often seen in Alishan.

70001938.name: Drongo
70001938.description: Black bird that inhabits the croplands and urban areas in Taiwan and China. Distinguished by the upside-down Y split of its long tail.

70001939.name: Vinaceous Rosefinch
70001939.description: Bird that inhabits the croplands and forests at the base of mountains. Males have a bright red colour, and stand out clearly, but are rarely seen. Seen on Alishan on Taiwan Island.

70001940.name: Capitoninae
70001940.description: Bird with five-different colours on its body, inhabiting from the south of China to the southeast of Asia. They use their beaks to create round holes in tree trunks for their nests. They sleep in these nests at night.

quests.name: Request for Investigation of a Far Away Land

70001941.name: Mikado Pheasant
70001941.description: Rare bird that only inhabits the high-altitude mountain region of Taiwan. About 70cm long and large. Signified by its long tail.

quests.name: Once More for Taiwanese Bird Investigation

70001942.name: White-whiskered Laughingthrush
70001942.description: Bird that inhabits the mountain region of Taiwan. Characterized by its golden wings, and its distinct eyebrows. Since it is tame and numerous, it can be seen often.

70001943.name: Buergeria Robusta
70001943.description: Frog inhabiting mainly Taiwan. Has a triangular pattern from its mouth to its eyes, and from its eyes to its back. Its colour ranges from light brown to dark brown, depending on its environment.

70001944.name: Swinhoe's Japalura
70001944.description: Lizard 20cm in length that only inhabits Taiwan. Often attaches itself to tree trunks. Its body is similar in colour to trees, but it bears a yellow stripe on its back, so it is not difficult to find.

70001945.name: Taiwan Squirrels
70001945.description: Squirrel dispersed widely across all of Asia with a chirp that sounds like a dog bark. Its front teeth are sharp, and they sharpen them on trees, which are often stripped of their bark. It is rough-natured, and acts alone after infancy.

70001946.name: Chinese Box Turtle
70001946.description: Turtle with a domal shell that inhabits the waters near Tamsui. Can completely close the space between its upper shell and its lower shell. There are many types, such as those with brown heads and those with dark green heads.

70001947.name: Asian House Shrew
70001947.description: Mouse widely dispersed across Taiwan and China. Inhabits urban districts and farmlands. The young can be seen binding their tails with their parents', moving and acting together.

70001948.name: Brown-spotted Pitviper
70001948.description: An extremely poisonous snake that mainly inhabits Taiwan and China. Face is long and thin, with long fangs. Thus when bitten the venom will enter deeply into your bloodstream. Nocturnal and can frequently be found in trees.

70001949.name: Reeve's Muntjac
70001949.description: Small deer with a dog-like yelp found through Taiwan and eastern China. The scent glands near its eyes look like another set of eyes, thus it is sometimes referred to as four-eyed deer.

70001950.name: Formosan Rock Macaque
70001950.description: Monkey found in Taiwan. Its whole body is grey-brown except for the end of its 4 limbs which are black. Its tail is comparatively long and fat.

70001951.name: Formosa Sika Deer
70001951.description: Deer mainly found in Taiwan. Its Chinese name comes from its white spots that resemble a plum flower. Since ancient times, its horns and buckskin have been highly valued. It is often hunted.

70001952.name: Snorkel Viper
70001952.description: Poisonous snake that inhabits the south of China and the Taiwan island. It is said that after being bitten you will die within 100 steps. Therefore, also called Hundred-pace Snake.

70001953.name: Sambar
70001953.description: Deer dispersed among the expansive regions of Taiwan and India. Grows to over 150cm in height. The males have horns. A nocturnal animal that can be seen resting under the shade of trees during the day.

70001954.name: Risso's Dolphin
70001954.description: Creature that inhabits temperate and torrid ocean zones. It collides into other creatures, so it bears scratches on its skin.

70001955.name: Chinese Snakehead
70001955.description: Fish about 30cm long found across Taiwan and China. Used in food and medicine. There are red, brown, and green ones.

70001956.name: Tamsui
70001956.description: A city located in the northern area of Taiwan. Nearby is a large river. City was created when Koxinga drove out the Dutch.

70001957.name: Anping
70001957.description: City that is the center of Taiwanese government and military. Assessed as an appropriate location to dock ships, it was established as a large port.

70001958.name: Tamsui River
70001958.description: A tranquil river flowing near Tamsui. Boasting a plentiful water supply, it is the main source of water for the north of Taiwan.

70001959.name: Beinan River
70001959.description: A river that runs along the eastern part of Taiwan. Named after the native Beinan people. It's complex landscape has been compared to China's Mount Huang.

quests.name: The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source
The Securing of a Water Source

70001960.name: Xueshan Range
70001960.description: A range of mountains running north-south along Taiwan where ancient roads can be found. Some of those routes were likely used by the Atayal people.

70001961.name: Alishan
70001961.description: General term for the mountains in mid-south region of Taiwan. Rare animals and plants that live in tropical areas can be found here.

70001962.name: Two Sisters Pond
70001962.description: General term for two lakes of different sizes in the mountains of Alishan. According to legend, two daughters that once living in these mountains lost their lives here.

70001963.name: Eight Immortals Cave
70001963.description: A cave in a cliff wall facing the ocean formed by wave erosion. There are a number of caves. There are also some remains of the Changbin culture, one of the ancient civilizations of Taiwan.

70001964.name: Shihyusan
70001964.description: Rock on the coast of Taiwan formed by sea erosion.A single, thin and long rock supports a larger rock, giving the impression of an umbrella.

70001965.name: Chinghsui Cliff
70001965.description: Cliff made from 2000m high mountains lined along the eastern side of Taiwan. The steep cliffs stretch out endlessly, so few draw near.

quests.name: Terrain Investigation of Taiwan East Coast

70001966.name: Tailuge Gorge
70001966.description: Gorge formed by eroded marble spreading across the southeast of Tamsui. The surrounding mountains proclaim heights of over 3000 metres. Noted for its naturally-formed cliffs.

70001967.name: Orchid Island
70001967.description: An isolated island floating offshore to the southeast of Taiwan. Points of interest are a large cave made from sea water erosion and rocks of strange shapes.

70001968.name: Penghu Island
70001968.description: Once used by Koxinga as a foothold on his way to Taiwan. It has been devastated by pirate influence, but there is much evidence remaining that peoples have lived here since long ago.

70001969.name: Kinmen Island
70001969.description: Island that was once Koxinga's base. Famous for a product called Gongtang, or more literally Tribute Sugar, an ingredient made from sugar and peanuts.

quests.name: Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site
Investigation of Tributary Goods Production Site

70001970.name: The Great Wall
70001970.description: A strong castle wall that is over 6000km long. It's construction was first started by the first Qin Emperor, who began by connecting some of the fortifications built on the north side of the country.

70001971.name: Yuyuan Garden
70001971.description: A Chinese garden made by a governor of Sichuan as a comfort for his father. It means 'Garden of Happiness.'

70001972.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
70001972.description: Sitting stone Buddha statue that is about 70m tall and carved into the western mountain wall in Sichuan. Created to pray for the safety of the river and navigation. It's said that at its creation, the body was wholly gold-coloured.

70001973.name: Lao Tzu Statue
70001973.description: Giant statue modeled after the Taoist god, Lao Tzu. It's believed by the people in the area that touching the statue's beard brings good luck.

70001974.name: Tiger Tally
70001974.description: Tiger-shaped tally mainly used between the Warring States period and the Han period. Used in military drafts. When tallies did not correspond, the troops could not be moved.

70001975.name: Feng Ni Sealing
70001975.description: Clay used when sealing documents, a custom continued into the late Han dynasty. Opening the document breaks the seal, thus preventing others from opening it. This Feng ni sealing is engraved with a symbol of the emperor.

70001976.name: Jue
70001976.description: Wine vessel used during the Zhou Dynasty for ceremonial purposes. Its three legs stand for heaven, earth, and god. This Jue has a depiction of a strange beast called a Taotie.

70001977.name: Armillary Sphere
70001977.description: Astronomical device invented in the Later Han dynasty. Three disks are arranged with a detailed angle index carved into each. Through this, an astronomical object's position in space can be read.

70001978.name: Seismoscope
70001978.description: Copper seismometer invented by the Later Han dynasty inventor, Zhang Heng. When a tremor occurs, the ball on the opposite side of the seismic center falls. It has even picked up earthquakes from around 1000km away.

70001979.name: Jade Burial Suit
70001979.description: Mourning dress worn by people of high standing and believed to have been made in the Early Han dynasty.Made of square jade plaques woven together with golden wire. Covering the deceased with this is believed to prevent decomposition.

70001980.name: Masque with Protuding Eyes
70001980.description: Mask with a unique shape. Has protruding 14cm cylindrical eyes. Its design is reminiscent of the legendary first king of Shu, Can Cong.

70001981.name: Book of Han
70001981.description: Historical book recounting the Former Han Dynasty. Signified by its focus on each emperor and person.

70001982.name: Records of the Grand Historian
70001982.description: Historical book recounting from the ancient age to the Han Dynasty. Later came to be called Shiji.

70001983.name: Chinese Repeating Crossbow
70001983.description: An enhanced repeating bow that can fire numerous arrows rapidly. Invented by the military strategist of Shu of the Three Kingdoms period, Zhuge Liang, to fight against Wei.

70001984.name: Zizhi Tongjian
70001984.description: Historical book covering the Spring and Autumn Period to the Song Period. Written in a different style than the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han, likely to emphasize readability.

70001985.name: Ritual Jade Ware of Emperor Xuanzong
70001985.description: Jade ware dedicated in a ritual by Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty. On it is carved a written paean celebrating the god of earth.

70001986.name: Burnt Bamboo Slip
70001986.description: Burnt bamboo slip found in the outskirts of Yizhou. It is notably charred and its contents cannot be read. Based on its state, one can assume it was burned on purpose. It is well known that the first Qin emperor enacted book burning under the guidance of the chancellor, Li Si.

70001987.name: Amida Fragment
70001987.description: Work that shows the state of the Pure Land with sutras and drawings. Based on the sutra Amitabha Sutra, and translated by the monk of the Six Dynasties, Kumarajiva.

70001988.name: Sutra Box with Gold Lacquer
70001988.description: A box to store Buddhist sutras believed to be from the Yuan Dynasty. The box depicts the paradise realm described in the sutras.

70001989.name: Jade Cicada
70001989.description: Burial Jade from the Yin dynasty shaped like a cicada.In ancient times, it was believed to prevent decay when placed in the holes where dead bodies lay.

70001990.name: Nestorian Stele
70001990.description: Stele detailing the propagandizing of Nestorianism, a sect of Christianity. Nestorianism spread far during the Tang Dynasty, but with Wu Zong's anti-Buddhism policies, it appears this stele was also cast aside.

quests.name: Exchange of Eastern and Western Religion

70001991.name: Standing Statue of Guan Yin
70001991.description: Stone statue of a bodhisattva made in the Northern Wei Dynasty. The bodhisattva of the Northern Wei Dynasty is smiling and is very expressive.

70001992.name: Wu Zetian's Sutra
70001992.description: A faked copy of the Buddhist scripture, the Mahamegha (Great Cloud) Sutra, altered by Wu Zetian. Gained a foothold for the position of empress by adding a prophecy of an empress to the text.

70001993.name: Taijitu Shuo
70001993.description: Book detailing the principle of all creation, based on Taoist-centered Tai Chi. Theorizes that all things were created by Yin-Yang and the five elements.

70001994.name: Taiping Qingling Shu
70001994.description: A Taoist sutra. Became a sutra of Taiping Tao, a movement started by Zhang Jiao. Also called the Taiping Sutra.

70001995.name: Analects of Confucius
70001995.description: Book of sayings by the Spring and Autumn period thinker, Confucius, recorded by his disciples. Composed of 20 volumes. One of the subjects of the civil service examinations, and an invaluable work of Confucianism.

70001996.name: Account of Buddhism Sent from the South Seas
70001996.description: Book written by the Buddhist monk, Yi Jing, telling of the precepts in India concerning food. Clothing styles and rules concerning food are explained in detail.

quests.name: Monk who Travelled the South Sea

70001997.name: Silk Painting of Mawangdui Tombs
70001997.description: A painting from the Early Han Dynasty symbolic of esoteric Taoism, it depicts a dragon carrying the spirits of the dead to heaven. In the celestial realm there are ten suns, and birds dwell within them.

70001998.name: Li Di Still-life Painting
70001998.description: Painting of flowers by the Southern Song court artist, Li Di. This flower changes from white to red. Particularly highly-esteemed work among Bird-and-Flower paintings.

70001999.name: A Palace Concert
70001999.description: Picture depicting a scene of women in the court practicing their instruments. The particular details about the person who wrote it is unclear, but they are believed to be Chinese.

70002000.name: Guo Xi Landscape Painting
70002000.description: Painting by the court artist of the Northern Song Dynasty, Guo Xi. Expresses the scene of winter snow starting to melt, and the green of plants and trees starting to appear.

70002001.name: Mao Song Painting
70002001.description: Picture depicting monkey that is believed to be a Japanese Macaque. Believed to be a work of Southern Song painter, Mao Song. A famous work exhibiting outstanding expressiveness.

70002002.name: Gu Kaizhi Painting
70002002.description: Painting by the Eastern Jin painter, Gu Kaizhi. Depicts a book of morals in painting form. It seems many copies were produced for later generations, possibly for educational purposes.

70002003.name: Wang Meng Landscape Painting
70002003.description: Painting depicting the scenery of Waihu cave at Taihu Lake. Chu-chu refers to Lake Taihu. The artist, Wang Meng of the Yuan dynasty, was apparently proficient at grand and precise landscape paintings.

70002004.name: Huang Gongwang Ink Painting
70002004.description: Ink painting by the Yuan Dynasty artist, Huang Gongwang. Various scenes are depicted by the contrasting shades of ink. The painting is over 6m tall.

70002005.name: Mao Yi Painting
70002005.description: Painting of plants and animals by Mao Yi, artist of the Southern Song period. Petals are drawn one by one in fine detail. Though old, the painting has not lost much of its colour.

70002006.name: Neijing Tu
70002006.description: A pictoralization of the Taoist practice of Neidan that depicts aspects of the human body in the form of a landscape painting. Animals and celestial objects are placed within the diagram with symbolic meaning.

70002007.name: Li Di Painting
70002007.description: Drawing by the Song dynasty court artist, Li Di. Work featuring livestock cattle often is a way to sing praises to peaceful rural areas without war.

70002008.name: Hui Zhong Flower and Bird Painting
70002008.description: Work of the Song Emperor, Huizong. Huizong was adept at Bird and Flower paintings, and this work has also been highly praised.

70002009.name: Sancai
70002009.description: A colourful type of ceramics fired in the Tang Dynasty. Mainly used as burial wares for nobles. Often modeled after dolls or household items.

70002010.name: Pi-hsieh
70002010.description: Beast statue used as a talisman against evil. Found in the ruins of Chongqing. The beast of legend depicted is believed to ward off evil spirits. It is made from beads and is very valuable.

70002011.name: Ruan
70002011.description: Instrument believed to have been made during the Han Dynasty. Named after one of the seven scholars, Ruan Xian who was said to love playing the instrument. It is simply called Ruan in modern times.

70002012.name: Lion Dance
70002012.description: Traditional folk art where people dress up as a lion and dance to music. Widely developed in the Tang Dynasty, and performed before the people to greet the new year.

70002013.name: Journey to the West
70002013.description: Ming Dynasty novel based on Great Tang Records on the Western Regions.Story of the Buddhist monk, Xuanzang, along with Sun Wukong, Zhu Bajie, and Sha Wujing on their journey to India to obtain Sutras.

quests.name: Tracing Back the Footsteps of Xuanzang

70002014.name: Romance of the Three Kingdoms
70002014.description: Historical Novel from the Ming Dynasty based on Three Kingdoms. Depicts the political/military strife between the three nations of Wei, Shu, and Wu. Centers around the animosity between Liu Bei and Cao Cao.

70002015.name: Water Margin
70002015.description: Popular novel of the Ming Dynasty read often by commoners. Story about 108 outlaws who assemble in a fort and defeat evil government agents to save their country.

quests.name: Book Loved by the Ming People

70002016.name: Lantingji Xu
70002016.description: Cursive-writing done by Wang Xizhi. Characters that appear frequently in sentences are written in different shapes according to context, giving the writing a sense of movement.Treasured by Emperor Taizong of the Tang Dynasty.

70002017.name: The Inner Canon of Huangdi
70002017.description: Book that has formed the basis of Chinese medicine since ancient times. Though to have been compiled in the former Han dynasty. As a variety of medical theories have been brought together, the authors and compilers are unclear.

70002018.name: Shen Nung's Pen Ts'ao
70002018.description: Pharmacology book recording the effect of each individual drug, thought to have been compiled in the later Han dynasty. Over 300 types of medicines are characterized by their effect. Shen Nung was an ancient individual of legend, and the godfather of agriculture and medical science.

70002019.name: Mid-Autumn Manuscript
70002019.description: Work of Wang Xianzhi, son of the Eastern Jin Dynasty writer, Wang Xizhi. The work begins with the phrase, Mid-Autumn, thus its name. Primer enumerating the writing style of Chinese.

70002020.name: Guandishizu
70002020.description: Poem written by the Three Kingdoms Period hero, Guan Yu, to express his loyalty to his lord, Liu Bei. By covering its words with drawings of bamboo, its contents remained hidden from others.

70002021.name: Three Kingdoms
70002021.description: Historical record documenting the destiny of the nation from the end of the Han Dynasty to the Three Kingdoms period. Believed to have been edited by Chen Shou of Shu. Many legends are based on this record.

70002022.name: Great Tang Records on the Western Regions
70002022.description: A record of Buddhist Monk, Xuanzang's life and the Buddhist ruins found in India and the West. Spans 12 volumes, and has been highly influential on succeeding generations.

70002023.name: Yongle Encyclopedia
70002023.description: Book compiling original copies of various works on astronomy, topography, and yin and yang. Covers valuable literature up to the Ming Dynasty. However the book grew into a massive compilation exceeding 20,000 volumes, and only a portion has been reproduced.

70002024.name: Sun Tzu's Art of War
70002024.description: Book on warfare written by the general, Sun Tzu in the Spring and Autumn Period. Analyzes the reasons for victory and defeat that were believed to only be decided by the heavens at the time.

70002025.name: Tanka Poem
70002025.description: Poem that is said to have been read by the hero, Cao Cao at the feast on the night before the Battle of Red Cliffs. The first half is about alcohol and the second half a call for men of talent.

70002026.name: Eternal Lament
70002026.description: Long-form poem telling the story of Emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei of the Tang Dynasty. There are many inconsistencies with real history, such as the setting being changed from the Tang Dynasty to the Han Dynasty.

70002027.name: Imperial Seal
70002027.description: Seal of the emperor, established by Emperor Shi Huang. Historically, it was said to have been made of precious stone, but for some reason it was covered in gold. We believe it is the legendary Imperial Seal, but that is not completely certain.

70002028.name: Tai Gongwang's Fishing Rod
70002028.description: Fishing Rod believed to have been owned by Tai Gongwang, who was a military strategist in the Zhou Dynasty. According to one theory, while fishing along the Wei River, he was greeted by the late King Wen, and was praised as the great man his grandfather was waiting for.

70002029.name: Meiping
70002029.description: A general term for a kind of tall earthenware with a small mouth. It gets gradually wider from the base. Seen since the time of ancient China, of the many different types, the Jingdezhen Porcelain is the most popular.

70002030.name: Massive Elephant Bones
70002030.description: Bones of a large elephant discovered near the Yellow River. The space between the tusks on the left and right is small, and does not look big enough for the trunk to pass through.

quests.name: Contentious Chase for Large Animal's Bones

70002031.name: Small Winged Dragon Bones
70002031.description: Bones of a creature as small as a sparrow found near the Yuntain Mountains. Characterized by its thin wings and curved legs as small as a fingertip.

70002032.name: Petrified Turtle like Animal
70002032.description: Petrified creature thought to be like a turtle discovered south of the Yellow River. Its head cannot be found. Did it break off?

70002033.name: Bones of Fish with Sunken Eyes
70002033.description: Bones of a creature thought to be a fish discovered near the Yellow River. Characterized by its large eye cavities.

70002034.name: Bones of Dragon with Long Tail and Neck
70002034.description: Bones of a long and slender creature found near Chongqing. The length of its neck and tail is notable. Seems to have arms and legs best suited for swimming, but it may have walked on land.

70002035.name: Bones of Turtle-like Dragon
70002035.description: Bones of a turtle-like creature found near Quanzhou. It's stomach is bloated and it seems to wear a shell on its back.

70002036.name: Japanese Iris
70002036.description: Plant found in China and Japan with an ultramarine blue flower that blooms in the Spring. It grows in dark places. The flower withers the day after flowering.

70002037.name: Primula
70002037.description: Plant with light-purple and peach-colour flower found in southern China. A fragrant flower that blooms for a long time. It is considered a harbinger of spring.

quests.name: Flower Search for the City Girl

70002038.name: Kaen-Take
70002038.description: Mushroom dispersed among China and Japan. Grows near rotting trees. Its Japanese name comes from its bright red and flame-like shape.

70002039.name: Yellowhorn
70002039.description: Plant mostly seen in China. It grows a white flower, but as the days pass it gradually changes into a light red colour from the center.

70002040.name: Buddleja Davidii
70002040.description: A plant that primarily grows in China with small flowers blossoming in tufts on its branches. Its fragrance often attracts butterflies.

70002041.name: Crataegus
70002041.description: Plant inhabiting China. Said to have been used in Christ's crown. Used as bonsais and garden shrubs. Its fruit can be used as food and medicine.

70002042.name: Chinese Cymbidium
70002042.description: Plant that grows from south China to Taiwan. Blooms from January to February, and is used as an alcove ornament during the New Year. Highly valued for its attractiveness. Liked by the people in the higher ranks of society.

70002043.name: Hardy Begonia
70002043.description: Plant that mainly inhabits China. A red flower that blossoms from the end of Summer to Fall. Prefers shade and dampness, and can be seen blooming in various locations.

70002044.name: Mulan Magnolia
70002044.description: Plant with a purple flower that mainly inhabits the southwest of China. Considered a very valuable flower. Releases a sweet and elegant fragrance.

70002045.name: Tartarian Aster
70002045.description: Light purple flower that blooms in fall, and inhabits China and Korea. The root is used as a medicine.

70002046.name: Japanese Pagoda Tree
70002046.description: Plant with lots of white flowers, mostly found in China. Famous as a medicinal plant, and dried buds are used as a hemostatic.

70002047.name: Corn Poppy
70002047.description: An annual herb resilient to winter that grows from China to Europe. Has four thin petals. In Chinese, it's name comes from Consort Yu, the lover of the Qin Dynasty commander, Xiang Yu. The flower is often laid at her tomb.

70002048.name: Kaiser-i-hind
70002048.description: Butterfly living in a mountain range in the southern part of China. It has brilliant red and green wings, and daringly dives at considerably fast speeds. Called the king of butterflies.

70002049.name: Assassin Bug
70002049.description: Bug found from China to southeast Asia. Lives in groups in the trunks of large trees. Stabs its long and narrow mouth into other insects and sucks out their liquids. Humans are also sometimes stung. Be cautious.

70002050.name: Silkworm
70002050.description: Bug domesticated and seen often in northern China. Does not exist in the wild.Creates cocoon to produce silk or cotton.

70002051.name: Calyptotrypes Hibinonis
70002051.description: Bug inhabiting the south of China. Said not to land on the ground even once during its lifetime. Often seen flying around the top of tree leaves.

70002052.name: Chinese Nightingale
70002052.description: Small bird that inhabits southern China and northern India. Has a bright red beak and yellow throat. As it moves in pairs, they have been called love birds.

70002053.name: Hwamei
70002053.description: Bird that inhabits a wide area from the south of China to southeast Asia. Often runs on the ground and rarely flies. Characterized by the pattern around its eyes, and thus called Painted Eyebrow.

70002054.name: Golden Pheasant
70002054.description: Bird that inhabits the mountains of southwest China. Has a red and luxurious coat. Very alert and talented at hiding. Very rarely seen.

70002055.name: Chinese Bamboo Partridge
70002055.description: Bird with a strange chirp that inhabits China and Taiwan. It's a very alert animal and is rarely seen. Searches for food in the early hours as a flock.

70002056.name: Otter Civet
70002056.description: Otter-like animal inhabiting the south of China. A long white beard fills its face from around its mouth to behind its eyes.

70002057.name: Oriental Small-clawed Otter
70002057.description: Extremely small otter dispersed across Indonesia and the south of China. Has a flat body adapted for swimming. Live in groups and familiar with people.

quests.name: Small Animal Appearing in the Yangtze River

70002058.name: Chow Chow
70002058.description: Dog kept as a watchdog for livestock. Due to its blue-black tongue, it is called black-tongued dog in some regions. It's said that they were also kept by the Tang Emperor.

70002059.name: Golden Snub-nosed Monkey
70002059.description: Monkey inhabiting the cold regions of western China. Covered in long orange hair. Characterized by its blue-white face and its smashed nose.

70002060.name: Argali
70002060.description: Large sheep of 120cm, back-to-front, that mainly inhabits the plateau regions of central China. Both males and females have horns. Male horns grow to over 1m in length.

70002061.name: Giant Panda
70002061.description: Animal mainly living in the southwest of China. Distinguished by it clearly divided white and black hair. The tail is not very developed and does not stand out. Does not form groups or families and lives on its own.

70002062.name: Takin
70002062.description: Animal distinguished by its large curved horns that inhabits southwest China. It forms large flocks in the summer, but tend to split into smaller groups in winter.

70002063.name: Milu
70002063.description: Animal found in China from the north to the middle area. It has hooves like a calf, a head like a horse, horns like a deer, and a body like a donkey. Since all of these characteristics are different from each other, it is also called Four Unlikes.

70002064.name: Eel Goby
70002064.description: Animal with a thin, long, bluish-purple body inhabiting China and Korea. It has eyes at birth, but they atrophy as it ages and submerge under the skin.

70002065.name: Chinese Alligator
70002065.description: 150cm-long alligator that inhabits down stream from the Yangtze River. It lives near the living area of humans, such as rivers and marshes. But due to its tame demeanor, it rarely attacks humans.

70002066.name: Yangtze Dolphin
70002066.description: Dolphin that lives downstream of the Yangtze River. As it lives in a cloudy river, it's eyes have regressed. Also called, Goddess of the Yangtze.

70002067.name: Yellow Pond Turtle
70002067.description: Nocturnal turtle spread across the regions of China. Spends the days in the mud in the bottom of water or in holes. Has an aggressive side, as can be seen in its biting of other individuals.

70002068.name: Macau
70002068.description: Town with a large port. Though originally a small village focused on fishing, it has become an important port of trade between Europe and East Asia since the Portuguese started to reside here.

70002069.name: Quanzhou
70002069.description: Town that once flourished as a point of sea commerce. In the Late Jin period, many immigrants moved over from the central plains, and techniques and cultures from the central plain were brought over.

70002070.name: Hangzhou
70002070.description: Town that was lauded by Marco Polo as beautiful and lively. A cradle of civilization where many temples and old ruins are lined up one after another.

70002071.name: Yuntaishan
70002071.description: A historical town that was the capital of King Goujian of Yue in the Spring and Autumn Period. Famous for its extensive flat farming land and tea production.

70002072.name: Chongqing
70002072.description: A city upstream from the Yangtze River and surrounded by nature. The summers are blistering, but winter is relatively bearable. It's name means overlapping celebrations due to two joyous events that happened at the same time in the land's history.

70002073.name: Yellow River
70002073.description: A large river flowing in the north of Yizhou. The region downstream is called Zhongyuan and is a cradle of civilization. Since ancient times, the river often floods and the flow of the river has changed.

70002074.name: Yangtze River
70002074.description: Large river flowing through northern Hangzhou used since ancient times as a main traffic route. Rice cropping is also abundant along the river. Also called the Yangzi River in the south.

70002075.name: Mount Pan
70002075.description: Towering mountain north of the Yellow River famous for its natural spring water and Buddhist temples. Has landscapes of pine trees and beautiful water, and looks dazzling from any direction.

70002076.name: Mount Tai
70002076.description: Mountain revered as the center of religious belief. Since the first Emperor of Qin, emperors have performed Fengshan Sacrifices here to proclaim the unity of the empire. There are hokora and mausoleums dotted all over the mountain.

70002077.name: Mount Huang
70002077.description: Mountains near Hangzhou where many temples have been built as Taoist and Buddhist ascetic training sites. Many poets have visited here, and it has given birth to many paintings, poems and unique traditions.

70002078.name: Mount Qingcheng
70002078.description: One of the mountains around Chongqing and a centre of Taoism. It's named after it's numerous aged trees and the fact that it is covered in green all year long.

70002079.name: Wuyi Mountains
70002079.description: Mountains that maintain a warm climate and where many tea leaves can be extracted. Relics of the Song Dynasty and books used by the progenitors of Neo-Confucianism remain here.

70002080.name: Mount Sanqing
70002080.description: One of the famous Taoist mountains. Named thusly because the Taoist mountains looks like The Three Pure Ones sittings in a row.

quests.name: Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion
Study on the Local Mountain and Religion

70002081.name: South China Karst
70002081.description: Land spreading out far south of Chongqing, where a forest of strange rocks stand. Blessed with an abundant landscape and calm weather.

70002082.name: Wulingyuan
70002082.description: A scenic area of lined sandstone pillars. There are said to be over 3000 pillars here. There is a legend that the emperor of the Han Dynasty lived and met his demise here.

70002083.name: Djed Pillar
70002083.description: Pillar symbolizing eternal stability. Also call the backbone of Osiris, after the ancient Egyptian God. Printed on walls and amulets as a sign of regenerative power.

70002084.name: Heart Scarab
70002084.description: Special amulet, one of those modeled after a scarab. The Book of the Dead is inscribed on its back. Placed on the heart of a mummy as a prayer for resurrection.

70002085.name: Thoth Statue
70002085.description: A god of ancient Egypt. As a judge of the dead, he and Anubis weigh the sins of the dead and pass final judgment. He holds a list of the names of the dead and is called the Scribe of the Gods. Considered the inventor of hieroglyphs.

70002086.name: Cartouche
70002086.description: A hieroglyph of ancient Egypt. Written on walls around the names of Pharaohs. Believed to thus protect the name of Pharaohs.

70002087.name: Ptah Statue
70002087.description: A god of ancient Egypt. Guardian god of craftsman. Also called the god of the underworld. The inner sanctum of the Abu Simbel Temple is constructed so that light will not touch this statue.

70002088.name: Hathor Statue
70002088.description: A god of ancient Egypt. Not only called the mother of the gods, but also the goddess of the sky and a guardian of the dead.

70002089.name: Altered Maedate
70002089.description: Helmet worn by certain generals of Japan. Love is written on the tatemono on the face. Tatemono were originally only worn by generals with specific patterns, but in recent years they have been added to the helmets of lower-ranked soldiers with varying designs.

70002090.name: Shirabyoshi Costume
70002090.description: Male dance costume. Shirabyoshi refers to a type of dance that occurred at the end of the Heian period, or a dancer. Dancing while singing. Most of the dancers were women, but there were male dancers as well.

70002091.name: Hakchang-ui
70002091.description: Korean clothes worn by those who have learned or taught Confucianism. Korean Confucianism is not a religion but rather academia--many have learned Confucianism and acted on its principles.

70002092.name: Paiwan Tribe Clothes
70002092.description: Clothing worn by the Paiwan peoples, the native tribe of Taiwan. Bright long garments with glass beads and fine stitching. According to legend, the Paiwan people were said to have been born of a marriage between a poisonous snake called a Snorkel Viper and a human.

70002093.name: Peking Opera Costume
70002093.description: Costume worn in the Chinese performing art called Peking Opera. The play developed among the people and became popular in the city, where it came to be called, Peking Opera. Subject mattered revolved around the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Water Margin, and other subjects popular among the masses.

quests.name: A New Trend in the Arts

70002094.name: Raikiri
70002094.description: Japanese sword said to have cut lightning thus saving it's owner. Incredibly sharp sword said to have been made by the hand of a master swordsman. There is a mark on the blade that seems to be where the lightning was cut.

70002095.name: Yunnan Zhan Ma Dao
70002095.description: Single-edged, long-blade sword used by the troops organized by Koxinga. Difficult to use due to its weight, but it is highly powerful and can cut both horse and rider.

70002096.name: Green Dragon Crescent Blade
70002096.description: Long handled weapon said to have been used by the Late Han Chinese general, Guan Yu. A large dragon is carved in the blade. The scimitar shape was developed in the Ming Dynasty, and was used more for performance than actual combat. It's hard to imagine Guan Yu actually used this....

70002097.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
70002097.description: A historical site on Terra Nova, on the northern tip of the New Continent. It is believed to be the place where the Vikings of Northern Europe moved to. A number of buildings have been found in good condition. They are believed to have been used as a place to work.

quests.name: A Dream to End the Nightmare

70002098.name: Cahokia Mounds
70002098.description: Giant mounds built by the people of the Mississippi River Valley. People of high rank reportedly lived atop them. The largest one is 30 meters tall, covering an area of 300 x 250 meters.

70002099.name: Serpent Mound
70002099.description: A mound in eastern North America formed in the shape of a snake and surrounded by a moat. The hill may have been a tomb, but there is much about it that is unknown. The serpentine shape may have some connection with a constellation.

70002100.name: Joggins Fossil Cliffs
70002100.description: Cliffs where one can see numerous strange stones. It used to look like a regular stone cliff, but the tide eroded it to reveal the numerous petrified animals.

70002101.name: Underwater Panther Jug
70002101.description: A domestic tool of a tribe that lived on the Gulf of Mexico coast near the Mississippi River. This jug is decorated with the underwater panther, a mythological creature that appears in the tribe's legends.

70002102.name: Birdman Copper Plate
70002102.description: A copper plate with a unique design, it has been worked into the shape of a person with feathers. It was placed in a tomb as a burial item for a high-ranking person near the Etowah River in North America.

quests.name: The Winged Human Engraved on a Copper Plate

70002103.name: Shell Gorget
70002103.description: A collar carved from a shell. It was discovered in a tomb near the Etowah River in North America. The gorget is uniquely carved and contains geometrical patterns.

70002104.name: Adena Pipe
70002104.description: An ancient pipe found near the Ohio River in North America, it is a relic of an agricultural society from thousands of years ago. It shows that people have smoked tobacco since very long ago.

70002105.name: Head Pot
70002105.description: A pot in the shape of a human face discovered near the Mississippi River in North America. Such items come bearing many kinds of expressions, but most are carved with tattoo-like patterns and holes in the ears.

quests.name: The Urn Patterned After a Face

70002106.name: Clovis Point
70002106.description: A stone implement thought to have been used by the prehistoric Clovis civilization, it is characteristically fluted at the base. Such points were often used to hunt mammoth and bison.

70002109.name: Dragon Bones with Holes
70002109.description: Dragon bones with large holes in the ears discovered in the northern part of the New World. Perhaps the ears helped them hear better or maybe served some other purpose.

70002110.name: Stone with a Plant Pattern
70002110.description: A stone with strange patterns and impressions that look like a fern leaf... Could it be a petrified ancient plant?

70002111.name: Stone with a Pattern
70002111.description: A giant stone covered with a pattern of six-sided shapes. It was discovered near a coal deposit. Could there be a connection?

70002112.name: Rock like a Fanged Lizard
70002112.description: A stone resembling a lizard dug up in Joggins. It has a long and narrow snout for a lizard. Could such a creature have once lived long ago?

70002113.name: Rock like a Long-snouted Lizard
70002113.description: A rock that looks like a lizard measuring over 60 cm long. It was overlapped by other stones when found.

70002115.name: Fanged Animal Bones
70002115.description: An unusual animal with enormous fangs. Its body resembles a cheetah or tiger, meaning that it was likely an agile hunter that used its fangs to tear apart its prey.

70002116.name: Cotton Rosemallow
70002116.description: A plant that grows on the plains of North America that tends to favor sunny areas. It can grow up to 1 meter tall and blooms with large flowers spanning roughly 20 cm.

70002117.name: Tillandsia
70002117.description: A plant that is found from southern North America to central South America. It survives arid climates by absorbing moisture with its leaves and has no roots. There are many varieties possessing a wide range of appearances.

70002118.name: Welwitschia
70002118.description: A giant plant that inhabits the Namib Desert. Its leaves are 1.5 meters wide and reach 3 to 4 meters in length. It has an extremely long lifespan extending hundreds of years.

70002119.name: Venus Flytrap
70002119.description: A carnivorous plant inhabiting the eastern coast of North America. It features pairs of leaves with fang-like projections on the ends and hairs growing on the inward sides. Touching a hair causes the leaves to snap shut. With this mechanism, the plant thus captures and devours insects.

70002120.description: A saprophytic plant found in East Asia, it grows on rotting wood and leaves in dark forests. It seems to have a faint white glow and bears an uncanny resemblance to a cicada.

70002121.name: Dorstenia Foetida
70002121.description: A succulent plant native to the Arabian Peninsula. Its star-shaped center houses a large number of tiny male and female flowers.

70002122.name: Goldenglow
70002122.description: A native plant of North America, it can grow up to 2 meters in height and blossoms with large yellow flowers. It can breed with both its seeds and underground stems.

70002123.name: Mayflower
70002123.description: A plant that is distributed wide and far from Europe to North Africa. It is also called crataegus. Its five-petaled flowers bloom in May.

70002126.name: Laburnum
70002126.description: A native plant of southern Europe. In early summer its yellow flowers blossom in butterfly-shaped trusses. Care should be taken as the entire plant contains a poisonous substance.

70002129.name: American Wisteria
70002129.description: A type of wisteria distributed in southern North America with relatively small flowers growing in trusses that are 15 cm in length.

70002130.name: Pigmy Waterlily
70002130.description: An aquatic plant distributed in East Asia, North America and elsewhere, it grows wild in ponds and other bodies of water with a calm surface. It blooms during the day and has white flowers from early summer to autumn.

70002131.name: Sarracenia
70002131.description: A carnivorous plant with cylindrical leaves that trap insects inside. Its prey is broken apart and absorbed in a digestive fluid at the bottom.

70002132.name: Bluebonnet
70002132.description: A flower that inhabits North America. Its dense formation of small blue flowers looks like a long rug.

70002133.name: Kalmia
70002133.description: A flower that inhabits North America and has star-shaped petals. Each individual flower is small, but together they look like a large blossoming globe.

70002134.name: Phlox
70002134.description: A flower with brightly colored petals. The red variety comes in a fiery hue. It grows in places with ample sunlight.

70002135.name: Monarch Butterfly
70002135.description: A butterfly with a black edge around the entire wing and white spots. Its ability to fly exceeds that of other species, allowing it to migrate thousands of kilometers like a migratory bird.

70002136.name: Bald Eagle
70002136.description: A large eagle inhabiting the New World. Unfurled, its magnificent wings stretch as wide as an adult man's height. The natives respect it as a sacred bird and use its feathers to decorate their clothes.

70002137.name: Golden Eagle
70002137.description: A large bird found throughout North America. Its wingspan exceeds 2 meters. The entire body is covered by dark brown feathers, except for the back of the head, which is a brilliant gold. This bird preys on deer and foxes.

70002138.name: Blue Jay
70002138.description: A bird that lives in eastern North America. The top of its head, back and tail have blue feathers. The crest of feathers upon its head is raised when aggressive or excited.

70002139.name: Northern Cardinal
70002139.description: A red bird often sighted in eastern North America. The male has bright red feathers while the female's are brown.

70002140.name: Purple Gallinule
70002140.description: A bird with vivid bluish feathers that is often sighted in warm swamps and marshes. It appears to stand on the water when it is actually walking on aquatic plants with its skinny legs.

70002141.name: Roseate Spoonbill
70002141.description: A bird with brightly colored pink feathers. It uses its spatulate bill to scoop up fish.

70002142.name: Snowy Owl
70002142.description: A large owl with beautiful white feathers. It rarely inhabits high elevations and is often sighted on plains in cold climates.

70002143.name: Cottontail Rabbit
70002143.description: A rabbit whose name derives from its white cotton-like tail. It runs fast and zigzags to evade predators. This animal's speed has been recorded at over 30 kph.

70002144.name: Lesser Siren
70002144.description: An amphibian with an eel-like body and two legs. The legs have four toes with a well-developed structure.

70002145.name: Common Box Turtle
70002145.description: A type of box turtle inhabiting eastern North America. It has a dome-shaped shell that appears circular when viewed from above. The male has a larger head than the female's as well as thicker, shorter claws on the hind legs.

70002146.name: Common Snapping Turtle
70002146.description: A large turtle that can exceed 40 cm in length. Its stout frame makes it seem even bigger. Hungry snapping turtles are aggressive and best to be avoided.

70002147.name: Megamouth Shark
70002147.description: A shark that inhabits relatively warm waters in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. Despite its enormous body few have seen it, thus whether the sighted specimens were young or full-grown is unknown. It seems to feed by sucking various matter into its gaping mouth.

70002148.name: Frilled Shark
70002148.description: A shark with a long and skinny eel-like body. Reports indicate it dwells in the ocean depths, though details are lacking. It is occasionally caught as bycatch by fishermen. There is much that is unknown about this shark species.

70002149.name: Basking Shark
70002149.description: A large shark reaching 12 meters in length. It often inhabits relatively cold waters. Despite its large body, this shark is gentle and harmless to humans. It is easy to catch when it ventures near the coast.

70002150.name: Bering Wolffish
70002150.description: A fish that inhabits waters in relatively cold regions. It feeds on shellfish and crab by prying their shells open with its sharp, strong teeth. It is calm and will not bite humans if left alone.

70002151.name: Blue Sea Slug
70002151.description: A small sea slug measuring 5 to 8 cm in length. It lives off the east and south coasts of Africa. Some call this creature a gem of the sea for its brilliant blue and silver body.

70002152.name: Giant Isopod
70002152.description: A large crustacean that lives on the floor of the Atlantic Ocean, it can grow as long as 50 cm and weigh more than 1 kg. It swims by turning its rear section towards the sea floor while alternately curling and uncurling its body.

70002153.name: Alligator Gar
70002153.description: A large freshwater fish inhabiting North America that can grow up to 3 meters in length. It feeds on other fish and crustaceans such as shrimp. It has also been known to prey on aquatic birds and small mammals, but it rarely attacks humans.

70002154.name: American Paddlefish
70002154.description: A relative of the sturgeon that inhabits North America. Its distinctive feature is the long snout, but this body part's function is poorly understood. Many people enjoy salting and dining on its eggs, called American Sevruga Caviar.

70002155.name: Hard Clam
70002155.description: A common clam that is often consumed as food, its shell has a rough, ridged surface. It can be found in relatively many places.

70002156.name: Great Auk
70002156.description: A type of flightless marine bird. It is said to be the first creature to be called by the appellation Penguin, and yet it is of a different species than those creatures currently referred to as penguins.

70002157.name: Niagara Falls
70002157.description: The largest group of waterfalls in North America. The flow of the Niagara River is split into three currents by a pair of islands, through which Lake Erie drains into Lake Ontario. The clouds of mist constantly spewing forth make for an impressive sight.

70002158.name: Mosi-oa-Tunya
70002158.description: A giant waterfall located in southern Africa. The name means the Smoke that Thunders. Fittingly, the roaring water sounds like thunder when the rainy season adds to the river's volume.

70002159.name: Iguazu Falls
70002159.description: A giant waterfall in South America that is roughly 4 km wide. The name comes from a local phrase meaning big water. The sight of the falls, which is the widest torrent of falling water in the world, lives up to the name.

70002160.name: Mammoth Cave
70002160.description: A limestone cave system located in North America, its length spans over 500 km. The sandstone layer lying above the limestone makes the caverns remarkably stable.

70002161.name: Angel Falls
70002161.description: A large waterfall in the northern part of South America. Since the water falls nearly 1 km, most of it dissipates into mist before reaching the bottom, Therefore, the waterfall has no basin.

70002162.name: Prince Edward Island
70002162.description: An island in North America with a warm climate and productive land. It is said that the island's southern end was once connected to the mainland.

70002163.name: St. Lawrence River
70002163.description: A large river that flows from the North American continent's interior to its eastern coast. It is a very wide river with islands both large and small located between its banks.

70002164.name: Nantucket Island
70002164.description: A small island off the coast of North America, temperatures here are low year-round and snowfall is heavy in winter. There have been numerous sightings of whales in the waters nearby.

70002165.name: Mount Desert Island
70002165.description: This island is divided in half by an inlet. Bare granite can be seen protruding from the ground throughout the island. Many animals live here due to infrequent human visitation.

70002166.name: Cape Cod
70002166.description: An arm-shaped peninsula in northern North America with cool summers and warm winters. Its name stems from the fish of the same name often caught in the waters around the cape.

70002167.name: Outer Banks
70002167.description: A line of peninsulas and sandbars on the eastern coast of North America that stretches for over 500 km from north to south. The two ocean currents converging in the area make maritime navigation difficult.

70002168.name: Pamlico Sound
70002168.description: A triangular lagoon surrounded by peninsulas. The dreaded pirate Blackbeard supposedly had...or perhaps still has...his base of operations here.

70002169.name: Paris
70002169.description: A city that grew from a settlement on the island of Ile de la Cite, which is located between the banks of the Seine River. The ramparts built to surround Ile de la Cite were expanded to encompass present day Paris. The climate is relatively warm.

70002170.name: Florence
70002170.description: A city that grew as a manufacturing, trade and financial center. Florence has drawn together and strengthened bonds between countless merchants and artisans, including the famous Medici family of financiers. The city's current name comes from Florentia, as it was called in Ancient Rome.

70002171.name: Labrador Peninsula
70002171.description: A peninsula on the north of the new continent. An area with extreme climate, where it is said that even in the southern regions, the ocean is frozen over for long periods of time. It is believed to be the place referred to in Viking legends as Markland.

quests.name: The bounty of the frozen sea

70002172.name: Terra Nova
70002172.description: An island on the northern part of the new continent. The land is cold and even in summer, snow crowns the mountains. It was discovered by Cavot, an explorer of Genoa. It is believed to be the location of Vinland, a place reached by the Vikings nearly 500 years before Cavot arrived there.

quests.name: The Future of the Land of Grapes

70002173.name: Albacore
70002173.description: A type of tuna with a long pectoral fin. Seen from above it appears to be spreading a pair of wings. It is a fatty fish with valuable uses in cooking and more.

70002174.name: Roman Forum
70002174.description: The ruins of the Roman Forum, the center of ancient Roman politics, economics, and religion. Multiple buildings remain, the Plaza, the Parliament, the Temples, all of which give witness to the prosperity of ancient Rome.

70002175.name: Coliseum
70002175.description: A circular arena built during the time of the Roman Empire. It is said to have held over 40,000 people and hosted numerous events and fights. It is thought that its name came from its proximity to the huge statue of Nero, called the Colossus.

70002176.name: Cathedral of Notre Dame
70002176.description: A Christian cathedral built to honor the Blessed Virgin Mary. Notre Dame is French for Noble Lady, and refers to the mother of Jesus Christ. Buildings of the same name can be found in many places within the French sphere of influence.

quests.name: The Cathedral Dedicated to the Holy Mother

70002177.name: Sainte-Chapelle
70002177.description: A Christian chapel built on Ile de la Cite in Paris that hosts numerous relics. It is known for its beautiful stained glass and Gothic structures.

70002178.name: Paestum Ruins
70002178.description: Ruins of ancient Greece and Rome. It can be found in the Campagna area of Italy. In addition to its religious remains, it also shows the ruins of a plaza and a market.

70002179.name: Viking Steel Spike
70002179.description: A steel spike discovered from the remains of what appear to be workshops in the L'Anse aux Meadows ruins. It is believed to have been used in the ships the Vikings built. It is an artifact that shows the steel culture brought by the Vikings to the American continent over 1000 years ago.

70002180.description: A traditional percussion instrument of the Korean peninsula. Both ends are covered with leather. The right side is struck with a small stick and the left is struck with either a stick with a rounded end or the palm of the left hand. Most often used in prayers for the harvest or in festivals for the ancestors.

70002181.name: Black Spruce
