70002181.description: A type of tree that grows from the eastern part of North America to the north. Grows to be almost 25 meters tall, with branches growing like a cone around the trunk. Very hard wood, making it a popular material for building.

70002182.name: Balsam Fir
70002182.description: A tree that grows in the north eastern area of North America. It attains around 20 meters in height, with branches growing in a circular pattern around the tree. It gives off a faintly sweet aroma similar to vanilla.

70002183.name: Jack Pine
70002183.description: A tree that grows from the north to northeast of North America. The tree forms a wide cone shape with the branches bending irregularly.

70002184.name: American Mink
70002184.description: A North American animal who inhabits the areas around rivers and lakes. Has a dark brown fur of fine quality. A bit larger than the European mink.

quests.name: The Beguiling Fur of the New Land

70002185.name: Newfoundland
70002185.description: A breed of dogs originating in the area of Terra Nova, along the northern section of the North American coast line. With its large size, resistance to cold, and ability to swim, it was known as a fishing dog and could be frequently found in fishing villages.

70002186.name: American Black Bear
70002186.description: Lives in both the warm and cold areas of North America. A relatively calm, peaceful type, still it is extremely quick and loves to climb trees.

70002187.name: Giant Squid
70002187.description: A type of huge squid. It is said to achieve a length of over 10 meters in length. Thought to live in the deep ocean, sightings of the giant squid are extremely rare.

70002188.name: Gros Morne
70002188.description: A mountain in western Terra Nova, along the northeastern coast of North America, reaching around 800 meters in height. Due to the cold currents that flow beside the island, the temperature is extremely low and plants normally found on extremely high mountains can be found here.

70002189.name: Long Range Mountains
70002189.description: A mountain range located in the western part of Terra Nova, along the northeastern part of North America. It is the northern edge of the Appalachian mountain range.

70002190.name: Cabot Strait
70002190.description: A strait found along the northeastern coast of North America. About 11km wide, it is the widest strait allowing entrance into the Gulf of Saint Lawrence from the Atlantic Ocean.

70002191.name: Lewis Hills
70002191.description: A mountain found in the western part of Terra Nova, along the northeastern coast of North America. Rising to a height of 814 meters, it is the highest mountain on Terra Nova, being slightly taller than Gros Morne, the other tall mountain of the Long Range mountains.

70002192.name: Appalachian Mountains
70002192.description: A mountain range in the eastern part of North America. Running northeast to southwest, the range stretches over 2000km in length. The western side of the mountain range is rich in coal deposits.

quests.name: The Geography of Eastern North America

70002193.name: Cape Spear
70002193.description: A cape located on the northeastern part of Terra Nova, along the northeastern coast of North America. It is considered the eastern most point of North America. The cape looks out over the Atlantic Ocean, and whales can sometimes be seen swimming in the waters from there.

70002194.name: Grand Banks
70002194.description: A plateau on the bottom of the ocean, spreading out from the south eastern bay of Terra Nova. Well known as an excellent fishing spot due to the junction of the cold Labrador current and the warm current that flows up from the Gulf of Mexico.

quests.name: Rumors of a Fine Place to Fish

70002195.name: Labrador Current
70002195.description: A cold current flowing south from the southwest coast of Greenland to the northeastern coast of North America. With thick fogs and icebergs floating down from Greenland as the heat rises in spring, sailing in these seas can be dangerous.

quests.name: A Sea of Ice and Mist

70002196.name: Palatine Hill
70002196.description: One of the hills of Rome. The hill sports the remains of ancient Roman temples and living quarters. Of all the many hills of Rome, this one is believed to have the oldest history.

70002197.name: Cape Farewell
70002197.description: The cape located at the southern most tip of Greenland. The land of Greenland is covered in ice and snow for the most part, but during the summer, you can see land from the coast along capes like these.

70002198.name: Strait of Belle Isle
70002198.description: A strait located between North America's Labrador Peninsula and Terra Nova. It is an extremely narrow strait with an average width of only 18 km and a maximum of 60 km. The current is strong and the fairly bad climate produces occasional fog and strong winds, which makes sailing the area fairly difficult.

70002199.name: Bay of Fundy
70002199.description: A bay located between the eastern coast of North America and the peninsula of Nova Scotia. The variation in tides is great, with a difference of 15 meters between high and low tide.

70002200.name: Strait of Messina
70002200.description: A strait situated between the Italian peninsula and the island of Sicily. At its narrowest, it is only from 3-4 km wide and is known for its swift currents.

70002201.name: Saga of Erik the Red
70002201.description: A tale centered on the Viking hero, Erik the Red. Tells the story of Erik's move to Greenland and the search of the west by Thorfinn the Valiant.

70002202.name: Iceland
70002202.description: An island northwest of the British Isles. Uninhabited for the longest time, around the 10th century, waves of Celts and Scandinavians moved there. As its name implies, much of the land is covered in ice glaciers. However, as it is in a volcanic belt, the land itself is relatively warm.

70002203.name: Greenland
70002203.description: An island northwest of Iceland. Covered in sheets of ice and perpetual snow, much of the island remains unexplored. Only a portion of the coastline is free of ice and inhabitable. However, the Vikings called this land the Land of Green and encouraged people to immigrate there.

70002204.name: Saga of the Greenlanders
70002204.description: A tale of Erik's entry and life on Greenland, as well as that of his children. Includes the tale of Thorfinn's western explorations. Part of it seems to be based on the Saga of Erik the Red. But unlike the former tale, this one seems to be slightly exaggerated.

quests.name: Clues to the Land of Fables

70002205.name: Ancient Spool of Thread
70002205.description: A spool of thread found at the remains of L'Anse aux Meadows. Made after an old European method, this shows that the Vikings brought it and attempted to live here.

70002206.name: Silver Armour
70002206.description: Viking mail found on the Scandinavian Peninsula. Like the helmet, it has been decorated with silver. Believed to belong to Thorfinn. It has been passed down for generations in Snorri and Olga's clan.

70002207.name: Mjolnir
70002207.description: Hammer of Thor, Norse god of thunder, so powerful that it could defeat any enemy in a single blow. The one exception to this was the Midgard Serpent, child of Loki. In Europe, pendants in the form of Mjolnir are used as protection charms.

70002208.name: Avalon Peninsula
70002208.description: A peninsula on the southeastern part of Terra Nova. With a convoluted coastline, there are numerous bays and inlets in that area. An excellent fishing spot.

70002209.name: Silverware
70002209.description: Silver eating utensils used by the Medici family. These utensils were not uncommon among the nobility. It is said that it was first introduced to guard against poisoning, as it darkens when it comes in contact with the same.

70002210.name: Medicine of the Medici
70002210.description: A medical treatment from the secret stores of the Medici family, traders in medicines. Rumors have it that those who use this medicine, get well quickly.

70002211.name: Cameo of Cupid and the Lion
70002211.description: One of the cameos gathered by Lorenzo. An engraving of a lion and an angel.

70002212.name: Medici Prescription
70002212.description: A prescription from the secret stores of the Medici family, traders in medicines. Describes how to compound certain medicines from herbs, wild medicinal plants, bark, and other things.

70002213.name: Plato's Complete Works
70002213.description: Books on philosophy written by Plato, student of Socrates. It was translated into Latin by Marsilio Ficino, court physician to Cosimo de' Medici, and gained popularity in Florence.

70002214.name: Text on Hermes
70002214.description: A book obtained by Cosimo and translated into Latin by Marsilio Ficino. It was put together in the Eastern Roman Empire, but appears to be based on a book on philosophy written in Egypt.

70002215.name: Cosimo's Medal
70002215.description: A golden medal engraven with the profile of Lorenzo's grandfather, Cosimo. Cosimo contributed much to the development of both the Medici family and Florence, being a patron of the arts and of literature.

70002216.name: Monadnock
70002216.description: A level mountain found in North America. It's name comes from the languages of one of the North American native tribes. Loosely translated, it's name means mountain that stands alone.

70002217.name: Gaspe Peninsula
70002217.description: A peninsula located on the southern side of the mouth of the St. Lawrence River. Numerous ancient fossils have been on its southern shores.

70002218.name: Puffin
70002218.description: A water fowl found on the northern parts of North America's eastern shores, as well as on the shores of northern Europe. From the small, black horn above its eyes, it is sometimes called a Horned Puffin. Though it somewhat resembles the penguin, this bird is capable of flight.

70002219.name: Osprey
70002219.description: A large bird found on most of the coasts of North America. Fish eaters, they tend to fly low over the water and drop down to get there prey. Overall a blackish brown color, their heads sport a white crown of feathers.

70002220.name: Black-capped Chickadee
70002220.description: A small bird found in the northern area of North America. Alert for danger, this small bird changes its cry depending on the level of danger it senses.

70002221.name: Rome
70002221.description: The great capital of Italy, dating far back. It lasted through many changes, from a kingdom, to a republic to an empire and left behind numerous ruins. The coliseum is one of those remains.

70002222.name: Silver Helmet
70002222.description: A Viking helmet found at the remains of L'Anse aux Meadows. Decorated with silver, it appears to be something a normal warrior would have. Was there a silver mine nearby? Or was it brought here in trade?

70002223.name: Shining Golden Bow
70002223.description: A large bow, decorated with gold and silver. Beautiful in appearance, the decorations make it extremely heavy, requiring great strength to use. The Vikings used bows in their sea battles. Skilled people with bows were said to be the difference between victory and defeat.

70002224.name: Desert Rose
70002224.description: A hardened lump of a rock-like substance in the form of a rose seen only rarely in the desert. Thought to be comprised of sand, but also has a transparent substance in it that may be crystal.

70002225.name: Atlas Mountains
70002225.description: A mountain chain running from Algiers to Casablanca along the North African coast. Snow can be seen on the higher peaks. It's name is taken from the Greek mythological Titan Atlas, who was forced by Zeus to hold up the world in the west.

70002226.name: Toubkal
70002226.description: Located in Morocco, this peak is the highest peak in the Atlas mountains. From its top, you can see the beauty of the Atlas mountains spread out before you.

70002227.name: Spathodea
70002227.description: A flowering tree frequently seen in western Africa. It's red flowers are like flames reaching up from the trees, captivating the eyes with its beauty. The tree reaches over 10m in height.

70002228.name: Kalahari Desert
70002228.description: A large desert spreading over much of the southern parts of Africa. The sand is a dark red and there are few oasis. With scattered savannahs in many shallow basins, the area is populated with numerous animals.

70002229.name: Kora
70002229.description: A stringed instrument from western Africa. It's 21 keys are plucked using the thumb and forefinger. Using this instrument, musicians have passed on the both the traditions and stories from ancient times and the news of current times.

70002230.name: Azawakh
70002230.description: A dog breed found in western Africa. Though it's legs and tail are long and slender, it's extremely muscular and has excellent physical abilities.

70002231.name: Twyfelfontein
70002231.description: A site of over 2000 ancient rock engravings in the western Africa. Comprised primarily of animals such as elephants and giraffes, there are also pictures of what might be human feet.

70002232.name: Djembe
70002232.description: An instrument used in western Africa. Also known as a Jembe. A one sided drum, with the head being around 30 cm in diameter and the body about 60 cm deep. Held between the knees, it makes a variety of sounds ranging from high to low depending on how and where the drumhead is struck.

70002233.name: Lake Retba
70002233.description: A lake found in West Africa. A salty lake with a higher salinity than the ocean itself. The waters appear pink, and when the water levels fall during the dry season, the color becomes even more rich and beautiful.

70002234.name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
70002234.description: A grove revered by the natives of West Africa. Said to be the living place of the Orisha, Oshun from the mythology of the Yoruba people.

70002235.name: Blue Crane
70002235.description: A type of crane found in South Africa. Its body is a bluish gray color of about 100cm in length. The feathers of the breast and tail are long, with the tail in particular often reaching the ground.

70002236.name: King Protea
70002236.description: A flowering plant found in South Africa. The branches grow to almost 2m in length and its flower is approximately 30 cm in diameter.

70002237.name: Honey Badger
70002237.description: A widely spread animal who lives in savannas and plains from Africa to west and south Asia. It's skin is thick and elastic. In particular it's back is proof against the fangs of other predators. It also is resistant to poisons, like snake venom, making snakes one of its prey.

70002238.name: Secretarybird
70002238.description: A bird of prey found from central to southern Africa. The long feathers growing from the rear of its head looked like the feather pens used by secretaries at the time, resulting in its name.

70002239.name: Hadrian's Wall
70002239.description: Earthworks built at the command of Emperor Hadrian during the time of the Roman Empire. It is said to have guarded against incursions by the Celts into Empire territory. The wall is said to have taken 10 years to build and covered 110 kilometers.

70002240.name: Antonine Wall
70002240.description: Earthworks built at the command of Emperor Antoninus Hadrian during the time of the Roman Empire. The 60 km wall was built over the extremely short period of only 2 years.

70002241.name: Bath
70002241.description: An area located in the southwestern portion of the British Isles. Famous for the hot springs that come up in the area. During the Roman empire, the area was developed under the personal control of the Emperor, and there are still the remains of a number of Roman style buildings in the area.

70002242.name: Mesa
70002242.description: A land formation that appears in the form of a table and common to the western portion of North American. It is said that these outcroppings evolve when a hard layer of earth lies atop softer layers. As time goes on the lower layer is eaten away resulting in this form.

70002243.name: Butte
70002243.description: A land formation that looks like a giant pillar. Formed when the table like mesas are broken up and eroded. Commonly seen in the North American west.

70002244.name: Prairie
70002244.description: A huge area of flat grasslands in the center of North America. The grass grows long. The land is exceptionally fertile and good for farming,

70002245.name: Great Plains
70002245.description: A plateau like plain area located in the central western area of North America. The area is covered in a shortbladed grass. There is little rain and the area is generally dry.

quests.name: On to the Plains of Freedom!

70002246.name: Prairie Dog
70002246.description: An animal from the Great plain area of central North America. It's body is between 30-40 cm long. It digs deep into the ground to create it's nest. It's name originates from the sound it makes, which is said to resemble the cry of a dog.

70002247.name: Southern Magnolia
70002247.description: A flowering tree that grows in the south of central North America. White flowers bloom in early summer. The upper side of the green leaves are lustrous, but the reverse side is covered in tiny hairs giving it a brownish look.

quests.name: A Tree like the Mulan Magnolia

70002248.name: Flowering Dogwood
70002248.description: A flowering tree of North America. In late spring it blooms with a white or faint pink flower and carries a red fruit in the fall.

70002249.name: Carlsbad Caverns
70002249.description: A series of caves in the south western part of North America. Has a huge underground cavern and numerous stalactites. The caves are the home to bats, and when night falls, you can see hordes of them leaving the caves.

70002250.name: Loch Ness
70002250.description: A lake in the northern part of the British Isles. It sports a long gourd-like shape with a width of approximately 2km. The waters of the lake glow with a dark blueish color. Rumors have it of a mysterious creature living there.

70002251.name: Isle of Skye
70002251.description: An island on the west in the northern parts of the British Isles. They say the name of the island originates either from the old Nordic language, or from the legends of Scathach. It is also sometimes called the Isle of the Mist.

70002252.name: Islay
70002252.description: An island on the west in the northern parts of the British Isles. Due to the surrounding currents, this island has milder weather than the main island.

70002253.name: Lewis
70002253.description: Northern part of the British Isles. Island to the west. The island with the largest land mass of the nearby islands. The southern part is called also by a different name. The island has ruins showing the use of huge rocks and stones.

70002254.name: Burren
70002254.description: The plains that spread out in the western part of Ireland. In Irish the name means the desolate plains. As the name implies, ancient rocks can be found across the area. The area was never tamed by man and unique plants and ancient ruins can be found there.

70002255.name: Giant's Table
70002255.description: An ancient site located in the Burren in Ireland. It is thought to be a burial site created in the Neolithic period. The largest mystery was how this large stone was moved.

70002256.name: Book of Kells
70002256.description: A hand written copy of the Bible created in the 8th century. With beautiful calligraphy done in the Celtic Insular Art style, it appears more a work of art than a book. It contains the four gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.

quests.name: The most beautiful book in the world

70002257.name: Book of Durrow
70002257.description: The oldest handwritten copy of the bible created in Ireland or the British Isles. Similar to the Book of Kells, it is decorated in beautiful calligraphy. The letters are written in a peculiar style called Island letters.

70002258.name: Lindisfarne Gospels
70002258.description: A handwritten copy of the four books of the Gospels. Though done in beautiful calligraphy similar to the Book of Kells, it is written in Latin. Originally, it was decorated with gems and precious metals, but these were lost to the Vikings.

70002259.name: Skellig Michael
70002259.description: A lone island to the west of Ireland. The Irish name translates to Michael's rock in English. The island is a rocky mountain with a distinct tilt. There is a convent at the top of the mountain there. It is said that it withstood viking attacks in the past.

70002260.name: Coyote
70002260.description: A type of dog from North America. The name derives from the Nahuatl word meaning singing dog and originates from their tendency to howl. It resembles the wolf, but with a body length of around 1m, it is smaller than a wolf.

70002261.name: Red Wolf
70002261.description: A type of wolf found in the central and southern parts of North America. Resembles the coyote, with whom it shares territories, but is slightly larger in size. Large differences can be found in fur color, but it is generally reddish in color.

70002262.name: Passenger Pigeon
70002262.description: A bird that lives on the east coast of North America. Its body is around 40cm in length, with long pointed wings and tail. It tends to migrate in extremely large groups, spending summers in the north-eastern parts of North America and winters primarily around the Bay of Mexico.

quests.name: Birds of a Feather Flock Together

70002263.name: Red-headed Woodpecker
70002263.description: A type of woodpecker found in the eastern parts of North America. Has a body length of around 25 cm. The black and white striped appearance on it's back and the deep red color of it's head make this bird stand out.

70002264.name: White Clover
70002264.description: A plant that grows primarily in Europe. Puts out a white flower from spring to fall. Flourishes even in infertile and barren land, and has the added effect of improving the ground's fertility.

quests.name: The Good Acts of a Farmer's Daughter

70002265.name: Battersea Shield
70002265.description: A trove of shields discovered near London. Primarily bronze but also including some wooden shields. From the decorations, it is believed to be of Celtic origin.

70002266.name: Cliffs of Moher
70002266.description: The cliffs touching the sea west of Southern Ireland. Its name means the Cliff of Ruin. The colors there on a clear day are said to be spectacular.

70002267.name: Loch Tummel
70002267.description: A slender, long lake running east to west in the northern part of the British Isles. Green trees and fields surround the deep blue waters of this lake. In particular, the north eastern banks of this lake are exceptionally beautiful.

70002268.name: Purple Coneflower
70002268.description: A plant that grows from the east to the central southern portions of North America. From summer to autumn, reddish-purple blossoms grace the trees. It's root is also used as a medicine.

quests.name: Request for Cooperation from Market Keeper

70002269.name: Gamla Uppsala
70002269.description: The name of the region to the north of Stockholm. Until the middle ages, it was considered the center of Northern European culture and hosted the castle and mausoleum of the kings of Sweden. Nearby is Uppsula University, the oldest University in Europe. Also, several influential men originated here, like Axel Gustafsson Oxenstierna, right hand man to Gustavus Adolphus.

70002270.name: Discourse on the Method
70002270.description: A book by the French philosopher, Descartes. Discusses how to think or consider things and also discusses some of the background of Descartes himself. Some say it is from the period when he was enlisted in the army of Maurice of Nassau.

70002271.name: The Exercise of Armes
70002271.description: Written by Maurice of Nassau, Prince of Orange. He details the training of men, and was able to improve understanding of the process. This book contained all the information he used to make his army one of the most successful in the Europe of his time.

70002272.name: Iona
70002272.description: A very small island to the west of the northern part of the British Isles. Small enough to circle the island on foot in one day. The convent on this island was built by Saint Columba, who then used the island as the center of his missionary efforts.

70002273.name: Oxford
70002273.description: A university town located to the northwest of London. Prospered as a source of wool in its early days. In the 8th century a convent for nuns was built there. Then in the 12th century, students began to assemble there, and it began to prosper as a seat of learning.

70002274.name: Tchoga Zanbil
70002274.description: A religious structure build by the ancient Elamites. The area is surrounded by 3 walls with a ziggurat in the innermost area. It is surprisingly well preserved.

70002275.name: Uruk
70002275.description: A Sumerian city that flourished in ancient Mesopotamia. Many clay tablets covered with ancient writing have been found, showing that this place was once the political and economical center of the area.

70002276.name: Lagash
70002276.description: A Sumerian city that flourished in ancient Mesopotamia. It dwindled after being conquered by Lugal-Zage-Si, King of the neighboring country of Umma.

70002277.name: Nin-me-sara
70002277.description: A poem written by Enheduanna, High Priestess of Ur and daughter of Sargon, first King of Akkad. The poem is thought to seek the blessings of Inanna against the rebellions that were bringing chaos to the land.

70002278.name: Ferula Gummosa
70002278.description: A plant commonly found in the mid-east. It's stalk grows to around 2 meters in height, with yellow flowers growing at the end. The oil taken from its sap is used in perfumes and medicine.

70002279.name: Date Palm
70002279.description: A tree found in the Mid-East and in Northern Africa. The tree grows to over 15 meters in height, with leaves as long as 3 meters. It was highly prized in areas like Mesopotamia and Egypt for its highly nutritional fruit.

70002280.name: Epic of Atra-Hasis
70002280.description: An epic poem from ancient Mesopotamia that records legend of a flood, similar to that recorded in the Epic of Gilgamesh. The name of the person who survived the flood was called Atra-Hasis or Exceedingly Wise.

70002281.name: Enuma Elish
70002281.description: An epic recording the Babylonian creation myths. It names numerous gods and is intended to show how the formerly great Babylonian Empire was better than all other countries.

70002282.name: Zagros Mountains
70002282.description: A huge mountain range that stretches from Hormuz to Turkey. The remains of a once flourishing kingdom can be found there. Legends say that the ship that survived the flood came to ground somewhere in these mountains. However, the truth is still unclear.

70002283.name: Stele of Naram-sin
70002283.description: The stele of Naram-sin, King of Akkad. The Akkad kingdom was located in the northern regions of the southern Mesopotamian land of Babylonia. Naram-sin conquered the surrounding areas, increasing the size of his empire. He later proclaimed himself a god.

70002284.name: Relief of Ea
70002284.description: Ea appears in Babylonian myth and is believed to have originally been the patron god of the city of Eridu in the south of Ur. In the Flood mythology, he is said to have been the one to teach the hero how to build the ship. He is called Enki in Mesopotamian mythology.

70002285.name: Statue of Inanna
70002285.description: Inanna was the Sumerian goddess of fertility and love and was revered as the patron goddess of Uruk. She was called Ishtar in Akkadian lore.

70002286.name: Frankfurt
70002286.description: The town, located in the western part of Germany, grew as the center of the Holy Roman Empire. It is said the name originated in the 5th century as the place for the Franks to ford the Main river. St. Bartholomew's Cathedral was appointed the location of the Imperial Elections and the Coronation ceremony.

70002287.name: Shakespeare's Sonnets
70002287.description: An anthology of poetry comprised of 154 sonnets presented by Shakespeare. The main themes include love, human beauty, and death. Sonnets are poems of a set rhyme scheme over 14 lines that originated in Italy in the 12th century.

70002288.name: Yew
70002288.description: A conifer tree commonly found in European gardens. The red berries are edible, but the seeds and leaves are poisonous. Frequently planted around churches in England and Ireland.

70002289.name: Sutton Hoo
70002289.description: An ancient cemetery located in the eastern part of the British islands. Some bodies were found buried in boats with numerous other burial items, rather than in coffins. It is a great source of knowledge regarding ancient living practices.

70002290.name: Galilei's Lute
70002290.description: Galileo's father Vincenzo was a lutist who advanced his own unique theories in music. His lute was said to control even dissonance. It looks normal, but…

70002291.name: Oresund
70002291.description: The strait separating the island of Zealand on which is located Copenhagen with the Scandinavian Peninsula. At its narrowest, it is only 7 km across. It is a strategic point for trade between the North and Baltic seas.

70002292.name: Hawaii
70002292.description: A town on a solitary island in the heart of the Pacific Ocean. Polynesians presumably migrated here between the 4th and 8th centuries. It has many volcanoes and its land is composed of hardened lava.

70002293.name: Kokkola
70002293.description: A town in Finland, located on the coast of the Gulf of Bothnia, which Gustav II Adolf charted. The town was originally built as a port for industrial trade but later thrived as a shipbuilding base.

70002294.name: Kanawao
70002294.description: A hydrangea indigenous to Hawaii. Its fruits, often eaten simmered or dried, are believed to bring the blessing of children. Because of this, people were delighted when this fruit blossomed, believing it to be a sign of good luck.

70002295.name: Heiau
70002295.description: A place to worship gods, goddesses and spirits, they are surrounded by stone walls and located all over the Island of Hawaii. Some of them have different names depending on what is worshipped there.

quests.name: A holy place surrounded by stones

70002296.name: Lono-makua
70002296.description: Ornament symbolizing the Hawaiian god, Lono, associated with fertility, agriculture and rainfall. Lono's face is carved in the center of a wooden stick with a white cloth hung from it. Displayed at harvest festivals.

70002297.name: Uli Uli
70002297.description: Hawaiian musical percussion instrument, decorated with colourfully dyed feathers. Made of dried nut shells or gourd shells filled with seeds or dried beans. Also used in rituals.

70002298.name: Maile
70002298.description: A native Hawaiian vine considered to be sacred. Its dark green leaves have a fresh aroma. It was used as decoration and was worn around the necks of duel winners in ancient times.

70002299.name: Alae Ula
70002299.description: A bird that, according to legend, brought fire to Hawaii. Its forehead and beak are red in colour. Ula means red in the local tongue.

70002300.name: The Island of Hawaii
70002300.description: The largest of the Hawaiian Islands, located in the North Pacific Ocean. This volcanic island consists mostly of congealed lava.

quests.name: In the middle of the Pacific Ocean

70002301.name: The Life Records of a Saint
70002301.description: The life story of an individual of the Kievan Rus' that later became a saint. Written by Nestor the Chronicler, it is described in the Primary Chronicle as well.

70002302.name: The Portrait of Boris and Gleb
70002302.description: The portrait of the two brothers of Kievan Russ who were later canonized. They piously followed their Christian principles despite oppression from their older, pagan brother.

70002303.name: Gold Coin of Vladimir I
70002303.description: A gold coin depicting the ruler of the Kievan Rus', Vladimir the Great. The Grand Prince, a skilled diplomat and politician, married the younger sister of the Eastern Roman Emperor, Basil the 2nd, and contributed to the strengthening of the Kievan Rus'.

quests.name: The golden age of the Kievan Rus'

70002304.name: The Tale of Igor's Campaign
70002304.description: An epic recording the failed campaign of Prince Igor. It is said to have been written during the time of the Kievan Rus'. Igor undertook a campaign to repel nomads.

70002305.name: Handprint of Peter the Great
70002305.description: A handprint of the Russian Emperor, Peter the Great. To learn how to establish a navy, he himself went to the shipyards and learnt to swing a hammer. This stalwart strength can be seen from his large handprint.

quests.name: A thorough investigation of a czar

70002306.name: Wooden Sculpture of Perun
70002306.description: Perun is the highest god of the Slavic pantheon. His name means the one who strikes down in old Slavic, and is the god of thunder and storms. In myth, he smote down opposing gods with lightning bolts, and thus was worshipped by warriors as a god of victorious wars.

70002307.name: Wooden Sculpture of Velez
70002307.description: A wooden sculpture of a god of Slavic myth. Velez was the god of livestock and wealth, and was loved by the commons. Velez is also associated with the souls of the dead. In the Tale of Igor's Campaign, a legendary bard is said to be a grandson of Velez.

70002308.name: Relief of Dazbog
70002308.description: A sculpture of the sun god of Slavic myth. In the Tale of Igor's Campaign, the people on the Russian side were said to be descendants of Dazbog.

70002309.name: Relief of Svarog
70002309.description: A sculpture of a god of Slavic myth. Svarog is the father of the sun god, Dazbog, and represents fire and the hearth.

70002310.name: February Daphne
70002310.description: A shrub commonly found from Southern Europe to Russia. It flowers in early spring. Its fruit and branches carry toxins.

70002311.name: A Silver Cross
70002311.description: A silver cross thought to have been carried by the Slavs. They were distributed on the coastal region of the Baltic coast, Balkans and the Black sea coast from the 6th century.

70002312.name: Stone Fragment with Phags Pa Characters
70002312.description: A stone fragment inscripted with characters from the Mongolian Empire. It's read from top to bottom.

70002313.name: Eelpout
70002313.description: A fish that lives in the deeps of cold seas, like the Arctic Ocean. It is about 20 cm in length, and has no scales. It swims as if crawling in the seabeds.

70002314.name: King Salmon
70002314.description: Also known as Chinook salmon. Lives in the North Pacific, and has the distinct characteristic of returning to the place in the river of its birth to spawn. Its length can be as long as 1.5 metres. Its flesh is fatty and delicious.

70002315.name: The Jamaica Channel
70002315.description: A channel located to the northeast of Jamaica. This region is full of small islands which house pirates. Exercise caution when sailing these waters.

70002316.name: Mongolian Cattle
70002316.description: A type of cattle of Central Eurasia kept by nomads. They are often allowed to roam freely. Its size is small, yet it is well adapted for cold climates.

70002317.name: Yurt
70002317.description: Mobile dwellings of the nomads, made of wood and cloth. They are found in Xanadu. A circular frame is covered by cloth, it is easy to assemble and disassemble.

70002318.name: Composite Bow
70002318.description: A small bow made from a variety of materials, including wood or bamboo, animal bone, and metal plate to increase the range and power. Because the bow craftsmen keep its construction method secret, you do not know the details on how it is made.

quests.name: The skills of the Mongolian archers

70002319.name: Morin Khuur
70002319.description: A type of string instrument named after its horsehead decoration. A 100 horse tail hairs are used as its two strings, and they are played with a bow. The music sounding from the square box-shaped instrument has depth of tone.

70002320.name: Urga
70002320.description: A traditional Mongolian tool. A long stick with a hooped rope at its tip. Used to capture small horses.

70002321.name: Lake Baikal
70002321.description: A large lake located between Southeast Russia and northern Mongolia. Its water is fed by many lakes and streams, boasting a richness of animal life.

70002322.name: Historic Mongolian Texts
70002322.description: A text that records the Mongolian Phags pa scripts, and east Asian languages. Author unknown, with many copies in existence.

70002323.name: Bactrian Camel
70002323.description: Camel with two humps on its back. It has shorter limbs than a regular camel. Valued for transport, locomotion and various other purposes

70002324.name: Pirate's Contract
70002324.description: An agreement between pirates. As a contract between pirates that follow no laws, it is of questionable binding power.

70002325.name: Fading Pirate Flag
70002325.description: It appears to be a pirate flag of sorts. Pirate flags are used for the identification of allies are known as the pride of a pirate fleet

70002326.name: Lysmata Amboinensis
70002326.description: A type of shrimp found in the corals of the Caribbean. Has a single white line running down its back, sandwiched by vivid red lines on either side.

70002327.name: A View of the Caribbean
70002327.description: A pale blue stone called Larimar, found in the vicinity of the Bahamas. Its beautiful color is reminiscent of the Caribbean Sea, and is relaxing to the mind of the bearer.

70002328.name: Greater Bulldog Bat
70002328.description: A type of fishing bat native to South America and the Caribbean. It catches small fish from the surface of lakes and swamps. Because of its diet, it has a strong body odour.

quests.name: The sound of water in the darkness of night

70002329.name: Grouse
70002329.description: Coastal birds of the Arctic Ocean and alpine areas of northern Eurasia. Its feathers change from brown in the summer to white in the winter.

70002330.name: Ab Urbe Condita Libri
70002330.description: A monumental history of the founding of Rome, reconstructed from scattered chapters. The original work by Titus Livius had over 100 chapters, and many have not been found.

70002331.name: Campeche Fortress
70002331.description: A fortress built in Campeche which is a trade port facing the Gulf of Mexico. Made for defense from any pirate attacks.

70002332.name: The Legend of Vampires
70002332.description: A literary work that compiles the many legends in Europe of a monster that thrives on human blood. At night, buried corpses are said to crawl forth from their graves and prey on humans. They seem to be based on Slavic folklore.

quests.name: The legend of one that cannot die

70002333.name: Samovar
70002333.description: A Russian water heater. Water goes into the outer compartment of the cylinder and is heated from a fire inside. Thermal insulation is possible if objects are placed inside the lid. A unique tool, essential to cold regions.

70002334.name: The Secret History of the Mongols
70002334.description: A Mongolian history book. Author unknown. Mainly revolves around Ghengis Khan's life. It also touches on the ruling of his successor Ogedei

quests.name: History book of the Yuan dynasty

70002335.name: History of Pirates
70002335.description: A collection of biographies of pirates active from the end of the 17th century through the early 18th century. The lives of many pirates are written down scrupulously.

quests.name: A Pirate Tale Handed Down in Europe

70002336.name: The Seafarer's Castaway Story
70002336.description: The writings about the Scottish sea captain, Alexander Selkirk, and his life during the time he was stranded on a deserted island. His state and how he lived a self-sufficient life there is written down vividly.

quests.name: Materials for a Sea Adventure Story

70002337.name: Altai Mountains
70002337.description: Mountain range spanning from western Siberia to Mongolia. Has been occupied by men since ancient times, apparent from many pictures carved in stone

70002338.name: Gobi Desert
70002338.description: An enormous desert in Mongolia. Gobi means 'dry land' in the Mongolian language. Just as its name describes, dry winds blow across the land

70002339.name: Petroglyphs of the Altai Mountains
70002339.description: Rock carvings of animals, found nearby Xanadu. Animals such as sheep, horses, and goats, are being chased by hunters. These ruins are precious windows into the lives of prehistoric peoples.

70002340.name: Mongolian Plateau
70002340.description: A seemingly endless plateau. Perhaps due to low precipitation, the center region is desert.

70002341.name: Ackee
70002341.description: A tree native to West Africa that bears red fruit. Since the unripe fruit is poisonous, it is never consumed at its place of origin. However, in Jamaica, it is a beloved ingredient and food source.

70002342.name: Blue Mountains
70002342.description: Mountain range located in eastern Jamaica. With elevations above 2000m, the mountain range appears blue from afar

70002343.name: Brown Recluse Spider
70002343.description: Highly venomous spider distributed in central and south America. With no known antidote, the pain from its bite will persist until it naturally heals

70002344.name: Solenodon
70002344.description: A nocturnal animal that inhabit areas of the Caribbean rainforest such as Haiti. Its length is about 30 cm, and it has a characteristically thin nose. It sticks this nose into narrow places and catches insects, its natural prey.

70002345.name: Ginger Lily
70002345.description: White flowers blooming in the late summer. Fragrant and soothing, suitable for perfume.

quests.name: The Scent of the Late Summer

70002346.name: Great Blue Hole
70002346.description: A huge hole in the sea from time immemorial. Its surrounding areas are shallow, but the hole is very deep, causing it to appear very dark. One wonders where it leads to.

quests.name: The jewel, hidden in the sea

70002347.name: The Catacombs of Rome
70002347.description: The ruins of an underground cemetery located outside the walls of Rome. In order to escape oppression by the Roman Empire, Christians dug the underpass, and used them as cemeteries and meeting places. It is said to be over 20 km long.

70002348.name: Ancient Amphora
70002348.description: A ceramic jar widely used in ancient times in the Mediterranean. It comes with two handles and was used to store and transport wine and olive oil until around the 7th century. This amphora seems to have been brought to the catacombs for use in rituals.

70002349.name: Buried Glassware
70002349.description: A glass vessel buried in the catacombs of Rome. Glassblowing technology was born in the 1st century in the Near East, and glassware came to be used widely in the era of the Roman Empire. This vessel is believed to have been used by the early Christians.

70002350.name: Sarcophagus
70002350.description: A sarcophagus discovered in the catacombs of Rome, decorated with carvings. On the Italian peninsula, decorating the sarcophagi of the rich with carvings was a tradition since the era of the Etruscans. This sarcophagus is believed to be of a wealthy individual who converted to Christianity.

70002351.name: A Marble Statue of Archimedes
70002351.description: A marble statue of the great mathematician and physicist, Archimedes, who is famed for his discovery of the Law of the Lever. Archimedes was a native of Syracuse, and his grave once used to stand next to its gates.

70002352.name: Fabric of the Andes
70002352.description: A vividly dyed fabric made of alpaca fur and cotton. Not only is the color stunning, but the complex pattern is very difficult to weave and reproducing it is a challenge.

70002353.name: Statue of Chasca
70002353.description: A statue of the goddess of dusk, dawn, and Venus of Incan mythology. She is the guardian of young women and flowers.

70002354.name: Canopic Jars
70002354.description: Jars that are said to have held important organs other than the heart during the mummification process in ancient Egypt. The lids depict each of the four sons of the god Horus.

70002355.name: Pharaoh Khufu's Tombstone
70002355.description: A limestone slab thought to be used in death rites. The flat stone is engraved with hieroglyphs and painted. Hieroglyphs were sacred to the Egyptians and were only used for very special occasions.

70002356.name: Medical Texts of Ancient Egypt
70002356.description: Medical texts written in Hieratic script on papyrus. Perhaps partly due to the anatomical knowledge gained from the mummification process, the medical technology of ancient Egypt was very good, and referred to in Greek and Roman literature as well.

70002357.name: Statue of Khnum
70002357.description: A statue of the sheep-headed god of creation worshipped in ancient Egypt. Khnum was said to be the source of the Nile River, and Khufu's name is likely based on him.

70002358.name: The Annals of Thutmose III
70002358.description: A relief dedicated to the exposition of the campaigns of Thutmose the 3rd, which greatly expanded the Egyptian empire. Thutmose often campaigned on the Syrian front against neighboring states such as Mitanni, and brought spoils and tribute to the Amun temple.

70002359.name: Statue of Sekhmet
70002359.description: A statue of the goddess Sekhmet, who had the head of a lioness. She was said to be dispatched to earth to destroy humans who did not worship the sun god Ra. She heals infectious diseases, and manifestations of her worship are often excavated around the Karnak Temple.

70002360.name: Statue of Cleopatra
70002360.description: A stone statue of the last pharaoh of the Ptolemy dynasty, Cleopatra. It seems Augustus, who ended the dynasty, removed it when he rebuilt the temple.

70002361.name: Statue of Pharaoh Hatshepsut
70002361.description: As the first female pharaoh of ancient Egypt, Hatshepsut repaired the destroyed Karnak Temple and made several additions to it, including an enormous obelisk. This statue was likely made during this time.

70002362.name: Sermermiut
70002362.description: The oldest and largest settlement remnant in Greenland. The size is not large, and it seems just like a normal valley at first glance.

70002363.name: Greenland Ice Sheet
70002363.description: A mass of glacier ice that covers over four fifth of Greenland. Formed from constant snowing.

70002364.name: Muskox
70002364.description: An Arctic mammal primarily living in Greenland and the far north lands. Approximately two meters in length, stiff long guard hairs grown on a layer of soft down hairs.

quests.name: The Ox in the Land of the Far North

70002365.name: Baffin Bay
70002365.description: The Bay located in the west of Greenland. There are icebergs floating within the bay, making it hard to navigate.

70002366.name: Eastern Greenland Caribou
70002366.description: A type of caribou living on the eastern part of Greenland. Moving in small flocks and eat lichens.

maps.name: Map of Caribou Living on Island

70002367.name: Common Redpoll
70002367.description: Small birds that live in cold climate and alpine area. Characterized with dark streaks and a bright red patch on its forehead. They are omnivores, eating a wide range of seeds and insects.

70002368.name: Bowhead Whale
70002368.description: A species of the right whale living in fertile Arctic and sub-Arctic waters. It has a strongly bowed lower jaw and narrow upper jaw and a massive bony skull which it uses to break through the Arctic ice to breathe.

quests.name: The Inhabitant of the Frozen Sea

70002369.name: Silene Acaulis
70002369.description: Also known as cushion pink. A small mountain-dwelling wildflower that is common all over the high arctic and tundra. It is a ground-hugging plant, its pink flower is approximately 1cm.

quests.name: The Flower that Blooms in the Land of Extreme Coldness

70002370.name: Shi Pan
70002370.description: A tool used in one of the divination technique in East Asia, Shi Zhan. It's made with a circular Sky panel combined with a square Earth panel, and various symbols are marked on the two panels. User operates the panels while observing their arrangement to obtain the information required for divination.

quests.name: The Fortune Telling Tool from the East

70002371.name: Senji Ryakketsu
70002371.description: One of the texts written by the legendary Abe no Seimei during the Heian Period in Japan. The text contains six thousand forecast and thirty-six fortune-telling techniques based on divination through use of Shikigami.

quests.name: The Fortune Telling Guide in the East

70002372.name: Bow of Ramesses II
70002372.description: The bow used by ancient Egyptian pharaoh, Ramesses II. However, the bowstring is too strong for normal person to pull, so it's not used as a weapon.

70002373.name: King's Obituary
70002373.description: An obituary written by Ramesses II for his wife, Nefertari. It's filled with words of deep sorrow, represening the depth of Ramesses II's love for her.

70002374.name: Mural of Ramesses II
70002374.description: Mural depicting Ramesses II in the Battle of Kadesh. It shows Ramesses atop a chariot with a drawn bow in his hands, suggesting his bravery.

70002375.name: Ancient Scale
70002375.description: Sun god Ra's Scale. According to the Book of the Dead of ancient Egypt, Anubis used it to weigh the sins of the dead and determine the fate of their souls.

70002376.name: Bayeux Tapestry
70002376.description: An embroidered cloth nearly 70 meters long depicting the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England concerning William, Duke of Normandy, and culminating in the Battle of Hastings. The picture of Halley's Comet was depicted as an ominous sign for the English.

70002377.name: Coin of Caesar's Comet
70002377.description: The coin depicting the comet appeared after Caesar's assassination. Casted by his successor, Octavianus. Suetonius wrote about when a Roman Citizen saw the comet, they believed that it was Caesar's soul ascending to the Heavens.

quests.name: A Great Comet in the Ancient Times
A Great Comet in the Ancient Times
A Great Comet in the Ancient Times
A Great Comet in the Ancient Times
A Great Comet in the Ancient Times

70002378.name: Polaris
70002378.description: The brightest star in the constellation Ursa Minor. It is very close to the North Celestial pole, making it the current Nothern Pole star. It is easy to find due to no bright stars close to it, so it's an important star to distinguish the orientation at night in the northern hemisphere.

70002379.name: Betelgeuse
70002379.description: One of three stars that make up the Winter Triangle, second-brightest in the constellation of Orion. Located on the right shoulder of Orion on the constellation maps. In Arabic, it means 'armpit'.

70002380.name: Rigel A
70002380.description: The brightest star in the constellation Orion. It's locatedon the lower right part of Orion, and on the constellation maps, it's the left knee. In Arabic, it means the left foot. It is a corner of the Winter Diamond.

70002381.name: Sirius
70002381.description: The brightest star in the Earth's night sky. One of the three vertices of the Winter Triangle, belonging to Canis Major. The heliacal rising of Sirius, occurs just before the annual flooding of the Nile. Due to this, it's highly regarded in ancient Egypt. The name 'Sirius' is derived from the Ancient Greek, Seirios, meaning glowing or scorcher.

quests.name: The Shining Star of the Southern Sky
The Shining Star of the Southern Sky

70002382.name: Procyon
70002382.description: Forms one of the three vertices of the Winter Triangle asterism, in combination with Sirius and Betelgeuse. Belonged to the constellation Canis Minor, and the name means 'before the dog' in Greek. In ancient Egypt, it's an important star due to it rising before Sirius indicating the Nile flooding.

70002383.name: Aldebaran
70002383.description: An orange giant star which is the brightest star in the zodiac constellation of Taurus. In the constellation maps, it's located at the eyes of the bull. It is the first bright star of the three stars from right to left of Orion's belt. Astrologically, Aldebaran is a fortunate star, portending riches and honor. It is a corner of the Winter Diamond.

70002384.name: Pollux
70002384.description: The brightest star in the northern constellation of Gemini. In the constellation maps, it's located at the head of Pollux. He is the younger brother of the Gemini twin, Castor and Pollux, who joined Jason's expedition as crew of the ship, the Argo. It is a corner of the Winter Diamond.

70002385.name: Capella
70002385.description: The brightest star in the constellation Auriga. Appears to be yellow, and is a corner of the Winter Diamond. In the constellation maps, it's located at the heart of the female goat that the charioteer is carrying. It was used in making the calendar of ancient Babylonia.

70002386.name: Castor
70002386.description: The second brightest star in the constellation Gemini. Located at the head of the twin's older brother. The name originated from the twin sons of Zeus and Leda. Castor and Pollux has been categorized into the same group in many places and have been made into legends.

70002387.name: Arcturus
70002387.description: The brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, belonging to constellation Bootes. An easy way to find Arcturus is to follow the arc of the handle of the Big Dipper. By continuing in this path, one can find Spica, 'Arc to Arcturus, then spike to Spica'.

70002388.name: Spica
70002388.description: The brightest star in the constellation Virgo. The name Spica is derived from Latin, meaning 'the virgin's ear of wheat grain'. Together with Arcturus, they are called couple stars. Arcturus symbolizes the man, and Spica symbolizes the woman.

quests.name: A Spear Head which Shines Brightly in the Sky

70002389.name: Denebola
70002389.description: The name means 'tail of the lion' in Arabic, and it's the third brightest star in the zodiac constellation of Leo. It's located at the tail of Leo in constellation maps.

70002390.name: Regulus
70002390.description: The brightest star in the constellation Leo. It means 'prince' or 'little king' in Latin. In Astrology, it's associated with kings and royal families in many places. In Arabic, it means 'the heart of the lion', corresponding to its location in constellation maps.

70002391.name: Antares
70002391.description: The brightest star in the constellation Scorpio, and is often referred to as 'the heart of the scorpion'. In ancient Greek, the meaning is 'equal to-Ares'(Mars), due to the similarity of its reddish hue to the appearance of the planet Mars.

70002392.name: Fomalhaut
70002392.description: The brightest star in the constellation Pisces Austrinus. The name is derived from Arabic, meaning 'mouth of the Southern Fish', and it's located at the corresponding location of Pisces Austrinus. Another name in Western use is 'the Lonely Star of Autumn'.

70002393.name: Pleiades
70002393.description: An open star cluster located in the constellation of Taurus. The cluster is dominated by hot blue and extremely luminous stars. In Greek mythology, it was the name of seven divine sisters, whose name was imagined to derive from that of their mother Titan Pleione, effectively meaning 'daughters of Pleione'.

70002394.name: Sunspot
70002394.description: Temporary phenomena on the photosphere of the Sun that appear visibly as dark spots compared to its surrounding regions. A telescope can project the image onto a white screen where it can be viewed indirectly. In East Asia, there were legends that some crows live on the Sun, most likely due to how the sunspot was observed in ancient times.

70002395.name: Lunar Surface
70002395.description: Aristotle believed the moon is a sphere. Galileo proved the moon surface is not smooth through observations using telescopes. In reality, the lunar landscape is characterized by impact craters, their ejecta, a few volcanoes, hills, lava flows and depressions filled by magma.

70002396.name: The Morning Star
70002396.description: The name in Greek is Phosphorus, meaning 'Light-Bringer'. It's the planet Venus in its morning appearance. It shines brightly in the Eastern skies before dawn. In Ancient Greece it was referred to as Phosphoros, in Latin it was called Lucifer. In Buddhist stories it is said that the morning stars appears when reaching enlightenment.

70002397.name: The Evening Star
70002397.description: The name is Hesperus, the planet Venus in the evening. A star which shines brightly in the West when the sun sets. In Ancient Greece it was called Hesperus.

70002398.name: Venus
70002398.description: Appears at dawn and when the sun sets, a star which is the third brightest next the sun and the moon. In Ancient Greece, they discovered that the evening star and the morning star were of one in the same. Starting from Venus in Roman mythology, it is often referred to as the goddess which governs the name of beauty.

quests.name: The Star of the Goddess of Beauty
The Star of the Goddess of Beauty
The Star of the Goddess of Beauty
The Star of the Goddess of Beauty
The Star of the Goddess of Beauty

70002399.name: Mercury
70002399.description: A planet you can only see briefly during sunset and sunrise. In Ancient Greece, Mercury was called Hermes during the evening, and Apollo during the morning. It is darker in comparison to Venus, and as it moves closer to the sun, it is difficult to observe.

70002400.name: Mars
70002400.description: A reminder of the colours of blood and warfare, beginning from Mars of the Roman myths it was named after the God of war in various places. In comparison to the other planets, what stands out the most is that the brightness levels will change greatly and the brightest time occurs every 780 days.

quests.name: The Shining Star in the Night Sky
The Shining Star in the Night Sky

70002401.name: Jupiter
70002401.description: As it spends 12 years to circle the ecliptic, starting from Jupiter of the Roman myths, it is often named after the gods of high stature. In China it is called the Tai Sui star in which Taoism deified it as the star of divine punishment.

70002402.name: Saturn
70002402.description: In reference to the farming god in Roman mythology, the planet is named after the origins of Saturn. It takes roughly up to 30 years to circle the ecliptic. Galileo has observed Saturn using the telescope, but it is said that he was perplexed by the shape of it.

70002403.name: Aries
70002403.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. Originally sent by Zeus to save the children of King Boeotia, Phrixus and Helle, it is the form of the golden sheep which was sent to the heavens. Later, Jason sailed on the Argo ship in search of its Golden Fleece.

quests.name: A Sheep that Shines to the Heavens
A Sheep that Shines to the Heavens
A Sheep that Shines to the Heavens

70002404.name: Taurus
70002404.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. It is known as Zeus transformed as a Bull to get closer to Europa. According to Ancient Mesopotamia it is called the Bull of the heavens. The first magnitude star Aldebaran is considered to be the eye of the bull.

70002405.name: Gemini
70002405.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. The form of the twins who participated in the search on Argo, Castor and Pollux who were sent to the heavens. Outside of Greek mythology it is common that the two are depicted together, and in Norse mythology there are considered to be the eyes of the giant Thiazi.

70002406.name: Cancer
70002406.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. The giant crab Karkinos which was crushed by Hercules while trying to save their sibling Hydra. Karkinos was later sent to the heavens as the Goddess Hera took pity on him. In comparison to the other zodiacal constellations it does not contain bright stars so it does not stand out.

70002407.name: Leo
70002407.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. It is the form of Nemea's lion which was defeated by Hercules in one of his first adventures. Nemea's fur could not be slain by any weapon, and Hercules defeated him by strangling him for three days.

70002408.name: Virgo
70002408.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. Such as the Goddess of justice Astrae, the Goddess of spring Persephone, and the Goddess of fertility Demeter, it is based on various Goddesses. In Ancient Mesopotamia, It is said that it is of two of women holding an ear of wheat and a leaf of the date palm.

70002409.name: Libra
70002409.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. Considered to be a scale which scaled the balances of good and evil owned by the Goddess of justice Astrae. The Libra has stars which are named North Claw and South Claw which seem to originate from the Scorpio, and is said that it was previously a part of the constellations of for it.

quests.name: The Scale of the Night Sky
The Scale of the Night Sky
The Scale of the Night Sky
The Scale of the Night Sky

70002410.name: Scorpio
70002410.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. It is the form of the Scorpion which killed the arrogant Orion by the order of the Goddess Hera. Drawing an S shape into the Milky Way and having many bright stars along the way starting with Antares, it is a constellation easy to find.

quests.name: A Scorpion Which Shines to the Heavens
A Scorpion Which Shines to the Heavens
A Scorpion Which Shines to the Heavens
A Scorpion Which Shines to the Heavens

70002411.name: Sagittarius
70002411.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. It is the form of the wise-man centaur Kyron who ascended to the heavens. The parts which gets into contact with the Milky Way contains stars which align like a ladle, and is referred to as the Milk Dipper in Europe and in the East is referred to as the Southern Dipper Asterism

quests.name: The Archer that Aims for the Scorpion
The Archer that Aims for the Scorpion
The Archer that Aims for the Scorpion
The Archer that Aims for the Scorpion
The Archer that Aims for the Scorpion

70002412.name: Capricorn
70002412.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. In the astronomical chart it is often depicted as the top half being of a mountain goat and the lower half being of a fish. It is said that it is the form of the goat headed god Pan who transformed after being surprised by the attack of the monster Typhon.

quests.name: Constellations of The Goat and Fish
Constellations of The Goat and Fish
Constellations of The Goat and Fish
Constellations of The Goat and Fish
Constellations of The Goat and Fish

70002413.name: Aquarius
70002413.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. Depicted as Ganymede who serves the Nectar of eternal life to the twelve Olympian gods. In Ancient Mesopotamia, it is depicted as a man carrying a vase connected to the God of water Enki, and was referred to as Gulla, meaning The grand being

70002414.name: Pisces
70002414.description: One of the Zodiacal Constellations. It is depicted as two fish being tied together with a ribbon. It is said to be the form of Aphrodite and her child Eros after they transformed and escaped from being attacked the monster Typhon. Having no bright stars, it is considered to be a constellation harder to find than most of the zodiacal constellations.

70002415.name: Orion
70002415.description: A constellation that can be seen in the European Southern sky during the winter. It is the form of Orion who was killed by being stung by a Scorpion and was later sent to the heavens. There are two first magnitude star in the three stars forming Orion's belt, making it easier to find the Orion constellation.

quests.name: The Giant of the Southern Sky

70002416.name: Cassiopeia
70002416.description: A constellation which can be used as a mark to find the Polaris. It is the form of the conceited Queen Cassiopeia who ascended to the heavens. Boasting of her own beauty and enraging Poseidon, it is said that she is forbidden to descend to the ground to rest.

quests.name: The Constellation of the Ethiopian Queen
The Constellation of the Ethiopian Queen
The Constellation of the Ethiopian Queen
The Constellation of the Ethiopian Queen
The Constellation of the Ethiopian Queen

70002417.name: Piscis Austrinus
70002417.description: A constellation which appears in the European Southern sky during the fall. Not having many bright stars surrounding it, it is easy to find using the first magnitudes star Fomalhaut as a mark. Associated with the form of the fish Aphrodite turned into while escaping from Typhon, it is also considered to be the parent fish of Pisces.

70002418.name: Orion's Belt
70002418.description: The three stars within the Orion constellation. It is easy to find due to the three second magnitude stars being lined up together. It is depicted as the belt of Orion in the astronomical chart. The star on the right is called Mintaka, It is on almost on top of the celestial equator so it appears to be on the same orbital track as the both the days of the Spring equinox and the Autumnal Equinox.

70002419.name: The Big Dipper
70002419.description: The seven stars which created the shape of a ladle, and is the famous alignment of stars which is used as a mark to locate the Polaris. Many myths about have been created about it throughout the world.

70002420.name: Winter Triangle
70002420.description: Appearing in the European Southern sky during the winter, it is depicted as three stars being tied together the shape of a triangle. All three stars are of the first magnitude, and it is almost a equilateral triangle and it is easy to find. It is used as a mark to locate other various constellations.

70002421.name: The Winter Diamond
70002421.description: Expanding the area from Betelgeuse out of the Winter Triangle and connecting the six first magnitude stars into a shape of a hexagon is referred to as the Winter Diamond. It is also called that while including the second magnitude star Castor

70002422.name: The Spring Arc
70002422.description: A star group in which can be a mark to locate the many constellations in the European southern skies of spring. Drawing a line to draw an arc from the part of the handle of ladle of the Big Dipper, Alioth, Mizar, and Alkaid, to Arcturus and Spica will let one be able to see few stars of the first magnitude. This alignment is called the Spring Arc.

quests.name: The Arc Depicted in the Night Sky
The Arc Depicted in the Night Sky
The Arc Depicted in the Night Sky

70002423.name: The Spring Triangle
70002423.description: The two first magnitude stars which create the Spring Triangle, it is a triangle which ties the constellations Arcturus of Bootes, Spica of Virgo, and the second magnitude stars of Leo's Denebola. It is used as a mark to find various constellations.

70002424.name: The Sculpture of Zemi
70002424.description: A stone sculpture which was made by the Taino tribe who have lived in the Caribbean area since long ago. It is shaped as gods or spirits of ancestors as well as many other types of figures.

70002425.name: The Book of Genesis
70002425.description: The first book of the Old Testaments. It includes stories about the beginning of the world, the creation of mankind, and the history about the people of Israel.

70002426.name: The Cross of Voodoo
70002426.description: A cross used in Voodoo religious ceremonies. It also symbolizes the voodoo god of graveyards and death, Baron Samedi.

70002427.name: Hidden Pirate Treasure
70002427.description: Plundered gold and silver treasures hidden in a box by a pirate. As it has been abandoned for a long period of time, the box has aged, however the contents inside are still kept intact.

70002428.name: Conch Pearl
70002428.description: A type of pearl which can be found in conch shellfish. It is generally a soft pink colour, though there are ones with uneven colours or ones with detailed patterns.

quests.name: A Pearl Born from a Conch

70002429.name: Port Royal Currency
70002429.description: Currency which was cast by the Mint Bureau in Port Royal. The ingredients consist of precious metals which flow into Port Royal.

70002430.name: Polymita
70002430.description: A type of snail which resides in a region of Cuba. The soft body part is a dark blue, but each of their shells will contain a variety of colours.

70002431.name: Coqui Frog
70002431.description: A small type of frog native of the island where San Juan is located. Their main characteristic is their high pitched voice which carries far.

70002432.name: Conch
70002432.description: A univalve shell which is also referred to as pink shellfish. The main characteristic is that the interior of their shell is a light pink. They reside in the whole Caribbean area, and are also used as a food source.

quests.name: The Reason for the Peach Colour

70002433.name: Yellow Stingray
70002433.description: A type of ray which resides in the Caribbean Sea. The body is close to a circular shape with a short tail. Their main characteristic is the spotted design on their body surface.

70002434.name: Green Moray Eel
70002434.description: A type of Moray which inhabits the west part of the Atlantic Ocean. Being rather large, it can also exceed 2m in size. The body colour is yellowish brown with no pattern, and its colour balanced with the sea's colours make it appear bright green.

70002435.name: Squirrelfish
70002435.description: A fish which resides in the reef area of the Atlantic Coast. The body colour is silver or red, has long fins, and big eyes.

70002436.name: Kaieteur Falls
70002436.description: A waterfall which is located in the Northeast part of South America. The drop is approximately 220m and each step of the waterfall is of a considerable scale.

quests.name: The Geographical Information of Northeast South America

70002437.name: The Waterfalls of El Limon
70002437.description: A waterfall which is located in the northeast part of Hispaniola. The drop is approximately 40m, the water flow is comparatively gentle.

70002438.name: Martinique
70002438.description: A volcanic island which belongs to the Caribbean West Indies. A beautiful island where the bumpy landforms are covered by green trees and surrounded by a blue ocean.

70002439.name: Eleuthera
70002439.description: An island which belongs to the Bahama Islands among the Caribbean West Indies.

70002440.name: Pink Sand Beach
70002440.description: A beach from the Harbour Island in the Caribbean seas. It is located in the Northern part of Eleuthera of the Bahama islands. Sea shells and coral tinged with red are mixed in with the white sand, making it appear pink.

70002441.name: Altair
70002441.description: A first-magnitude star. The brightest one in the constellation Aquila, it creates the corner of the summer triangle. It is an abbreviation of an Arabic phrase which means 'the flying eagle'.

70002442.name: Vega
70002442.description: Vega creates one corner of the summer triangle. It is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, the fifth brightest star in the night sky, and the second brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, after Arcturus. It is said that the constellation Lyra was formed from the harp of Orpheus, with Vega as its handle.

70002443.name: Deneb
70002443.description: It is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus, and one of the vertices of the Summer Triangle. The name Deneb is derived from 'dhaneb', the Arabic word for 'tail'.

70002444.name: The Summer Triangle
70002444.description: An astronomical asterism involving an imaginary triangle drawn on the northern hemisphere's celestial sphere. It covers the milky way, and is used as a mark to search for other stars and constellations.

70002445.name: Saturn's Ring
70002445.description: A ring which surrounds Saturn. The existence of the ring was found by the early telescope, but observing it was difficult. Once the function quality of the telescope was enhanced, observations of the ring became successful. However it is still unknown as to what it is made up of.

70002446.name: Waxing and Waning of the Venus
70002446.description: Venus not only waxes and wanes like the Moon does, but also it appears to be a different size depending on the time. This creates the solid evidence of Venus revolving around the sun, and not the earth.

70002447.name: Galilean Satellites
70002447.description: Pointing to the four satellites revolving around Jupiter, the Galilean satellite has a brightness of five to six magnitudes and would be able to be seen with the naked eye if the planet Jupiter was not so bright.

70002448.name: Spiral Nebula of Andromeda
70002448.description: A nebula shaped like a spiral in the constellation of Andromeda. It is at the position equal to the right side of the waist of the Andromeda, and can be seen with the naked eye.

70002449.name: The Large Magellanic Cloud
70002449.description: Named after Magellan as he kept records during his travel across the world. Prior to Magellan, European voyagers referred to it as the Cape Clouds. It cannot be seen in the Northern Hemisphere unless one heads south towards the equator.

maps.name: Astronomer's Observation Record
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70002450.name: The Small Magellanic Cloud
70002450.description: A dwarf galaxy near the Milky Way. It is classified as a dwarf irregular galaxy. It is slightly darker than that of the Large Magellanic Cloud. It can be seen directly with the naked eyes. As it is closer to the South celestial pole, it could only be seen from a low-altitude in the Northern Hemisphere.

70002451.name: Orion's Umbrella-like Nebula
70002451.description: A nebula in the center of three small stars attending to the south of the three stars of Orion. It is one of the brighter nebulas, and can be seen with the naked eye.

70002452.name: Rose-shaped Nebula of Monoceros
70002452.description: A rose-shaped nebula located in the north of the Monoceros. It is within the Milky Way, and cannot be seen with the naked eye.

70002453.name: The Horsehead Nebula of Orion
70002453.description: It is a nebula located just to the south of the star which is farthest east on Orion's Belt. In front of the brighter cloud, a dark cloud in the shape of a horse's head can be seen.

70002454.name: A Ring-like Nebula in Lyra
70002454.description: A nebula in the constellation of Lyra. The center is slightly dark, and can be seen with a ring containing various colours.

70002455.name: A Trifurcated Nebula in Sagittarius
70002455.description: A nebula in the constellation of Sagittarius. It is seen as though the brighter cloud is split into three by the darker cloud.

70002456.name: The Round Nebula of Ursa Major
70002456.description: The nebula located under the bowl of the Big Dipper. There are two darker parts which make the nebula resemble the face of an owl.

70002457.name: Spiral Nebula in Triangulum
70002457.description: Located slightly west of the Triangulum, it is a nebula shaped like a whirlpool. Because it is spread out faintly, it is difficult to see with the naked eye.

70002458.name: Parent and Child Nebula in Canes Venatici
70002458.description: A nebula in the Canes Venatici. Spiral shaped, it appears as though the small and large nebulas are connected.

70002459.name: Spiral Nebula of Canes Venatici
70002459.description: A spiral shaped nebula in the Canes Venatici. Though it cannot be seen with the naked eye, through a telescope the differences can be noticed between the nebula and the fixed star.

70002460.name: Spiral Nebula of Coma Berenices
70002460.description: The spiral-shaped nebula in the Coma Berenices. The main feature is its clear black cloud.

70002461.name: Supernova of Cassiopeia
70002461.description: A new star which emerged in the constellation of Cassiopeia in 1572. It is occasionally referred to as Tycho's Star after the Danish Astronomer, Tycho Brahe, left his detailed records of the star. He suggested that it was not even a planet, but a fixed star in the stellar sphere beyond all the planets after he had found that it did not change its position.

70002462.name: Supernova in Ophiuchus
70002462.description: A new star which appeared in Ophiuchus in 1604. As it matured, it became the brightest star excluding Venus. The star was researched immensely by German astronomer, Johannes Kepler, and is also referred to as Kepler's Star.

70002463.name: The Great Comet
70002463.description: Some comets were observed during the 19th century. The comet that appeared during the same time as the gold rush was extremely bright, so the observation records still remain in each area.

70002464.name: Mira
70002464.description: A fixed star of Cetus changing its brightness from the second magnitude star to the tenth magnitude star during a period of approximately 332 days. The Latin name for it means 'something peculiar'. It had become bright enough to be a first magnitude star in 1779.

70002465.name: Leonids
70002465.description: The meteor shower looks as though it is coming from the direction of Leo. A burst occurred in 1833, where the meteors were so bright that it is said to have woken the people in eastern North America.

70002466.name: Lyra
70002466.description: It is a constellation which is said to be in the form of Orpheus's harp that appears in the Greek myth. Orpheus was a master at the harp, and it is said that his melody was beautiful enough to calm down storms.

70002467.name: Aquila
70002467.description: It is said to be the form of the eagle, which Zeus had transformed into when he kidnapped prince Ganymede of Troy, which is sent to the heavens. In the astronomical chart, it is described as an eagle that aims for Aquarius that Ganymede had transformed into.

70002468.name: Cygnus
70002468.description: The form of a swan Zeus transformed into in order to see the Spartan Queen Leda, which later rose to the heavens. The cross-shaped center part is also referred to as the Northern Cross.

70002469.name: Cetus
70002469.description: The form of the sea monster that attacked Andromeda, daughter of Cassiopeia. After being transformed into stone by Perseus, it is said that it was sent towards the heavens.

70002470.name: Andromeda
70002470.description: Named for Andromeda, daughter of Cassiopeia in the Greek myth, who was chained to a rock to be eaten by the sea monster Cetus. It is said to be the form of Andromeda ascending to the heavens after her death. Andromeda gave birth to six children with Perseus, and it is said that the eldest child Perseus became the descendant of the Persian Royal Family.

70002471.name: Monoceros
70002471.description: The constellation positioned on the Winter Triangle. The unicorn is a horned beast which looks similar to a horse. There are various perceptions as to who set this constellation and therefore it is uncertain.

quests.name: The Constellation That Was Made In Germany

70002472.name: Vulpecula
70002472.description: The constellation positioned at the center of the Summer Triangle. It was set by the Astronomer, Hevelius, in Poland during the 17th century. As it does not have any bright stars, it is not a constellation which stands out.

quests.name: The Constellation That Was Made in Poland

70002473.name: Triangulum
