70002473.description: Goddess Ceres, guardian of agriculture, asked Zeus to send the shape of Sicily up towards the heavens to turn it into a constellation. Although it is a small constellation with no bright stars, it is easy to find because there are no bright stars surrounding it.

70002474.name: The Canes Venatici Constellation
70002474.description: It is known to be the constellation of the hunting dogs of Bootes' cattleman. Comprised of two hunting dogs, the dog in the north is Asterion, and the one in the south is Challah.

quests.name: A Constellation Taken Away by a Coward

70002475.name: The Comae Berenices Constellation
70002475.description: It is said to be Queen Berenice's, of the Ptolemies dynasty, hair offered to goddess Aphrodite in ancient Egypt. Berenice's hair was as famous as it was beautiful, and the pleased Aphrodite is said to have sent it up to the heavens.

70002476.name: The Bootes Constellation
70002476.description: Described in the epic Odyssey of ancient Greece, it is a constellation which has existed for a long period of time. It is said to be a cattleman that is after Ursa Major, but there is no definite origin within Greek myths.

quests.name: The Constellation That Appears in an Epic

70002477.name: Ursa Major
70002477.description: After being favoured by Zeus and angering the Goddess Hera, Callisto was changed into a large bear by Hera. Callisto was later sent to the heavens by Zeus and became a constellation. It is also mentioned in the myths of the Indigenous people of North America that it is of a bear who was later sent to the heavens.

70002478.name: The Canis Major
70002478.description: It is said to be the figure of the hunting dog, Laelaps, which was destined to catch any prey, and was later sent to the sky. Chasing after a fox that had the destiny of never being caught, Laelaps, was later transformed into stone by Zeus and was sent to the heavens.

quests.name: The Legend of the Hunting Dog
The Legend of the Hunting Dog

70002479.name: The Canis Minor
70002479.description: In Greek mythology it is said to be the form of the loyal dog, Myra, which was sent to the heavens. As his master was taught the making of wine by Bacchus Dionysus, he died tragically. It is said that Myra continued protecting the grave of his master and the master's daughter until his own death.

70002480.name: Ophiuchus
70002480.description: The form of the skilled physician, Aesculapius, in Greek mythology who rose to the sky. Aesculapius had the ability to resurrect the dead, which enraged Hades, god of the underworld. As a result Hades orders Zeus to shoot him down with lightning in order to kill him.

70002481.name: Taos Pueblo
70002481.description: A village founded by the indigenous people of Pueblo in North America. The buildings are made with red-brown bricks and have multiple floors.

70002482.name: Cliff Palace
70002482.description: The remains of a village which seems to have belonged to the indigenous people of North America. It is made up of a large stone wall which has been carved out.

quests.name: Investigating the Remains of a Cave

70002483.name: The Totem Pole
70002483.description: A wooden sculpture which was hand made by the Indigenous people on the west coast of North America. It contains designs of animals and people who were associated with the tribe's history, and was placed as pillars for houses or as a grave. Although it is damaged, it continues to not be repaired and returns to soil to resemble their way of thinking of being born in nature and later return to it.

70002484.name: San Dagger
70002484.description: A piece of equipment made of rocks built on top of each other located in the center of North America. It seems it was used for astronomical observation. It is built so that the sunlight shines through the gap of stacked rocks, appearing in the shape of a dagger on the stone wall. On the side of the stone wall, a pattern is carved in to indicate the light which enters during summer solstice.

quests.name: A Light Shining Towards a Wall Painting

70002485.name: The Wall Mural of Kokopelli
70002485.description: A god made by the indigenous Hopi tribe in North America. Kokopelli is the god of fertility, and is said to bring in crops and children by playing his flute.

quests.name: Additional Research About the Flute of the Natives

70002486.name: Anasazi Flute
70002486.description: The end-blown flute of the indigenous Anasazi tribe of North America. It is made of wood and is approximately 70cm long, and has six holes.

70002487.name: Turquoise Accessories
70002487.description: An accessory made up of fragments of turquoise. Turquoise was often collected in southwestern North America, and crafting and trading them were common. Among the indigenous people, it was said that turquoise possessed special powers.

70002488.name: Neckerchief of the Cowboy
70002488.description: A cloth cowboys wrap around their neck in the West Coast of North America. Other than as an accessory, it has practical uses such as preventing from inhaling sand and signaling other comrades.

quests.name: A Person Who's After a Cow

70002489.name: Lariat
70002489.description: A loop of rope designed as a restraint to be thrown around a target and tightened when pulled. It is usually used to capture animals such as cows.

70002490.name: Lyrics of Yankee-Doodle
70002490.description: Notes with the lyrics of the song which was popular in North America during the American Revolutionary War. Many parody songs have been made and the lyrics behind it carry countless different meanings.

70002491.name: Bones of Long-crested Dragon
70002491.description: Bones of a dragon with a long crest which was discovered in North America. Judging from the size of its head, its body is estimated to be fairly large.

70002492.name: Whooping Crane
70002492.description: The crane which inhabits the wet grassy plain in North America, including Canada. The body being big for a Crane, it is covered in white feathers.

quests.name: Biological Research on the North American Crane

70002493.name: Vancouver Marmot
70002493.description: A type of squirrel that inhabits a part of the West Coast of North America. They live within the holes they've dug, and hibernate during the winter.

70002494.name: Harbour Seal
70002494.description: A seal that inhabits the northern parts of the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. It has ring-like patterns on its body and lives around rocky places or reefs.

70002495.name: Grizzly
70002495.description: A large bear that inhabits North America. They are omnivorous and predominantly eat plants and berries, but also prey on animals. Despite its size they are agile, and are fast at both running and swimming. They also attack people, so it is good stay cautious.

70002496.name: American Bison
70002496.description: A type of large cow that inhabits western North America. It is also referred to as a buffalo. Their main feature is their fur which has superior insulation, and has a close relation to the lives of the indigenous people.

70002497.name: Kermode Bear
70002497.description: A subspecies of the American black bear, but its fur is white in color. Its height is matching of an average man. Some indigenous people refer to them as 'Spirit Bear'.

70002498.name: Mule Deer
70002498.description: A type of deer that inhabits the West Coast of North America. Named after the fact that its ears resemble that of a mule. The main features include having a set of branched-out horns that only the male deer have.

70002499.name: Bighorn Sheep
70002499.description: A species of sheep native to western North America, named for its large, curved horns. They range in color from light brown to grayish or dark, chocolate brown, with a white rump and lining on the backs of all four legs. Females also have horns, but they are shorter with less curvature.

70002500.name: Minke Whale
70002500.description: The small whale which inhabits the northern sea areas above the equator. They inhabit the outer ocean and migrate exclusively.

70002501.name: Gray Whale
70002501.description: A slightly small whale that migrates around the northern coast of North America and Eurasia. Their main features are the sea shells placed on their black skin which appear as a pattern.

70002502.name: Pink Salmon
70002502.description: A type of salmon that inhabits the North Pacific. Born in a river, and though it lives in the sea once an adult, it returns back to the river during its laying period in order to lay its eggs. During the breeding period, only the males' backs develop a pronounced hump.

70002503.name: Northern Pike
70002503.description: A type of pike. It is a fish which inhabits the fresh or brackish water area. It is found in areas of high latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere. A large carnivorous fish that is more than 1m in length with sharp fangs.

70002504.name: Moraine Lake
70002504.description: The lake in a place of high elevation in western North America. It is said to have been formed by the melting of glacial ice. During the summer season, it becomes filled with water. When the sand that flows into it becomes refracted by the sunlight, the water's surface becomes dyed a beautiful turquoise blue.

70002505.name: Ninstints
70002505.description: A village where the indigenous people live, located on the island of the North American Coast. The totem poles they make depict patterns of killer whales and other sea creatures, and are directed towards the ocean. There are large totem poles that are as tall as 10m.

70002506.name: Eagle Ridge Bluff
70002506.description: The cliff of a particular mountain in western North America. Not entirely an area of rock walls but contains places full of greenery. As it is also the habitat of bald eagles, the indigenous people consider it as a sacred place.

70002507.name: Horse Tail Fall
70002507.description: A waterfall located in Western North America. The water flows only during the winter and early spring. On rare occasions, when the light of the setting sun hits the waterfall, the water appears red as magma.

70002508.name: Balance Rock
70002508.description: A large boulder in the inlands of western North America. Most likely due to erosion after many years, it appears unstable but it still stands.

70002509.name: San Francisco
70002509.description: A city in western North America. Due to California's gold rush, its population grew exponentially, resulting in the rapid growth of industry and trade markets. Though it is a lively town, there has been a rise of fear in the deteriorating state of the city's peace and order.

70002510.name: Tacoma
70002510.description: A city which prospers as a city port in western North America. It boasts a lumber industry with a vast forest stretching on the east side of the city.

70002511.name: Muramasa
70002511.description: An old Japanese sword with the signature Muramasa carved into its blade. It is said to have been made by a swordsmith, Muramasa, in Kuwana during the Muromachi period. Though the sword has been abandoned for a long period of time, it has a whimsical energy behind it, making it harder not to stare at it.

70002512.name: Uma-jirushi of Golden Japanese Umbrella
70002512.description: The golden umbrella used to show the status of a Japanese military commander on the battlefield.

70002513.name: Conch Horn
70002513.description: A wind instrument used by feudal warriors to signal troops to attack, withdraw, or change strategies during the battle in the East. It is a shell trumpet and requires great practice to make a sound.

70002514.name: Golden Ring Earrings
70002514.description: A unique set of golden earrings. There is part of it which is cut, and is thought to be used in putting it on the ears.

70002515.name: Hinoshi Flatiron
70002515.description: A tool used to press clothes to remove creases. It was thought to be used by putting heated charcoal into a container-shaped part, followed by stretching out creases of the cloth using the bottom of the container.

70002516.name: Ancient Copper Mirror
70002516.description: An old copper mirror which was discovered from remains. Not only does it show one's reflection, but it was apparently used for religious services and magic.

70002517.name: Kaoliang Wine
70002517.description: A strong distilled liquor usually made in China or Taiwan. It is also referred to as Baijiu. It is made from grains called sorghum, and contains a high percentage of alcohol.

70002518.name: The Contract of a Bloodless Surrender
70002518.description: An oath which was thought to be created during the case of the bloodless oath to surrender the castle of Fort Santo Domingo. It is stamped by both Spain and the Netherlands. It's not been well-preserved so it's partially torn.

70002519.name: Sho
70002519.description: An instrument made mostly of bamboo. As the same sound is produced from breathing either into or out of the instrument, there is no requirement to take breaths. Multiple holes are opened on the side, and by changing how you press down on them various sounds can be created.

70002520.name: Spring Hope (Chun Wang)
70002520.description: It is said to be written by the poet, Du Fu, when he was imprisoned by the An Lushan military force. It displays the feelings of Du Fu as he saw the ruins of the city of Chang An after battle.

70002521.name: Bronze Drum (Tong Gu)
70002521.description: A percussive instrument made of bronze. It is excavated widely in places such as China and Southeast Asia. Aside from musical performances, it is also used for religious services.

70002522.name: Fanzhen Account
70002522.description: A book, which existed in rural districts of China, explains how to structure their governmental organization. It records the roles of Jiedushi and observers, the number of soldiers, taxation and includes articles on an extensive amount of subjects.

70002523.name: Brown Guitarfish
70002523.description: A fish that has a stingray-like head and a shark-like body. It is considered to be a type of stingray. They reside in the warmer parts of the ocean such as the Indian and Pacific Ocean, and feed on fish and other crustacean.

70002524.name: Hagfish
70002524.description: A fish that has an eel-like body. There seems to be no traces of a set of eyes. Having seven gills, it is considered to be part of the lampreys species. When attacked, it will produce a mucus-like liquid in order to protect itself.

70002525.name: Flying Squid
70002525.description: A type of squid which lives in the warmer areas of the sea. When attacked or scared, it spreads its legs like wings, and it blows sea water from its funnels and flies upward. It's said that the distance it can fly is over 50m.

quests.name: The Creature That Flies Over the Sea Surface

70002526.name: Steller's Sea Cow
70002526.description: A large sea creature which inhabits the island east of the Kamchatka Peninsula. Their tendencies of not being cautious of humans and protecting their companions who have been hurt is putting them at risk of becoming extinct.

70002527.name: Rai Stones
70002527.description: A large stone coin that is said to be used in an island northeast of Davao city. Larger sizes of the coin can reach up to 3m in diameter. Due to its size it cannot be moved, however, the owner of it may change when handed over in cases of ceremony.

70002528.name: Oro
70002528.description: A board used for wave riding, which can only be used by those with certain social status in Hawaii. Made up of wood and rather long in length, it can be as long as over 6m and is extremely heavy. Other residents seem to be using a much smaller one to enjoy wave riding.

70002529.name: Ohia Lehua
70002529.description: A flower which is used for lei, which one puts on during Hawaii Island's traditional ceremonies. A legend remains of the flower being the form of two lovers that were forcefully parted by the Fire Goddess, Pele.

70002530.name: Breadfruit
70002530.description: A plant which is grown in Oceania. Its fruits can be eaten either baked or roasted. It is a useful plant that can also be preserved as a source of emergency food.

quests.name: A Nut That Can Be a Staple Food

70002531.name: Sequoia
70002531.description: A type of cedar which grows in western North America. Being able to grow extremely tall in height, some of them could easily reach up to 100m. It is surrounded by thick bark and is apparently strong against forest fires.

70002532.name: Laughing Owl
70002532.description: A bird characterized by its strange call usually described as a stifled laugh or a whistle. Previously it was not that rare of an animal, but due to the environmental changes in its habitat, they could potentially become extinct due to their rapid decrease in population.

70002533.name: I'iwi
70002533.description: A bird which inhabits the Hawaii Islands, and is roughly the size of a sparrow. They use the nectar of flowers as their source of food. Their feathers are used as accessories on the clothing of local leaders.

70002534.name: Diamond Head
70002534.description: A mountain located on the island northwest from the Island of Hawaii. There seems to a crater that apparently used to emit a large quantity of volcanic smoke. It was named after a transparent stone, resembling a diamond, was found near the mountaintop.

70002535.name: Kilauea Volcano
70002535.description: An active volcano located in the southeastern part of the Island of Hawaii. Continuously active, it frequently spills lava, and the mountain is named after the term 'to disperse' by the locals.

70002536.name: Mauna Kea
70002536.description: A mountain located in the north part of the Island of Hawaii. Being the tallest mountain in the Hawaii islands, it becomes snowcapped during the winter. The main feature is its incredibly large mountain shape.

70002537.name: Statue of Kamapua'a
70002537.description: A hero who appears in Hawaiian myths as half human and half god. Normally he appears as a handsome young man, but can transform into a beastly bear or a fish. He is married to the Fire Goddess, Pele, and had a child with her. They often get into fights.

70002538.name: Statue of Kanaloa
70002538.description: One of the four major gods widely known in both Hawaii and Polynesia. Aside from being considered the god of the sea, it is also seen as the god of magic and the underworld. Often depicted in the form of either a squid or an octopus, it is also referred to as Tangaroa.

70002539.name: Statue of Pele
70002539.description: The goddess of volcanoes of the Hawaii islands. She is known to have been born in the far southern islands. With her many siblings, she moved to Hawaii and since then has resided in the volcano in the southeast part of the island.

70002540.name: Statue of Poli'ahu
70002540.description: The Snow Goddess of the Hawaii islands. It is said that she resides in the Mauna Kea mountain when it is snowbound during the winter. There is a legend in which she fought with the Fire Goddess, Pele, and sent her to the volcano on the southern part of the island.

70002541.name: The California Peninsula
70002541.description: A peninsula separating the Gulf of California from the Pacific Ocean. Desert areas are spread out. It was mistaken as an island for a long period of time.

70002542.name: The Aleutian Islands
70002542.description: A chain of islands which extend from the Kamchatka Peninsula to the North American Alaskan Peninsula. It acts as the border between the Bering Sea and the Pacific Ocean.

70002543.name: Nineveh
70002543.description: The city where the Late Assyrian empire established a capital. It is said to have the Library of Ashurbanipal where all books of Assyria were collected.

70002544.name: Hatra
70002544.description: Fort city of the Parthian empire. Built with more than 100 defence towers, it has successfully prevented many attacks from the Roman Empire. One of the characteristics of the city is that there are both orient style temples and Greek style temples built near each other within the city.

70002545.name: Tepe Gawra
70002545.description: An ancient Mesopotamian settlement. From the Neolithic era to the old Assyria era, houses from different eras still remain. There is the world's oldest temple decorated with archivolts and pilasters that can also be seen in both Italian and Greek architecture.

70002546.name: Borsippa
70002546.description: An ancient city of the Sumerian civilization. The name means the 'Horn of the Sea'. There is a large ziggurat called the 'Tongue Tower', that is thought to be the ruins of the Tower of Babel in some cultures.

70002547.name: Malwiya Minaret
70002547.description: A spiral minaret constructed by the 8th Abbasid caliph, Al-Mu'tasim in Samarra. Many paintings that depicted the Tower of Babel are modeled after this minaret.

70002548.name: Borsippa Inscription
70002548.description: An inscription of Nebuchadnezzar II who built the golden age of Borsippa. It includes how he used the 'bricks of noble lapis lazuli' to restore the temple that enshrined god Nabu.

70002549.name: Fragment of the Second Temple in Jerusalem
70002549.description: The fragment of a Jewish holy temple built to replace Solomon's Temple which was destroyed during the Babylonian captivity. It is labelled in Hebrew as 'the place of roaming'. The inscription reads 'To the Trumpeting Place' written in in Hebrew.

70002550.name: Musussu
70002550.description: A holy animal depicted on the Ishtar Gate of the city of Babylon. It is worshipped as the sacred animal of city god Marduk and his son, Nabu.

70002551.name: Babylonian Harp
70002551.description: An ancient Babylonian harp. Can be seen on many wall murals as well as stone tablets. It is thought to have been mainly used on religious occasions. Though rather large in size, it is difficult to play while sitting down and is played while standing.

70002552.name: Goliath Heron
70002552.description: The world's largest heron that inhabits areas from South Africa to West Asia. It is approximately 1.5 meters in length, and the lengths of the wings are over 2 meters.

quests.name: The Dream of the Large Bird

70002553.name: Saluki
70002553.description: One of the world's oldest dog breeds. A sculpture of the dog has even been excavated at Tepe Gawra in Iraq. It is a hunting that has been bred in pursue of slimmer and longer limbs, and faster running speed. It is considered to be the breed that runs the fastest.

70002554.name: Persian Leopard
70002554.description: The largest leopard subspecies inhabiting the Middle East. Unlike the average leopard, it has spots on both its chest and stomach.

70002555.name: The Mesopotamian Marshes
70002555.description: A wetland area located in the lower Tigris Euphrates. It is a part of the Fertile Crescent, and since ancient times, it has been prosperous in agriculture.

70002556.name: Ursa Minor
70002556.description: A constellation that's believed to represent the hunter, Arcas, who was sent up to the heavens, according to Greek mythology, when he tried to shoot his mother who had been transformed into a bear without knowing it's her. He has been turned into a bear just like his mother. Also known as the Little Bear.

70002557.name: Cepheus
70002557.description: A constellation named after Cepheus, King of Aethiopia in Greek mythology. He was married to Cassiopeia and was the father of Andromeda.

70002558.name: Corvus
70002558.description: A constellation that represents a bird which served under sun god Apollo in Greek mythology. For providing false information to Apollo, resulting in him killing his lover, the bird was punished and banned from the heavens to become a constellation.

70002559.name: Crater
70002559.description: A constellation that depicts a large cup. Well known for ages in various regions, it is said to belong to or be a symbol of god.

70002560.name: Hydra
70002560.description: A constellation of the sea monster, Hydra, who, according to Greek mythology, was sent up to the heavens after having been defeated by Hercules and his nephew, Iolaus.

70002561.name: Draco
70002561.description: A constellation of the dragon which appeared in Greek mythology. Aside from the origin of the dragon being a guardian of the golden apples, there seems to be many other myths revolving around the constellation.

70002562.name: Auriga
70002562.description: The constellation with the distinctive feature of having the stars aligned in five corners. It is said to represent either the king of Athens, Erichthonius, or the son of Hermes, Myrtilus.

quests.name: A Great King Who Was Sent to the Heavens

70002563.name: Perseus
70002563.description: A constellation of the hero Perseus from the Greek mythology, who was said to have been sent up to the heavens by goddess Athena. He is apparently holding onto the head of Medusa with one of his hands.

quests.name: The Hero Who Shines in the Night Sky

70002564.name: Eridanus
70002564.description: A constellation based on a meandering river. It is said to be modeled after the Nile in northern Africa, or the Po in northern Italy. In Greek mythology, after the son of Helios recklessly drove the chariot across the heavens, Zeus struck lightening down on him, thus falling into the river.

quests.name: The Band in the Southern Sky

70002565.name: Algol
70002565.description: A star included within the constellation Perseus. The star's brightness changes approximately every three days. Algol is said to mean the Demon Star, and according to the star map, it is located at the head of Medusa that Perseus is carrying.

70002566.name: Alphard
70002566.description: The brightest star within the constellation Hydra. It means 'the solitary one' in Arabic. As it is located at what could be the heart of Hydra, it is also referred to as 'Cor Hydrae', meaning 'snake's heart'.

70002567.name: Albireo
70002567.description: According to the star map, it is the star located at the head of the constellation Cygnus. When looking through a telescope, you can see it is a double star consisting of the brighter yellow one and the fainter blue one.

70002568.name: Erakis
70002568.description: A red star that is included in the constellation Cepheus. Because of its very fine, deep garnet colour, it later started being referred to as the 'Garnet Star'.

70002569.name: Achernar
70002569.description: It is the brightest star in the constellation Eridanus which is located at the southern end of the constellation. It stands out well in the Southern Hemisphere, but the areas you can observe it from in the Northern Hemisphere are limited.

70002570.name: The Cat's Eye Nebula
70002570.description: A nebula in the constellation Draco, that is shaped like a cat eye. It seems to have an incredibly complex composition.

70002571.name: Round Nebula of Aquarius
70002571.description: A ring-like nebula located in the constellation Aquarius. Through an astronomical telescope, it does not appear to be very bright, but it looks very big.

70002572.name: The Double Cluster of Perseus
70002572.description: Two star clusters located in the constellation Perseus that consist of countless very old stars. Even with the naked eye, they can be seen as a faint light.

70002573.name: Perseids
70002573.description: A meteor shower that appears to come from the direction of the constellation Perseus. It is visible for roughly one month within the year. As it contains a number of bright meteoroids, it can be observed easily.

70002574.name: Geminids
70002574.description: The meteor shower that appears as though it is coming from the direction of the Gemini constellation. It appears for roughly 15 days within the year. Compared to other meteor showers, it appears to look relatively calmer.

70002575.name: Temple of Apollo Epicurius
70002575.description: A temple dedicated to the Sun God Apollo, located in the mountains of the Peloponnese Peninsula. Its construction mixes three major styles of Ancient Greek architecture, and is built with locally produced calcite tinged with blue.

70002576.name: Parthenon
70002576.description: A temple on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece, dedicated to the goddess Athena, whom the people of Athens considered their patron. It is built using white marble, with delicate decorations, in the Ancient Greek architectural style.

70002577.name: Epidaurus
70002577.description: Ruins located in the East of the Peloponnese Peninsula. It is said to be the sacred site of God of Medicine Asclepius in Greek mythology. Besides the temple, there is also a theatre, lodging, baths, and a round theatre that could fit a crowd of 10,000 people.

quests.name: Sacred Place of the God of Healing

70002578.name: Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights of Rhodes
70002578.description: A castle built on the island of Rhodes by the Knights of Rhodes after they had lost their original headquarters. They built castle walls around the town, four kilometres long and twelve metres high. Those walls are said to have repelled the attacks of enemy nations countless times.

70002579.name: Mycenae
70002579.description: The ruins located in the northeast of the Peloponnese Peninsula. It was the heart of the flourishing Mycenaean civilization in the B.C. era. Numerous objects crafted with gold have been found at this site.

quests.name: The Legendary City Rich with Gold

70002580.name: Tiryns
70002580.description: The ruins of the Mycenaean civilization, located in the east of the Peloponnese Peninsula. Huge stones have been stacked up to make the massive wall surrounding the ruins, so it is said that the one-eyed giant in Greek mythology, Cyclops, stacked them. The site is also believed to be the legendary hero Hercules' birthplace.

70002581.name: Painted Churches of Cyprus
70002581.description: A group of churches located in the mountains on Cyprus. Their exterior is simply made with wood and stones, but the inside is a beautiful Byzantine style fresco.

70002582.name: Mystras
70002582.description: A fortified town in the South of the Peloponnese Peninsula. It has the palace of the legendary hero Menelaus, monasteries decorated with fresco murals, and a lot more Byzantine architecture. It was originally built as fortification, but later started to function as a town as well.

70002583.name: Meteora
70002583.description: Monasteries built on top of giant stone mountains located at the foot of the Pindus mountain range. They are separated from the earthly world, and were built to facilitate prayer and meditation. They are called 'meteora,' meaning 'floating in the air' in Greek.

quests.name: A State of Prayer and Meditation

70002584.name: Rhyton
70002584.description: A type of ancient vessels mainly used in rituals. There is a hole in the bottom to allow to distribute the wine drawn with this vessel among other containers. It's said that wine poured from this vessel contains a sacred power.

70002585.name: Snake Goddess Figurine
70002585.description: A goddess figurine found on Crete. Its hands hold a snake, and there is a lion on top of its hat. From the fact that women and snakes were considered sacred, and snakes and lions were symbols of mother goddess, it is certain that this figurine was an object to worship for the local people.

70002586.name: Theseus and the Minotaur
70002586.description: The statue of the legendary Greek hero Theseus's battle with the Minotaur. It is said that Theseus decided to eradicate the Minotaur of the Labyrinth in Knossos Palace on Crete to end the Cretan tyranny over Athens.

quests.name: The Story of a Bull Monster

70002587.name: Lefkara Lace
70002587.description: Handmade hemp lace made in a village called Lefkara on Cyprus. Has a simple yet elegant design, using the techniques from both Lefkara and Venice.

70002588.name: Anemone
70002588.description: A flower native to the Mediterranean region. It has a variety of bright colors. In Greek mythology, it is said that it was born from the blood shed by Adonis, the beautiful boy who was favored by Goddess Aphrodite.

70002589.name: Acanthus
70002589.description: A flowering plant native to the Mediterranean region. Its shiny dark green leaves are more than 60 centimeters in length. Thought to be a sacred plant in ancient Greece, it was carved on the columns of the temples.

quests.name: The Flowers Engraved on the Columns

70002590.name: Eleonora's Falcon
70002590.description: A falcon breeding on the islands in the Aegean Sea. They both hunt and raise their young as a group. This fact contributes to ensuring more successful hunting, and a safer environment against enemies.

70002591.name: European Ground Squirrel
70002591.description: A squirrel found throughout eastern Europe, which grows to a length of approximately 20 centimeters. They live in colonies of individual burrows in pastures or grassy embankments. They feed upon seeds, plant shoots, and roots, and have a habit of taking food back to their nest by carrying it in their mouths.

maps.name: Map of Squirrel Living in Burrow

70002592.name: Greek Tortoise
70002592.description: A tortoise inhabiting dry areas in North Africa and southeast Europe. Their colors and shapes vary depending on their habitats, but all of them have the same spurs at the base of their rear legs. Its name originated from its shell pattern, reminiscent of a Greek mosaic.

70002593.name: Aegean Sea
70002593.description: An elongated embayment of the Mediterranean Sea, located between the Greek and Anatolian peninsulas. It has many islands. The sea was traditionally known as one of the most flourishing areas from ancient times, and as the birthplace of Aegean civilization which is the oldest civilization in ancient Greek.

70002594.name: Cyclades
70002594.description: One of the island groups in the Aegean Sea, comprised of about 220 islands. The island which was the most important religious site in ancient Greek is surrounded by the other islands. The name, Cyclades, refers to those surrounding islands.

70002595.name: Peloponnese
70002595.description: A peninsula located in the southernmost part of Greece. It is connected with the mainland Greece by the narrow land bridge called the Isthmus of Corinth. It has a mountainous interior and deeply indented coasts. It has many ruins, indicating that it's been a prosperous area since ancient times.

70002596.name: Mount Olympus
70002596.description: The highest mountain in Greece, located in the southwest of Salonika. Being close to the sea, it is one of the mountains that have highest relative elevations in Europe. It is described in Greek mythology as the home of the Twelve Olympians.

quests.name: Search for the Mountain of the Gods

70002597.name: Pindus
70002597.description: A mountain range located in northern Greek. It is roughly 160 km long, with an average elevation of 2,000 meters. Because it runs right across the Balkan Peninsula, the Pindus range is often called the 'spine of Greece'.

70002598.name: Crete
70002598.description: Located in the southern Aegean Sea, and the largest of the Greek islands. Being the center of the Cretan civilization, it has a large number of ruins which include the Knossos Palace.

70002599.name: Rhodes
70002599.description: An island located in the northeast of Candia. It is said that there was a huge statue of the ancient Greek Sun God, Helios, at the port on Rhodes.

quests.name: The Huge Image of the Sun God

70002600.name: Pegasus
70002600.description: A constellation that represents the winged horse, Pegasus, that appears in Greek mythology. Comprised of relatively bright stars, it is a well-known autumn constellation in Europe.

quests.name: The Birth of Pegasus, and Thereafter
The Birth of Pegasus, and Thereafter

70002601.name: Corona Borealis
70002601.description: A constellation that represents the crown the god of fertility and wine, Dionysus, gave to his wife, Ariadne. Ariadne is the daughter of King Minos, who helped Theseus find his way out of the Minotaur's labyrinth.

70002602.name: Delphinus
70002602.description: A constellation that represents the dolphin which saved the Greek court musician Arion. His ship crew was conspiring against him after he had amassed a fortune in the music festival in Sicily, and he had to escape overboard.

70002603.name: Grus
70002603.description: A constellation conceived from the observations by Dutch voyagers Pieter Keyser and Frederick de Houtman in the 16th century. It was previously part of the neighbouring constellation Piscis Austrinus.

quests.name: The Constellation Made in the Netherlands

70002604.name: Centaurus
70002604.description: A constellation that represents one of the centaurs, Pholus, who offered hospitality to Heracles when he was on the way to capture the Erymanthian Boar. The constellation was discovered in ancient Greece, but it is difficult to observe it in Greece now, because the rotational axis of the earth has since shifted.

70002605.name: Southern Cross
70002605.description: The smallest constellation of the 88 modern constellations, bordered by the constellation Centaurus. Comprised of two first-magnitude stars, it is frequently used to mark south.

quests.name: Mark of the South
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70002606.name: Mizar and Alcor
70002606.description: Mizar is the second star from the end of the Big Dipper's handle, and Alcor is right next to Mizar with a magnitude of 4. The two stars have been used to test people's eyesight since ancient times.

70002607.name: Spiral Galaxy in the Virgo Cluster
70002607.description: A spiral galaxy in the constellation Virgo. The dark dust lane and the bulge give this galaxy the appearance of the Mexican hat, a sombrero.

70002608.name: Bird-shaped Galaxy in Ophiuchus
70002608.description: A bird-shaped galaxy located between the constellation Ophiuchus and the constellation Sagittarius. It has a large number of small stars.

70002609.name: Dumbbell Nebula in Vulpecula
70002609.description: A planetary nebula in the constellation Vulpecula. Characterized by its oval shape and its narrow central part.

70002610.name: Flower-like Nebula in Cepheus
70002610.description: A spiral galaxy located near the star around the waist of the constellations Cepheus. Its shape and color are associated with a blue flower.

70002611.name: Trifid Nebula in Sagittarius
70002611.description: A nebula located in the west of the constellation Sagittarius. It is an unusual combination of different types of nebulas including a dark nebula. It can be observed with the naked eye under good conditions of darkness.

70002612.name: Alnair
70002612.description: The brightest star in the constellation Grus. The name is from Arabic, meaning 'the bright one of the tail.' It was part of the constellation Piscis Austrinu in the past.

70002613.name: Spiral Glaxy in Hydra
70002613.description: A spiral galaxy located in the South of the constellation Hydra. The central part is brighter than its rim. Has very well defined 3 spiral arms stretching from the center.

maps.name: Astronomer's Observation Record
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70002614.name: Titan
70002614.description: The largest moon of Saturn, discovered following the Galilean moons. It's larger by volume than the smallest planet, Mercury.

70002615.name: Rare
70002615.description: The largest moon of Saturn next to Titan. It was discovered after Ttian.

70002616.name: Lyrids
70002616.description: A meteor shower which has its peak in April each year. The radiant is located in the constellation Lyra. It has been known since ancient times, and the oldest observation records date back to some 2,000 years.

70002617.name: Hadar
70002617.description: A first-magnitude star located around what could be the foot of the constellation Centaurus. The name comes from Arabic, meaning 'on the ground.'

70002618.name: Rigil Centaurus
70002618.description: A first-magnitude star located around what could be the foot of the constellation Centaurus. The name means 'the foot of the Centaur.'

70002619.name: Globular Cluster in Centaurus
70002619.description: A globular cluster located at what could be the horse's back of the constellation Centaurus. Can be observed with the naked eye. It had been called 'Omega Centauri' until it was recognised as a globular cluster in the 19th century.

70002620.name: Caspian Sea
70002620.description: The world's largest lake. Over 100 rivers provide inflow to it. Has a wide variety of unique species inhabiting it, including sturgeons.

70002621.name: Caucasus Mountains
70002621.description: A mountain system in Eurasia between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, that appears in Greek mythology. Its geographical characteristics vary greatly depending on the regions.

70002622.name: Saiga
70002622.description: An antelope recognized by an unusual, over-sized nose. Hunted extensively as food and for their fur. The horn is considered an effective medicine, but it's not certain.

70002623.name: Zmeevik
70002623.description: A necklace bearing a portrait on it, especially popular in the Middle Ages. One side has a Christian saint and snakes, and the other side has prayer words inscribed on it.

70002624.name: Alexandrite Cat's Eye
70002624.description: A rare gemstone with a sharp cat's-eye shape at its center. Occasionally more valuable than diamonds.

70002625.name: Russian Desman
70002625.description: A mole which inhabits a river and marsh. Adapted for a more aquatic lifestyle, they can hunt fish. Their number has declined because of uncontrolled hunting for their fur.

70002626.name: Russian Wolfhound
70002626.description: A breed of large hunting dog, descended from dogs brought to Russia from central Asian countries. A quiet, but athletic and intelligent dog. Wild species inhabit the forest as well.

70002627.name: The Manio 'Giant'
70002627.description: A 6.5 metre tall menhir, or standing stone, which is situated in the forest called Manio. Being away from the groups of stone rows, it stands quietly and solemnly in a mysterious manner.

70002628.name: Figurine of Astarte
70002628.description: A figurine of a goddess of fertility. Astarte is considered a goddess equated with Aphrodite in ancient Greece. Also, in Phoenicia, she is worshipped as a goddess who controls death and reproduction.

70002629.name: The Venus of Leptis Magna
70002629.description: A marble statue of Venus, which is believed to have been displayed in the bath house in Leptis Magna. Standing after a bath, Venus begins to cover her breasts with her right hand, and her groin with her left hand.

70002630.name: Paphos's Necropolis
70002630.description: Underground tombs, called the 'Tombs of the Kings', which were constructed in the same architectural style as Parthenon. The tombs are cut into the native rock, and at times imitated the houses of the living.

70002631.name: Stele Fragments with Byblos Characters
70002631.description: A fragment of a stele with ancient characters inscribed on it in a careful manner. The characters are thought to be used in ancient Byblos. It is unknown if it will be legible when the fragments are pieced together.

70002632.name: Ancient Macedonian Gold Accessory
70002632.description: A luxurious accessory decorated with gold garnishes representing oak leaves. Its three-dimensional and delicate figure is a good example of fine ancient Macedonian techniques.

70002633.name: Clay Tablet with Cretan Characters
70002633.description: A clay tablet with the characters used in the ancient Cretan civilization. Can be found all across Crete. The characters look like a derivative of hieroglyphs, but it's not possible to decipher.

70002634.name: Ezaza Stone
70002634.description: A stele which documents the conversion of King Ezana to Christianity and his subjugation of various neighboring areas, including northeast Africa, in three separate languages.

70002635.name: Relief of Kali
70002635.description: A relief of the Hindu god Shiva's wife, Kali, sculpted on a temple wall. She is portrayed dancing on Shiva, who lies calm and prostrate beneath her.

70002636.name: Ancient Indian Architecture Book
70002636.description: An architecture book that is said to be found widely in India. It explains the methods of constructing temples and palaces, and introduces some of the reliefs that decorate those buildings. Also, the book contains the name of a person who is presumably the author.

70002637.name: Friar's Heel
70002637.description: A 6 meter tall single large block of stone, also known as the Heel Stone. It's elaborately designed to be kept securely standing. It is said that the Altar Stone located in the center of Stonehenge and the Friar's Heel are aligned in the direction of the sunrise of the summer solstice.

70002638.name: Cross Necklace
70002638.description: A Christian cross necklace. It is believed to have been worn by the people who fled to this place. It is a wonder as to what they prayed for in an underground city like this where the sunlight doesn't reach.

70002639.name: Thutmose I's Obelisk
70002639.description: A 22 meter tall obelisk of the Egyptian pharaoh, Thutmose I, built for the Sun God Amun-Ra. It has inscriptions by Thutmose I on the center, and by Ramesses IV on the sides.

70002640.name: Bronze Ceremonial Sword
70002640.description: A bronze sword used for ceremonial purposes, discovered near the settlement called Acropolis. It is thought to be used as the symbol of local rulers' power on ceremonial occasions.

70002641.name: The Code of Ur-Nammu
70002641.description: The oldest law code known, promulgated by the first king of the Sumerian third dynasty of Ur, Ur-Nammu. It is said that it influenced the Code of Hammurabi of ancient Mesopotamia. It institutes monetary fines for bodily damage.

70002642.name: The Relief of Pacal the Great
70002642.description: A relief of Pacal the Great from Palenque. It portrays him receiving a crown from him mother, Sak K'uk'. After he acceded to the throne at age 12, he successfully managed to rebuild the failing city of Palenque during his long reign.

70002643.name: Theravada Scriptures
70002643.description: Scriptures that document the core doctrine of Buddha. Theravada is a branch of Buddhism, and is the dominant form of religion in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and Thailand. The scriptures are believed to have been used by the founder of the Pagan Empire, King Anawrahta, to spread Theravada across his empire.

70002644.name: Olisihpa and Olosohpa's Canoe
70002644.description: The canoe believed to have been used by the Olisihpa and Olosohpa brothers, who founded The Saudeleur Dynasty, to travel to the island Pohnpei. The canoe is thought to have continued to be used to travel between the islands, judging from its extent of damage.

70002645.name: Incan Earthenware
70002645.description: Earthenware that has similar patterns to the ones used in the Incan Empire. It is believed that is here because the Incan people used to visit this island for unknown reasons.

70002646.name: Altar Relief
70002646.description: A stone relief discovered in the Copan ruins, with all of the 16 kings carved on it. It portrays the 16th king receiving the royal scepter from the first king.

70002647.name: King Muryeong's Stone Monument
70002647.description: A stele that documents the demise of King Muryeong of Baekje. Baekje was declining because of Goguryeo's invasions. King Muryeong, also known as 'Great General Tranquilizing the East,' successfully repelled attacks by Goguryeo, and turned Baekje into a great power by allying with the Liang dynasty in China.

70002648.name: Oyama Magnolia
70002648.description: A species of magnolia native to East Asia. The flowers are exceptionally fragrant and pure white in color, and open in the early summer. The view of the nodding flowers is lovely and angelic.

70002649.name: Shigaraki Pottery
70002649.description: Beautiful warm orange Shigaraki pottery. The local sandy clay has been thought to be suitable for making pottery since ancient times. The pottery has been heralded by a number of Japanese tea ceremony masters and artists.

70002650.name: The Story of Yuriwaka
70002650.description: An epic story about a young man by the name of Yuriwaka. He managed to find his way home after he had been betrayed by his subordinates, and marooned on an island on the way home from battle. There seems to be a similar story in ancient Greece. It's not certain if they are related.

70002651.name: The Sinckan Manuscripts
70002651.description: A series of leases, mortgages, and other commerce contracts used among Taiwanese Plains Aborigines, written in Latin after translating from their language, Syraya. It's considered to be traces of Dutch missionaries' educational activities in Taiwan.

70002652.name: Saoba Stone Pillars
70002652.description: Two adjacent giant stone pillars, 6 meter tall and 4 meter tall. The site is considered the home of the indigenous people of Taiwan, the Ami.

70002653.name: Statue of Bixia Yuanjun
70002653.description: Bixia Yuanjun is one of the Seven Heavenly Maidens, also known as the 'Heavenly Jade Maiden.' Thought to be the most compassionate goddess, especially venerated on Mount Tai in China.

70002654.name: Stone Pagoda
70002654.description: A 5-story Chinese pagoda which is believed to have been constructed during the Song dynasty era. Thought to be modeled after the pagoda which actually enshrines Buddha's ashes. Each storey has a Buddha image carved on it.

70002655.name: Iron Viking Shield
70002655.description: An iron shield believed to have been used by the Vikings who used to colonized this land. There were traces of a furnace and iron nails found in the area as well.

70002656.name: Cretan Pottery
70002656.description: A piece of pottery which is believed to have been made on Crete. The colors on it have faded but there seems to be a cow drawn on it if examined closely.

70002657.name: Villa Adriana
70002657.description: A large complex constructed as a retreat from Rome for Roman Emperor Hadrian at Tivoli, Italy. It is filled with reproductions of the emperor's favorite buildings of the Roman world.

70002658.name: Nuraghe
70002658.description: Large constructions made with stones stacked up like towers, seen on the island of Sardinia. It is believed that there were originally more than 20,000 of them when they were built in the prehistoric age.

70002659.name: Temple of Artemis
70002659.description: A Greek marble temple dedicated to the goddess Artemis, which originally existed from the BC period to the 3rd century AD. It was rebuilt three times after destroyed multiple times by acts of arson and a flood. One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

70002660.name: Golden Jackal
70002660.description: A type of jackal native to southeastern and central Europe, Asia Minor, the Middle East, and South Asia. The fur color varies seasonally from pale yellow to light gold.

70002661.name: The Goddess of Justice
70002661.description: A statue of Justitia, the roman goddess of justice. She holds balance scales, which represent the weighing of Justice, and a sword, symbolizing Power. She is often associated with other goddesses of justice.

70002662.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
70002662.description: A replica of a seated statue of the god Zeus, originally enshrined at the sanctuary of Olympia in ancient Greece. Its right hand holds a statue of Nike, goddess of victory, and its left hand holds a scepter. The original statue is said to have been about 13 m tall. One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

70002663.name: Apoxyomenos
70002663.description: Ancient Greek sculpture of an athlete who is believed to be scraping sweat from his body with some kind of instrument. It is unknown why they chose this human act as a subject, but it gives off a special mystique.

70002664.name: The Hercules Constellation
70002664.description: A constellation that represents the Greek hero Hercules. It is a large constellation located between Lyra and Corona Borealis, but has no first or second magnitude stars.

70002665.name: The Sculptor Constellation
70002665.description: A small and faint constellation in the southern sky, introduced by a French astronomer, Lacaille, who carried out observations at Cape Town. Despite its size, it's hard to find because it has no bright stars.

quests.name: The Constellation Made in France
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

quests.name: The Constellation Made in France
quests.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70002666.name: The Sculptor Galaxy
70002666.description: A spiral galaxy which lies between Sculptor and Cetus. It's a bright galaxy, but Europe is too far North to be able to observe it.

70002667.name: Uranus
70002667.description: The seventh planet in the Solar System. Its magnitude is 5.6, which makes it possible to observe it with the naked eye. It had been mistaken for a star more than 20 times before it was recognized as a planet. Its axis of rotation is tilted sideways.

70002668.name: Halley's Comet
70002668.description: A short-period comet visible from Earth every 75-76 years. The periodicity was first determined by English astronomer Edmond Halley. The comet seen before the Norman conquest of England in 1066 is thought to be Halley's Comet.

quests.name: The Appearance of a Prophesized Comet
The Appearance of a Prophesized Comet

70002669.name: Orionids
70002669.description: A meteor shower which can be seen in October every year. It appears to originate from the point located between the constellations Orion and Gemini. They are believed to be produced by Halley's Comet.

70002670.name: Almagest
70002670.description: A 2nd-century mathematical and astronomical treatise written by Claudius Ptolemy in Alexandria. It's the critical source of information on ancient Greek astronomy and mathematics.

70002671.name: Sidereal Messenger
70002671.description: The first book published by Galileo Galilei. It covers various topics, from the mechanism of a telescope, to the results of observations of the Moon and other astronomical objects. It's one of the most beautifully written masterpieces by Galileo as well.

70002672.name: Red Mullet
70002672.description: A type of goatfish. Characterized by its crimson body color. It can grow as big as 50 cm in length. The ancient Romans favored its delicate white flesh.

70002673.name: Nyau Mask
70002673.description: A mask that the Chewa people of Southeastern Africa wear at funerals. The dancers who put on the masks become a being called 'Nyau,' whose role is to deliver the deceased's soul to the world of their ancestors.

70002674.name: Libyan Desert Glass
70002674.description: Natural glass found in the Northeast of the Sahara. It's been used as a gemstone in jewellery since ancient Egyptian times. It's not clear how the glass formed in an area with no source of intense heat, like a volcano.

70002675.name: The Desert Locust
70002675.description: A type of grasshopper that lives around the Sahara. It can ride on the wind to distant places, and has even landed in Europe and India. If there is a surge in their population, they can have a devastating effect on crops.

70002676.name: Sahara Desert Ant
70002676.description: An ant that lives in the Sahara, that has an excellent sense of direction. Even if they wander here and there looking for food, they can find their way back to their nest in a straight line. Furthermore, even if the wind changes the shape of the sand dunes, they never get lost.

70002677.name: Oxpecker
70002677.description: A small bird that lives in Africa, to the South of the Sahara. Possibly because they eat the parasites that live on mammals' skin, large animals let them sit on their back, or even head.

70002678.name: Saddle-Billed Stork
70002678.description: A large bird that lives in the wetlands stretching from Central to Southern Africa. It's name comes from the yellow spot on the base of its bill, which looks like a saddle. It has a spot on its breast with no feathers, which it uses to keep its eggs warm when nesting.

70002679.name: Shoebill
70002679.description: A large bird that lives in the wetlands in the center to the South of Africa, with a characteristic huge bill. It is so calm, it is often mistaken for a statue. It's thought that it moves slowly so as not to alarm the fish it hunts.

70002680.name: Cape Vulture
70002680.description: A large bird which inhabits the South of Africa. They assemble tree branches to build nests on cliffs. Because the terrain suited to their nests is rare, their nests tend to collect in the same areas, and they will use the same spot to build a nest for generations.

quests.name: A Vulture from the South of Africa

70002681.name: Wattled Crane
70002681.description: A crane that lives in the wetlands of Southern Africa. Its neck and head are white, and the feathers on its body are dark. It's characteristic feature is the wattle which hangs below its cheeks. Also, from the base of its beak and around its face, it has no feathers, with exposed red skin.

70002682.name: Armadillo Lizard
70002682.description: A lizard which inhabits rocky areas in the South of Africa, and grows to about 20cm long. It has hard scales along its spine. When it's attacked, it runs and hides in rock crevices. But if there's nowhere to run, it will bite its tail and roll its body into a ball, using the scales on its body as defense.

70002683.name: Black-Footed Cat
70002683.description: A wild cat that lives on the Savannah in the South of Africa. In contrast to its small stature, it is very fierce, and may take down enemies larger than itself. According to locals, it can kill a giraffe by biting its neck.

70002684.name: Cape Ground Squirrel
70002684.description: A member of the squirrel family that inhabits the arid region of Southern Africa. It lives in a burrow underground. Unlike squirrels that live in trees, it doesn't store food, but spends most of the day eating. If it senses danger, it alerts its fellow squirrels with a bird-like call.

maps.name: Map of Squirrel Living in Burrow

70002685.name: Rinkhals
70002685.description: A snake which inhabits the South of Africa. It is venomous, and when it feels threatened, it spits the venom at its enemy's eyes. It is also good at playing dead, so approaching it carelessly is dangerous.

70002686.name: Eastern Green Mamba
70002686.description: A snake that lives in Southeastern Africa. It has a long, thin body, and some species reach over 3 meters. Its body is bright green, and it often hides in evergreen trees. Compared to the black mamba it is rather docile, and its venom is weaker, although it is still deadly.

70002687.name: Puff Adder
70002687.description: A snake which lives in the Center of Southern Africa. It has a thick body with a herringbone pattern, and can be almost 2 meters long. When it senses danger, it blows a puff of air as a threat, hence its name. It has large fangs with high levels of venom, so is extremely dangerous.

70002688.name: Black-Necked Cobra
70002688.description: A snake that lives in Central Africa. The back of its head is black, which is the reason for its name. Its back is dark brown. When attacking, it spits venom at the enemy's eyes, which can fly a distance up to 3 meters. The venom is very poisonous, and body parts that are bitten can experience necrosis.

70002689.name: Saharan Horned Viper
70002689.description: A poisonous snake that lives in the Sahara. It has characteristic horn-like protrusions, one above each eye. It has a pattern on its back, and can hide in the sand to wait for prey. It can travel quickly through sand by moving diagonally.

quests.name: Investigation of a Snake with Horns

70002690.name: Bell's Dabb Lizard
70002690.description: A herbivorous lizard that lives in the Sahara. They can grow to over 40cm long. It's thick tail is covered in spiny scales, and it attacks with it when protecting itself. It is mostly active in the daytime, but when the heat is too intense it will hide in a hole.

70002691.name: Giant Girdled Lizard
70002691.description: A lizard that lives on the grasslands in Southeastern Africa. Large ones will reach 40cm long. It has hardened scales on its back, which is the source of its name. It seems to love basking in the sun.

70002692.name: African Hunting Dog
70002692.description: An animal resembling a dog, which lives on the Savannah in Central South Africa. Its body is patterned with black, white, and orange spots, and it has large, round ears. They live in highly social packs of around a few dozen. The pack hunts together cooperatively.

quests.name: The Famous Hunters of the Savannah

70002693.name: Patas Monkey
70002693.description: A monkey that inhabits the African Savannah. It's quick in trees, but on the ground it can also run extremely fast, more than 55km/h. They seem to spend their day on the ground, then often climb low trees to sleep at night.

70002694.name: African Spurred Tortoise
70002694.description: A tortoise that inhabits the arid environment of the Southern Sahara. It has protrusions like spurs between its tail and each of its back legs, hence its name. It is quite active for a tortoise.

70002695.name: Common Warthog
70002695.description: An animal that can be seen in sub-Saharan Africa. Its appearance resembles a boar, and it has the wart-like bump under each eye. Watching them sprint with all their might with their tails sticking up is somehow entertaining.

70002696.name: Addax
70002696.description: An animal whose characteristic is its corkscrew-shaped horns. It's suited to the desert climate, with thick skin to withstand strong sun rays, and wide hooves that won't sink into the sand. Furthermore, it can live for more than one month without drinking water.

70002697.name: Scimitar Oryx
70002697.description: A herbivorous animal that lives around the edge of the Sahara, with characteristic long, bent backward horns. They migrate North and South with the seasons, in large herds. They can withstand dry conditions, able to go a long time without drinking, but when there is water available, they will drink a lot.

70002698.name: Mbuna
70002698.description: A freshwater fish with a vivid striped pattern, that lives in Lake Malawi. They are very territorial, and each individual's pattern is slightly different. It seems that the stronger the fish is, the clearer the pattern is.

70002699.name: African Lungfish
70002699.description: A fish that lives in the lakes and marshes of Southern Africa. The fins on its chest and belly are whip-like. It must rise to the surface of the water to breathe occasionally. If the lakes dry up in the dry season, it burrows underground and makes a cocoon, and survives by hibernation.

70002700.name: Tassili n'Ajjer
70002700.description: A plateau mountain range in the middle of the Sahara. The impressive rock formations were formed by erosion. There are some rocks in caves with drawings of herds of cattle and crocodiles. It's thought that the drawings show the appearance of the environment long ago, but it's hard to believe that when it's now a desert.

70002701.name: Shea Tree
70002701.description: A tree that grows in the Savannah, South of the Sahara, and can be 7m to 20m tall. It is able to grow even in areas with little rain. A high-quality oil, Shea Butter, can be harvested from its seeds, and it is used as a food and a medicine.

70002702.name: Chongoni Rock Art
70002702.description: Paintings that appear on rocks and in caves across a wide area of Southeastern Africa. The drawings of hunters are especially ancient, and the sites have been used in ceremonies for a long time.

maps.name: Map of an Ancient Wall Painting
maps.prerequisite: The Rock Paintings of Tsodilo Hills

70002703.name: The Rock Paintings of Tsodilo Hills
70002703.description: Rock paintings in the hills of the Kalahari Desert. In an extremely small area, there are thousands of vivid drawings, and they may be a clue to the history of the area.

70002704.name: Okavango River
70002704.description: A river that flows in the arid region of Southwest of Africa. It is an inland river that does not flow to the ocean, so huge wetlands form at its lower reaches. It is a valuable resource for the life around the river basin.

70002705.name: Makgadikgadi Salt Flats
70002705.description: One of the World's largest salt flats, in the South of Africa. Several rivers flow in, but only during the rainy season they fill with water and become saltwater lakes. Many different animals come looking for salt, water, and grass.

70002706.name: Stone Tools of Homo Habilis
70002706.description: Stone tools thought to have been used in prehistory. Because there are no traces left of their manufacture, they are presumed to be even older than stone tools found in other areas. They seem to mostly be for hunting.

70002707.name: Tadrart Acacus Rock Paintings
70002707.description: Paintings on walls, thought to be from prehistory. There are depictions of people riding horses, and giraffes, elephants, and camels, so it could be inferred that they show the appearance of the area at that time. ‘Tadrart’ means ‘Mountains’ in the local language.

70002708.name: Nyami Nyami Figure
70002708.description: A figure depicting a god with the head of a fish and the body of a snake. People in the present day still believe that those who provoke his anger will be met with great disaster.

70002709.name: Camel Spider
70002709.description: An animal resembling a spider. Almost one third of its body length is taken up by its jaws. Larger species feed on mice and small birds. They aren't said to be poisonous, but it's probably still better not to approach carelessly.

70002710.name: Rainbow Agama
70002710.description: A lizard whose head and back are red and yellow, turning to blue and green by its tail. They are diurnal, and live in open, rocky areas.

70002711.name: Lakes of Ounianga
70002711.description: Lakes dotting the Sahara Desert. They all have different sizes, depths, and water colours. Although there is little rain, they get an abundance of water from underground springs, so never dry up.

70002712.name: Manchester
70002712.description: A town located in the western part of the British Isles. This town originates from the fort of 'Mancunium' which was built by the Ancient Roman Empire during the 1st century. At the end of the 18th century, due to the textile industry making use of the steam engine, the city has undergone rapid growth.

70002713.name: The Whydah
70002713.description: The ship of Samuel Bellamy, a pirate known for his love of giving speeches. While his crew was passed-out drunk, the captives seized their chances and ran the ship aground. The whole lot of them were arrested.

70002714.name: Scombrops Boops
70002714.description: A large deep sea fish, some reaching over 1 meter long. They have fatty bodies, and are delicious.

70002715.name: Lanternfish
70002715.description: A deepwater fish that rises close to the water's surface at night. It's body is bioluminescent, which is the reason for its name.

70002716.name: Blue Shark
70002716.description: A shark with its population distributed from tropical to temperate oceans. They can be up to 4 meters long, and have been known to attack people and boats.

70002717.name: Slender Snipe Eel
70002717.description: A deep sea fish, whose characteristic features are its long, thin body, and protruding jaw. It's thought to use it for hunting crustaceans.

maps.name: Map of a Long, Thin Fish

70002718.name: Flapjack Octopus
70002718.description: A species of deep sea octopus. Different to other octopi, it only has one row of suction cups on each tentacle. Its body is so soft that it will collapse if it leaves water. As it has a briny taste and strong smell, it's not very suitable for eating.

70002719.name: Neptune
70002719.description: A planet whose existence was conjectured from an irregularity in Uranus' orbit. It is roughly the same size as Uranus, but is a deeper blue.

70002720.name: Triton
70002720.description: Neptune's satellite. It is one of the largest moons in our solar system. Its special trait is that it revolves around Neptune in the opposite direction of its rotation. Thus, its orbital speed is gradually slowing, and it's thought that it will collide with Neptune in the distant future.

70002721.name: Peacock
70002721.description: The brightest star in the constellation Pavo, a magnitude 2 star. Its name is the English translation of the constellation's Latin name.

70002722.name: Pavo
70002722.description: A constellation located near the south celestial pole. Aside from its brightest star, the magnitude 2 star Peacock, many of its stars are dark, but its shape is clear, so it is easy to find.

quests.name: The Constellation of a Bird of India
The Constellation of a Bird of India

70002723.name: Columba
70002723.description: A constellation designated at the end of the 16th century, based on the dove that appears in the Biblical story of Noah's Ark. It led Noah to land after the great flood.

quests.name: The Constellation Derived from the Scripture
The Constellation Derived from the Scripture

70002724.name: Sagitta
70002724.description: A constellation in the shape of the golden arrow that mythical Greek God of Love, Eros, shot at the god, Zeus. It's said that this arrow is what caused Zeus' heart to be stolen by Ganymede.

70002725.name: Lupus
70002725.description: A constellation formed of the shape of the king of Arcadia, Lycaon, who incurred the wrath of Zeus, and was turned into a wolf. Lupus and Centaurus have often been paired since ancient Mesopotamian times.

70002726.name: Scutum
70002726.description: A constellation designated in 1684 by a Polish astronomer, Hevelius, in commemoration of King John III Sobieski. John III was hailed for his courage in the Battle of Vienna.

70002727.name: Scutum Open Cluster
70002727.description: An open cluster in the constellation Scutum, with a considerable number of stars.

70002728.name: Dorado
70002728.description: A constellation near the Large Magellanic Cloud. Plotted at the end of the 16th century by Frederick de Houtman and Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser.

70002729.name: Hekla
70002729.description: A volcano in the South of Iceland. Hekla means 'hood' in Icelandic. It is the most active volcano in Iceland, and many eruptions have been recorded.

70002730.name: Mount Cameroon
70002730.description: A volcano on the coast of Central Africa. It's thought that it may be the volcano recorded by Hanno the Navigator from Carthage in ancient times.

70002731.name: Trinidad
70002731.description: An island to the North of continental South America. On the South side of the island there is a channel called the Serpent's Mouth, and on the North side there is one called the Dragon's Mouth. It is an island where the beauty of tropical nature can be appreciated.

70002732.name: Tristan da Cunha
70002732.description: A volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is named after the Portuguese explorer who discovered it at the beginning of the 16th century. It's hoped it can be used as a resupply and refuge port.

70002733.name: Fernando de Noronha
70002733.description: An archipelago of 21 islands, located off the coast of Cape Sao Roque.

70002734.name: Temple of Saturn
70002734.description: A temple for Saturn, the agricultural god in ancient Rome, equivalent to Cronus in ancient Greece. The temple was used to store treasury and official documents during the Roman Republic era.

quests.name: Temple of the God of Agriculture
Temple of the God of Agriculture

70002735.name: Temple of Eleusis
70002735.description: Ruins of a temple to goddess Demeter, located in Eleusis, northwest from the center of Athens. Secret rituals held here were so well known that Hadrian participated before his accession.

70002736.name: Chains of Prometheus
70002736.description: Strong chains found in the Caucasus mountains. According to legend, they were used to chain Prometheus to a rock where his liver was eaten daily by an eagle as punishment for stealing fire from Mount Olympus and giving it to mankind.

70002737.name: Theatre of Dionysus
70002737.description: A major theatre in Athens, dedicated to Dionysus at the foot of the Athenian Acropolis, where the festival Dionysia was held. Considered to be the birthplace of Greek tragedy plays.

70002738.name: Bilbao
70002738.description: A town located in the northern part of the Iberian Peninsula. It has been a business-oriented town since ancient times and upon entering the 19th century, its industries have also developed.

70002739.name: Pyramids of Guimar
70002739.description: Stair-shaped rectangular pyramid structure built on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands. It is a mystery who built it, and what they built it for.

70002740.name: Relief of the Land of Punt
70002740.description: The Land of Punt is an ancient kingdom. It was known for producing and exporting gold and wood as a trading partner of ancient Egypt. The relief depicts the ship fleet sent by the pharaoh Hatshepsut.

70002741.name: Narmer Palette
70002741.description: A black shield-like stone with inscriptions on both sides, that depict the king fighting enemies. Thought to be used in rituals judging from its size.

quests.name: The Stolen Momento of the King
The Stolen Momento of the King
The Stolen Momento of the King

70002742.name: Bust of Serapis
70002742.description: Serapis is a Graeco-Egyptian god. Widely worshipped in the Ptolemaic Kingdom as well as in the Roman Empire. On his head is a grain-measure, the Greek symbol for the land of the dead.

70002743.name: Statue of Neith
70002743.description: Neith is the goddess of war and weaving. She is usually portrayed bearing a shuttle on her head, and an arrow in her hand.

70002744.name: Tusks of a Giant Boar
70002744.description: Tusks of a giant wild boar. Thought to be a prize for boar hunting in ancient time. Some episodes about the Calydonian Boar of Greek mythology describe how boar hunting is dangerous yet honoured.

70002745.name: Temple of Castor and Pollux
70002745.description: A temple built based on the legend of the twin brothers Castor and Pollux helping the Roman Republic in the war against Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, the last king of Rome. All that is left now of the temple are three pillars.

quests.name: The Rise of the Roman Republic
The Rise of the Roman Republic

70002746.name: Head of a Cyclops Statue
70002746.description: A Cyclops is a one-eyed giant in Greek mythology. In ruins of the Mycenaean civilization there are a number of structures with huge stones stacked up, which is believed to have been done by a Cyclops.

70002747.name: Stratagems in War
70002747.description: A book written by Polyaenus. One of the episodes is about Cambyses II, emperor of the Achaemenid Empire, who tactfully used cats which are regarded as sacred animals in Egypt, when he attacked the town of Pelusium.

70002748.name: Bibliotheca
70002748.description: A compendium of Greek myths and heroic legends, which had not yet been influenced by Roman mythology. Chronologically compiled from the 'origin of the world' to the Trojan War.

70002749.name: Ancient Egyptian Ceremonial Sword
70002749.description: A ceremonial version of a sickle-sword called khopesh. The blade is only sharpened on the outside portion of the curved end.

70002750.name: Senet
70002750.description: A board game from predynastic and ancient Egypt. Often placed in the grave alongside other objects.

70002751.name: Uraeus
70002751.description: A representation of an Egyptian cobra, used as a symbol of sovereignty, royalty, deity and divine authority in ancient Egypt. Made of gold and gemstones.

70002752.name: Argonautica
70002752.description: A Greek epic poem that tells the myth of the voyage of Jason and his fifty heroic companions in their giant ship, the Argo, to retrieve the Golden Fleece from the remote Colchis.

70002753.name: Polycrates' Ring
70002753.description: A jewel-encrusted ring believed to have been owned by Polycrates, the tyrant of Samos. He threw the ring into the sea to escape a reversal of fortune, but he later discovered it inside of the fish a local fisherman caught for him.

70002754.name: Hyacinth
70002754.description: A flower native to the eastern Mediterranean region. According to Greek mythology, the flower is believed to have been born from the blood of Hyacinth whom the sun god Apollo favored.

quests.name: A Beautiful Flower and its Story

70002755.name: Mulberry
70002755.description: A 10-15 m tall deciduous tree that bears reddish purple fruits in early summer. According to Greek mythology, the fruits of the tree were originally white but later became reddish purple due to the tragic deaths of the lovers Pyramus and Thisbe.

quests.name: Finding a Subject for a Play
Finding a Subject for a Play

70002756.name: Red Clover
70002756.description: A flowering plant native to Europe. The flowers are dark pink with a paler base. Commonly used to make an herbal tea. Helps increase soil fertility as well.

70002757.name: Mount Etna
70002757.description: The tallest active volcano in Europe, located on the east coast of Sicily. A number of eruptions have been recorded in the literature of every age. In Greek Mythology, the deadly monster Typhon was trapped under this mountain by Zeus.

70002758.name: Samos
70002758.description: A Greek island in the eastern Aegean Sea. Believed to be the birthplace of the goddess Hera; it has a temple enshrining her. The Greek mathematician Pythagoras was born on this island.

70002759.name: Triangulum Australe
70002759.description: A small constellation near Centaurus. Consisting of three of the brightest stars that shape a triangle. Was depicted on a celestial globe by a Dutch astronomer, Petrus Plancius.

70002760.name: Carina
70002760.description: A constellation in the southern sky, which contains the second brightest star in the night sky, Canopus. Represents the keel of the ship Argo.

70002761.name: Volans
70002761.description: A constellation in the southern sky. It represents a flying fish. In celestial maps, the flying fish was often depicted as being chased by the predatory fish represented by the adjoining constellation Dorado.

70002762.name: Canopus
70002762.description: The second brightest star in the night-time sky, after Sirius. Its color is white but it looks reddish when viewed from the northern hemisphere because it appears fairly low in the southern sky.

70002763.name: Flower-like Nebula in Carina
70002763.description: Diffuse nebula located in the constellation Carina. Although it is four times as large and even brighter than the famous Orion Nebula, the Carina Nebula is not as well known, due to its location in the southern sky.

maps.name: Astronomer's Observation Record
maps.location: Cape of Good Hope, Open Sea

70002764.name: Acropolis of Atlantis
70002764.description: The capital city of the legendary Atlantis. Its city plan is shaped like a circle. It is heavily fortified with castle walls and canals built in and around the city.

70002765.name: Bombilla
70002765.description: Type of drinking straw, used by Guarani people in South America to drink a tea. Has a filter in the lower end to separate the mate infusion from leaves and stems.

70002766.name: Yerba Mate
70002766.description: A plant grown in South Africa. The leaves are widely known as the source of the tea called 'mate.' Takes years to become fully grown, but can be harvested for decades.

70002767.name: Acai
70002767.description: A species of palm tree grown in South America. Bears small bluish-purple fruits. The fruits are highly nutritional, and widely consumed by local people.

70002768.name: Red-legged Seriema
