70003095.description: A ring created by a young person originating from the Claddagh village in Ireland. It features designs of a heart, two hands and a crown.

70003096.name: Cathedral Stained Glass
70003096.description: Stained glass depicting the life of a certain saint. Dozens of these stained glasses decorate the interior of the cathedral.

70003097.name: Lace Glass Goblet
70003097.description: A Venetian goblet made of lace-patterned glass. As the techniques for making Venetian glass are kept within Venice, it is most likely not possible for people from other countries to recreate it.

70003098.name: Lehmann Glass Carving
70003098.description: Glasswork made by Bohemian glass artisan, Lehmann. Carvings are left on glass, creating a beautiful appearance like jewelry.

70003099.name: Pomegranate Earthenware
70003099.description: Porcelain with pomegranate painted on it. As not many Europeans knew of pomegranate, the piece was called the 'Blue Onion'.

70003100.name: Countryside Earthenware
70003100.description: Earthenware made by someone by the name of Palissy. It features three-dimensional reliefs of small animals and plants with a reproduced scenery of the countryside as a background.

70003101.name: Pique Accessory
70003101.description: An accessory created with a technique called Pique. It features a tractable base material.

70003102.name: Small Islamic Carved Box
70003102.description: Ivory work created in the Caliphate of Cordoba. It features detailed reliefs of different scenes on each side, connected together with engravements; created by a noble.

70003103.name: Crystal Pot of the Sasanian Empire
70003103.description: A pot that the king of France, Louis VII was gifted from queen Eleanor in the 12th Century. Thought to be originally produced during the period of the Sasanian Empire, detailed gold work has been applied to it, creating the form it now has.

70003104.name: Bird Calligraphy
70003104.description: Calligraphy in the shape of a bird. Composed of meaningful words containing symbolism, it is quite difficult to read and comprehend the writing.

70003105.name: African Mask
70003105.description: Mask used by an African tribe during rituals. The shape and meanings of these masks differ from tribe to tribe.

70003106.name: Hatsuhana Katatsuki Tea Canister
70003106.description: A Japanese tea canister that is known as one of the Three Greatest Specialties in Japan. It is said to have been owned by many historical figures; it's priceless.

70003107.name: Shigisan-Engi
70003107.description: A handscroll from Japan in the 12th century. It uses the 'Ijidozu' technique for representing the passing of time throughout the scroll. It is considered to be one of Japan's four greatest narrative scrolls.

70003108.name: Labu Sayong
70003108.description: A black pot with a peculiar shape. A traditional craft piece made in the Malay Peninsula, loved by the locals.

70003109.name: Andes Retablo
70003109.description: A boxed-shape altar made in Andes. Depicts the local customs and landscapes of the area. It contains colorful, distinctive designs and is considered as a work of art.

70003110.name: Codex Gigas
70003110.description: A holy manuscript written in Latin. From what is currently confirmed, it is the world's largest manuscript. There have been rumours that devils took part in the creation of this manuscript.

70003111.name: Mammoth Fang Flute
70003111.description: A flute made from a mammoth fang. Known as the oldest wind instrument.

70003112.name: Talisman of Charlemagne
70003112.description: A pendant-shaped talisman said to have been worn by Charlemagne. It is said that whoever holds this talisman shall become king. Who will be the next owner of the talisman?

70003113.name: Perfection of Wisdom Palm-leaf Manuscript
70003113.description: A Perfection of Wisdom manuscript written on palm-leaf. Considered as a substitute for palmyra leaves, palm-leaves are used as a writing medium throughout Southern and Eastern Asia.

70003114.name: Shofar
70003114.description: A musical horn made from the horns of a male sheep. It appears in the Old Testament.

70003115.name: Solomon's Shields
70003115.description: A gold shield made by King Solomon. It is said that 200 large shields and 300 small shields were made, but they were stolen by the pharaoh of Egypt.

70003116.name: Balafon
70003116.description: An instrument played in West Africa. Below this wooden xylophone are uniquely shaped gourds. Inside the gourds are spiderwebs and bats wings, which amplify the vibration effects of the instrument.

70003117.name: Bhagavad Gita
70003117.description: One of the Hindu scriptures and is part of the Hindu epic, Mahabharata. Set in a narrative framework of a dialogue between Lord Krishna and prince Arjuna, it talks about the roles of the various casts within the story.

70003118.name: The Creation of the Gods
70003118.description: A piece of literature written during the Ming dynasty. A story featuring many gods, set during the decline of the Shang dynasty and the rise of the Zhou dynasty. It greatly influenced the religions of mankind.

quests.name: Literature About the Hopeful Grand Duke

70003119.name: Jin Ping Mei
70003119.description: A popular novel from the Ming dynasty. A side story of the Water Margin, said to provide a precise depiction of the culture and lifestyles of the time.

70003120.name: The Tale of the Heike
70003120.description: A war tale depicting the rise and fall of the Taira clan. A tale passed down by blind monks known as Biwa Hoshi.

70003121.name: Yashiori-no-Sake
70003121.description: Japanese sake that was found at the location said to have been where a 8-headed, 8-tailed dragon was slayed. Although it looks quite old, the liquor inside seems strangely fresh.

quests.name: Dragon Slayer of the Far East

70003122.name: Resplendent Quetzal Feather Crown
70003122.description: A crown decorated with the feathers from the resplendent quetzal. As it is already a rare species, there are concerns that it may become extinct from having too many become captured.

70003123.name: Codex Mendoza
70003123.description: Pictorial documents created with tree fibers. Contains information of the lives of the mysterious Aztec civilization.

70003124.name: Large Herbivore Fossil
70003124.description: The bones of a large four-legged animal. Many of these fossils have been discovered throughout the Eurasian continent, and research is underway. Although it's habitat is not yet known, as its incisors are more developed than its canine teeth, it is thought that the animal may be a herbivore.

70003125.name: Manul Cat
70003125.description: A species of cat which inhabits the area around Lake Baikal. It's fur may appear chunky due to the long length and density of the hair growing. When it feels threatened, it will raise one side of its upper lip, revealing its canine teeth.

70003126.name: Tibetian Sand Fox
70003126.description: A species of fox which inhabits Central Asia. They create nests in grasslands as well in the gaps beneath rocks and inhabit them. They feature a long muzzle with small eyes, making them appear dazed.

70003127.name: Alpacas
70003127.description: A species of camel which inhabits South America. As they have high quality fur, they are considered as great livestock since ancient times. However, when threatened, they have the habit of spitting saliva with a strong odor.

70003128.name: Markhor
70003128.description: A species of goat which inhabits Central Asia. They are known for their pair of long twisted horns and white beards. They're mainly found in the grasslands and rocky areas of alpines, and move towards areas with lower altitude during the winter. They are hunted in some areas as their horns are said to have medicinal effects.

70003129.name: Friesian Horse
70003129.description: A horse originating from the northwestern parts of Europe. They have long hair with a black body. As they are quite strong, they are used as war horses as well as for carrying luggage.

70003130.name: Gypsy Vanner Horse
70003130.description: A horse originating from England with a small but powerful body. Used for pulling carriages since ancient times. As it has a long mane and tail, and similar hair grows on their ankles, they're quite warm.

70003131.name: Frogmouth
70003131.description: A bird inhabiting the area centering around Southeast Asia. They feature a large flattened hooked bill with a frog-like gape, hence the name.

70003132.name: Paradise Tanager
70003132.description: A bird inhabiting South America. It's head, stomach and back feature bright colors, and is known for its beauty. They're carnivores with a size of approximately 10 centimeters. Many of the other tanagers also feature beautiful colors.

70003133.name: Arachnocampa
70003133.description: An insect inhabiting places such as Australia. The larva inhabits the ceilings of caves, drips light emitting mucus from its body to lure insects and prey.

70003134.name: Spurge-Laurel
70003134.description: A poisonous shrub found all over Europe. Its flowers, seed, and grass parts are all highly toxic; touching the sap alone can cause rashes. If ingested, it can cause damage to nerves and internal organs.

70003135.name: Stinging Brush
70003135.description: A poisonous plant found in Australia. Its height reaches to approximately 1 meter. The body of the entire plant is covered with stinging hairs, and causes extreme pain when it makes contact with your skin. It is said that in the worst-case scenarios, this pain can continue for several of years.

70003136.name: Death Camas
70003136.description: A poisonous plant found in the western parts of North America. As the name suggests, it is highly toxic; ingesting a small amount can cause organ dysfunction, leading to death. Utmost caution must be taken as they greatly resemble the edible herb, Camas.

70003137.name: Stubby Squid
70003137.description: A squid inhabiting the Pacific Ocean. It is sometimes mistaken for an octopus due to its thick torso. As it inhabits the deep ocean, its eyes are greatly developed. It is said that its taste is similar to octopus.

70003138.name: Pacific Seaweed Pipefish
70003138.description: A fish that inhabits the waters near Japan. It is characterized by its elongated mouth and body. It is suspected that the shape of its body is made for it to hide in the gaps between things such as seaweed. The male gender of this fish gives birth as opposed to the female. This fish is not suitable for eating.

70003139.name: Ellesmere Island
70003139.description: An island located in the northernmost part of Canada. It has the most northern mountain range in the world and features several fjords and glaciers.

70003140.name: Rhone River and Arve River
70003140.description: Rivers flowing in eastern France. Although the rivers merge, as the water quality of the two rivers are different, for a brief period, the two bodies of water do not mix and the flow is divided into two colors.

70003141.name: Taurus Nebula
70003141.description: A nebula thought to have been created through the explosion of a star. Records around the world of having witnessed this explosion several hundred years ago indicates the size of the explosion.

70003142.name: Elongated Galaxy of Ursa Major
70003142.description: A elongated galaxy located in Ursa Major. As it is hard to observe with the naked eye, observing this would require specialized equipment.

70003143.name: Carina Nebula
70003143.description: Nebula located in the Carina constellation. Although it is classified as one of the larger nebulas, as it cannot be observed without reaching high latitude areas such as the Cape of Good Hope, it is not well known. It is said to have been discovered by Lacaille.

70003144.name: Icarus
70003144.description: One of the small planets. As its orbit is quite close to the sun, it was named after Icarus from Greek mythology. It passes by close to the Earth every ten or so years.

quests.name: An Asteroid Getting Close to the Sun

70003145.name: Star of Bethlehem
70003145.description: The legendary star, said to have notified the Three Wise Men of the East of the birth of Christ. However... After putting together a report and looking up to find the star once again, it is nowhere to be found. Was it really the legendary star that you saw? There's no way to confirm this.

70003146.name: Camelopardalis
70003146.description: A constellation of the northern skies, located near the North Pole. Although there are locations where it can be observed throughout the year, as it does not stand out, it is not well known. It's based off of a giraffe, an animal which inhabits Africa.

70003147.name: Lepus
70003147.description: A constellation located south of Orion. One of the 48 Ptolemaic constellations. According to its lore, due to the selfishness of humans, as a warning, a rabbit was made into a constellation.

70003148.name: Tucana
70003148.description: One of the constellations of the southern skies. Established during the 16th Century. It's supposedly based off of the toucan bird, but as there were many involved with the establishing of this star, there are multiple different stories regarding the bird this constellation is based off of.

quests.name: Bird constellation in the New Continent

70003149.name: Hydrus
70003149.description: One of the constellations of the southern skies. Established during the 16th Century. Its name means 'male water snake' as opposed to Hydra that represents 'a female water snake.'

70003150.name: Equuleus
70003150.description: One of the smallest constellations. It does not contain any bright stars. Although it is one of the 48 Ptolemaic constellations, no one knows of its mythological origins or who established it. It's a constellation surrounded by mystery.

70003151.name: Comet Encke
70003151.description: One of the comets which orbit the sun. It has a short orbital period. It's believed to be the originator of several related meteor showers known as the Taurids, and it emits substances which become the base for meteor showers.

70003152.name: Azure Dragon of the East
70003152.description: One of the sky ecliptic regions divided by ancient Chinese Astronomers, containing 7 of the 28 mansions, assigned to the Azure Dragon of the East. It contains Virgo and Scorpio within it.

70003153.name: Black Tortoise of the North
70003153.description: One of the sky ecliptic regions divided by ancient Chinese Astronomers, containing 7 of the 28 mansions, assigned to the Black Tortoise of the North. It contains Aquarius and Pegasus within it.

70003154.name: White Tiger of the West
70003154.description: One of the sky ecliptic regions divided by ancient Chinese Astronomers, containing 7 of the 28 mansions, assigned to the White Tiger of the West. It contains Aries and Orion within it.

70003155.name: Vermillion Bird of the South
70003155.description: One of the sky ecliptic regions divided by ancient Chinese Astronomers, containing 7 of the 28 mansions, assigned to the Vermillion Bird of the South. It contains Gemini and Cancer within it.

70003156.name: Almendres Cromlech
70003156.description: One of the cromlechs located around Portugal. Located in the outskirts of the ancient capital Evora which is east of Lisbon, it's one of the oldest and largest in Portugal.

70003157.name: Guimaraes Castle
70003157.description: A castle in which the first king of Portugal, Afonso I was born in. In the past, Guimaraes consisted of only monasteries and settlements. However, in order to protect the city from the raids and attacks from Vikings from the North, a castle was built.

70003158.name: Siega Verde Rock Art Site
70003158.description: Ruins that spread throughout Coa Valley in northern Portugal to Siega Verde in western Spain. Contains thousands of line drawings depicting people and animals. It is said to have existed since 20 thousand years ago, and is the largest scale of ancient rock art in the outskirts of the area.

70003159.name: Prague Orloj
70003159.description: An astronomical clock built in Prague, the ancient capital of the Holy Roman Empire. It combines the functions of an astrolabe used at that time with the functions of a clock. Not only can it tell time, but it can also tell the position of the sun and moon.

70003160.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory Ruins
70003160.description: Observatory built by Ulugh Beg, the ruler of Samarkand whom is also an astronomer. It was considered one of the most advanced research facilities of the Islamic world at the time.

70003161.name: Batalha Monastery
70003161.description: Officially known as the 'Monastery of Saint Mary of the Victory.' It has the name of Batalha as it was built in commemoration of the victory against the Castilians. Construction lasted for centuries, during which various popular architectural styles throughout Europe was incorporated.

70003162.name: Azulejo
70003162.description: A form of Portuguese and Spanish tilework featuring detailed decorations. The techniques were brought about during the age when the Islamic state advanced to the Iberian Peninsula, and has expanded to become an important part of Portuguese architecture.

70003163.name: Gold Print Art
70003163.description: Print art made with the most advanced printmaking technology of the time which made use of gold work technology. Invented in Germany, it features the use of fine lines and has spread widely throughout Europe along with the spread of printing technology. It has played an important role in art history.

70003164.name: Zink
70003164.description: Brass instrument developed from a horn. Like a recorder, the sound can be adjusted by covering the holes of the instrument. The instrument is popular throughout Europe and is called zink in Germany and Northern Europe while in other areas it is known as cornett.

70003165.name: Dead Grass
70003165.description: Dead grass found in Africa West Coast. Found while searching for an 'undying plant'; but it appears to already be dead...

70003166.name: Anastatica
70003166.description: A rare plant which changes its appearance during the dry and rainy seasons. Due to its amazing change in appearance, it is also known as 'Revival Grass' in some cultures and is said to be able to survive for several decades without the need of water.

70003167.name: Alfarrobeira
70003167.description: Another name for the carob tree in Portugal. As its fruit is sweet and contains high nutritional value, it is highly valued as an ingredient for sweets.

70003168.name: Pico Island Vineyard
70003168.description: One of the Azores Islands. Although it was a barren volcano, the monks who had immigrated there had planted grapes between the gaps of the lava; and the built up lava blocks formed walls which protected the plants from the wind. As a result of this, a unique landscape was formed.

70003169.name: Sagres Point
70003169.description: Known as the 'Village of Navigators', it is located near Cape St. Vincent which is on the southernmost end of the Eurasia Continent and Sagres. This area, together with the cape in Sagres, is used as a landmark for seafarers traveling through the Mediterranean Sea.

70003170.name: Incomplete Chapel
70003170.description: One of the chapels of the Batalha Monastery. Prince Duarte was in charge of the construction of this building so that it can be used as a place for royal family members to be at rest.

70003171.name: Elmina Castle
70003171.description: A castle built by Portugal for protecting the trade with Africa. The land it's built on is also known as the Gold Coast as the area is known for the production of gold. The castle played a major role in trade.

70003175.name: Garrus Pottery
70003175.description: Islamic pottery made using the Sgraffito technique. It features a distinctive pattern that is layered with a green glaze.

70003176.name: Guinnea Pepper
70003176.description: Plant inhabiting places such as West Africa. Another name for it is melegueta. Its dried seeds are considered hot spices and are used instead of pepper in some areas.

70003177.name: St. Andrew's Island
70003177.description: An island located in a river that flows in western Africa. The Europeans who settled there built a fortress and developed it as a trading post. Various countries fought over the territory, causing the name to change each time the ownership of the island changes.

maps.name: Map of a Trading Post Island

70003178.name: Duarte Writings
70003178.description: A piece of literature written by Prince Duarte himself. Contains various information regarding the way of politicians, knowledge of horseback riding among other things from various fields.

70003179.name: Threatening Letter Addressed to Jose's Father
70003179.description: A crumpled piece of paper. Although mostly unreadable, you can make out the following... 'Your daughter's life.... ship...... royalty...... kill......' The details of the paper are unknown, perhaps it is a threatening letter.

quests.name: Truth of the Ship with Royalty that Sank

70003180.name: Fernando's Bible
70003180.description: The holy bible that Prince Fernando uses. The pages appear to be old, but hardly any damage can be seen on them. It appears to have been well kept and used for a long time. There are two memos saying 'until the end of faith' stuck in between the pages.

70003181.name: Letters from Pedro
70003181.description: A copy of the letters from Prince Pedro to his brothers. The letters seem to be regarding various cultures, trades, wars, and religion. The number of letters addressed to Prince Henrique is the largest and they contain information on the trading between East Asia and Venice.

70003182.name: Longbow of Aljubarrota
70003182.description: A longbow used by the King of Portugal, John I. It was entrusted to his son, Henrique, and was being kept at the school in Sagres.

70003183.name: Phobos
70003183.description: A secondary planet of Mars. It is the first satellite orbiting the innermost orbit. It's gradually approaching Mars and the collision between the two in the distant future is to be expected.

70003184.name: Oberon
70003184.description: A secondary planet of Uranus. It carries the name of Oberon, the king of fairies. Its craters have the name of 'Macbeth' and 'Hamlet', the names of various characters in the works of Shakespeare.

70003185.name: Titania
70003185.description: The largest secondary planet of Uranus. It carries the name of Titania, the queen of fairies. The name was given by the discoverer's son after the discoverer's death.

70003186.name: Blue Fire
70003186.description: A phenomenon that can be seen from the Java Island of Indonesia where blue fire is being expelled. It is thought that the sulfur gas being expelled gives off a blue light when burning and that the gas may change states into a liquid and flow while burning.

70003187.name: Secondary Rainbow
70003187.description: When two rainbows occur in parallel to each other, the outer rainbow is known as a secondary rainbow. Although the reason for this phenomenon is unknown, the color alignment of the two rainbows are opposite to each other.

70003188.name: Sagres
70003188.description: A village that is said to have been built by a certain member of the royal family in Portugal. Located at the edge of the Iberian Peninsula, it is said to be a place to watch over the fleets sailing the seas as and also functions as a fortress during conflicts with other countries.

70003189.name: Valaam Monastery
70003189.description: A monastery located on Valaam, an island in Ladoga Lake. Its history dates back before Christianization in Russia, but due to its geographical state, it was involved in warfare multiple times and was blighted for a period of time. It is said that it is recently getting rebuilt.

quests.name: Wishes from the Edge of North

70003190.name: Notes of a Secretary from the Byzantine Empire
70003190.description: Notes left by a secretary of the Byzantine Empire. The author appears to have died in battle during the Fall of Constantinople along with Constantine XI Palaiologos. The note contains the words of the Emperor when he revealed his intention to go against Mehmed II of the Ottoman Empire.

70003191.name: Saint Olga's Baptism Clothes
70003191.description: Clothes said to have been worn by Olga, the wife of Igor I of Kiev during her Baptism in Constantinople. It features a simple design but contains a unique embroidery.

70003192.name: Codex Buranas
70003192.description: A medieval codex stored at the monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in Germany. Contains hymns and secular poems in ancient languages of Europe such as Latin. The secular poems, in particular, contain many themes ranging from literature to satire, sex and alcohol, as well as gambling.

70003193.name: Hypatia's Writings
70003193.description: Parts of the writings during the late Roman Empire by the female, Hypatia. She was an excellent Scholar in the academic city of Alexandria, but was killed by Christian mobs, and most of her works have been lost.

70003194.name: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
70003194.description: Records written by a Greek voyager in the 1st century in Egypt which then was a province of the Roman Empire. The records were written for traders involved in the trades between Egypt and India, and the Far East, China, is also introduced as an area for the production of silk in them.

quests.name: Better to Ask the Way than to Go Astray
Better to Ask the Way than to Go Astray
Better to Ask the Way than to Go Astray
Better to Ask the Way than to Go Astray
Better to Ask the Way than to Go Astray

70003195.name: Mabinogion
70003195.description: A compiled book containing the traditional stories told in Wales since ancient times. Contains stories such as 'Four Branches of the Mabinogi' which originated from ancient mythology, and the 'Three Welsh Romances' which originates from the legend of King Arthur.

70003196.name: The Forme of Cury
70003196.description: A cookery book written for the royalty and the aristocracy in England in the 14th century, which uses terms derived from French. The book is said to have been compiled by the chef of Richard II and contains many dishes using sugar which was rare at the time as well as spices and herbs from India, Asia, and the Middle East.

70003197.name: Virgin Mary's Clothing
70003197.description: According to Orthodox Church, a simple piece of clothing said to have been worn by Virgin Mary while she was alive. Stored in the church of Istanbul during the period of the Byzantine Empire, it is said by the Orthodox Church that a miracle had happened there.

70003198.name: The Book of the Love-Smitten Heart
70003198.description: A picture book of a chivalrous story written by royalty from 15th century France, Rene d'Anjou. The story is about a 'heart' possessed by 'love' and sets out on a journey to rescue the captured woman it loves. The book is quite popular with ladies due to the poetry and beautiful drawings.

70003199.name: Nantucket Lightship Basket
70003199.description: Traditional crafted baskets passed down by fishermen in Nantucket Island in North America. Traditionally made with techniques used for making barrels for whale oil. It features a symmetrical shape and contains pattern that one would not imagine that it's made with wood. A lid was not included during the early creations of the basket.

maps.name: Map of a North American Basket

70003200.name: He Shi Bi
70003200.description: A treasure from the Zhao state in northern China during the Spring and Autumn period. The jade used for this treasure was discovered by Bian He of the Chu state. It was later obtained by the Zhao state. It's a treasure with a complicated history and is also the origination of the Chinese term for 'perfection'.

70003201.name: White Sugar Dessert
70003201.description: A model of a mansion or castle, made solely from white sugar. Served all over Europe at banquets for royal aristocrats since ancient times, after appreciating the dessert visually, it is then shattered in front of the audience. In order to display the wealth of families, luxurious accessories are sometimes also added to the dessert.

quests.name: The Groom's Reputation is on the Line

70003202.name: Cape Jasmine
70003202.description: A plant that can be found in Japan, China, Taiwan, and the Indo-China Peninsula. Mainly found in clusters within forests, these white flowers bloom and release a strong fragrance between early summer and summer. Its fruits are used for traditional Chinese medicine, as well as food and dyes.

maps.name: Map of an East Asian Plant

70003203.name: Snake of Yongzhou
70003203.description: The snake which was featured in the 'Tale of the Snakecatcher,' written by Liu Zongyuan, a poet during the Tang Dynasty. It is said that it causes plants to dry and contains deadly poison that will kill all those it bites. There was apparently a period when it was used to make medicine effective for incurable diseases, as well as a form of taxation.

70003204.name: Monasteries of Mount Athos
70003204.description: Monasteries located on the Athos Peninsula and Mount Athos area, east of Salonika. The area contains large monasteries as well as small houses where monks lived in. Although Virgin Mary is the patron saint of the area, females are not permitted to enter the mountain area; only males are permitted to enter.

70003205.name: Felis
70003205.description: A cat loving constellation established by a cat lover for other cat lovers. Lalande, a famous French astronomer, thought to be a huge cat lover, established this constellation as he felt sorry that there was not yet a cat among the constellations, though it seems that its name has yet to fully settle in.

quests.name: Sending It to the Starry Skies
Sending It to the Starry Skies

70003206.name: Amarna Ruins
70003206.description: A capital city that was once ruled by the pharaoh of ancient Egypt, Amenhotep IV. Shortly after his death, the capital city was changed to Thebes and the city was abandoned. The city was also called 'Akhetaten' which means the 'Horizon of the Aten.'

70003207.name: Castel del Monte
70003207.description: A castle built by the Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, Frederick II. Although it was not planned during its construction, but there is a theory that it was not intended to be built as a military fortress but a hunting base. It features a octagonal structure.

70003208.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
70003208.description: A monastery located at the bottom of Mount Sinai. It was built during the early years of the Byzantine Empire and is famous for having ancient manuscripts and icons that are dated prior to iconoclasm. It has been treated as an important place for pilgrimage ever since crusaders began staying there.

70003209.name: Memphis Ruins
70003209.description: The remains of Memphis, one of the religious cities of ancient Egypt. This land with Ptah as their main god was also known as the 'White Walls' and was the largest city of lower Egypt.

70003210.name: Amarna Letters
70003210.description: Diplomatic correspondence of ancient Egypt from the period of the pharaoh, Amenhotep IV. Contains mostly diplomatic correspondences from the officials of neighbouring countries and countries under the rule of Egypt addressed to the pharoah written in Akkadian which was the official language of the time.

70003211.name: Belisarius's Treasure Sword
70003211.description: A sword favored and used by Belisarius, a general which shined during the period when the Eastern Roman Emperor, Justinian I was in reign. Belisarius was talented in commanding soldiers, and would often win battles with small amounts of cavalry, but was said to have had misfortune during his later years.

70003212.name: Siete Partidas
70003212.description: A statutory code compiled during the reign of the king of the Kingdom of Castile, Alfonso X of Castile. It was compiled under things such as the codes of Ancient Rome, the Byzantine Empire, and the church law; and had successfully eliminated the disagreement of customs caused by the integration of the late Kingdom of Leon during the previous generation.

70003213.name: Sword of Frederick II
70003213.description: A sword treasured by Frederick II, the king of the Holy Roman Empire. Capable of speaking six languages, Frederick was known as an open-minded monarch of Western Europe. However, throughout his life he had opposed the Knights Templar and the Guelphs, and was excommunicated on multiple occasions.

70003214.name: Panagia
70003214.description: A necklace containing an icon of the Theotokos, Mary and Jesus Christ. Its name is also one of the titles of Mary and means 'Perfect Saint" in Greek, and is said to be worn by priests whom have obtained a status higher than bishop within the Orthodox church.

70003215.name: Orthodox Church Icon
70003215.description: An icon commemorating the establishment of the first seven ecumenical councils (Second Council of Nicaea) due to the intensification of iconoclasm activities in the Byzantine Empire. It is said that it is prayed for in Orthodox churches during the first Sunday within the 40 day period prior to Easter.

70003216.name: Bust of Nefertiti
70003216.description: A bust of Nefertiti, the wife of the pharaoh of ancient Egypt, Amenhotep IV. At the workshop site where it was found, multiple similar busts were also excavated. As such it is said that it may have been made for the purpose of training and educating students.

70003217.name: Painting of Saint Christopher
70003217.description: A painting depicting Saint Christopher widely known in Western Europe. The painting depicts a man carrying young Jesus Christ, traveling through storms. The saint is widely worshipped he is said to have protected young Jesus Christ from all kinds of danger during the journey.

70003218.name: Icon of Saint Christopher
70003218.description: An icon of Saint Christopher, passed down within the Orthodox church. Although the icon is traditionally of a giant with a dog head, it is said that Saint Christopher was converted to Christianity and then martyred. In Russia, the icon was changed to a human form under the reason of 'removing pagan influences.'

70003219.name: Icon of the Dormition of the Mother of God
70003219.description: One of the icons passed down within the Orthodox church. It depicts the death of Virgin Mary. The celebration of Mary's eternal slumber started from the east, and is known as the 'Assumption of Mary' in Western Europe.

70003220.name: Procopius's Wars
70003220.description: A work of Procopius, the secretary of the famous general of the Eastern Roman Empire, Belisarius. It contains records of the reign Justinian I whom was the emperor at the time, the heroic acts of Empress Theodora, and the accomplishments of Belisarius as a general.

70003221.name: Procopius's Secret History
70003221.description: A work of Procopius, the secretary of the famous general of the Eastern Roman Empire, Belisarius. Contrary to the 'Wars of Justinian', this work boldly contains the scandals and criticism of Justinian I and his Empress as well as Belisarius and his wife.

70003222.name: Cantigas de Santa Maria
70003222.description: A collection of poems about Virgin Mary in which Alfonso X of Castile is said to have helped write. Although the military and domestic affairs during his reign were unsuccessful, he had greatly influenced the culture, and this collection of poems is said to be one of his representing works.

70003223.name: Plague Elegy
70003223.description: A poem recorded by a priest living in the northern regions of Mosul. The original poem was written in 248 parts in the Aramaic language. It contains content of mourning of the plagues that affect people, including Cholera which was widespread at the time.

70003224.name: Dragon Robe
70003224.description: Robes worn in the royal court by emperors throughout the history of Chinese dynasties. These robes are covered with writings of prayers for happiness and longevity. It also contains nine embroideries of a dragon with five fingers which is only permitted for emperors.

maps.name: Map to a Luxurious Bestowed Gift

70003225.name: Northern Saw-whet Owl
70003225.description: An owl which inhabits North America. It features a small body and gold eyes. They can be spotted near villages and in shrubs and bushes. It's favoured by humans as it catches and preys on rodents.

maps.name: Map of a Small Bird of Prey

70003226.name: Mandarin Duck
70003226.description: A bird which inhabits Eastern Asia and Southeast Asia. The male mandarin duck features bright colours. The first symbol of its Chinese name represents the male, while the second symbol of its Chinese name represents the female. In China, the Korean Peninsula, as well as in Japan, it is a symbol of intimate couples.

70003227.name: Pekingese
70003227.description: A breed of small dogs. For many years it has been favoured as a lap dog or companion dog within the royal courts of China. It's yellow hair in particular is highly valued. Although it is said that those who take them outside of the royal court will be sentenced to death, other kinds of small dogs can be found in markets and some people secretly keep them as pets.

70003228.name: Apus
70003228.description: One of the constellations of the southern sky. It was established based on the records left by Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser who created the star chart for the southern sky. The constellation was named after the birds of paradise, discovered in the Southern Hemisphere during the same period of time. In 'Uranometria,' it is mistakenly recorded as 'Apis Indica' which refers to the 'Indian Honey Bee.'

quests.name: Bird of the South, in the Skies of the South
Bird of the South, in the Skies of the South
Bird of the South, in the Skies of the South
Bird of the South, in the Skies of the South

70003229.name: Chamaeleon
70003229.description: One of the constellations of the southern sky. It was established based on the records left by Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser who created the star chart for the souther sky. The constellation was named after the chamaeleon which was discovered in the Southern Hemisphere during the same period of time.

70003230.name: Edge of the World
70003230.description: Cape Bajador located south of the Canary Islands. In the past, to seafarers, beyond that cape was considered unknown waters. A demonic boiling sea spewing lava... such superstitions bounded seafarers until Henrique's courageous subordinate successfully crossed over to the other side of the cape.

quests.name: Folklore of the Edge of the World

70003231.name: Charybdis Whirlpool
70003231.description: In ancient times, there are countless myths which originated from natural phenomena. The Strait of Messina is no exception. It is said that there dwells a hungry monster which creates whirlpools, causing fear to seafarers.

70003232.name: Pool Bethesda
70003232.description: A pool located in Bethesda which means 'God's Grace.' It is said that when the water is 'stirred' by a servant of God, the pool will be able to cure all illness.

70003233.name: Undine
70003233.description: One of the four elementals, the spirit who controls water. It is said that this spirit has the form of a beautiful female, and upon marrying a human, she'll be able to obtain a soul. However, if she is betrayed by her husband, she'll lose her soul, seek revenge on her husband, and return to the form of water.

70003234.name: Boogie Man
70003234.description: A scary ghost said to have been born from the minds of children. Legends of this being vary over different regions. It was probably used in various regions by parents to make their children behave.

70003235.name: Walpurgis Night
70003235.description: A night which occurs mainly in Central Europe and Northern Europe. It is said to be a night in which the boundaries between the dead and living become faint, and witches gather around a bonfire and worship the devil; though the truth of behind this is unconfirmed.

70003236.name: Kitsune no Yomeiri
70003236.description: In Japan, foxes are said to be animals that are capable of changing their appearances to resemble humans. When such foxes have wedding ceremonies, it is said that they celebrate the occasion with lanterns. However, it is said that as it is difficult for the human eyes to see, humans can only see eerie fireballs floating.

quests.name: Folklore of the Row of Fireballs

70003237.name: Mangalore
70003237.description: A port city located in southwestern India. Regarded as an important port since long ago, and many dynasties fought for the control of it. Like the Mangaladevi Temple located within the city, it's name originates from the name of a God in Hinduism.

70003238.name: Visakhapatnam
70003238.description: Port city located on the eastern coast of India. There are many Buddhist ruins there, which have been historically visited by pilgrims. The city flourished with the protection from Ashoka the Great of the Maurya Empire. The cityscape also shows the influence of later rulers.

70003239.name: Manama
70003239.description: Situated within the Persian Bay, this city is located northeast of Bahrain Island. It thrived as a hub for maritime trades thanks to its location. Pearls harvested from the surrounding seas are extremely high in quality, making them popular in Europe.

70003240.name: Yanbu
70003240.description: A port town that faces the Red Sea, which has flourished as a transit port for spice trades. It has maintained connections with places like Egypt and the Mediterranean nations. There are steep mountains northeast of the town, creating a fantastic view.

70003241.name: Inhambane
70003241.description: One of the cities thriving since ancient times, located on the east coast of Africa. What was once considered a major production location of cotton, has been developed as a base of trading for things such as ivory. Due to the warm climate, various crops such as cashews are being produced.

70003242.name: Gabon
70003242.description: The area of Central Africa facing the Gulf of Guinea in the Atlantic Ocean. Many large mammals inhabit that area due to the rich forests in the area. The area is famous for being a source of various minerals.

70003243.name: Red Cliffs
70003243.description: The location said to have been where Cao Cao, who had subjugated North China during the late Han Dynasty, was defeated by the allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei. It is said that the allied forces had burned down Cao Cao's army, while at the same time some say that Cao Cao's army had spread a plague and had set fire to the ships themselves before retreating. However, the truth regarding this remains unknown.

70003244.name: Dongpo Red Cliffs
70003244.description: The location in which Su Dongpo, a man of literature and art of the Northern Song dynasty, was said to have written the first and second 'Chibifu' at during the period in which he was sent to Hangzhou, which is not far from the location of the famous Red Cliffs mentioned in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms. It is said that people sometimes confuse this with the Ancient Chibi Battlefield written in the work by Du Mu, a poet of the late Tang dynasty.

70003245.name: Convent of Christ in Tomar
70003245.description: A convent built during the 12th century for the Templar Knights. After the disbanding of the knights, it had become a base for the Knights of the Order of Christ. Prince Henrique who became the leader, had expanded the corridors, and throughout almost a century, had made various expansions to the place.

70003246.name: Humayun's Tomb
70003246.description: The tomb of the 2nd Mughal Emperor, Humayun, is located in the outskirts of Delhi of which he had declared as a capital city.It is considered as an excellent example of Islamic architecture in India and it had later influenced the Taj Mahal and is considered to be the base of garden architecture in India.

70003247.name: Sword of the Prince of Portugal
70003247.description: A sword that Philippa of Lancaster, the wife of the King of Portugal, John I, while on her deathbed, bestowed upon her sons whom were heading to conquer Ceuta. It was given to one of the Princes by the church.

70003248.name: Neumagen Wine Ship
70003248.description: Burial goods excavated from the grave of the Neumagen wine merchant. Neumagen was a city located along Moselle which had thrived in wine production during the period of the Roman Empire. Initially composing of two vessels, the galley ship is equipped with multiple wine barrels, and carried two tax collectors and many rowers.

70003249.name: Changxin Palace Lamp
70003249.description: A lamp created in the shape of a court lady; one of the burial goods discovered in Liu Sheng, Prince of Zhongshan and his wife's tomb. It burns oil to create light. Within the bronze statue exists empty space, designed to keep the smoke and soot inside.

70003250.name: Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae
70003250.description: A theology book written by the theologian and Dominican Friar, Thomas Aquinas.The book contained the 'logic' which was discussed during the philosophy of that time in regards to the method of proving the existence of God; the book had successfully secured Thomas Aquinas's fame. On the other hand, it is said that there are some that view those ideas as dangerous.

70003251.name: Rosario of Francis Borgia
70003251.description: A rosario of Francis Borgia, the 3rd commissary-general of the Society of Jesus. With his great uncle being Cesare Borgia, he was able to obtain a certain position under Charles V, the Holy Roman Emperor; to find the belongings of such a person is quite rare.

70003252.name: Talmud
70003252.description: A collection of books compiling the 'Oral Torah', considered as another set of commandments passed down from Moses. The collection is composed of written collections such as Mishnah and Gemara. Also known as the 'incomplete book of commandments', it has become a part of the religion and lifestyle of Judaism.

70003253.name: Biblia Pauperum
70003253.description: A block-book illustrating the events that appear in the Bible. When it was established in southeast Germany and Austria during the mid-13th century, it spread throughout Europe together with the popularity of letter press printing. It was produced based on the pretype theory which was mainstream for churches at the time.

70003254.name: Scivias
70003254.description: A work of Hildegard of Bingen, a nun from 11th century Germany. It features prophesizing text and allegorical illustrations. It contains content related to the church and religion which is said to have been written under God's revelation.

70003255.name: The Ladder of Divine Ascent
70003255.description: A book for monks, created by John Climacus, a monk of 7th century eastern Rome. 'Climacus' means ladder in Greek, hence the title of the piece. The piece discusses the teachings of monks with a thirty-step hierarchy.

70003256.name: The Trinity
70003256.description: An icon that Andrei Rublev, a monk in 15th century Russia, had requested a certain monk to create. The icon depicts the three angels that visited Abraham, sitting under a tree. It has been interpreted as a symbol of the Holy Trinity.

70003257.name: Fork with Two Tines
70003257.description: A type of cutlery brought by the Byzantine Empress Theodora when she married and became the governor wife of Venice during the 11th century. At the time in Europe, as the custom of using forks was obsolete, she was accused of being in possession of 'pagan artifacts'.

70003258.name: Tonkori
70003258.description: A five-string plucked instrument played by the Sakhalin Ainu which are located in the Far East of Russia, and the northern parts of Japan. It has a flat shape with a smaller end. According to the customs of Sakhalin Ainu, each part of the instrument is supposed to be modeled after the various parts of the human body.

quests.name: Folklore Regarding the Lighthouse of Alexandria
Folklore Regarding the Lighthouse of Alexandria

70003259.name: Psaltery
70003259.description: An instrument containing 24 strings stretched over a thin trapezoidal resonance box that is played with either fingers, feathers, or sticks. It is thought that the instrument had originated from the ancient Greek instrument, psalterion, and has now been brought to Europe. Even Hildegard of Bingen was said to have learned how to play the instrument from a nun.

70003260.name: Bai Zhi Wen Ji
70003260.description: A collection of poetry written by Bai Juyi, a poet of the Tang dynasty. He was well known as a poet throughout his life and his works have been widely read by people regardless of their backgrounds. His poems had quickly spread to Japan and Silla, but at the same time it is said that many fake works were also distributed.

70003261.name: Carta Pisana
70003261.description: The first portolan chart said to have been made in Pisa during the 13th century. It's a map used for sailing which graphically depicts ports and coasts, and was heavily produced up until the 14th century.One of its features is that it does not contain references of other portolan charts, and was made without the consideration that the earth is in the shape of a sphere.

70003262.name: Catalan Atlas
70003262.description: A map given to King Charles VI of France from King Aragon. The map was created by the Jewish cartographers, Abraham and Jehuda Cresques. It is said to be made based off of the information from people such as Marco Polo and John Mandeville.

70003263.name: Shy Plant
70003263.description: A plant native to South America. It's other name is 'Mimosa Pudica'. When stimulated by hands, wind or heat, the leaflets will close, hence the name of 'Shy Plant'. It's quite rare for people to refer to these plants by their official name.

maps.name: Map of a South American Plant

70003264.name: Corpse Lily
70003264.description: A parasitic plant that can be found in many places of Southeast Asia; it features a large flower with close to 1 meter in diameter. They were apparently discovered by England through an expedition, however, as it emits a strong odor to lure insects, perhaps just approaching the flower requires a certain amount of courage...

70003265.name: Socotra Dragon Tree
70003265.description: A tree which features countless branches spread out from a certain height of the trunk. Resin from this tree is known as 'dragon's blood'. The dragon's blood extracted from the Socotra Island in the Indian Ocean has been famous since ancient times. However, there's apparently a closely related species found in the Canary Islands of Africa where dragon's blood can also be extracted from.

70003266.name: White Egret Flower
70003266.description: A plant that can be found in the far East of Asia, such as Japan. It often grows in groups in low wetlands such as valleys. When it blooms, the flower resembles a swan with its wings spread open.

70003267.name: Madagascan Sunset Moth
70003267.description: A kind of moth which inhabits in Madagascar. The adults of these moths are day-flying moths. They feature beautiful wings that have a base color of black, and feature green and yellow. Perhaps they may even be the most beautiful kind of moth among the entire world.

70003268.name: Himalayan Monal
70003268.description: A large pheasant which inhabits places such as India. In comparison to other pheasants, they feature a good physical shape as well as short tail feathers. The male features multicolored plumage with a metallic shine.

70003269.name: Great Frigatebird
70003269.description: A seabird belonging to the frigatebird family, inhabiting mainly in the Pacific and Indian Ocean. When spread open, its wings have a length exceeding 2 meters. However, they are quite light. Although both the male and female feature a black body, they are easy to distinguish as the male features a red gular sac, while the female features a white gular sac.

70003270.name: Tarbagan Marmot
70003270.description: A species of rodent which inhabit Mongolia and Russia. They are hunted by Nomads for their meat and fur, as mentioned in 'The Travels of Marco Polo'. As it is said to carry plagues, utmost caution must be taken when making contact with it.

70003271.name: Norwegian Forest Cat
70003271.description: A kind of cat which inhabits Northern Europe. There are even mentions of such cats in Norse mythology. Although this kind of cat is now quite common, it has been theorized that a cat that was brought by the Vikings from the Byzantine empire may have been its ancestor.

70003272.name: Gaboon Viper
70003272.description: A viper which inhabits the middle southern parts of Africa. It has poisonous fangs that can exceed the length of 5 centimeters, which is the longest among snakes. Although they apparently have gentle natures, as they're lethally poisonous, it would probably be wise to not disturb it.

70003273.name: Sei Whale
70003273.description: A type of whale which inhabits various locations such as in the Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Ocean. They eat crustaceans as well as fish. Their body shape is slenderer in comparison to other kinds of whales, and perhaps because of their agile movements, though they widely inhabit the seas, there have been very few sightings of it.

70003274.name: Chinese Sturgeon
70003274.description: A type of sturgeon that has inhabited various places throughout China since ancient times. Many can be seen in the Yangtze River, and during spawning season, they can even be found upstream in the Jinsha River. According to the 'Compendium of Materia Medica', they are very nourishing, but it is rare for someone to catch them, and their population is unclear.

70003275.name: Cape Chashikotsu
70003275.description: A cape located in the northern parts of Japan. Named after the land 'Utoro', there's a fort named Utorochashi. According to the local language, 'chashi' refers to a fort or meeting place, as such, the ruins of such a place is called 'chashikotsu'. Although it was first used as a sanctuary or meeting place, it later had functions to act as a fort.

70003276.name: Cape Hafun
70003276.description: A cape located in the easternmost parts of Africa. It has thrived as a trading post since ancient times, and there are mentions of this place within the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.' It is said that there are ancient ruins located there where artifacts can be found.

70003277.name: Porto Seguro
70003277.description: A region in which Cabral, a knight of the Order of Christ had landed in. Cabral had succeeded Gama in leading an expedition to India and is the first Portuguese person to step foot into South America. Regardless of it having the name of 'Safe Port', it is a lively Port City with many great coasts.

70003278.name: Antinous
70003278.description: Mourning the death of his aide, Antinous, the Roman emperor, Hadrian, had established a constellation using a star on the south side of Aquila. There are records of this in the 'Almagest'. As it is neighbouring Aquila, it is often confused with Ganymede from Greek mythology.

70003279.name: Rebirth of the Phoenix
70003279.description: Based on its appearance and characteristics, the phoenix is also known as the undying bird or firebird. As it has the characteristics of 'resurrection' similar to Jesus Christ, it is a highly recognized symbolic creature. As such, it is widely known among folklore creatures.

70003280.name: Rainbow Serpent
70003280.description: Just as the sun is sometimes viewed of as a god, the rainbow is also regarded as a symbol of great existence. The Rainbow Serpent, having said to have the characteristics of a creator, it said to stand out among the dragons and other serpents that are often spoken of.

70003281.name: Kesaran Pasaran
70003281.description: A mysterious creature; whether it's an animal or a plant is unknown; its habitat is unknown; the origin of its name is unknown. Only thing that is told is its furball appearance and the rumour that happiness will be brought unto its owner.

70003282.name: Tooth Fairy
70003282.description: A fairy that is said to exchange baby teeth that are placed under a pillow with money. Although there many folklores regarding baby teeth that have been pulled, the tales regarding this fairy originates mainly from Europe.

70003283.name: Thunderbird
70003283.description: A large bird which manipulates thunder. It is widely worshipped in North America as a spirit that is capable of causing lightning to strike at will. Lore regarding this creature varies from land to land such as it being able to understand the human language, or it being capable of eating whales whole.

70003284.name: Umibozu
70003284.description: A creature said to appear on the night seas and destroy ships. Mainly described as a giant with a dark figure. According to folklores, it is described as being various sizes and forms, and even conducts various actions. It is said that when it appears, the weather becomes unstable and unusual accidents such as ships suddenly sinking occur.

quests.name: Folklore Regarding a Giant that Dwells in the Sea

70003285.name: Melissa Figurehead
70003285.description: The figurehead of a sunken ship owned by royalty from Portugal, made by Jose's father with repentance and prayer. 'Please punish me for building this ship. Please save those who board this ship. Please allow my daughter to find happiness. Please protect them... My dear wife, Melissa' is carved on it.

70003286.name: Pamukkale
70003286.description: The ancient Greco-Roman city of Hierapolis. It is well known for its many hot springs in the area since the era of the Kingdom of Pergamon as well as a number of cemeteries as well. There is a hole known as the 'Gate to Hell' near the Temple of Apollo.

70003287.name: Mutitjulu Waterhole
70003287.description: It is said that due to the rainwater that comes from the rocks, it never runs dry. There is a legend believed by the local residents that the ancestor of a Python named Kuniya turned into a rainbow-colored snake and still dwells in the hole.

70003288.name: Kata Tjuta
70003288.description: Large rock formations considered sacred to the local people along with Uluru. It means 'many heads' in the local language. Various rituals seem to be performed at night in the area, including penalizing criminals.

maps.name: Map of Indigenous People's Holy Grounds

70003289.name: Gobekli Tepe
70003289.description: Remains called 'Potbelly Hill' in the local language. A number of giant stone pillars are arranged in circles. Some of them have the sculpture of animals. They seem to have been made quite a long time ago, but it is unknown who made them and what they were made for.

70003290.name: Monastery of Lindisfarne
70003290.description: The ruins of a historical monastery founded around the same time when Christianity was first introduced to the British Isles. It's known for its illuminated manuscript of the gospel. The place had become ruins after the invasions of Vikings and England.

70003291.name: Erinna's Poem
70003291.description: A copy of the poems of Erinna, an ancient Greek poet, referred to as the 'goddess of poems.' It is said that she's either a friend or student of Sappho but not confirmed. She was best known for her long poem, the Distaff, a three-hundred line hexameter lament for her childhood friend, Baucis.

70003292.name: Oxyrhynchus Papyri
70003292.description: One of the papyrus manuscripts discovered near Oxyrhynchus in Egypt. Although they consist mainly of public documents and court records, they also contain the writings of ancient Greek philosophers and poets such as Plato, literature relating to the faith of the time and music score of chants.

70003293.name: Aramaic Letter
70003293.description: During the fifth century BC, a papyrus of a letter that seemed to be written by a Jew who lived in Elephantine in the southern parts of Egypt. Egypt of that time was under the rule of the Persian kingdom, and there were a number of residential areas for Jewish mercenaries there as well.

70003294.name: Pilgrimage to the Holy Lands
70003294.description: A record of pilgrimages to the holy lands, written by Egeria, a woman from the southern part of the Iberian Peninsula in the 4th century, then dominated by the Roman Empire. It's written about the events that had taken place during her pilgrimages to Jerusalem and the Sinai Peninsula.

70003295.name: Legenda Aurea
70003295.description: Biographies of saints, written by Blessed Jacobus de Varagine, who was an archbishop of Genoa in the 13th century. It is also called the 'Golden Legend'. Descriptions about major holidays can be seen as well. It was printed in more editions than the Bible.

70003296.name: Saint George's Icon
70003296.description: An icon depicting Saint George who is well known for his tradition of slaying a dragon. In Eastern Europe, it is said that the number of livestock that wolves can catch is determined every year. Therefore, Saint George is occasionally referred to as the guardian of sheep and wolf.

70003297.name: Thesis of Double Faith
70003297.description: A record written about 'Double Faith' in Russia under anonymity. The author is allegedly a Russian cleric. It contains quite interesting contents such as how Vladimir I converted pagan temple ruins to churches and adopted pagan customs to the churches.

70003298.name: Animal Mummy in Coffin
70003298.description: An animal mummy made around the temple in Egypt during the late dynasty. Originally, it was performed by the nobles hoping their pet animals and livestock would resurrect in paradise after death, but in this era it became a mere facade and was often treated as just a charm for luck.

70003299.name: Manuscript of Ulster Stories
70003299.description: Also known as the 'Ulster Cycle,' it's one of the four great cycles of Irish mythology. It contains many stories about kings and knights from Ulster. Most of them are considered to have taken place during the same era of which Jesus Christ lived in.

70003300.name: Another Version of Ulster Stories
70003300.description: It is written about one of the legends of Cu Chulainn, a hero who appears in the Ulster Stories. The contents of the stories reflect Christian doctrines strongly, which is clearly different from the depiction in other Ulster Stories.

70003301.name: Berimbau
70003301.description: A single-string percussion instrument originally from Africa. It consists of a bow and a string. A gourd, dried, opened and hollowed-out, attached to the lower portion of the bow by a loop of a tough string, acting as a resonator.

70003302.name: Mistletoe
70003302.description: A hemiparasite on several species of trees. It has always been surrounded by a number of myths and legends in Europe. In the ancient Celt, it was considered sacred especially when growing on oak trees.

70003303.name: The Major Oak
70003303.description: A large English oak tree in the midst of Sherwood Forest on the outskirts of Nottingham. It's said that it has been rooted in the forest for hundreds of years and it was Robin Hood's shelter where he and his merry men slept.

70003304.name: Bermuda Petrel
70003304.description: A bird inhabiting the Bermuda waters, the top of the body is gray brown and the underside of the body is white. It's apparently feared by seafarers because of its eerie cries and the fact that its habitat is called 'the seas of devil.'

70003305.name: Raven
70003305.description: It differs from the crows by having a greater body size. There are several references to ravens in the Old Testament of the Bible and Norse mythology. A group of ravens is kept at the Tower of London to protect the Crown and the tower. A superstition holds that 'if the Tower of London ravens are lost or fly away, the Crown will fall and Britain with it.'

70003306.name: Muskrat
70003306.description: A medium-sized semiaquatic rodent native to North America. It inhabits wetlands. In several Native American creation myths, the muskrat dives to the bottom of the primordial sea to bring up the mud from which the earth is created.

70003307.name: Egyptian Cobra
70003307.description: One of the largest cobra species native to Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. It's not only feared as a dangerous venomous snake, but also it has been revered as a guardian of farming as it preys on mice since ancient times.

70003308.name: Flying Fish
70003308.description: It can make powerful, self-propelled leaps out of water where their long wing-like fins enable gliding for considerable distances above the water's surface. This ability is considered as a natural defense mechanism to evade predators.

70003309.name: Pilot Fish
70003309.description: A large-sized fish widely distributed and lives in warm or tropical open seas. It features a characteristic vertical striped pattern. In ancient Greece, it was called 'Pompilos' and its fondness for ships led the seafarers to believe that it would navigate a ship to its desired course.

70003310.name: Invisible City
70003310.description: An invisible city widely known all over the world, that is believed to exist somewhere in the world. Legends suggest that it got lost after being involved in battle or it was sunk to the bottom of the sea by the power of God. However, no one has actually seen it or returned after visiting it.

70003311.name: Burning Bush
70003311.description: In the biblical narrative, the Burning Bush is the location at which Moses was appointed by God to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and into Canaan. Flame is often considered as a boundary that God creates.

70003312.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
70003312.description: Also called the Pharos of Alexandria , it's a lighthouse built by the Ptolemaic Kingdom in Alexandria, during the reign Ptolemy II Philadelphus. It was as high as the Great Pyramid of Giza but was destroyed after being badly damaged by three earthquakes.

70003313.name: Madara Rider
70003313.description: An early medieval large rock relief carved on the Madara Plateau east of Shumen in northeastern Bulgaria. It is thought that the relief was created during the rule or immediately after the Bulgars settled in the 7th century.

70003314.name: Gommateshwara Statue
70003314.description: A 57-foot high monolithic statue located on Vindyagiri at Shravanbelagola in the Indian state of Karnataka. The statue depicts Gommateshwara's prolonged meditation of Bahubali.

70003315.name: Wallace Sword
70003315.description: A two-handed large sword used by William Wallace, a Scottish knight who became one of the main leaders during the First War of Scottish Independence against England.As the length of the sword is longer than the height of an adult, he may have been quite tall.

70003316.name: Kalibangan Seal
70003316.description: A cylinder seal found further past Mohenjo-Daro, near Karlibangan. It closely resembles the one found at the Indus ruins. Cows are engraved on it, which suggests that they were highly valued within the area.

maps.name: Map of an Ancient Indian Relic

70003317.name: The Seven Sights of the World
70003317.description: The work of ancient Greek mathematician, Philon, introducing seven must-see structures that existed at that time in the Mediterranean area. Although 'The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World' is said to be based on this, the Lighthouse located in Alexandria, where he lived at the time of writing, is not included.

70003318.name: Carta Marina
70003318.description: The first map of the Nordic countries to give details and place names, created by Swedish ecclesiastic Olaus Magnus in the 16th century. Some rare animals and monsters are also drawn on it as well. It seems that it was created based on books of all ages and countries and stories randomly heard from seafarers.

70003319.name: A Description of the Northern Peoples
70003319.description: A monumental work by Olaus Magnus, a Swedish Catholic ecclesiastic, on the Nordic countries. It contains a large amount of information about living, nature and lore in northern Europe. It consists of 22 books and is illustrated with 481 woodcuts.

70003320.name: Pizzigano Map
70003320.description: A portolan chart created by a 15th-century Venetian cartographer, Zuane Pizzigano. Mysterious islands are drawn on the outer sea west of Europe and they are clearly indicated by red and black paints as if they are newly discovered islands.

70003321.name: Whale Bones
70003321.description: Whale bones washed up on a beach. The carcasses of whales or big fish are usually decomposed by various living creatures in the sea, but rotten carcasses or skeletons are occasionally washed up by the sea during that process.

70003322.name: Giant Bird Bones
70003322.description: The bones of a very large bird, found in a jungle. Even when its wings are closed, its body is larger than a human. Because it has robust and big feet, it may have been preying on big fish or animals.

70003323.name: Amazonian Giant Centipede
70003323.description: One of the largest centipedes with a length up to 30 centimeters, found in various places in South America and the Caribbean. It preys on not only insects and small snakes, but also bats by catching them in the air while hanging from the ceiling of the cave.

70003324.name: Pygmy Hog
70003324.description: A wild boar inhabiting humid grasslands in the areas from the northeastern part of India to the southern part of the Himalayas, which is the smallest of its kind as the name suggests. The whole body is covered with brown or dark brown hair. It's constantly exposed to a number of predators because of its small body size.

70003325.name: Fishing Cat
70003325.description: A medium-sized wild cat inhabiting the vicinity of wetlands along rivers and swamps in South and Southeast Asia. It normally catches fish near water but can swim long distances as well, even under water for hunting. Its full adult size is as large as that of a tiger cub.

70003326.name: Barbary Lion
70003326.description: A lion inhabiting mainly the regions from the Atlas Mountains to Egypt, also known as the Atlas Lion. Its body size is larger than the regular lion and its manes are darker and longer extending over the shoulder. Because of this, it's been a target for trophy hunting and showing since ancient times.

70003327.name: Ghaggar-Hakra River
70003327.description: A river said to have flown parallel to the Indus river in ancient times but now flows only during the monsoon season. It's mentioned in 'Rigveda' as the Sarasvati River. In one theory, Hindu goddess Salasvati is said to be a deification of this river.

70003328.name: Red Rainbow
70003328.description: A rainbow that is red in color. After a misty rain, a bright and wide rainbow with thinner colors may be formed. When this happens at sunrise or sunset, its color turns red after the blue and green of its rays weaken.

70003329.name: Fire Devil
70003329.description: A fire tornado. It's created when a wildfires or firestorms creates its own wind, which can turn into a vortex of fire. Its fire whirls spread fear to its witnesses, but some people find it strangely beautiful.

70003330.name: Mars
70003330.description: A Swedish warship that was built in the 16the century. It caught fire and exploded during the First battle of Oland in the Baltic Sea.

70003331.name: The Encarnacion
70003331.description: A Spanish merchant ship built for the purpose of transporting supplies to the New World. It sank in a storm at the mouth of the Chagres River in Panama.

70003332.name: The Atocha
70003332.description: A Spanish treasure galleon. It sank in a hurricane off the Florida Keys when carrying back copper, silver, gold, tobacco and gems back to Spain.

70003333.name: Alhambra
70003333.description: A palace and fortress complex located in Granada, the old capital city of Spain. It was originally built in the 9th century by the Moors that dominated the area back then. After the Reconquista, it became Holy Roman Empire's Charles V's summer retreat and was altered for the purpose of removing Islamic design from the structure.

70003334.name: Fort of the Berlengas
70003334.description: A fort located on the island of Berlenga Grande, north of Lisbon. It's also known as the 'Fort of Sao Joao Baptista.' It was constructed from the remains of a pre-existing monastery, and was subject to repeated attacks from the Barbary pirates.

70003335.name: Kalibangan
70003335.description: An ancient site of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in Western India. It is said that the site was on the southern banks of the large river flowing in the area back then. Unlike Mohenjo-daro, the fort and houses were built of dried mud bricks.

70003336.name: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral
70003336.description: A Roman Catholic cathedral located in Galicia, Spain. It's known as the goal of the pilgrimage route called the Way of Saint James, stretching across France and the Iberian Peninsula. Legend has it that the remains of Saint James, son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus, is buried here.

70003337.name: Capela do Fundador
70003337.description: One of the chapels located within the premises of the Batalha Monastery. It is the first royal pantheon in Portugal. It enshrines John I of Portugal, Philippa of Lancaster, Prince Pedro, Henrique the Navigator, and Ferdinand the Holy Prince, who died as a prisoner in Fez.

70003338.name: Arkadi Monastery
70003338.description: A Venetian-style monastery built on the island of Crete in the 16th century. It is said that it was built by upgrading a pre-existing monastery there. It's highly respected by the local Christians as their spiritual pillar.

quests.name: It's Not Only Ruins That Talk
It's Not Only Ruins That Talk
It's Not Only Ruins That Talk

70003339.name: Mendana's Logbook
70003339.description: Records of voyage around South American and Oceania, kept by a 16th-century Spanish navigator, Alvaro de Mendana de Neira. His navigation in search for treasure ended in vain during his first voyage. However, he discovered the Solomon Islands.

70003340.name: The Natural History
70003340.description: Written by a Roman politician and a naturalist, Pliny the Elder, it consists of 37 books and contains topics ranging from the natural world to geography, astronomy, and history. It also includes descriptions of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World as well as monsters he had heard about in various regions.

70003341.name: Glagolitic Stone Tablet
70003341.description: A stone tablet whose inscription is written in the Glagolitic script, said to be the oldest alphabet in Eastern Europe. The Glagolitic script was created by Saint Cyril, a Byzantine monk, and his brother, Saint Methodius, based on Greek writing. It is said that it had become the prototype of the Cyrillic alphabet.

70003342.name: Currach
70003342.description: A type of ancient Irish boat that uses animal hides cured with oak bark for the outer layer. It's mentioned in the books written by Julius Caesar and Pliny the Elder. One theory is that the boat Saint Brendan of Clonfert used for his voyage was of the same type.

quests.name: A Boat That Traveled Across the Story
A Boat That Traveled Across the Story

70003343.name: Surya Mask
70003343.description: A mask of Surya, the Sun Deity in Hindu mythology. It's apparently common in India to decorate houses and temples with the masks of their deities, made with metal or stone. Its facial expression represents how the local people interpret the light and the heat of the sun.

70003344.name: Chandra Mask
70003344.description: A mask of Chandra, the Lunar Deity in Hindu mythology. Its face represents the color of moonlight as well as the characteristics of the moon, that are described in mythology. It seems masks are used for plays and are displayed at homes and temples as well.

70003345.name: Avvakum's Letter
70003345.description: One of the letters sent by Avvakum, a Russian Old Believers leader, to his followers. He was imprisoned for a total of 15 years for his opposition to the reforms of the Russian Orthodox Church, led by the tsar Alexis of Russia. It includes his autobiography written in spoken languages.

70003346.name: The Voyage of Saint Brendan the Abbot
70003346.description: A book written about the famous voyage of 7 years for Paradise, made by Saint Brendan of Clonfert, one of the early Irish monastic saints. It was widely read throughout Europe for hundreds of years.

70003347.name: Book about the Master of the Wolves
70003347.description: A book with compiled lore regarding Saint George, widely spread throughout Russia and Eastern Europe. It contains the story about Saint George as the 'Shepherd of the Wolves' and his 30 wolves. It shows the process of how the local old beliefs united with the Christian lore.

70003348.name: Azores Bullfinch
70003348.description: A bird inhabiting the eastern part of Sao Miguel Island, in the Azores archipelago, locally called 'Priolo.' It mainly inhabits the forest areas of the island. However, its population is decreasing due to the destruction of its habitat.

70003349.name: Steller's Jay
70003349.description: A bird native to western North America, particularly seen more often in the forested areas. Being omnivorous, it eats fruits and insects as well as other birds' eggs. It has a pronounced black crest, however, its lower body is bright blue. Its vocalizations are quite loud.

70003350.name: Kereru
70003350.description: A type of pigeon inhabiting Aotearoa, also known as the wood pigeon. In local mythology, Maui, a half human and half deity hero, is said to have turned himself into a Kereru. It has relatively larger body size and is able to eat the largest native fruit at a mouthful.

quests.name: Further Research into the Queen of Andes

70003351.name: Brown Greater Galago
70003351.description: A nocturnal primate mainly inhabiting the forest areas in Southern Africa, also known as the thick-tailed galago. During the day, it rests at the top of the trees or in the hollow of a tree. Its diet consists of fruit, seeds, flowers, insects and even small birds.

70003352.name: Asian Golden Cat
70003352.description: A medium-sized wild cat native to the northeastern Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. In China, it's thought to be a kind of leopard. Its fur is much-prized and its bones are believed to have medicinal effects.

70003353.name: Indian Rhinoceros
70003353.description: A rhinoceros native to the Indian subcontinent. It has one horn and a hard skin that resembles armour. It's often hunted relentlessly because it's believed that its horns have medicinal effects. It's not uncommon for hunters to be attacked and killed by these rhinoceroses.

70003354.name: Fiordland Penguin
70003354.description: A crested penguin species mainly inhabiting the south-western corner of the South Island of Aotearoa, locally known as Tawaki. It has a prominent bright yellow crest on its head.

70003355.name: Terceira Island
70003355.description: An island in the Azores archipelago. It was called 'the island of Brasil' when it was first discovered. It's drawn on the Pizzigano Map as well. There is a town called Angra do Heroismo meaning 'Port of Hero' and a number of fortresses were built in case of a pirate attacks.

70003356.name: Solomon Islands
70003356.description: An archipelago in the western South Pacific Ocean. The first European to visit the islands was the 16th-century Spanish navigator Alvaro de Mendana de Neira. It was named after the wealthy biblical King Solomon by Mendana.

70003357.name: Mount Gorongosa
