70003357.description: A mountain, west of Sofala, believed to be a dwelling place for God by local residents. It's surrounded by pristine wilderness where a number of undiscovered animals and plants are considered to inhabit.

70003358.name: Greek Anthology
70003358.description: A collection of poems, compiled by a 10th century Byzantine scholar, Constantine Cephalas. It contains roughly 4,500 epigrams and songs made by more than 300 poets from the 7th century B.C. to the 10th century. It's been highly valued as an excellent poem collection for a long time.

70003359.name: Yukihime
70003359.description: Personified snow that is believed to appear on a snowy mountain during the night in the form of a young maiden. The story goes that it eats hikers who get lost on the mountain or freezes them to death. However, there are some other versions with Yukihime getting married to a human man, giving a birth to a baby, and living happily ever after all together.

70003360.name: Ryujin
70003360.description: A legendary creature found in traditional Japanese and Chinese folklore. It is said to live in remote mountains or deep lakes, and can freely control water and rain. Especially in Japan, there are several stories of Ryujin transforming into a white snake to interact with humans.

70003361.name: The Colossus of Rhodes
70003361.description: A statue of the Greek sun-god Helios in the city of Rhodes. It is said that it fell apart when it was hit by an earthquake decades after the construction. Its size was enormous so very few people could wrap their arms around its thumb and each of its fingers was larger than any other statues ever made.

70003362.name: Ruins of Shu
70003362.description: Ruins of an ancient state in China, Shu. It's unknown when it was established but it had been flourishing until the 4th century B.C. They are located in the upstream area of the Yangtze River. It is said that a number of precious relics are yet to be unearthed there aside from the 'Masque with Protruding Eyes.'

70003363.name: Huaca Pucllana
70003363.description: Ancient ruins in central Lima with a pyramid made with sun-dried bricks. It was once a city that dominated the whole surrounding area and it served as an important ceremonial and administrative center.

70003364.name: Alii's Sash
70003364.description: A waistcloth worn by Hawaiian rulers as a symbol of authority. It's decorated with red and yellow feathers which are believed to possess the forces of nature.

70003365.name: Crape Myrtle
70003365.description: A shrub native to East Asia also known as 'Hundred Days Red.' Its flowering period is quite long and its bark is a prominent feature known for being smooth, pinkish-gray and mottled, shedding each year.

70003366.name: Chinese Saluki
70003366.description: A Chinese dog breed. Characterized by its slim body. It appears on ancient art and murals as a hunting hound.

maps.name: Map of a Slim Hunting Dog

70003367.name: Mount Maunganui
70003367.description: An extinct volcano located on the North Island of New Zealand. It is considered very important and sacred by the local Maori.

70003368.name: Halema'uma'u Crater
70003368.description: A pit crater located within the much larger summit caldera of Kilauea in Hawaii. It is believed to be home to Pele, goddess of fire and volcanoes, according to the Hawaiian traditions.

70003369.name: Cabo de los Amantes
70003369.description: A cape located on the northern coast of Guam. Legend has it that two lovers threw themselves over the cliff to death after realizing that their love was unacceptable because of their difference in social status.

quests.name: Flowering Tree of a Tragic Love

70003370.name: Badlands
70003370.description: A vast wilderness area located in central North America. Its unique-looking terrain is made with sharply eroded buttes and pinnacles.

70003371.name: Piopiotahi
70003371.description: A fiord located on the Tasman Sea side of New Zealand's South Island. It is surrounded by sheer rock faces that rise 1,000 meters or more. Known as the wettest place in New Zealand, rainfalls create dozens of temporary waterfalls.

70003372.name: The Coins of the Lighthouse of Alexandria
70003372.description: Coins manufactured in ancient Alexandria with the inscriptions of various elaborated designs such as Isis, the guardian goddess of journeys across the seas, along with the Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the World's Seven Wonders.

70003373.name: Heptastadion
70003373.description: A 1 kilometer long giant causeway that linked Pharos Island the Lighthouse of Alexandria was constructed on and the mainland coast. Its name is based on its length, 'hepta' meaning seven and 'stadion' a Greek unit of length measuring approximately 180 meters.

70003374.name: The Inscription of Sostratus
70003374.description: Sostratus of Cnidus, who was involved in the construction of the Lighthouse of Alexandria, secretly placed an inscription with his name on it within the foundation stone of the Lighthouse of Alexandria and covered it with mortar and engraved the then ruler's name, Ptolemy I Soter, on it. Sostratus of Cnidus apparently did this in order to earn his name in history.

70003375.name: The Triton Statues of the Lighthouse of Alexandria
70003375.description: The statues of Triton placed at the four corners of the 130-meters tall Lighthouse of Alexandria, which is also said to have the statue of Poseidon on its top. The Lighthouse of Alexandria was apparently blessed by various deities that represent the sea.

quests.name: Statues of the Lighthouse of Alexandria

70003376.name: Sun God Sculpture
70003376.description: The sculpture of the sun-god Helios used as a model for the Colossus of Rhodes. In ancient Greek, it was believed that the sun rises in the morning and sets in the evening because Helios would drive the chariot of the sun from the East to the West across the sky each day.

70003377.name: Helepolis
70003377.description: A large siege tower, 40 meters tall and 20 meters wide, sent by Demetrius I of Macedon during the Siege of Rhodes in an attempt to capture Rhodes. It is believed to have consisted of multiple floors which were equipped with various armaments.

70003378.name: Ancient Armaments of the Siege
70003378.description: Due to the arrival of enemy reinforcements during the Siege of Rhodes, it is said that the Demetrios' armies were forced to withdraw quickly, leaving behind many armaments, some of which were melted down and used as building materials for the Colossus.

70003379.name: The Coins of the Sun God
70003379.description: Coins manufactured on ancient Rhodes. It is said that many coins were engraved with Helios, the sun god who was greatly worshipped then, along with roses, the symbol of the island.

quests.name: The Coins of the Sun God
quests.location: Office of the leader of the knights

70003380.name: Gold Llama
70003380.description: A gold statue of llama. Its eyes, nose and ears are elaborately made. In the Inca Empire rituals, it seems that llamas were occasionally used as sacrifices.

70003381.name: The Letter of Indios
70003381.description: A letter written by native people in North America. It records the history of the Andean civilization and the Inca Empire as well as colonial policies and thoughts along with many illustrations.

maps.name: Map of an Incan History Book

70003382.name: The Statue of Moenjo-Daro
70003382.description: A stone statue discovered in South Asia. It is said that it is modeled after a person from the upper class. The clothes worn by the statue have an elaborate pattern on them, which seems to be a result of the influence of Western culture.

70003383.name: Golden Oriole
70003383.description: A migrant bird that switches its habitat seasonally. It can be found widely in Europe, Africa and West Asia. The colors of its body and wings are different. Especially males, they have a beautiful contrast between the yellow body and black wings.

70003384.name: Indian Flying Fox
70003384.description: A large bat that uses fruit juice as its staple food. Its eyes are fairly large as it relies on vision when flying. The face seen from the side resembles that of a fox, hence the name.

quests.name: Search for a Large, Kind Bat

70003385.name: Luan
70003385.description: A mythological bird that appears in Chinese legends. It is believed to appear when society is more stabilized. It is also said that it sings in the five standard pitches and its blood could be used as an adhesive for attaching strings to musical instruments. However…

70003386.name: Seaberry
70003386.description: A plant widely found in the Eurasian continent. The fruits are nutritious but they are sour and difficult to eat as is. There are many thorns on the trunk and branches, making it difficult to harvest fruits. The fruit has a bright orange color and is sometimes cultivated for ornamental purposes.

70003387.name: Emei Moustache Toad
70003387.description: A frog that inhabits the mountains of East Asia. There are thorn-shaped spines around the mouth of the male, and it seems that the superiority of males is determined by comparing their sizes.

70003388.name: Mount Damavand
70003388.description: The tallest volcano in Asia. Since it is a volcano with a beautiful peak, it appears in the scriptures of Zoroastrian that admires fire. It is believed that the three-headed dragon, Azi Dahaka, has been imprisoned deep underground below the mountain.

70003389.name: The Siglos Sliver Coins
70003389.description: Silver coins issued in Achaemenid Persia. The head of the coin is engraved with the figure of a king who hunts with a bow and a spear, representing the authority of the king.

quests.name: First Silver Coin with Someone Inscribed

70003390.name: Allahverdi Khan Bridge
70003390.description: A 300-meters long bridge built in the Middle East, popularly known as Si-o-se-pol. It has 33 arches and is built in the style of Safavid, one of the Islamic architectural styles.

70003391.name: Hairy Bush Viper
70003391.description: A snake that inhabits Central Africa. It is capable of climbing even reeds and stalks because of its heavily keeled dorsal scales covering the entire body. It hunts for prey using two kinds of venoms, neurotoxin that stops prey's movement and the hemorrhagic toxin that promotes massive bleeding.

70003392.name: Mokele-mbembe
70003392.description: A giant creature or spirit believed to inhabit the Central African rainforest. While having a long neck and tail, its four legs are short. It is said to appear often around the water.

quests.name: Folklore Regarding a Giant Creature in Africa

70003393.name: Glasswing Butterfly
70003393.description: A butterfly that inhabits in Central and South America with transparent wings like glass. Contrary to its beautiful appearance, it is capable of carrying something 40 times heavier that its own weight. It feeds on toxic plants as a caterpillar and stores the toxins inside its body tissues. Males use these toxins as a pheromone.

70003394.name: Puya Raimondii
70003394.description: A large plant found in the alpine zone of the Andes. After about a hundred years, it blooms a huge flower once and then it withers. Its large and long leaves have many hard and sharp spines. Also known as 'Queen of Andes.'

70003395.name: Juan Fernandez Islands
70003395.description: An island group in the South Pacific Ocean off the coast of Southern South America. It consists of three main islands. The topography of the islands is rugged. With rich nature, it's home to many plants and animals.

70003396.name: Commerson's Dolphin
70003396.description: A dolphin that inhabits seas in South America and the Indian Ocean. Since it has sharply-delineated black-and-white patterning, it's also called a Panda Dolphin. Males have a black tear-drop shape on the belly while females have a more rounded one.

70003397.name: Chinchorro Mummies
70003397.description: Mummies from the South American Chinchorro culture. They are considered older than the Egyptian mummies. It is often the case that children and babies received the most elaborate mummification treatments. In the Chinchorro culture, they performed mummification on not only those who had power but also all members of their society.

70003398.name: Skunk
70003398.description: An animal that inhabits widely from North America to South America. Characterized by its white and black fur. When it senses danger, it takes a warning posture and, as a last resort, it sprays a liquid with a strong, unpleasant smell, its anal scent glands. The range is about 5 meters. Since the scent is less effective for raptors that are insensitive to odors, skunks are often preyed on by them.

quests.name: Further Research on the Sugar Maple

70003399.name: The Diquis Spheres
70003399.description: Stone spheres found in dense forests in Central America. The size varies, with the largest being over 2 meters in diameter. The purpose and method of production are unknown.

maps.name: Map of Stone Spheres in Jungle

70003400.name: Blue Argus
70003400.description: A beautiful butterfly that inhabits temperate areas such as Southeast Asia. Characterized by the two large pairs of eye patterns on its forewings and hindwings. The male wings are blue while the female wings are brown with bigger eyeball patterns than the males'.

quests.name: The Whereabouts of a Blue Butterfly

70003401.name: African Giant Snail
70003401.description: One of the largest snail species inhabiting East Africa. It eats a wide range of things including even sand and stones as well as plants. It's edible if cooked. However, if you touch it or even its trace directly, you may be infected by parasites harbored by it.

70003402.name: Twelve-wired Bird-of-paradise
70003402.description: A bird that inhabits Southeast Asia. Only males have twelve fine wire-like tail feathers from their tails. During the breeding season, courtship is carried out by grazing the tail feathers on the face of females.

quests.name: Bird with Fur Growing from Its Behind
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70003403.name: Giant Oarfish
70003403.description: A deep-sea fish found in the Pacific Ocean, the Indian Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean. From the front, you can see that it's very narrow laterally. It has a mysterious silver body and red fins, but when it dies, it loses its colors. It looks for prey using its pelvic fins. There is a record it was used for food, which is said to be delicious.

70003404.name: Elephanta Cave Temples
70003404.description: A temple on Elephanta Island located in the northwestern part of the Indian Ocean. It's rock-cut architecture, predominantly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. Most of the stone statues are heavily damaged as the site was used as a firing range and for target practice in the 17th century.

70003405.name: Higai-style Toiletry Case
70003405.description: A small box made in Japan. The lid is made larger than the body of the box, so the lid fits over it. The surface of the box is processed with lacquer and detailed patterns are drawn. It is sometimes used as a box for scriptures.

70003406.name: Azuchi Gumo
70003406.description: A type of a crab spider that inhabits Asia widely. Characterized by its narrow eyes. The female body is white and has a mottled pattern, and its color changes according to the surrounding environment. It's about three times larger than males. The male body is brown and does not resemble the female.

70003407.name: Japanese Red Armour
70003407.description: Japanese armor that is uniformly red in color. As it's eye-catching even in a battlefield, it helps the wearer attract the attention of its enemies and distinguish friends from foes. In particular, it is said to have been worn by elite generals and units.

70003408.name: Stone Monuments of the Dancers
70003408.description: Stone monuments found in South America, engraved with pictures of people who seem to be dancing. However, the current mainstream theory is that they represent tortured, sacrificed war prisoners.

70003409.name: Monte Alban
70003409.description: The center of the Zapotec civilization that flourished in southern North America. The site is located on a low mountainous range rising above the plain and includes an astronomical observatory and a ballpark. Although it has developed greatly, it is said to have declined as the population declined.

maps.name: Map of Ruins on a Mountaintop

70003410.name: Gate of Xerxes
70003410.description: A large gate located in Persepolis the Middle East ruins. Each side of the gate had the statues of Lamassu, a human, bird, and lion hybrid deity. Constructed by Xerxes I, it is said that large-scale construction projects including this Gate affected the financial stability and even le to the decline of the nation's power.

70003411.name: Jebel Barkal
70003411.description: A small sandstone mountain in northeast Africa. It means 'sacred mountain' in Arabic. The ruins at the feet of the mountain was Napata, the capital city of the Egyptian 25th Dynasty. As such, there are many temples and shrines with Egyptian influence.

70003412.name: Mahabodhi Temple
70003412.description: A large temple in northeast region of India. It's said to be the place where Buddha achieved enlightenment after his long meditation. The 52 meter tower is constructed with 9 layers of brickwork, and has a stupa at the very top of the structure.

70003413.name: Ggantija
70003413.description: A megalithic shrine on a Mediterranean island. According to folktales, it was built by giants. There is evidence that there were roofs and doors and it appears that animal sacrifices were done on the alter.

maps.name: Map of a Large Ancient Temple

70003414.name: Book of Distillation
70003414.description: A book about distillation. Introduced from Europe and translated in German, the distillation technique became widely known. It had records about extracting refined oil from plants, its effects and preservation methods. Refined oil made from distillation was likely used as treatment against the plague.

70003415.name: Nuremberg Chronicle
70003415.description: A book that was published in the southeast German city of Nuremberg. It was widely published using metal typographic printing method. In this book it explains world history in seven sections alongside many illustrations.

70003416.name: Astilbe
70003416.description: A kind of flower that is mainly found in Asia. It is a perennial plant that first blooms in early summers. It grows fluffy spikes along the stem and the flowers range in red, pink, and white colors. Strong against the cold, it grows best in moist soil.

70003417.name: Darwin's Beetle
70003417.description: A large beetle that lives in South America, recognizable thanks to the male's large jaws. But because of its small head, the jaw cannot pinch hard, so it's instead used to toss over the opponent. Both males and females are generally aggressive.

70003418.name: Pencil Fish
70003418.description: A fresh water fish that is found in rivers in South America. It has a thin body and small mouth, and eats moss in the water. There are some kinds of pencil fish that swim along the surface of the water with its body at an angle like a pencil, hence its name.

70003419.name: Giant's Causeway
70003419.description: A coast located in northeast Ireland. Lava was cooled and created the many stone pillars here, many of the pillars being hexagonal. According to a folktale, it is said that this was made by giants on their way to a battle.

70003420.name: Downburst
70003420.description: A phenomenon that occurs when air that was cooled and heavy is suddenly shot out from the clouds. The blast of wind is powerful enough to cause significant damage. It occurs when the cold air stored inside cumulonimbus drops due to the weakening of the vertical air currents.

70003421.name: Rime Ice
70003421.description: A phenomenon where dense fog supercools and freezes onto surfaces of objects. They are often seen in the mountains during winter, and are called Hard Rime or Soft Rime depending on how it froze. It is white because it contains a lot of air in it, and breaks easily when touched.

70003422.name: Supercell
70003422.description: A giant Cumulonimbus cloud and the harsh storm that comes with it. Torrential rain, lightnings, and hailstorm occurs for an extended time. The horizontal rotation of the air makes the Cumulonimbus cloud to grow, and the division between the updraft and downdraft allows the storm to last for a long time.

70003423.name: Upside-Down Rainbow
70003423.description: A phenomenon where a colorful rainbow appears an upside-down arc. It is said to appear mostly right above the sun. The order of the colors is also reversed from regular rainbows, with the bottom color being red. This occurs due to ice crystals in the air bending the sunlight.

70003424.name: Dust Devil
70003424.description: A phenomenon in which a sudden gust of wind forms into a whirlwind shape. It occurs when warm air that is rising is impacted by strong horizontal winds. It is often found in open areas and raises dirt and dust. However, unlike a tornado it is not accompanied by a cloud.

70003425.name: Floating City
70003425.description: A city that floats in the sky and is recounted by regions around the world. The cityscape changes every time it's seen and sometimes city residents are seen. Witnesses say that for an illusion, the outline is much too clear.

quests.name: Folklore Regarding a City in the Sky

70003426.name: Hanging Temple
70003426.description: A wooden monastery built on the cliffs in southeast China. Notable for combining Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism, there are sculptures of each religion's founder next to each other. It's said that when the poet Li Bai visited this place, the wrote 'spectacular' on a stone.

maps.name: Map of a Temple on the Cliff

70003427.name: Map of Piri Reis
70003427.description: A world map created by the Ottoman navy admiral, Admiral Piri. It's said that he used many other maps as reference when making this map. Eventually the map was gifted to Selim I, the grandchild of Mehmed the Conqueror.

70003428.name: Charlemagne's Ring
70003428.description: A ring rumored to have enchanted Charlemagne. It's believed that it was originally worn by one of Charlemagne's lovers. There is a legend that should one wear the ring, a strange magic makes them charm people.

70003429.name: Bones of a Reptile with a Flat Head
70003429.description: Bones of a lizard-like creature found in eastern North America. It has a unique quality of having a flat skull. Sharp teeth can be found on it.

maps.name: Map of Bones of a Strange Lizard

70003430.name: Monstera Deliciosa
70003430.description: A perennial herb that is distributed around Central America, also known simply as 'Monstera'. Holes develop on the leaves according to its growth. These holes connect to create a large divide. Its fruits are edible but if eaten unripe they leave strong sensations in the mouth.

70003431.name: Chinese Mantis
70003431.description: A large praying mantis found in East Asia. It is aggressive and carnivorous, and sometimes cannibalistic. The females lay a foam-like egg case on the branches of plants. Nearly 200 larvae hatch from it, but it's said that only a handful can successfully survive into adulthood.

70003432.name: Guinea Pig
70003432.description: A rodent that is found in areas such as Central America. Although docile, they are always on high alert. If they too stressed, they may stop eating. They form a herd and communicate to each other through their calls. They jump in a unique way.

70003433.name: Gray Fox
70003433.description: A fox spread from North America to South America. It has a unique characteristic of a gray fur. They are known to be good at climbing trees. Because they are nocturnal, they spend their time during the day in their burrows.

70003434.name: White Cliffs of Dover
70003434.description: White cliffs that face the Strait of Dover, which are white because they are formed from limestones. It acts as the gates and stronghold of England. The alternative name of the island of Great Britain, Albion, is derived from Latin meaning white, and it's believed be inspired from these cliffs.

70003435.name: Ptolemy Cluster
70003435.description: Cluster of stars near Scorpius that are so bright that they can be seen with naked eyes. Because it was recorded by Claudius Ptolemy who classified 48 constellations, it is also known as the 'Ptolemy Cluster'.

70003436.name: Arcus Cloud
70003436.description: A natural phenomenon where a cloud forms an arch. It is formed in the sections where the cold air from cumulonimbus collides with the warm air. When an arcus cloud forms, it often follows with strong winds and thunderstorms.

70003437.name: Ground Blizzard
70003437.description: A phenomenon where fallen snow is lifted and blown by strong winds. The snow blown up to the sky can create poor visibility, even enough to hide the sun. If one is trapped in a ground blizzard, they may lose their sense of direction and get lost.

70003438.name: Peri's Robe
70003438.description: A robe said to be worn by the Persian spirit, Peri. It's said that when wearing this robe, they can turn into doves. There is a folktale that Peri was bathing in the human world when a human man stole her robe and forced her to become his wife.

70003439.name: The Golden Princess
70003439.description: A legend about how sericulture, the cultivation of silkworms, began. The Golden Princess was hated by her step-mother and was abandoned numerous times by her, until the princess was rescued by a couple. However the Golden Princess died from illness and turned into a silkworm, teaching the couple how to spin threads from the cocoon.

70003440.name: Nereid Monument
70003440.description: A marble commemorative structure built in Lycia. Between the ancient Greek style pillars, you can find elegant sculptures of Nereids, the daughters of the god of the seas. It's said that this style was inspired by the architectures in Halicarnassus.

70003441.name: Persian Sphinx
70003441.description: A statue of a sphinx from ancient Persia. Unlike the Egyptian version which has no wings, it's said that they have the face of a human, wings of an eagle, and the body of a lion. Could this statue have been in Halicarnassus too?

70003442.name: Tomb of Cyrus the Great
70003442.description: The ruins of the tomb of Cyrus the Great, who was the first king and founder of the Persian Achaemenid Empire. A house-like grave is built on top of the foundation which is made by stacking cut stones. Later a large architecture was built in imitation of this.

70003443.name: Ancient Coin with a Pegasus
70003443.description: A coin with a Pegasus on it which was apparently used in the Caria region. In the Persian Achaemenid Empire, each region was governed by a viceroy and as such each viceroys issued their own coins and currencies. Caria had independence in an effect, and was governed by Mausolus.

70003444.name: Amphitheater
70003444.description: An ancient Greek outdoor amphitheater that was carved out from the hill behind Halicarnassus. It's said that it was constructed around the time of King Mausolus. In the center of the front row seats is an altar of the Greek god Dionysus.

70003445.name: Gates of Myndus
70003445.description: Powerful gates that Mausolus, King of Caria, made for Halicarnassus. It even withstood attacks from Alexander the Great, making it a cornerstone of defense. However when it eventually collapsed, the city of Halicarnassus was destroyed by Alexander the Great's armies.

70003446.name: Stone Painted with Lime Mortar
70003446.description: A large square rock painted with caustic lime mortar. Caustic lime mortar has also been used in the Pyramids of Giza. It's believed to be used for the purpose of adjusting the surface and heights, but it's also believed that this technique allowed the pyramids to withstand without getting weathered down.

70003447.name: Imhotep's Blueprint
70003447.description: A papyrus paper with Ancient Egyptian writing and what looks like a drawing on it. It could be the blueprints for pyramids by Chancellor Imhotep who built the Step Pyramid for Pharaoh Djoser, which is said to be the first pyramid.

70003448.name: Al-Aziz's Plans
70003448.description: Documents of Al-Aziz, who was the sultan that controlled Egypt during the Ayyubid dynasty. It appears to have the method on how to destroy large stonework. Perhaps it's the plans to destroy pyramids in Egypt made by Al-Aziz.

70003449.name: Khufu's Coffin
70003449.description: A granite coffin that's placed inside Pharaoh Khufu's Great Pyramid of Giza. Because the size of the coffin would not have been able to go through the hallway at certain points, it's believed that the coffin was made during the construction. Since the moment it was discovered, it had no lid and it was empty inside. It's hard to believe it might have encountered a grave robbery before it was discovered...

70003450.name: Bent Pyramid
70003450.description: It's said that this pyramid belongs for Khufu's father, Pharaoh Sneferu. When you look from the side, you can see that the angle towards the peak is curved. There is a theory that a pyramid made at the same time collapsed immediately after completion which disrupted this pyramid's construction.

70003451.name: Papyrus from Pharaoh Khufu's Time
70003451.description: A document from Pharaoh Khufu's time which is considered to be the world's oldest papyrus. There is a piece of paper made by crushing and spreading out papyrus stems and it seems to have detailed writing on the construction of the pyramids and the laborers who moved the stones.

70003452.name: Arctic Fox in Summer
70003452.description: An arctic fox with its summer furs. During the winter they grow thick fur to withstand the harsh cold, but in the summer the fur regrows into gray or brown colors. They eat a variety of things such as small animals, birds, fish and seal carcass. They do not go into hibernation during winter despite the lack of foods.

quests.name: Further Research into the Group of Stone Structures

70003453.name: Plato's Original Handbook
70003453.description: The original copy of a philosophy manuscript written by the philosopher Plato. It is written in an interactive style, and is believed to be originally aimed for the students in the Academia. The contents not only discussed politics but also education in great detail.

70003454.name: Golden Burial Accessory of Vergina
70003454.description: A goldwork ornament believed to belong to Philip II of Macedon. It's very elaborately made and as such might have been worn during banquets. In the grave there are other equipment buried there made from bronze.

quests.name: Further Research into the Treasures of Vergina

70003455.name: Holy Sword's Scabbard
70003455.description: The magical scabbard that held the holy sword Excalibur. Legend has it that it heals the wound on the wielder and gives them immortality. It was stolen by King Arthur's sister, Morgana, and was thrown into a lake. After losing the scabbard, King Arthur was injured and lost his life from it.

70003456.name: The Door to the Underworld
70003456.description: A cave near the Temple of Apollo. It's said that the cave emits 'breath of the dead' which takes away life from those who enter, hence the name 'Door to the Underworld' and 'Door to Hell'. When you enter it, you will start to feel sick and dizzy.

quests.name: Further Research into City to the Underworld
Further Research into City to the Underworld

70003457.name: Heart of Uluru
70003457.description: A heart-shaped cavity on Uluru, which is called 'Heart of Uluru' due to the shape. It's located near the Mutitjulu Waterhole which never dries up. The locals cherish as a holy place.

70003458.name: Grouse in Summer
70003458.description: Grouse in summer feathers, which is tinged in brown. The feathers takes about one month to change. They don't fly much, relying on walking to move around. It seems they like to avoid the heat during warm days be hiding in trees, caves or inside snow.

70003459.name: Stoat in Winter
70003459.description: The pure white appearance that stoats take during winter. Old sayings say that they are a symbol of purity. Because of this, stoat's winter furs known as ermine was very popular among royalties and nobilities.

70003460.name: Seal Pup Fur
70003460.description: Seals inhabit many coastal areas around the world. Among them are those that live on sea ice. These seal pups are born with white fur, making them an endearing sight.

70003461.name: Sugar Maple in Autumn Colors
70003461.description: The appearance that sugar maples take in autumn when their leaves change color. They can grow more than 300 meters tall and grow in colonies. It's said that with their uniquely shaped leaves they create a sight to behold.

quests.name: Further Research on the Dangerous Creature

70003462.name: Statue of Minotaur
70003462.description: A statue of the half bull, half human monster from Greek mythology, Minotaur. Minotaur was a child born between a white bull and King Minos's wife. As he grew up, he became increasingly violent that nobody could control him, and so was trapped in the labyrinth by King Minos's order.

quests.name: Further Research on the Bull Monster

70003463.name: Azoth Sword
70003463.description: A sword said to belong to the alchemist Paracelsus. There is a strange substance on the pommel that looks nothing like a precious stone or rock, and there is the word 'Azoth' carved on the surface.

quests.name: Further Research on the Philosopher's Stone

70003464.name: Frozen Young Mammoth
70003464.description: A mammoth young that got frozen. Compared to the adult, it is much smaller and it seems that this one was frozen before it grew the characteristically long body hair or tusks. It's unknown for how long it's been frozen in this land.

quests.name: Further Research on the Mythological Gigantic Creature

70003465.name: Leaf Insect's Eggs
70003465.description: The eggs of a leaf insect, which look like a plant leaf, follows in its parent's footstep as it looks very similar to plant seeds. You would not notice that they were eggs if you didn't know. It probably evolved to appear this way in order to blend in with the environment to survive.

quests.name: Further Research on the Leaf Insect

70003466.name: Sahara's Oasis
70003466.description: Deep under the Sahara Desert there is a layer of clay that prevents water from passing. It is here that underground water is stored. When the water evaporates it creates salt, making the sand white. This is used as a landmark for the oasis.

quests.name: Further Research on the Great Desert

70003467.name: Ferocious Grizzly
70003467.description: A large bear that was used for show by heartless humans. It's said to look very ferocious, and it has escaped. It's only a matter of time before it comes back to the town to attack people.

70003468.name: Relief of Ravana the Demon King
70003468.description: A relief of Ravana, the demon king that appears from the Ramayana. It's said that he is the king of rakshasa and has 10 heads and 20 arms. The relief seems to depict the battle between Ravana and Prince Rama with the monkey god's army.

70003469.name: The Great Pyramid of Giza's Past
70003469.description: A giant pyramid that stands on the land of Giza that's said to be Pharaoh Khufu's grave. It was made by stacking up large numbers of square rocks. The surface is covered with large marble stones, making it shine. It's believed that during its construction worker camps appeared around the area where they were supplied with food and beer.

70003470.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus' Past
70003470.description: An elegant mausoleum built in Halicarnassus. King Mausolus and his wife Artemisia II of Caria, who became a ruler after his death, are buried here. It is a tall structure made of marble and each step had a sculpture. It's said that at the top there was a sculpture of a giant war chariot with four horses.

70003471.name: Jar of Xerxes I
70003471.description: A jar with the name Xerxes I, the King of Achaemenid Empire in Persia, engraved on it. It was found in the land where the ancient city Halicarnassus was. It doesn't look like something a commoner would have had, so it most likely belonged to someone who ruled this land.

quests.name: Legacy TH2. Treasure Sleeping in Ancient City

70003472.name: Relief of Pharaoh Khufu
70003472.description: A section of a relief that depicts an Ancient Egyptian king, Pharaoh Khufu. Hieroglyphs known as cartouche surrounds the pharaoh's name. On the same relief you can find a depiction of a sacrificial cow and the king drawing a bow.

70003473.name: Salamis Tablet
70003473.description: A calculator that was used in ancient Greece around 300 B.C. It is said to be the oldest surviving line of abacus'. A white marble plate about the size and thickness of a table was used, and pebbles and other beads were placed along the lines engraved on the surface to perform the calculations.

70003474.name: Inca Yupana
70003474.description: A calculation instrument that was used in the Inca Empire. Calculations were done by putting pebbles and grains in the dent and moving them according to the rules created for it. Records dictate that it surprised Europeans by performing complicated calculations quickly, but it seems that its detailed usage is a mystery.

70003475.name: Pope Abacus
70003475.description: A calculation instrument that was used in the Roman Empire. Calculates by moving the beads fitted in the grooves of a metal plate such as bronze. Long forgotten in the Western world, it was improved and reintroduced by Pope Sylvester II around the 10th and 11th centuries.

70003476.name: Abacus of General Guan
70003476.description: An ancient Chinese abacus. There is a legend that it was invented by Guan Yu, a famous military commander of the Three Kingdoms, but some records state its usage predates this period. The abacus with oval beads on rods was invented in later generations, and has 2 beads on the heaven (upper) and 5 beads on the ground (lower).

70003477.name: Black and Red Counting Rods
70003477.description: A device used to calculate pieces of wood side by side, which was used throughout East Asia before the spread of the abacus. In medieval Japan, two-colored counting rods were used, red for positive numbers and black for negative numbers. Calculations were made by arranging them on a cloth or board on which a grid was drawn.

70003478.name: Napier's Bones
70003478.description: A calculator invented by John Napier of Scotland in the early 17th century by a method known as rabdology. In addition to being able to easily perform multiplication by incorporating a multiplication table, it is also possible to apply multiplication and division between multiple digits, and calculation to find the square root.

70003479.name: Shickard's Automatic Calculator
70003479.description: Created by Wilhelm Schickard, a Hebrew professor at the University of Tubingen, Germany, in the first half of the 17th century, it was the world's first automatic computer. Also known as 'calculating clock.' It is said that it was supposed to be used for astronomical calculations because it can perform 6-digit addition and subtraction and complicated multiplication.

70003480.name: Galileo's Military Compass
70003480.description: A calculator invented by Galileo Galilei that can determine the amount of gunpowder for cannons and shells of any inner diameter. It is said that it could be used for various calculations, as a protractor, and for recording astronomical observations. Galileo, who was a professor at the University of Padua, was said to have earned money from this compass.

70003481.name: Virga
70003481.description: A type of cloud that occurs when rain, snow, hail, etc. evaporate while falling from a cloud. Under the clouds, thin streaks and a columnar haze appear to hang like a tail. Observed in a wide area.

70003482.name: Blue Jet
70003482.description: An especially blue luminescence phenomenon that occurs from a thunderstorm directed at the sky. Sometimes called upward lightning. There are few observation examples due to the short light emission time and the altitude of the generated position.

70003483.name: Aromatic Oil of Egypt's Queen
70003483.description: Kyphi, a prepared fragrance that was cherished in Ancient Egypt. It was made from frankincense, myrrh and variety of aromatic flowers. If the conical item on the head of the woman in the mural is kyphi, it can be hypothesized that it would melt to release its scent. However, the details are unknown.

70003484.name: Alembic
70003484.description: A distiller developed in Persia during the 8th century. It was utilized by chemists and alchemists from the Islamic world all the way to Europe. Essential oils were made by distilling the components of a fragrance, which was combined with distilled alcohol to make the prototype perfume.

70003485.name: Scent of a Consort
70003485.description: Edible aroma that was used in Ancient China. It's said that it was Yang Guifei's favorite, who was believed to be the most beautiful woman in the world that was compared to peony flowers. It's rumored that if you keep ingesting it, your body will begin to release a sweet smell.

70003486.name: Queen of Hungary's Water
70003486.description: Medicinal liquor made with rosemary from Medieval Europe. It was also used as a perfume due to its pleasant scent. There is a legend that an aged and ill queen of Hungary was healed and became young and beautiful upon ingesting it, and was courted by princes from other nations.

70003487.name: Sultan's Mother's Incense Burner
70003487.description: An incense burner with handles used from a long time ago in the Middle East. It's said to be an item that was intended to be offered to a holy temple by a mother of the Ottoman Empire Sultan. It is made of iron with splendid gold and silver inlay work.

70003488.name: Scented Gloves of a Princess
70003488.description: Lady's gloves made in the Grass region of France. Fragrances were soaked to cover the smell of leather and release sweet perfume instead. Essential oil from orange flowers were used which were favored by a princess of Nerola. It has been called neroli since then.

70003489.name: Incense Burner of 3-Legged Frog
70003489.description: An incense burner in the shape of a frog. In Japan, warriors participated in 'kodo,' the art of enjoying fragrances. It's said that it was owned by the samurai lord who nearly took control of the whole country. There is also a legend that the incense burner frog croaked on the night before the samurai lord was assassinated in a revolt.

70003490.name: Santa Maria Novella Church
70003490.description: A church in Florence. The 'Queen's Water' perfume, which was brought by a consort marrying in from Florence to France, was made by the monks of this church. One can say that the perfume culture in Europe all began from this.

quests.name: Legacy TH4. A Fragrance Envied Even by the Home of Aroma
Legacy TH4. A Fragrance Envied Even by the Home of Aroma
Legacy TH4. A Fragrance Envied Even by the Home of Aroma

70003491.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
70003491.description: A monastery built on top of an island floating in the Gulf of Saint-Malo. The tides change drastically in this area, and it's possible to walk to the island during low tides. It was also used as a stronghold during the Hundred Years' War between England and France. Due to its mystique, it is also been described as a 'Wonder of the West'.

70003492.name: Royal Game of Ur
70003492.description: A board game that was played by kings and nobilities in the Ancient City of Ur in Mesopotamia. According to one theory it is one of the oldest board games in the world. Its rules are similar to sugoroku or backgammon and is considered to have been the origin for those games.

70003493.name: Salar de Uyuni
70003493.description: A large salt flat formed when the Andes Mountains rose and trapped large amount of sea water. The area floods when it rains, turning it lake-like. The surface of that water reflects the sky, hence the name 'mirror of the heaves'.

70003494.name: Becket Water
70003494.description: Holy water that is said to have the blood of Thomas Becket, a saint of the English church, diluted with water. It's believed that the divine protection from the saint helps against all kinds of illnesses. Becket was close with Henry II, King of England, but engaged in a conflict with him over the independence of the church. Becket was murdered by the king's solider inside the church.

70003495.name: The Prince
70003495.description: A political philosophy book written by Florentine diplomat, Niccolo Machiavelli. It was written from a perspective of realism and excluded mortality and religion, arguing that rulers must be cruel. The book was banned as it was seen as a dangerous book of conspiracies, but became the origin for realism political philosophy.

70003496.name: Temple Stairs with Snake Head
70003496.description: At the bottom of the stairs in the Chichen Itza temple, there is a sculpture of Kukulkan, the supreme deity of Maya. It's said that the pyramid's shadow casts on the stairway during the spring and autumn equinox, resembling the winding body of Kukulkan.

70003497.name: Monte Alban's Observatory
70003497.description: Monte Alban is said to have been built on top of a hill by a community with defense capability due to its strategic position. At the ruins, there are different kinds of buildings, an observatory, and stone slabs with carvings of conquered regions' names.

70003498.name: Ancient Iridescent Glassware
70003498.description: An ancient glassware with a colorful appearance like a rainbow. Glass that has been under sand or dirt for a long period can develop a metallic shine due to a chemical reaction by orthosilicic acid and aluminium oxide with surrounding substances. This is known as iridescence or iridescent weathering.

70003499.name: Karna's Golden Armor
70003499.description: Armor worn by the hero, Karna, in the Indian epic poem 'Mahabharata'. It's said that Karna was born with an immortal body by wearing an armor and earrings through his biological mother's wish. However, he let go of his golden armor as planned by his archenemy Arjuna's father, Indra.

quests.name: Further Research into the Red Desert

70003500.name: Narashiba Katatsuki Teaware
70003500.description: A Japanese tea canister that is known as one of the Three Greatest Specialties in Japan. Based on its value, it's said to have been in the hands of famous people. It was damaged after a large fire in Edo and was repaired, but since disappeared.

70003501.name: Hamsa
70003501.description: An amulet to protect oneself from evil, in the shape of a hand with an eye in its center. 'Hamsa' means the number five in Arabic. There is a theory that the Turkish talisman, Nazar Boncugu, is a variation of this amulet.

quests.name: Further Research on Amulet to Ward Off Evil

70003502.name: Molted Chilean Rose Tarantula
70003502.description: The Chilean Rose Tarantula, right after its molting. Due to the harsh climate it lives in, these spiders are sturdy, strong and are venomous. However, despite this, they are docile and are said to be easy pets. It has a tendency to not eat for a long period before molting.

70003503.name: Breeding Black-faced Spoonbill
70003503.description: A kind of spoonbill often seen in northwestern parts of the Korean Peninsula. It is a migratory bird that overwinters in large areas after flying south. Usually their feathers are white, however their neck turns yellow and yellow crest feathers appear during the summer in their breeding season.

70003504.name: Boarlet
70003504.description: The young of wild boars. It has a fat short body and short sharp fangs. Wild boars are very cautious and some may attack humans, but baby boars are very cute.

70003505.name: Hibernating African Lungfish
70003505.description: Lungfish in a cocoon made from slime and dirt while underground. Lungfish's lungs develop as it grows, and will do most of its breathing through its lungs instead of its gills. As such, during the dry season where there is no water, it is able to survive by hibernating in the dirt.

quests.name: Further Res. into the Flower in the Deep Forest

70003506.name: Intimidating Blue-ringed Octopus
70003506.description: A small octopus that lives in tropical seas. When it gets agitated, a beautiful blue ring pattern appears on its body. It's said that you can die if bitten by its venomous mouth, or even if you eat it or touch it.

quests.name: Flowering Tree of a Tragic Love

70003507.name: Valle del Bove
70003507.description: A large depression on the eastern slopes of Mount Etna, a volcano in Sicily. Mount Etna is the tallest active volcano in Europe, but its true height changes frequently due to its volcanic activity. There are various theories on this depression, including volcanic eruption, large landslide or surface collapse.

70003508.name: Multiple Vortex Tornado
70003508.description: A group of tornadoes where several vortices to combine into one vortex. Large versions can cause extensive damage to the area it's in. There are many cases where small tornadoes surround a large tornado too.

70003509.name: Light Pillar
70003509.description: A phenomenon where beams of light appear to be extending from the ground to the sky. The pillar-like appearance occurs in cold regions because the light from the ground is reflected from the thin clouds that contain ice particles.

70003510.name: The Colossus of Rhode's Head's Past
70003510.description: An enormous bronze statue of the sun god Helios that stands on the port of Rhodes. It was constructed to commemorate the resistance and victory against Demetrius's siege. On its head is a circlet that represents rays of the sun. It's said that Alexander the Great was used as model for the face.

70003511.name: The Colossus of Rhodes' Pedestal's Past
70003511.description: An enormous bronze statue of the sun god Helios that stands on the port of Rhodes. It was constructed to commemorate the resistance and victory against Demetrius's siege. It's said that it was constructed above a large marble pedestal with its legs standing over the port entrance.

70003512.name: Colossus's Torch
70003512.description: A large torch that is said to have been carried in the right hand of the Colossus of Rhodes. According to stories an elaborate mechanism was inside that could pour boiling hot oil over enemies to drive them out. It's also said that there was a lamp set inside the colossus's head and would emit light from its eyes.

70003513.name: Colossus's Thumb
70003513.description: The Colossus's thumb found in Rhodes. It's made from bronze. According to 'Natural History' by Pliny the Elder there were few who could carry the colossal thumb. According to him 'There were few who could carry the statue's thumb using the strength of their arms as the finger was larger than any other statues around.'

70003514.name: Rhodes' Merchant Ship
70003514.description: Merchant ship that sailed in and out of the port of Rhodes. Unlike navy ships it did not have oars or oarsmen, and was instead made to be able to carry as much cargo as possible. The island of Rhodes located between Greece and Egypt was a key point in the East Mediterranean trade route since ancient times.

70003515.name: Chares' Blueprint of Colossus
70003515.description: Blueprint believed to be for the Colossus of Rhodes. The colossus was supposedly made by placing sheets of bronze over an iron frame while stonework was used for the inside of the legs for stability. It's believed that Chares supervised the construction but some say that he died before the completion of the colossus.

70003516.name: Demetrius the Besieger's Coin
70003516.description: Coin of Demetrius I of Macedon who was also called The Besieger. He took part in the Wars of the Diadochi after the death of Alexander the Great. However he had to retreat after facing the islander's resistance during the Siege of Rhodes. It's said that the people of the island used his army's weapons to build the colossus to commemorate their victory.

70003517.name: Theophanes's Chronicle
70003517.description: Chronicle said to be a compiled in the early 9th century by a monk called Theophanes in the Byzantine Empire. There's even an account on the final days of the Colossus of Rhodes. Originally written in Greek but was later translated into Latin as well. It also includes references to historical documents from its time period that no longer exists making it a valuable item.

quests.name: Legacy TH5. After the Giant Statue

70003518.name: Artemis's Temple's Past
70003518.description: An enormous marble temple built in Ephesus that enshrined the goddess Artemis. Each time it was lost due to destruction or fire it was rebuilt even more beautiful than before. Ephesus's Artemis was influenced by Anatolia's mother earth goddess and as such has a different appearance and personality than the Greek depictions.

70003519.name: Carving of Medusa
70003519.description: A marble with Medusa carved into it. It's believed to have been placed above gate and building entrances. Although Medusa is described as a monster with a hideous face and snakes for hairs in Greek myth there is a theory that she was the goddess of earth in Ancient Anatolia region.

70003520.name: Record of Damnatio Memoriae
70003520.description: A record about someone receiving the damnatio memoriae punishment. The man who set fire to the Temple of Artemis in Ephesus because he wanted to be famous was executed and then later his name was erased from various records. However a historian from another country wrote down his name so his name remains to this day.

70003521.name: Carved Marble Column
70003521.description: A piece from a giant marble column. It's believed to be from one of the columns in Ephesus's enormous temple. On the sides one can see an intricate relief depicting a myth. It was originally colored brightly but it has faded due to time and deliberately removed by someone.

70003522.name: Coin from Ephesus
70003522.description: Coin from the ancient city of Ephesus. The design includes a carving of a deer and a bee which symbolize the goddess Artemis. It's said that Ephesus was a lively city full of visitors coming to worship at the enormous temple as well as merchants and Christian preachers as it was key trade hub.

70003523.name: Sculpture of Cybele on Throne
70003523.description: Throne of Ancient Anatolia's goddess Cybele. She was worshipped as a mother earth goddess in Phrygia and was also worshipped in Ancient Greece and Rome. The way she is depicted with a crown in the shape of castle walls and taming beasts makes her resemble the statue of Artemis from Ephesus.

70003524.name: Home of the Virgin Mary
70003524.description: A small house said to where Virgin Mary spent her final years in. It's located in Ephesus west of Anatolia Peninsula. It's said that one of the apostles took care of Mary during her old age. Later on Christianity flourished in Ephesus such as with the formation of the ecumenical council.

70003525.name: Silver Figurine of Artemis
70003525.description: A small silver figurine that is said to have been modeled after the goddess Artemis but she appears very different than she does in Greek myths. By comparison this Artemis is wearing a tall crown and several round decorations on her chest. The way she has her arms extended and legs together seems to indicate influence from Egypt or Anatolia.

quests.name: Legacy TH6. Praise Our Great Goddess
Legacy TH6. Praise Our Great Goddess
Legacy TH6. Praise Our Great Goddess

70003526.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia's Past
70003526.description: An enormous statue of Zeus in the Ancient Greek city of Olympia. It's said that its surface is covered in ivory and gold, and its ebony throne was decorated in gemstones. Once every four years, athletic competitions were dedicated to this statue of Zeus called the Olympic Games, where people competed in ancient sports.

70003527.name: Philippeion of Olympia
70003527.description: A circular architecture made from marble built in Olympia. It was made as an offering to Zeus to celebrate his victory by King Philip II of Macedon. After the king's death, his son Alexander the Great completed it. It's said that gold and ivory statues of the royal family lined up inside of it.

70003528.name: Stadium in Delphi
70003528.description: A tracking field stadium in Delphi. Named after an Ancient Greek unit of measurement for distance, where one stadion was about 180 meters, although it varied between cities. Delphi held a large-scale athletic competitions called the Pythian Games, which was as big as the ones in Olympia.

70003529.name: Statue of Nike in Olympia
70003529.description: A marble statue of Nike, the goddess of victory, believed to have been in the Temple of Zeus in Olympia. Although her face and wings are lost, it is characterized by beautiful expressions of her open arms and flowing clothes. It is thought to have been decorated on a tall column.

70003530.name: Statue of an Olympic Winner
70003530.description: A statue of an athlete who won in the athletic competitions that were held every four years in Olympia. The winner was given the honor of standing next to god and allowed to build his own statue in the sacred area. It's said that only Greek men were eligible to participate.

70003531.name: Olive Wreath
70003531.description: A crown awarded to the winner of each athletic competition at the Olympic Games. It was made by knitting a special young olive branch. Participants competed only for this crown and honor as their prizes. Stories say that even the Persians, who saw the Greeks as enemies, were impressed by their spirits.

70003532.name: Amphora Depicting Athletes
70003532.description: A pot depicting Ancient Greek competitors. It is either painted red on a black background or black on a red background. Besides running, discus throwing, javelin throwing, and long jumps, there were martial arts, boxing, chariot racing, and hoplitodromos for the sports games. It is said that the games were conducted without clothes.

70003533.name: Eagle Statue on Zeus's Staff
70003533.description: The golden eagle that's said to have been on a staff held by the Statue of Zeus in Olympia. This statue is seen as one of the Seven Wonders of the World. The eagle is a symbol of Zeus, and there is a myth that Zeus would take form of an eagle.

70003534.name: Statue of Narasimha
70003534.description: The form Vishnu took in order to take down Hiranyakashipu of the Asura clan who could not be killed by beast nor by human. He has the head of a lion and the body of a human. As he was a creature that was neither beast nor human he was able to defeat Hiranyakashipu. It's said that Nrisingha came to be based on the story of Narasimha.

70003535.name: Fossil of a Fish with Large Head
70003535.description: A fish fossil that has similar skull to a giant creature with strong-jaws despite the size difference. Compared to its thick skull the bones of its body is weak. As such, it's common that only the skull remains after it dies and turns into a fossil.

70003536.name: Chimera African Violet
70003536.description: A mutated variant of a small plant called African Violet that can only be found in the deeper parts of Southern Africa. Similar to the normal version the flower petals have a distinctive gloss. The mutated variant has a striped pattern unique to it which is very beautiful.

quests.name: Further Res. into the Flower in the Deep Forest

70003537.name: Fire Salamander
70003537.description: A newt with yellow spots that is found in relatively high altitudes in Europe. It has poison glands in which it's believed to release fire from which is why it is named after the Salamander a spirit that controls fire out of the four classical elements.

70003538.name: Spiral Minaret from Tulunids
70003538.description: A spiral minaret built on the Mosque of Ibn Tulun in Cairo. It's said that there is only three other minarets that is spiral-shaped so this is considered a valuable architecture alongside with the Malwiya Minaret.

quests.name: Further Research into the Spiral Tower

70003539.name: Acropolis in Zimbabwe Ruins
70003539.description: Zimbabwe Ruins is a group of stone buildings found in south of Africa. The ruins is divided into three groups 'surrounding walls' 'ruins of the valley' and 'acropolis' on the northern hill.

quests.name: Further Research into the Group of Stone Structures

70003540.name: Monolith of Baalbek
70003540.description: A monolith in the ruins in Baalbek. The ruins consists of three temples dedicated to three Roman gods. One of them is a set of three monoliths called the 'Monolith of Baalbek' which was used as a foundation for the temple of Jupiter.

quests.name: Legacy TH7. The Soaring King of Gods

70003541.name: Wing-Shaped Gusli
70003541.description: A traditional string instrument from Russia. The shape and number of strings of the gusli changed over time as part of its refinement until it finally reached to today's wing-shape. The tradition of guslis will likely continue to be passed onto the next generations through Russian bards.

70003542.name: Flower of Puya Raimondii
70003542.description: The flower of Puya Raimondii is said to bloom once every hundred years. Those who happen to witness this giant be covered in flower must be very lucky.

quests.name: Further Research on the Black-faced Spoonbill

70003543.name: Great Sandy Desert's Crater
70003543.description: An enormous crater in the Great Sandy Desert found in northwestern Australia. It's believed that it was formed due to a meteor impact. If you want to get the full picture you will need to look from significant height.

70003544.name: Rainbow Eucalyptus
70003544.description: A species of tall tree with vibrant colors in each of its bark. As time passes by the bark on the outside comes off, revealing a new bark on the inside. This repetition is what causes changes in the colors of the barks.

quests.name: A Peafowl-like Insect
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast

70003545.name: Peafowl Spider
70003545.description: A spider endemic to a certain region in Australia. The males' abdomens are colorful which they spread and use to dance during courtship.

70003546.name: Oreophrynella
70003546.description: A kind of frog that only lives in specific high altitudes, and likely evolved to fit with the surrounding environment. Its tadpole life stage is absent, meaning they hatch from their eggs as fully formed frogs. Other unique characteristics include the lack of webbed feet and their inability to swim or jump.

70003547.name: Tufted Puffin
70003547.description: A seabird with a large elegant beak and long tuft feathers that grow above its eyes during the summer. At a glance it looks like a penguin, but unlike a penguin this bird is able to fly.

70003548.name: Khirokitia
70003548.description: A prehistoric ruin on Cyprus, a large island in the eastern Mediterranean Sea. It's believed that the stone-made foundations in the ruins were cylinder residential sites and there was a wall surrounding to protect the colony.

70003549.name: Moeraki Boulders
70003549.description: Large spherical stones found along the Moeraki beach in south New Zealand. They have unique turtle-shell-like cracks on the surface. According to a Maori legend, the boulders came to be when the voyaging canoe Araiteuru crashed onto the beach and the gourd-shaped eel baskets from the canoe transformed into the boulders.

quests.name: Great fleets in the Azov sea

70003550.name: Mauritius Island
70003550.description: The largest island out of the islands of Mauritius, east of Madagascar. Surrounded by coral reefs and white sands, the beaches appear in a beautiful array of colors. Not only that, but there is a place in the interior of the island where a ground shines in rainbow-colors.

quests.name: Further Research into the Large Round Stone

70003551.name: Coyolxauhqui's Disk
70003551.description: A large stone disk with a relief of Coyolxauhqui, an Aztec goddess. The disk depicts the myth where she waged a battle against her brother, the sun god Huitzilopochtli, when he was born but was dismembered by him. It's said that the goddess's name comes from the bells on her cheeks.

70003552.name: Rani ki Vav
70003552.description: An enormous stepwell in northwestern India with the name meaning 'Queen's stepwell'. Originally built by a queen in memory of her king in 11th century, it got buried under due to a floor from a nearby river. It is seven floors deep and the pillars and walls are decorated with beautiful sculptures.

70003553.name: Jade Vine
70003553.description: A vine plant that is endemic to the Luzon Island. Its beautiful jade-green flowers grow in multiples and in a upwards claw-like shape. It's said that there are no other plants with jade-colored flowers. This plant can only be found in select regions.

70003554.name: Cylinder Music Box
70003554.description: An automatic music player that plays back music by winding up the clockwork. Sounds are produced because the pins from the revolving cylinder plucks the teeth inside. It is possible to recite a variety of songs by changing out the cylinder.

70003555.name: Wax Cylinder Phonograph
70003555.description: An automatic music player that recreates sounds by tracing the grooves on wax cylinders with a needle. The vibrations created with the needle are picked up by the sound box and transforms into sounds, which is then played out loudly through the horn.

quests.name: Further Research into the Automatic Music Player

70003556.name: Nebra Sky Disc
70003556.description: A bronze disc that was created in prehistoric Europe. The sun, moon and stars are depicted on it. It is large enough that it needs to be carried with both arms. This item is believed to have been used for astronomical observations.

70003557.name: Solar Observatory in Chanquillo
70003557.description: An ancient ruin atop a coastal sand dune in Northwestern South America, that is said to have been built in the 4th century B.C. The thirteen stone towers that are lined up along the hill appear to have been quite tall back in the day. It's believed that the dates were calculated by observing how the sun rose in relation to the towers.

70003558.name: Dendera Zodiac
70003558.description: A relief on the ceiling of Hathor Temple at Dendera, built during the Ptolemaic Dynasty in Egypt. It contains the twelve astrological signs used in Greece, except drawn in an Egyptian style. Celestial bodies look out of place because the relief depicts the stars when the temple was first built.

70003559.name: Gaocheng Astronomical Observatory
70003559.description: A large observatory constructed by a historical scholar, Guo Shoujing. It can calculate seasons and latitudes by measuring the length of shadows. As the main observatory out of the several set up across the nation, it is said that the calendar used records from these observatories as reference.

70003560.name: Tycho Brahe's Mural Quadrant
70003560.description: A brass plate with large divisions mounted over a wall that acted as an instrument to measure celestial bodies' angles. Located at the Uraniborg observatory, it was built by Tycho Brahe. There is an eyepiece near the brass plate and across it on the wall is a viewing hole. Measurements are made by looking through it.

70003561.name: Armillary Sphere
70003561.description: A celestial globe with several metallic rings attached to it, with each ring representing the equator, meridian, and latitude lines. At first, it tried to show celestial objects' movements around the earth, but later the center was replaced with the sun. It was used widely before the telescope, making it a symbol of intellect.

70003562.name: Al-Fazari's Astrolabe
70003562.description: Initially conceptualized in ancient Greece, Ibrahim al-Fazari and his son Muhammad are said to have been the first to build an astrolabe in 8th Century in the Islamic world. It developed significantly in the Islamic world later on. Many of them are made from brass plates with features to determine and predict the locations of the sun, moon and stars.

70003563.name: Keplerian Telescope
70003563.description: A refracting telescope designed by Kepler and later built by Scheiner. Both the eyepiece and objective lens use convex lens. Although it has a wider field and higher magnification compared to Galileo's model, it was mainly used for astronomical observations because the view is upside-down.

70003564.name: River Fog
70003564.description: A kind of evaporation fog that forms over rivers often seen in cold climates. A fog is created when the river's water first evaporates from the warm surrounding and then cooled by cold air.

70003565.name: Synchronized Flashing
70003565.description: A phenomenon where a group of fireflies' bioluminescence gradually synchs to glow at the same pace even though they were flashing separately before. Little is understood about this phenomenon, making it a mysterious behavior.

70003566.name: Gnome
70003566.description: A spirit that, out of the four classical elements, controls the earth. It appears as a small elderly man with lush beard and apparently likes fertile soils. They have the ability to detect buried treasures and can easily unearth gold and treasures. Clever and skillful, it is said that they are great at making handicrafts.

70003567.name: Salamander
70003567.description: A spirit that, out of the four classical elements, controls the fire. They possess the properties of creation and destruction. It is said that they appear in a form of a woman on fire, but this is not clear. In its body contains a deadly poison that can become a powerful medicine if processed right.

70003568.name: Sylphs
70003568.description: A spirit that, out of the four classical elements, controls the air. It flows in the atmosphere to travel around the world. It is said to take form of a slender young woman but also invisible. One theory claims that it is a spirit of a vain woman.

70003569.name: The Great Lighthouse's Past
70003569.description: An enormous lighthouse that was over 130 meters tall. Built around 3rd Century BC on the island of Pharos, it was located on the coast of Alexandria, the capital of Egypt during the Ptolemaic Dynasty. It is said that a large mirror was placed in the highest floor and was used to reflect sunlight during the day.

70003570.name: Island of Pharos's Past
70003570.description: The former appearance of the island of Pharos. There was a temple worshipping the goddess Isis who was also the protector of seas and seafarers. On the island's coast was the Lighthouse of Alexandria which was lit with large fire at the top floor.

70003571.name: Tower of Hercules
70003571.description: An Ancient Roman lighthouse in northwestern Iberian Peninsula. Named after the Greek hero Hercules, it is said that it was modeled after the Lighthouse of Alexandria. It is also called Farum Brigantium from a tale about Breogan, a legendary king of that land.

70003572.name: Kairouan's Minaret
70003572.description: A square pillar minaret that was built in Kairouan, an Islamic holy site in North Africa. It is said that the lower section was constructed in 728 by a governor of the Umayyad Caliphate. Ancient Roman lighthouses may have been modeled after this minaret's distinct shape.

70003573.name: Library of Alexandria's Collection
70003573.description: Scrolls from the Great Library of Alexandria which was the largest agglomeration of knowledge in the ancient world. It's said that all ships that passed through Alexandria was submitted to the Library where copies of it were made. This is supposedly how the Library had collected over hundred of thousands of documents.

70003574.name: Hydraulis
70003574.description: A type of water organ where it creates sounds from air let out by water pressure. It was created by Ctesibius of Alexandria around 2nd Century BC. His pupil, Heron of Alexandria, made improvements on it before it spread across the Mediterranean regions.

70003575.name: Euclid's Elements
70003575.description: Book compiled by Euclid, a mathematician in Alexandria, around 3rd Century BC. The work includes earlier people's work such as Pythagoras and his personal math theories. It became the foundation for many later mathematicians.

70003576.name: Fort of Qaitbay
70003576.description: A fortress located on the peninsula of Alexandria. After the Lighthouse of Alexandria was destroyed from an earthquake in the 14th Century, Sultan Qaitbay of the Mamluk Empire built this fortress on its site. It is believed that materials from the destroyed lighthouse was reused for the fortress.

70003577.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon's Past
70003577.description: An architectural structure said to have been constructed by the best craftmanship under Nebuchadnezzar II of the Neo-Babylonian Empire. Known as hanging gardens for its tiered stairway-like structure, it was built for his queen who missed her lush-green homeland.

70003578.name: Grand Walls of Babylon's Past
70003578.description: A grand wall constructed under Nebuchadnezzar II to protect the Neo-Babylonian Empire's capital city, Babylon. The wall surrounded the city and was richly decorated using blue glazed bricks and many relief sculptures. The north side of the wall is attached with a brilliant gate known as the Ishtar Gate.

70003579.name: Prism of Sennacherib
70003579.description: Prisms carved by King Sennacherib of the Neo-Assyrian Empire. It contains records of construction projects such as palace gardens as well as military affairs during his reign. It's said that it originally had a cylindrical shape but became hexagonal so more words can be carved on it.

70003580.name: Chain Pump
70003580.description: A water pump designed to carry water from lowlands to highlands. Invented in China, it was a wooden agricultural machine to carry water to paddy fields. Rotating boards would collect water from the cistern and because of its design it was called 'dragon backbones' in China.

70003581.name: Sigiriya
70003581.description: A ruin that can be found near the center of Ceylon Island. After Kashyapa I became the king of Anuradhapura Kingdom, he feared that his younger brother would usurp the throne and so moved the capital by building the royal palace on top of a nearly 200-meter-hign rock column.

70003582.name: Chan Chan
70003582.description: Ancient ruin of a massive Chimor Kingdom city in South America. It is characterized by sundried brick buildings and walled compounds. It's said that the city name means 'resplendent sun'.

70003583.name: Ait Benhaddou
70003583.description: Ruin of a fortified settlement located in the Moroccan interior, at the base of the Atlas Mountains. It is built like a fortress to protect the settlement against outside enemies with a single entrance, complicated passageways, and a lack of windows on first floors.

70003584.name: Blue Glazed Brick
70003584.description: Ancient colored bricks that were used for the legendary city of Babylon. The glaze on the brick gives it durability and a blue luster to the surface.

quests.name: Legacy TH10. Legendary and Ancient Architecture

70003585.name: Boyne Valley Tombs
70003585.description: A prehistoric passage tomb in Ireland. It is structure in such a way that sunlight pours inside during specific days of the year, suggesting that it was built using astronomical knowledge. While this passage tomb was built for the winter solstice, there is also a passage tomb built for spring solstice called Knowth.

70003586.name: Avebury's Stone Circle
70003586.description: A prehistoric ruin on the British Isles. The stone circle within the ruins is so large that a small town can fit inside it. It is unclear what the ruin was for but it was possibly used for ceremonies.

quests.name: Further Research on Ruin with Large Stones

70003587.name: Seax of Beagnoth
70003587.description: A sword discovered in the Thames River near London. The sword gives off a majestic and spiritual feeling, thanks to the runes carved on it.

quests.name: Further Research on Historical Relic of Thames

70003588.name: Statue of Vayu
70003588.description: The Hindu god of wind. He is said to be extremely beautiful and also was the first god to receive soma, a kind of ritual drink. He and Indra are powerful beings who control the skies.

quests.name: Further Research on Gods of India

70003589.name: Fossil of a Horn-like Seashell
70003589.description: A fossil accidentally found by a gold miner in North America. The miner claims that it is a fossil of a horned dragon due to its impressive size... But it's most likely a fossil of a large straight seashell.

quests.name: Further Research on Fossil of a Sea Creature

70003590.name: Late Oyster
70003590.description: Mushrooms that grow in groups on dead trees. With its smooth texture and mild flavor, it is commonly eaten. However it looks very similar to the poisonous tsukiyotake mushroom, so one must be careful when harvesting.

quests.name: Further Research on Glowing Poisonous Mushroom

70003591.name: Dinoponera
70003591.description: A kind of large ant that inhabits the rain forests of South America. Not only does it have a powerful jaw and poisonous sting, but it is also very aggressive, so it is known to attack all kinds of animals. It may be just as dangerous, or even more dangerous, than the bullet ants.

70003592.name: Warbling White Eye
70003592.description: A small East Asian bird with a green body and a distinctive white ring around its eyes. They are often confused with Japanese bush warbler which are seen in spring. They have a habit of crowding closely against each other on a same branch, which is very adorable.

quests.name: Further Research on the Round Bird

70003593.name: Malagasy Leaf-Nosed Snake
70003593.description: A snake native to the island of Madagascar. It has a distinctive beak-like snout. It's believed that this snout helps camouflage itself for life on trees.

quests.name: Further Research on the Cool Snake

70003594.name: Frogfish
70003594.description: A anglerfish with a strange appearance, it cannot swim well and instead uses its pectoral fins to walk along the seafloor. The more you look at its round frog-like body, it grows on you.

70003595.name: Statue of Ganga
70003595.description: The statue of Ganga, the deified form of the River Ganges. She is said to be the daughter of Himavat, the deified form of the Himalayas. She is worshipped like the sacred river that blesses people.

70003596.name: Lake Michigan
70003596.description: One of the lakes situated in northeastern part of North America. It is the fifth largest lake in the world. Some claim that it is part of the same lake as Lake Huron, which is besides a strait, because they both have the same water elevation.

70003597.name: Sumatran Rhinoceros
70003597.description: Rhinoceros native to the tropical rainforests in Indonesia. Compared to other rhinos, they are small and have long furs covering their body. It's said that they are hunted for their horns for medicine and craft.

quests.name: Further Research on the Armored Animal

70003598.name: Electric Catfish
70003598.description: A fish that can release a powerful volt of electricity like the electric eel. It releases electricity from its body to search its surroundings and capture small fish.
