It has inhabited the Nile River since ancient times, and has been described as a god of lightning in ancient texts.

70003599.name: Altuna Runestone
70003599.description: A stone monument in Sweden that's believed to have been made during the initial spread of Christianity. The runestone's front depicts the culture's conversion to Christianity, but the side's carving depicts the battle between Thor and Jormungandr from Norse mythology.

quests.name: Further Research on Lightning God's Hammer

70003600.name: Drinking Horn
70003600.description: A drinking vessel made from an animal horn. Not only has it been used for rituals but it also makes an appearance in ancient mythologies. According to the barkeep, drinking horns makes the booze taste good and lifts the spirit of the drinker.

70003601.name: Mosaic in Paphos
70003601.description: A mosaic floor found in Paphos, one of the ruins of Ancient Rome. It depicts the myth of the battle between Theseus and the Minotaur. This is one of the many mosaic artworks on myths in Paphos.

quests.name: Further Research on City Built by Paphos

70003602.name: Meditations
70003602.description: Marcus Aurelius was one of the Five Good Emperors of Ancient Rome. Because he was a great philosopher of stoicism while being an emperor, he acquired the reputation as a 'philosopher king.' His thoughts and philosophies are recorded as diary entries and poems in his book, 'Meditations,' and have been passed down for centuries.

quests.name: Further Research on ancient Roman Emperor's Relic

70003603.name: Animal-shaped Earthenware
70003603.description: Earthenware discovered in Japan. While most dogu figurines are in the shape of a woman to the worship the mother goddess, these ones are in the shape of animals. Perhaps it was made as part of a ritual for a good hunt.

70003604.name: Dulcimer
70003604.description: A percussion-stringed musical instrument. Its name means 'sweet song' in Latin. The instrument is played by stretching metal strings over a trapezoid box and then striking them with a mallet hammer.

70003605.name: Common Butterwort
70003605.description: A carnivorous plant native to the tropical high mountains in Central America. At first glance it looks like a violet, but is indeed a carnivorous plant. The leaves are covered with a sticky liquid and fine hair, which is used to capture and digest insects.

70003606.name: Sable with Winter Coat
70003606.description: A small animal from the Mustelidae family. Although they were widely distributed across the Eurasian Continent, their population has declined in the recent years due to fur trappers. They have beautiful winter coats. The sables exclusive to northern Japan look particularly beautiful in their winter coats.

70003607.name: Statue of Shiva and Parvati
70003607.description: A stone statue of Shiva, the Indian god of creation and destruction, and Parvati, his wife. Parvati is sitting on Shiva's lap, and a sacred animal rests at their feet.

70003608.name: Gaur
70003608.description: A kind of bison that can be found in India that is said to be the largest cattle known. These herbivores are usually tame, but their large body is known to even kill tigers.

70003609.name: Turquoise Mask
70003609.description: An Aztec mask that is believed to symbolize the god of fire, though it is not clear. The surface is covered with turquoise, while pearls were used for the eyes and seashells for the teeth.

70003610.name: South China Tiger
70003610.description: A wild beast native to the mountains and deep forests of southern China. Although slightly smaller than other species of tigers, they are still known to attack humans.

70003611.name: Arabian Angelfish
70003611.description: A fish that is found in the Red Sea. It is known for its arrays of colors, ranging from black, blue, dark purple, as well as a yellow stripe.

70003612.name: Sohal Surgeonfish
70003612.description: A fish native to the Red Sea and the Persian Bay. It has an oval body, small head, and a sharp knife-like spine in its tail. It lives within brightly colorful coral reefs.

70003613.name: Chinese Bahaba
70003613.description: A kind of large fish native to China, often found near estuaries where sea water and fresh water meet. There they consume small fish, shrimps, crabs, and such. These fish can be used in various ways including culinary and medicinal.

70003614.name: Shulba Sutras
70003614.description: An ancient Indian literature on mathematics. The book's focus is on preparing and repairing altars, including what geometry to use when measuring an altar. Readers can learn the various knowledge at the time through this book.

70003615.name: Geography
70003615.description: Book of geography by Eratosthenes of Cyrene, also known as the 'father of geography' in pre-BC Greece. The book is said to have been the highest level of geographical knowledge at the time.

70003616.name: Grey Mangrove
70003616.description: An evergreen mangrove tree that can be found along the tropical coasts of East Asia and Southeast Asia. Because of its resilience to salinity, it's believed that it can survive even in the highly saline soils by the Red Sea.

quests.name: A Tree that Grows in the Sea
A Tree that Grows in the Sea

70003617.name: Arabian Leopard
70003617.description: A subspecies of leopard native to the Arabian Peninsula mountains. They are nocturnal similar to other leopards. Its bright gray fur with black dots is strikingly beautiful.

70003618.name: Bojjannakonda
70003618.description: A monastery ruin on a hill slightly away from Visakhapatnam. It contains several grottos carved from the stone as well as a sitting Buddha statue inside of it. There is another monastery ruin called Lingalakonda in another hill near it.

quests.name: Research on a Cut Stone Ruin

70003619.name: Ashoka Tree
70003619.description: One of the three saint trees in Buddhism that's said to be important in the birth of Buddha. It has a red-orange flower. This tree is believed to fulfill love and bring fortune in India.

quests.name: Further Research on the Sacred Tree

70003620.name: Barbar Temple
70003620.description: An ancient temple located in northern Bahrain Island. It's said to have been built to pray to the Mesopotamian god Enki and his wife Ninhursag. The temple has three layers as it was built over itself through the ages.

quests.name: Research on the Ruins of Ancient Dilmun

70003621.name: Prosopis Cineraria
70003621.description: Also known as the ghaf tree, this tree is found in the drylands of the Middle East. It is a member of the pea family and has such strong life force so it can grow even in a desert-like environment. It's said that there are some trees that are several hundred years old.

70003622.name: Gundestrup Cauldron
70003622.description: Silver vessel believed to have been made during the late Iron Age. It is depicted with Celtic gods in various ways. It's considered the oldest exiting European Iron Age silverwork.

70003623.name: Portland Vase
70003623.description: A cameo glass vase created in Ancient Rome. The deep-blue background is contrasted with white glass carvings of angels and humans. Out of ancient glassworks, this one is one of the oldest and the most notable.

70003624.name: Tuxtla Statuette
70003624.description: A figurine of an egg-shaped monster with the duck beak and wings. It was carved around the late Preclassical Period and has the same carved letters as the one found in the La Mojarra ruin. Interestingly enough, it also has a Mayan Long Count calendar date between its chest and belly.

70003625.name: White-Lipped Deer
70003625.description: These deer are indigenous to China, but specifically found in the highlands of Tibet and its surrounding region. They are known for the white fur that covers their lips, lower jaw and throat. The males also have large antlers. Their velvet antlers are used for medicinal purposes.

quests.name: Research on Deer Indigenous to China

70003626.name: Reliquary of Becket
70003626.description: A reliquary that is believed to contain relics of Saint Thomas Becket of the English Church. The exterior depicts the murder of Becket by knights.

70003627.name: Cup of Jamshid
70003627.description: Cup of the legendary king, Jamshid, from a Zoroastrian myth. Many literatures have been written about this cup within Persia as it was seen as a symbol of royal succession in the Persian Empire. There is a legend that it can tell the future.

70003628.name: Pschent
70003628.description: A red and white crown that could only be worn by pharaohs in Ancient Egypt. The double crown is a combination of the Upper Egyptian crown and the Lower Egyptian crown.

70003629.name: Curtana
70003629.description: A sword passed down in the English royal family, also known as the Sword of Mercy or Sword of Justice. The blade's tip is missing but the sword is treated as one of the Crown Jewels of England.

70003630.name: Joyeuse
70003630.description: Holy sword said to belong to Charlemagne as described in the Song of Roland. Later, the sword became a symbol of the French king's royal authority and was also used during the king's coronations.

70003631.name: Crown of Saint Stephen
70003631.description: A crown given by the Pope to Stephen I, the first King of Hungary. It is a symbol is the Hungarian king's royal power. The gold crown is adorned with several enamel plaques as well as gemstones and pearls.

70003632.name: Nine Tripod Cauldrons
70003632.description: Symbol of royal authority in Ancient China. According to legend, the cauldron was made by Yu the Great, founder of Xia Dynasty, after he collected bronze from the Nine Provinces. The metal cauldron with three legs were also used for rituals and ceremonies.

70003633.name: Kusanagi
70003633.description: One of the Three Sacred Treasures of Japan. One story tells how Yamato Takeru cut down burning grass that was ignited by his enemies. Since then, the sword also known as the 'Grass-cutting Sword'. However, it's not certain if this is the real Kusanagi sword or not.

70003634.name: Relief of Ardashir I
70003634.description: An enormous relief from Sassanid Empire of Persia, located on a boulder in the Persian Gulf North Coast. The carving depicts Ardashir I receiving the symbol of royal authority from the creator deity, Ahura Mazda.

quests.name: Legacy TH11. Monarch Favored by the Gods

70003635.name: Giant Phantom Jelly
70003635.description: A jellyfish that can grow to more than 10 meters in length. It is one of the largest invertebrates. It is known as the 'phantom jellyfish' because there are few sightings of it as it lurks in the deep sea.

70003636.name: Five Flower Lake
70003636.description: A huge lake, one of the most scenic lakes in the Jiuzhaigou. Calcified components are submerged at the bottom of the lake. When sunlight shines into the lake, it emits various colors such as blue, orange, and purple depending on the reflections.

70003637.name: Busosanseong
70003637.description: The capital city of the Baekje kingdom. It was built on the Busosan Mountain, south of the Baengma River. The Samchungsa Shrine enshrines the tablets and portraits of the three loyal subjects who served King Uija, the last king of the Baekje kingdom.

70003638.name: African Penduline Tit
70003638.description: A bird native to Africa. It builds soft, bag-like hanging nests in trees. To deceive predators, it creates a false entrance that looks more real than the real one, in addition to the real entrance. This is truly the wisdom of a small bird that has many natural predators.

70003639.name: Takahe
70003639.description: A flightless bird of the Rallidae family. About the size of a chicken, it has a thick beak and thick legs to adapt to life on the ground. Their feathers turn blue or green depending on the angle at which they are exposed to light, and their colors become more vivid as they reach adulthood.

70003640.name: Tainan Confucian Temple
70003640.description: The oldest Confucius temple in Taiwan. It was built by Chen Yonghua, a military strategist, also known as 'Tungning Zhuge'. The temple also serves as an educational institution. In front of the main gate, there is a sign that reads 'First Academy of Taiwan'.

70003641.name: Ninety-five Theses
70003641.description: A critical paper against the Catholic Church, raised by Martin Luther. Unable to overlook the corruption of the church through the sale of indulgences, Luther posted it on the gates of a local church. The impact was so great that it caused the Christian schism in Western European countries.

70003642.name: Cnut the Great's Coin
70003642.description: Cnut was an 11th-century king of the Danes, who were also known as the Vikings. He conquered England, Norway and Sweden, and established the North Sea Empire. Coins with his portrait inscribed on them circulated far and wide as the Viking trade spread.

70003643.name: Groundhog
70003643.description: One of the largest animals in the squirrel family. Also known as woodchucks. Found around forested areas in North America, it builds intricate tunnel networks for its nests. When digging tunnels, it loosens the soil, making it a beneficial animal among farmers. However, they have a rough temperament.

70003644.name: Red Garra
70003644.description: Commonly known as 'doctor fish'. It is distributed in the rivers of western Asia. As they can tolerate relatively high water temperatures, they can be found in hot springs as well. They have the habit of eating dead skin cells of humans and do not have teeth, so they are used for natural peeling that does not damage the skin.

70003645.name: Yellow-blotched Map Turtle
70003645.description: A turtle that inhabits the Pascagoula River in the Mississippi basin. Its dorsal carapace has spiny projections and is speckled with yellow and orange.

70003646.name: Don Quixote
70003646.description: A novel written by a Spanish writer, Miguel de Cervantes. It is a tale of the adventures of a man who calls himself Don Quixote, deluding himself that he is a knight because he admires knightly tales so much. It is rich in critical spirit and reads as a satire on the old customs represented by chivalry.

70003647.name: Adenium
70003647.description: A plant native to the Arabian Peninsula. It is called the 'desert rose' for its beautiful flowers. The petals are bright and large, but the plant is susceptible to cold.

70003648.name: Hussar's Wings
70003648.description: Hussars were winged heavy cavalry. They were brave cavalrymen dressed in Polish splendor and carried large feather ornaments made of raptor feathers. They were said to make noise by letting the wind blow through the feather ornament to instill fear in the enemies.

70003649.name: Gili Trawangan
70003649.description: A small island in the South Pacific with beautiful coral reefs. It is the westernmost of the three Gili Islands in the Lesser Sunda Islands.

70003650.name: African Bullfrog
70003650.description: A frog that inhabits the area south of the Sahara Desert in Africa. Some grow to more than 20 cm in length. In addition to insects, they prey on small animals and even birds.

70003651.name: Ebony Jewelwing
70003651.description: A black dragonfly. The body is black with a green metallic sheen. Its distinctive feature is the black color of its wings, which are not transparent like those of other dragonflies. It moves its wings differently from other dragonflies, fluttering its wings like a butterfly and perching with its wings erect.

70003652.name: Fuchsia
70003652.description: A plant native to Central and South America. The flowers are beautiful and used for appreciation. It is also called a 'lady's earring' because of the way its flowers face down.

70003653.name: Pictor
70003653.description: A constellation in the southern sky. It can be observed mainly in the southern hemisphere. It is located south of Columba and Caelum. The constellation represents the shape of an easel placed in Caelum, established by the French astronomer Lacaille.

70003654.name: Leo Minor
70003654.description: This constellation represents a small lion. It is located between the head of Leo and the foot of Ursa Major. It is formed by faint stars and is not very conspicuous. It was established by the German astronomer Kepler.

70003655.name: Arctic Hare
70003655.description: Rabbits that live in the Arctic Circle and other regions. To adapt to the extreme cold, their bodies are covered with a thick coat of fur. Their fur changes with the seasons, turning brown and gray in summer and white in winter. This is said to allow them to blend in with their surroundings and hide from natural predators.

70003656.name: Siberian Bighorn Sheep
70003656.description: A wild sheep found in northeastern Siberia, also known as Snow Sheep. It is characterized by its twin horns that are curved backward. They live in high-altitude mountainous areas. The bottoms of their hooves have a special shape that allows them to run over precipitous cliffs in a single bound.

70003657.name: Congo Peafowl
70003657.description: The peacock that inhabits the tropical rainforests of Africa. The male and female peacocks differ only in body coloration, but not much else, and neither has brightly decorated feathers. Their staple diet consists of fruits and insects.

70003658.name: Mexican Wolf
70003658.description: A wolf that inhabits the forested areas of North America. They are smaller than ordinary wolves. When hunting prey larger than themselves, they form packs.

70003659.name: Billow Clouds
70003659.description: A phenomenon in which clouds become wavy. It is caused by atmospheric waves that move the air. It is often seen when a warm front or low-pressure system approaches and is said to be a sign that the weather is about to change for the worse.

70003660.name: Red Tides
70003660.description: A phenomenon in which seawater turns reddish in color. There are various theories as to the cause of this phenomenon, such as changes in water temperature and eutrophication. In the Book of Revelation, the second angel's trumpet causes the sea to turn the color of blood, and one-third of the sea creatures die, which has been feared by people for centuries.

70003661.name: Mirage
70003661.description: A phenomenon in which the scenery that should be beyond the horizon is visible. It is said to be caused by the refraction of light rays due to temperature differences above the sea surface. In China, there is a legend that a spirit animal exhales 'chi' and makes a mirage appear.

70003662.name: Nine-tailed Fox
70003662.description: A nine-tailed spirit beast from East Asia. It is considered to be a lucky animal that represents the reign of a superior monarch. On the other hand, it also has a malevolent side that deceives people by disguising itself as an immensely beautiful woman.

70003663.name: Cerberus
70003663.description: A guard dog of the underworld in Greek mythology. It has three heads, and while one head is asleep, the other two stand guard. It is said to guard the entrance to the underworld and never misses the escape of the departed from the underworld.

70003664.name: Tang Tri-color Glazed Camel
70003664.description: One of the sancai, also known as 'Tang Three Colors', ceramics produced during the Tang Dynasty. This masterpiece depicts a camel looking up at the sky and a foreign male band. Both the beautiful modeling and the gorgeous glaze are among the most perfect of the 'Tang Three Colors'.

quests.name: Legacy TH12. A Ship on a Sea of Sand

70003665.name: Shinan Shipwreck
70003665.description: A trading ship from the Yuan dynasty. It was carrying a large number of trading goods such as ceramics, copper coins, and incense wood. It sank while en route to Hakata, Japan.

70003666.name: Wanli Ship
70003666.description: A Ming Dynasty trading ship. Trade was thriving in the Ming Dynasty, and the Wanli Ship was also engaged in maritime trade. It is thought to have carried trading goods such as ceramics, tea, and silk. It sank off the coast of Malaysia.

70003667.name: Pepper Wreck
70003667.description: A Portuguese trading ship. It was loaded with pepper from India. After the opening of the Indian route, many traders sailed to India in search of spices. The Pepper Wreck should have been one of these ships. It was wrecked at the mouth of the Tagus River near Lisbon in the early 17th century.

70003668.name: Kyrenia Shipwreck
70003668.description: A trading ship active in Ancient Greece. Its main cargo was wine in ceramic jars called amphorae. It left the island of Samos in the 3rd century B.C. and sank just before was about to arrive on the island of Cyprus.

70003669.name: Uluburun Shipwreck
70003669.description: A merchant ship of the Fenician civilization in the 13th century BC. It is said that they were trading with Canaan and other cities in the Eastern Mediterranean. Its main cargo was copper ingots. It sank near the southern coast of Turkey.

70003670.name: Skuldelev Shipwreck
70003670.description: A Viking ship from the late Viking Age. It was sunk in the waters near Roskilde, the then capital of Denmark, to serve as a barrier against the enemy.

70003671.name: Peutinger Table
70003671.description: A map from the time of the Roman Empire. It depicts the roads and rivers of the time. The original map has already been lost, but a manuscript by Poytinger of Augsburg has been handed down.

70003672.name: Jiaozi
70003672.description: The first paper money in human history. It was issued in Sichuan during the Northern Song Dynasty. Initially, it was a deposit note for iron coins issued by a private bank, but later it was issued by the government and circulated as paper money.

70003673.name: Pompeii Lakshmi
70003673.description: A small statue of a woman carved from ivory, discovered in the ruins of Pompeii. Based on its shape, it is believed to be Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of beauty and fertility. A similar small statue was also found in India, which corroborates the Indo-Roman trade.

70003674.name: Burial Amber Necklace
70003674.description: A necklace made using lots of ambers. It is one of the burial accessories excavated from a tomb of the Hallstatt civilization. It is thought to have belonged to a noble family.

70003675.name: Silver Pepper Shaker
70003675.description: A Roman pepper shaker. It is shaped like a noblewoman. Back in the day, pepper was a precious commodity, and pepper shakers were also decorated with gold leaf.

70003676.name: Augustus' Coin
70003676.description: A gold coin excavated in a city in southern India. It is engraved with the portrait of Augustus, the first Roman emperor. It is believed to be proof of the existence of trade between ancient India and the Roman Empire.

70003677.name: Ubar Ruins
70003677.description: Ruins of an oasis city that prospered through the frankincense trade in BC. From the look of the remaining walls of the fortress, it is certain that the city once flourished as a strategic point on the frankincense trade route.

70003678.name: Australian Box Jelly
70003678.description: Also known as sea wasp. Its whole body is translucent and box-shaped, and its tentacles are long. It is the most toxic jellyfish in the world, and its sting is said to kill even a human within minutes. For this reason, it is feared and nicknamed the 'killer jellyfish'.

70003679.name: Northern Lapwing
70003679.description: A cute traveling bird with a cat-like characteristic call and beautiful crest feathers. It breeds in northern Europe in the summer and spends the winter in southern Europe and North Africa.

70003680.name: White Whale
70003680.description: Also known as Beluga Whale. They inhabit the high-latitude waters of the northern hemisphere, including the Bering Sea and the seas around Alaska. They produce a wide variety of sounds from the frontal regions of the head, which they use to detect food and communicate with their mates. They are nicknamed 'canaries of the sea' for the beauty of their calls.

70003681.name: Diocletian's Palace
70003681.description: The palace where the Roman emperor Diocletian lived after he retired from the throne. It was built in Split, a port town facing the Adriatic Sea. It is surrounded by a strong wall more than 20 meters high. It is both a military facility and a luxurious palace.

70003682.name: Crab-eating Fox
70003682.description: An extant species of medium-sized canid inhabiting shrublands and wetlands. They migrate to the lowlands during the dry season and to the highlands during the rainy season. They feed on small vertebrates and crabs during the dry season and insects during the rainy season. They have coarse body hair, a grayish-brown or yellowish-gray body, and a distinct black line on their back.

70003683.name: The Istanbul Runestone
70003683.description: During the age of the Byzantine Empire, a cathedral was built in the imperial capital, Constantinople. On the parapet of the cathedral, there is an inscription in runes. It is said to have been inscribed by a descendant of the Vikings called 'Varangians' who were sent as mercenaries to the Byzantine Empire.

70003684.name: African Wildcat
70003684.description: Being native to North Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, they inhabit a broad variety of landscapes ranging from deserts to savannas, shrublands, and grasslands. They are believed to be the ancestor of domestic cats after having been domesticated by the ancient Egyptians.

70003685.name: Call Duck
70003685.description: It is said to have been bred in the Netherlands from ducks. Their high-pitched distinctive call was used to lure other ducks into traps. They are also popular as pets.

70003686.name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
70003686.description: A Hindu temple in Trivandrum in southern India where the deity Vishnu is enshrined. It is said that a vast treasure lies underground. There is a door that cannot be opened unless a chosen one chants a spell because it is sealed with a Naga seal.

70003687.name: Maine Coon
70003687.description: A type of domestic cat. Because they inhabit cold regions, they have long fur. Although they are more than 1 meter long, they are also known as 'Gentle Giants' because of their mild-mannered nature. They are said to be highly intelligent and can skillfully lift objects and open doors.

quests.name: Further Research on Norwegian Forest Cat

70003688.name: Snow Leopard
70003688.description: A species of leopard, that inhabits the alpine regions of Central Asia, with fur that is whitish to grey with black spots. It has a tail about 1 meter long, which makes it easy to balance on uneven terrain in the mountains. Because it lives in alpine terrain far from where humans live, it is considered a mysterious creature in folklore and belief.

70003689.name: Tojinbo
70003689.description: A series of cliffs facing the sea. The massive pillar-like walls (columnar joints), 25 meters high, stretch for 1 km. It is said to have been formed by magma that blew out of the ground, cooled, and hardened, which has been eroded by waves and winds.

quests.name: Further Research on Giant Stone Columns

70003690.name: Woodcuts of the Apocalypse
70003690.description: One of Albrecht Durer's most famous woodcuts, depicting various scenes from the Book of Revelation. The text of the 'Book of Revelation was printed on the back of the woodcuts, and they were sold as a book.

70003691.name: Night-scented Lily
70003691.description: A member of the taro family with large leaves. As its name suggests, it is not edible, but toxic and causes severe abdominal pain. In China, it was used as a medicine based on the idea of using poison to conquer poison.

70003692.name: Mensa
70003692.description: A constellation in the southern sky. It can be seen mainly in the southern hemisphere. The French astronomer Lacaille named the constellation after Table Mountain overlooking Cape Town.

70003693.name: Tiangong Kaiwu
70003693.description: An encyclopedia covering a wide range of industrial techniques, written by the Ming Dynasty scholar Song Yingxing in the spirit of 'learning more by practice than by classroom learning' during his travels throughout China. It covers all industries of the Ming dynasty. It was not highly valued in China and was dispersed, but in Japan, it was highly valued by the philosopher Kaibara Mashiken and others and has survived.

70003694.name: Red-footed Booby
70003694.description: A seabird that inhabits tropical and subtropical waters of the Indian, Atlantic, and Pacific Oceans. It has a habit of living in flocks. It is characterized by bluish-gray skin around its eyes and bright red feet.

70003695.name: Gotland Pony
70003695.description: A horse native to Gotland Island, Sweden. It is about 120 cm tall and is classified as a pony. It is believed to be an old breed that existed in the Stone Age and descended from the extinct tarpan horse.

70003696.name: Horseshoe Cloud
70003696.description: A U-shaped cloud that looks like a horseshoe. It tends to form when a cumulus cloud is disappearing. It often changes its shape and disappears within a few dozen seconds after it appears.

70003697.name: Lenticular Cloud
70003697.description: It is often comparable in appearance to a lens or saucer, and can be oval, bowl-shaped, or various other shapes. Refers to clouds that appear away from mountain peaks. It is said to be a sign of rain.

70003698.name: Gothenburg
70003698.description: A city at the mouth of the Gota River on the Scandinavian peninsula. It is a prosperous trading center. The city was founded by Gustav II Adolf and has many Dutch-style buildings. Gothenburg means the city of the Goths.'

70003699.name: Alpheratz
70003699.description: The brightest star in the constellation of Andromeda. Its name means 'horse' in Arabic. Its other name, Sirrah, means 'navel' and is derived from the fact that it once belonged to the constellation Pegasus and was located at the abdomen of Pegasus.

70003700.name: Dubhe
70003700.description: The alpha star of Ursa Major and its brightest star which is second-magnitude. It is the tip of the bowl part of the Big Dipper. Together with the beta star Merak, it provides a clue to finding Polaris.

70003701.name: Schedar
70003701.description: The brightest orange star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It represents the breast of Queen Cassiopeia of Ethiopia and means breast' in Arabic.

70003702.name: Caph
70003702.description: A second-magnitude star in the constellation of Cassiopeia. It is located at the base of the arm of Queen Cassiopeia of Ethiopia. It means 'the stained hand' in Arabic. In Arabia, there was a star sequence called the 'hands of the Pleiades,' and this star represented the dyed nail of the Pleiades.

70003703.name: Alphecca
70003703.description: The brightest star in the constellation of Corona Borealis. Its name means 'the bright star of the broken' in Arabic. Its other name, Gemma, means 'jewel in Latin, and it represents a jewel shining in the center of the crown.

70003704.name: Menkar
70003704.description: A red giant star in the constellation of Cetus. It means 'nostril' in Arabic.

70003705.name: Deneb Kaitos
70003705.description: The brightest orange star in the constellation of Cetus. It shines on the tail of Cetus. It means 'the second frog' in Arabic. Fomalhaut in the constellation of Piscis Austrinus is 'the first frog.' The name comes from the Arabic 'southern tail of Cetus.'

70003706.name: Alderamin
70003706.description: The brightest star in the constellation of Cepheus. It represents the right shoulder of Cepheus, the king of Ethiopia, and means 'right forearm' in Arabic. It is predicted to become the north star in about the year 7500 AD.

70003707.name: Acrux
70003707.description: The brightest star in the constellation of the Southern Cross or Crux. Located at the lower part of the cross, it is the southernmost first-magnitude star. It was named Acrux because it is the alpha star of the constellation of Crux.

70003708.name: Great Mosque of Djenne
70003708.description: A large mosque constructed in Djenne, a trading city along the Niger River. Mud from the river was kneaded to make sun-dried bricks, which were then piled up and covered with mud. Inside the mosque, approximately 100 massive pillars made of mud can be found.

70003709.name: Cauliflower Fungus
70003709.description: A flower-like mushroom that grows wild at the base of larch and other conifers, thriving in humid, misty environments. This unique mushroom boasts a clean aroma and a fresh texture, making it a rare and elusive find.

70003710.name: Orchid Mantis
70003710.description: The praying mantis that inhabits Southeast Asia, specifically tropical rainforests. They utilize their appearance to mimic orchid flowers, luring and capturing other insects that come near them.

70003711.name: Humpback Whale
70003711.description: Large whales, measuring between 13 to 15 meters in length, typically inhabit polar regions. However, they migrate to tropical waters during the summer to feed on krill and other fish. When hunting, multiple whales release bubbles to create a circular wall, a distinctive aspect of their unique hunting behavior. This strategy concentrates the prey in one spot.

70003712.name: Rosy Maple Moth
70003712.description: The species belongs to the family Saturniidae and is primarily distributed in eastern North America and southern Canada. It has a body length of approximately 3 cm, and its entire body is adorned with pink and yellow hairs. The larvae primarily feed on maple leaves, while the adults, with degenerated mouthparts, cease feeding and focus solely on reproduction, which occurs at night.

70003713.name: Charaka Samhita
70003713.description: One of the classical medical texts that represents Ayurveda, the traditional medicine of India, is based on the writings of Charaka, the physician to King Kanishka of the Kushanas. This text provides particularly detailed studies on fevers, temper tantrums, and masses.

70003714.name: Timely Clearing After Snowfall
70003714.description: Work by Wang Xizhi, a calligrapher of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, consists of only 28 characters. It was penned as a letter to a friend following his retirement from worldly affairs and is regarded as the pinnacle among works in the semi-cursive script style.

70003715.name: Daurian Jackdaw
70003715.description: The crow widely distributed in East Asia and displays a variety of plumage colors, with many individuals featuring white plumage from the neck to the belly. They are migratory birds known for traveling long distances during winter.

70003716.name: Bayon
70003716.description: The ruins of a temple, situated near the center of the Angkor Complex, aptly named 'beautiful tower' in Khmer, bear witness to a unique construction process. The absence of standardized stone materials and piling methods suggests that it was built incrementally over many generations by royal order. Notably, the tower is renowned for the presence of human masks carved in various parts, including the central four-faced statue.

70003717.name: Pom-pom Crab
70003717.description: This small crab, measuring approximately 2 cm in length, is primarily found in coastal areas of the Indian and Pacific Oceans. It exhibits a unique behavior of attaching anemones to its claws and using their stinging tentacles to ward off predators, resembling boxing gloves. It is also commonly known as a boxer crab.

70003718.name: Silver Dirham
70003718.description: Silver coins minted in ancient Persia were widely circulated in the Middle East, and their circulation expanded as the power of the Islamic empire grew. The surface of the coins is engraved with Arabic characters representing the Islamic faith.

70003719.name: Kit Fox
70003719.description: A small fox that inhabits the deserts of the North American continent. They are omnivores, consuming small mammals, insects, and fruit. In addition to constructing their own burrows, they also utilize the abandoned nests of other animals.

70003720.name: Pitons
70003720.description: These are two small volcanoes on the Caribbean island of St. Lucia. The taller one is known as Gros Piton, while the shorter one is called Petit Piton. Together, they are often referred to as twin mountains.

70003721.name: Great Dusky Swift
70003721.description: This bird resides beneath the giant Iguazu Falls in South America. Its long wings enable it to fly horizontally at high speeds, allowing it to effortlessly navigate through the falls.

70003722.name: Lynx
70003722.description: A constellation in the northern sky, situated between Ursa Major and Auriga. It represents a slender wildcat and was established by the 17th-century astronomer Hevelius.

70003723.name: Dhritarashtra
70003723.description: A statue of Buddha, one of the Four Heavenly Kings and the guardian deity of the East. In his hand, he holds a lute, a treasured instrument.

quests.name: Legacy TH13. Buddhist Deity with a Musical Instrument

70003724.name: Bianzhong
70003724.description: A percussion instrument composed of multiple bells, it made its debut during the Spring and Autumn period. In the Ming Dynasty, ornate gold braided bells were even crafted. Each bell produces a distinct pitch and symbolizes power, often employed in court ceremonies.

70003725.name: King David's Harp
70003725.description: David was a king of ancient Israel who appears in the Old Testament. As a young boy, David played the harp to soothe Saul, the previous king, who was afflicted by an evil spirit.

70003726.name: Kaen Daiko
70003726.description: A pair of large drums used in ancient Japanese court music, known as 'Gagaku,' which are adorned with intricate dragon and phoenix carvings. The most renowned among them is said to have been donated by Yoritomo, the inaugural shogun of the Kamakura Shogunate.

70003727.name: Tin Whistle
70003727.description: A vertical flute with six finger holes and a mouthpiece similar to that of a recorder. It is believed to have originated in Ireland and is used in traditional music.

70003728.name: Veena
70003728.description: A traditional stringed instrument from South India, it is said to have been played by Sarasvati, a goddess in Indian mythology.

70003729.name: Zampona
70003729.description: A traditional wind instrument from the Andes region of South America, these instruments are typically made from bamboo or reeds of various lengths, which are then bound together. They are believed to have originated in the ancient Andean civilization before the Inca Empire, as evidenced by their discovery in the ruins of the Nazca culture.

70003730.name: Aulos
70003730.description: Ancient Greek woodwind instrument. The body is divided into two pieces, and each finger hole is held down with both hands to play. Legend has it that the instrument was invented by the goddess Athena, who appears in Greek mythology.

70003731.name: Acubens
70003731.description: Alpha star of Cancer, located on the left claw of the crab, its name means 'claw' in Arabic.

70003732.name: Al Tarf
70003732.description: The 4th-magnitude star in Cancer which is the brightest within the constellation. It is located at the end of the crab's legs. Its name means end in Arabic.

70003733.name: Praesepe Cluster
70003733.description: A cluster of stars in the center of Cancer. The name is Latin for 'manger.' It was once thought to be a single celestial body, but Galileo Galilei discovered that it was a cluster of stars.

70003734.name: Camelopardalis' Spiral Galaxy
70003734.description: A spiral-shaped nebula in Camelopardalis. It is located around the giraffe's forefoot.

70003735.name: Praecipua
70003735.description: The brightest star in Leo Minor, it is a faint star of approximately 4th magnitude and is situated at the rear end of the lion. Its Latin name means 'leader,' though this name is not commonly used anymore.

70003736.name: Mokoro
70003736.description: A small boat used in the vast wetlands of South Africa. They are made by burning the trunks of sausage trees, which are widely distributed in Africa, and hollowing out the inside. They are an indispensable means of transportation in the intricate waterways.

quests.name: A Small Boat Going Through the Marsh

70003737.name: Reef Manta Ray
70003737.description: A species of ray that is considered to be the second-largest ray in the world. It is similar to the giant oceanic manta ray and is often mistaken for one, but can be distinguished by the curved white pattern on its back and the coloration of its mouth. It is widely distributed in tropical and subtropical waters of the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

quests.name: Searching for a New Species of Large Marine Creature

70003738.name: Saona Island
70003738.description: An island located southeast of Santo Domingo on the island of Hispaniola. Columbus reached this island on his second voyage. Surrounded by coral reefs, it is home to a large number of birds and marine life. The crystal-clear waters and white sand beaches are beautiful.

70003739.name: Ivory Tablet of the Embroidered Uniform Guard
70003739.description: An ivory tablet used by the Embroidered Uniform Guard, one of the military units under the direct control of the Ming emperor. It was worn around the waist as proof of identity. A note was engraved on the back, and it was obligatory to wear it when on official business. Those who lent it to others or lost it were charged with a crime.

quests.name: Think of It as Helping People

70003740.name: Harris's Hawk
70003740.description: A medium-sized bird of prey that inhabits the New World. They hunt in flocks, which is a rare habit for birds of prey. It is known as a falcon that is friendly to humans and easy to keep.

quests.name: Longing to Travel with the Hawk

70003741.name: Taiwan Leopard Cat
70003741.description: A subspecies of the leopard cat believed to be endemic to the island of Taiwan. Its ears are rounded at the tips and have white spots on the back. It is closely related to the Japanese Iriomote wildcat. When it captures prey, it has the habit of striking it with its paws to weaken it.

quests.name: Cats Lurking in the Island's Forests

70003742.name: Pigeon on a Peach Branch
70003742.description: A Chinese painting depicting a pigeon perched on a peach branch, said to have been painted by Hui Zhong, the emperor of the Song dynasty. In the upper right corner of the painting, there is calligraphy in a rare script that indicates the time of completion, as well as a huaya, which is a stylized signature, along with a red seal that serves as proof of its authenticity.

70003743.name: Black Manta
70003743.description: A blackened onychophorid ray, which accumulates black pigment due to a melanism phenomenon. The cause of this occurrence remains to be determined. Sightings have been reported in various locations, and the encounter rate appears to be high near the island of New Caledonia.

70003744.name: Anna's Hummingbird
70003744.description: Hummingbirds, renowned for their stunning colors, are often referred to as 'flying jewels.' The head feathers of males reflect light, creating an illusion of color change when viewed from different angles. During the breeding season, males frequently alter their crown colors to attract females.

70003745.name: Ancona Cathedral
70003745.description: A cathedral situated on Piazza del Duomo, a hill overlooking the entire port of Ancona. It was constructed on the site of a Greek temple dedicated to Aphrodite, the patron goddess of navigation. It is also known as the Cathedral of Saint Ciriaco, named after Saint Cyriacus, the patron saint of Ancona.

quests.name: Temple Watching Over the Port Town

70003746.name: Black Snow
70003746.description: A phenomenon in which snow and ice turn black or gray. Although there is no definitive information on the cause of this phenomenon, one theory suggests a possible link to coal.

70003747.name: Fibratus
70003747.description: A type of cirrus or cirrostratus cloud, these thin, stringy clouds form in the troposphere above 5,000 meters. They are easily altered by strong winds and continually drift to different locations.

70003748.name: Aitvaras
70003748.description: A serpent spirit worshipped in the cities on the east coast of the Baltic Sea. Once it takes residence in a house, it is challenging to drive it out, but it is believed to bestow riches upon the house's owner. It is said to transform into a black cat or a rooster inside a room and into a dragon or a snake with a burning tail outside.

70003749.name: Xiangliu
70003749.description: A monster from ancient Chinese mythology, it is depicted as a serpent with nine human heads and the ability to devour nine mountains. It served the evil god Gonggong, one of the Four Perils. According to the Shan Hai Jing, it was vanquished by Yu the Great, the first king of the Xia Dynasty.

70003750.name: Elnath
70003750.description: The second brightest star in Taurus, located at the tip of the northern horn. Its name comes from the Arabic phrase 'to poke with the horns.' Due to its position between Taurus and Auriga, it was once considered to belong to Auriga.

70003751.name: Gomeisa
70003751.description: A star within Canis Minor, situated around the neck of the dog. Its name, in Arabic, means 'the little bleary-eyed one.'

70003752.name: Mirfak
70003752.description: The brightest star in Perseus, it appears yellowish-white in color. Its name means 'elbow' in Arabic. It used to be called Algenib, which means 'the side.'

70003753.name: Butterfly Cluster
70003753.description: An open cluster of stars in Scorpius, it is situated at the leading edge of the scorpion's tail. It is named after its resemblance to a butterfly with its wings spread.

70003754.name: Globular Cluster in Scorpius
70003754.description: A globular cluster of stars located in Scorpius, it is visible to the naked eye.

70003755.name: Globular Cluster in Pegasus
70003755.description: A globular cluster in Pegasus, it is relatively easy to find because it is located at the leading edge of Pegasus' nose.

70003756.name: Tarantula Nebula
70003756.description: A nebula in Dorado, situated at the leading edge of the Large Magellanic Cloud, it is believed to have been first discovered by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille during his 1751 expedition to the Cape of Good Hope.

70003757.name: Japanese Sea Cucumber
70003757.description: A type of sea cucumber, it is commonly found in the reef zone along the western coast of the Pacific Ocean. Dried sea cucumbers are distributed as a luxury foodstuff in the Orient and are renowned as an ingredient in Lu cuisine, a dish from North China.

70003758.name: Echeveria
70003758.description: A genus of succulent plants in the Bensaceae family, Echeveria was discovered by a Spanish expedition at the end of the 18th century and captivated European horticulture. The name honors the 18th-century Mexican botanical artist Atanasio Echeverria.

70003759.name: Sapsali
70003759.description: A breed endemic to the Korean Peninsula, it was kept by the royal family during the Silla period and was believed to possess spiritual power to drive away evil spirits. They are also known as Sapsal Gae in the Korean peninsula.

quests.name: A Dog That Fends Off Demons

70003760.name: Akoya Pearl Oyster
70003760.description: Widely found in the reef zone, they possess the ability to produce pearls by hardening foreign substances such as gravel that enter their bodies with their secretions. Pearls produced by the Akoya Pearl Oyster are renowned for their exquisite luster among shellfish. Since ancient times, numerous stories about pearls around the Persian Gulf have been told.

70003761.name: Pearlfish
70003761.description: Widely found in the tropics of various oceans, it has the habit of invading the interior of sea cucumbers and oysters and using them as a habitat. They are not harmful to the host, but they are not beneficial either.

quests.name: What Lurks in the Sea Cucumber

70003762.name: Osamedachi
70003762.description: A large wooden sword, it was traditionally used by visitors to Mt. Oyama, one of the holy mountains in Japan. This practice originates from the legend of Minamoto no Yoritomo, the first shogun of the Kamakura shogunate, who dedicated a sword to a shrine. In emulation of this legend, people now dedicate a wooden sword to the shrine with their wishes written on it. It is believed to bring prosperity in business and luck in victory.

70003763.name: Belem Tower
70003763.description: A tower built in the 16th century in the Belem district of Lisbon. It was constructed to commemorate Vasco da Gama's pioneering achievement of establishing the Indian route. The tower stands as a historic site and symbolizes the Age of Discovery.

70003764.name: Jeita Grotto
70003764.description: Limestone caves north of Beirut, extending approximately 9 km in length, are divided into upper and lower sections showcasing various stalactite formations. These caves contain traces of human remains from the Stone Age, along with discoveries of bronze vessels and other artifacts. They hold significant value as an important site for tracing prehistoric civilizations.

70003765.name: Roskilde Cathedral
70003765.description: A cathedral situated on the Danish Island of Chelan, it blends Romanesque and Gothic styles with its brick exterior walls. Originally a wooden church commissioned by King Harald the Bluetooth in the 10th century, it now houses the coffins of the kings of Denmark.

70003766.name: Kalmar Castle
70003766.description: A castle built in the 12th century in Kalmar, Sweden. Surrounded by the sea, it is connected to the land by a bridge extending from the front gate. In 1397, the Kalmar Union was agreed upon here.

quests.name: Personal Union of the Baltic Sea

70003767.name: Yukimushi
70003767.description: A type of aphid, they are covered with a waxy secretion resembling cotton and are known to appear in large numbers at the end of autumn, often flying in swarms. In Japan, they are nicknamed 'snow bugs' due to their resemblance to falling snow.

70003768.name: Lithops
70003768.description: A genus of succulent plants in the ice plant family, it is native to South Africa. Preferring dry areas, it is known for its slow growth. It typically grows in clusters in shady places, such as behind rocks, where it receives limited sunlight. The plant has a distinctive shape and blooms from a central crack, which is an unusual characteristic.

70003769.name: Saint John's Co-Cathedral
70003769.description: A chapel constructed in Valletta, the capital of Malta, in the late 16th century by Cassiere, a Knight Commander of the Order of St. John. The chapel, made of limestone, a specialty of Malta, serves as the final resting place for successive heads of knighthoods.

70003770.name: Mount Oyama
70003770.description: Also known as Mount Afuri, the summit of this 1252-meter-high mountain offers a commanding view of Sagami Bay. Since ancient times, the mountain has been revered as a deity associated with rain and the cessation of rain. During the Edo period, visiting Mount Afuri became immensely popular among the people of Edo.

70003771.name: Pungsan Dog
70003771.description: A breed of dog indigenous to Korea, the Pungsan dog has been utilized as a hunting companion since ancient times. Renowned for its fearlessness, it is said that the Pungsan dog is undaunted even by opponents larger than itself. Famed for its strength, once it bites, it tends to hold on tenaciously.

70003772.name: Albino Sea Cucumber
70003772.description: A white variant of the Japanese sea cucumber, this rare individual is believed to occur only once in every 100,000 sea cucumbers. The cause of this rarity is unknown, but it is attributed to a genetic mutation that leads to insufficient synthesis of melanin pigment, resulting in a white body surface. Due to its scarcity, the white sea cucumber is considered to bring good luck.

quests.name: Further Research on Japanese Sea Cucumber

70003773.name: Shaviana Truffles
70003773.description: A subspecies of Echeveria native to the desert regions of Mexico, it thrives in dry, well-ventilated sites. The blue-gray leaves of this plant overlap in folds, with only the edges displaying a peach-colored hue. The coloration becomes more vivid when exposed to full sunlight.

70003774.name: Feiyufu
70003774.description: Traditional Chinese clothing worn by Ming dynasty imperial guards. One of the costumes bestowed by the emperor on those who have distinguished themselves. It literally means 'flying fish clothing.' However, the creature used in its design is a dragon-like creature with wings and the fanned tail of a fish.

70003775.name: Jellyfish Lake
70003775.description: A salt lake situated on the island of Mecherchar in the central Palau Archipelago, Jellyfish Lake is connected to the open sea by several cracks and caves. However, it remains isolated from the traffic of living creatures. The lake derives its name from the millions of jellyfish, including the golden jellyfish, that inhabit its waters.

quests.name: Further Research on the Palau Islands

70003776.name: Magnificent Riflebird
70003776.description: A species of Paradisaeidae found in New Guinea, it's renowned for its elaborate courtship dance. During this display, the male spreads its wings and shakes its head regularly from side to side in a distinctive manner. Interestingly, male subadult birds closely resemble females and often mimic them, approaching mature males to observe and learn the intricate courtship dance up close.

quests.name: Further Research on Superb Bird-of-Paradise
quests.location: Island of New Guinea South Coast
